```txt
6. UPDATE — 2026-09-03, LATER SESSION
================================================================================
Three commits on main after 419c43a. Sections 4 and 5 above are superseded
where they conflict with this; the rest still stands.

  8b450d3  The cache the title could see but not use
  10516c5  Find the instruction that gives up
  71dfab6  The game is not waiting. It is showing an error.

6.1 THE STARTUP-COUNTER GAP IS CLOSED, NOT JUST EXPLAINED
Section 4 records it as UNASSIGNED. It was the disk cache. Upstream's
Partition3/4/5 rules gave \Device\Harddisk0\Partition5 a mapping it did not
have before; the cache probe used to fall through to "Unrecognized Xbox path"
and fail, and JSRF read that as "no cache" and loaded from the disc. With the
rule the probe succeeds, so the title starts caching, and every cache write
then failed: it writes through Z:\Media\Font\jetfont.dat~ without creating the
directories above it, and Font is not among the directories it makes at
startup. The lower counters were the title getting FURTHER into a path that
could not be served, giving up, and loading less. Not a translation or
renderer regression.

Fixed in kernel_file.c by creating parent directories whenever the disposition
creates, keyed on O_CREAT so it cannot drift from posix_open_flags.

From a pristine emulated HDD both binaries now agree exactly:
  9 NtOpenFile, 7 clears, 4 presents  (was 7 / 7 / 3 against 9 / 7 / 4)
The merged build additionally populates the cache and reads jetfont.dat back
from it in full, which the pre-merge tree never did.

6.2 THESE DELTAS REPRODUCE HEADLESS
Section 4 says desktop access is essential for a valid graphical comparison.
That is true for clears/flips against a window, but the open/present deltas
reproduce with no desktop at all, so iterate headless and save the time.
Reset state between runs: a pristine HDD is kept at
  build-macos/merge-audit/emulated-hdd-pristine
and emulated-hdd is mutable shared state that WILL change results if reused.

6.3 BOTH BINARIES WRITE JSRF_FATAL.ERR
Not a merge regression, and it predates all of the merge work. Section 4's
"neither run reported a guest fault" is true of the runtime and false of the
title.

6.4 WHY THE RENDERER IS NEVER ASKED TO DRAW
Section 5 points at ROUTE_B_PLAN sections 15/16 and frames the remaining work
as a game state machine to be costed separately. The answer is simpler:

    JSRF IS SITTING IN ITS DISC-ERROR DIALOG.

The object that writes JSRF_FATAL.ERR is stable across runs at 0x01943200,
vtable 0x001CC660, and its constructor copies a string into +0xA0:

    "There's a problem with the disc $nyou're using. $nIt may be dirty or
     damaged."

It never asks for a scene because it never reaches one. Section 15's
observations all fit: the renderer serves resource and query calls because the
dialog needs them, and slot 10 and the state setters are never reached because
there is no scene. The decision to write the marker is one instruction, at
0x0006EE5C:  test [esi+0x98], 0x400000 / je / call sub_00012770.

The dialog is built by sub_0006F450, message id 0x12B0, flags 0x10003 (both
visible in the instance at +0x08 and +0x04). FOURTEEN sites call it. Which one
fires is the open question, and it is now the highest-value one in the tree.

6.5 INSTRUMENTS ADDED (all env-gated, off by default)
  RECOMP_PATH_TRACE=1          path translation, incl. symlink resolution.
                               XBOX_TRACE is compiled out without _DEBUG, so
                               the path layer was silent in a release build.
  RECOMP_FILE_BACKTRACE=<sub>  guest stack scan at a matching file open, plus
                               a candidate this-pointer and its +0xA0 string.
                               This is what identified the dialog.
  NtOpenFile now prints the same "[FILE] -> status" line NtCreateFile does.

6.6 A TRAP THAT COST TIME
The guest-trace hooks in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/guest_trace.h are DEAD
in the current generated code. RECOMP_GUEST_FUNCTION appears nowhere under
build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/gen, so jsrf_trace_function is never called and a
hook placed there cannot fire for ANY function -- verified against the main
loop, which runs constantly. Catching a direct call such as sub_0006F450
requires regenerating with those emitted. There is no runtime-side substitute.

6.7 TRIED AND REVERTED
Padding a short read up to the requested length within the file's last 512-byte
sector, on the theory that JSRF asks for sector-rounded lengths (1180160 for a
1179952-byte jetfont.dat) and treats a short return as damaged media. It
removed every short read and changed nothing. The premise was wrong twice:
NT reports the true count at end of file, and an Xbox disc sector is 2048
bytes, so these were never sector reads. Do not re-try it.

6.8 SUGGESTED NEXT STEP
Find which of the fourteen callers of sub_0006F450 raises the dialog. That
needs a regeneration with RECOMP_GUEST_FUNCTION emitted (see 6.6), after
preserving evidence, per section 3's warning about the seed accumulator.
sub_00068250 is an error-state machine on [esi+0xa8] with three of the call
sites in it and is reached from sub_000689A0; sub_00067EF7 holds two more.

================================================================================
7. THE DISC ERROR WAS OURS — rdtsc  (commit 296a0a2)
================================================================================
Supersedes 6.4's "which of the fourteen callers" as the open question, and
supersedes ROUTE_B_PLAN section 15's conclusion.

THE CHAIN, end to end:
  sub_00145560 is JSRF's QueryPerformanceCounter and is literally `rdtsc`.
  sub_00145571 is its QueryPerformanceFrequency and returns the constant
  0x2BB5C755 = 733333333, the Xbox CPU clock. The title times a startup step
  and at 0x00025370 compares elapsed ticks against 0xE4E1C0 = 15000000, about
  20.5 ms. Over that it tail-jumps (0x0002537E) to sub_0006F730, which does
  `push 0x400000` at 0x0006F732 -- the exact bit tested at 0x0006EE5C -- and
  raises the disc-error dialog. The tail jump is why the guest backtrace showed
  the tree-walker's return address: dispatch is legitimate, vtable 0x001CB0A8
  slot 1 really is sub_00066440.

  rdtsc lifted to "/* TODO: rdtsc */". THAT IS NOT A NO-OP. EAX and EDX keep
  what they held, so the title sampled two stale registers, subtracted them,
  and compared garbage against its threshold. It failed every run, on this tree
  AND on the pre-merge one.

FIXED in src/kernel/recomp_tsc.c (monotonic host clock scaled to 733333333),
declared in templates/runtime/recomp_types.h, emitted by tools/recomp/lifter.py.

RESULT, from a pristine emulated HDD:
                        before            after
  JSRF_FATAL.ERR        written           NOT written
  files opened          9                 12
  cached assets         jetfont only      jetfont + se_sys
  command dwords        3,151             188,774,853
  methods               2,172             134,251,937
  clears / flips        7 / 3             250,319 / 250,312
  real geometry draws   0                 0

JSRF no longer declares a bad disc. It gets past the font, caches the
sound-effect set, and drives the command ring continuously instead of stopping
after initialisation.

7.1 GENERATED CODE IS HAND-PATCHED
build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/gen is hand-patched at the three rdtsc sites
(recomp_0006/0007/0009, functions sub_00145560, sub_0015FA20, sub_00193C40) so
this could be tested WITHOUT resetting the seed accumulator. The committed
lifter change emits the same code on the next regeneration; carry nothing by
hand. gen/recomp_types.h was refreshed from templates/ for the same reason.

7.2 WHERE IT STOPS NOW
Steady after ~25s and unchanged at 45s: 12 opens, two cached assets, no further
file activity, presenting continuously, draws still 0. It never writes
Z:\Media\Cache\JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE.CMP and leaves se_sys.dat~ behind, so the
cache build is incomplete rather than finished.

7.3 NEXT
The pusher, against a title that is finally submitting real state:
  - draws=0 while methods run to 10^8. Either the draw methods are not being
    decoded or the title still is not issuing them.
  - bad_headers is now NON-ZERO (6609) where it was always 0. New, and worth
    understanding before trusting the counters above.
  - The biggest unhandled block is sixteen consecutive dwords at
    0x0B00..0x0B3C in equal counts -- a 4x4 matrix -- plus 0x02B4, 0x02C0,
    0x02E0, 0x032C.
  - Then: why the cache build stops after two assets.

7.4 METHOD WORTH REUSING
Hand-editing build-macos/.../gen and rebuilding is a cheap, non-destructive way
to instrument or test a change to recompiled code: it is git-ignored, it does
not touch the seed accumulator, and a regeneration discards it. That is how the
disc-error call site was identified (a probe at sub_0006F450 and sub_0006F730
printing MEM32(esp), since each call site pushes a distinct return address) and
how the rdtsc fix was validated before touching the lifter. Note the guest
tracing hooks in guest_trace.h CANNOT do this -- see 6.6.

================================================================================
8. FIRST PIXELS FROM THE TITLE'S OWN GEOMETRY  (commit 1b44943)
================================================================================
Follows directly from section 7: once JSRF stopped declaring a bad disc it
began submitting a real method stream (331 distinct methods, against a couple
of dozen before), and the executor still drew nothing.

THE MISSING METHOD: NV097_INLINE_ARRAY (0x1818), pushed 1.2 million times in a
25-second run. nv2a_pb_exec.c knew only NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT16 -- indices into
arrays the title points at -- and had no handling for vertices carried in the
command stream itself. Implemented: the layout is implied by which attributes
declare a non-zero size and what format each gives, packed in attribute order,
recomputed per batch. fetch_vertex() is the single indirection; the rasteriser,
colour and screen-space code are unchanged.

  draws    0 -> 103,924        indices  0 -> 311,772  (3 per batch)

WHAT THE GEOMETRY IS. Batch: 3 vertices, prim 5, stride 4 dwords, attr0
position (2 floats), attr9 (2 floats):
    v0 (  -0.53,   -0.53)  uv (   0,    0)
    v1 (2559.47,   -0.53)  uv (2560,    0)
    v2 (  -0.53, 1919.47)  uv (   0, 1920)
A full-screen triangle in SCREEN SPACE at exactly 4x the 640x480 clip rect.
batch_is_screen_space() therefore rejects all of them, which is why draws rose
and rasterised triangles stayed at 0.

RECOMP_PB_EXEC_NOCLIPTEST=1 rasterises regardless. With it: 22,500 triangles,
and the framebuffer stops being black. Evidence:
  build-macos/merge-audit/inline-array-first-pixels.bmp
It is a flat fill, because the triangle is four times too large. THAT IS NOT A
PICTURE OF THE GAME and must not be described as one.

8.1 NEXT, in order
  1. Viewport. 0x0A20 is a top unhandled method and is viewport state. The 4x
     factor between the vertices and the clip rect is almost certainly the
     viewport scale/offset the executor does not apply. Applying it should put
     these triangles on the surface at the right size, at which point the
     clip test passes on its own and NOCLIPTEST can go back to being a
     diagnostic.
  2. The rest of the unhandled ranking, in count order: 0x0100 (x3.9M),
     0x0110 (x1.9M), 0x0A20 (x718k), and the 16-dword block at 0x0B00..0x0B3C,
     which is NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM -- the title uploads vertex shaders.
  3. bad_headers is non-zero (6609 over 45s) where it was always 0. Still not
     understood; understand it before trusting the pusher's totals.
  4. The cache build still stops after two assets and never writes
     JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE.CMP.

8.2 DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR IS UNCHANGED
None of the executor runs without RECOMP_PB_EXEC, and with it the clip test
still gates rasterisation exactly as before. The two new env switches are
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_NOCLIPTEST (rasterise rejected batches) and the existing
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_VERBOSE (now also dumps the first three inline batches: prim,
stride, per-attribute dword offsets, and raw words).

9. THE VIEWPORT, THE ONE TRIANGLE, AND WHAT THE STALL IS NOT
================================================================================
Commits e089140 (viewport + correction) and 69f3b24 (pad diagnostic).

9.1 CORRECTION TO SECTION 8
Section 8 called the decoded inline output "readable geometry", which overstates
it. Widening the verbose dump from 3 batches to 40 shows ALL FORTY BYTE-
IDENTICAL: prim 5, 12 dwords, stride 4 dw, the same full-screen triangle.
103,924 draws is one primitive drawn 103,924 times, not 103,924 primitives.
The title is blitting a blank screen every frame. INLINE_ARRAY was genuinely
missing and decoding it is correct, but it did not reveal a scene, and
inline-array-first-pixels.bmp is that one triangle filling the surface.

9.2 THE VIEWPORT IS NORMAL
The executor now tracks NV097_SET_VIEWPORT_OFFSET (0x0A20) and
NV097_SET_VIEWPORT_SCALE (0x0AF0) instead of counting them unhandled:
    scale  (320, -240, 16777215, 0)      = W/2, -H/2
    offset (320.531, 240.531, 0, 0)      = W/2 + 0.53125, H/2 + 0.53125
A textbook 640x480 D3D viewport, so the render target really is 640x480 and the
4x is not a surface misreading. The vertices are neither screen space nor NDC
(through that viewport v1 lands at x = 819350). They are inputs to the title's
VERTEX PROGRAM, uploaded by the 16-dword block at 0x0B00..0x0B3C
(NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM). Placing them needs an interpreter for it.
DO NOT divide by four: it lands this one triangle correctly and is a
coincidence fit, not a transform.

9.3 THE STALL, AND FOUR THINGS IT IS NOT
Steady state, unchanged between 25s, 45s and 120s runs:
  12 file opens, jetfont.dat + se_sys.dat cached, se_sys.dat~ left behind,
  JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE.CMP never written, no JSRF_FATAL.ERR, frame loop healthy.
Stack sample at 12s (build-macos/merge-audit/claude-sample-steady.txt):
  sub_00151DD0 (heaviest), sub_0018D0F0, sub_00013A80, sub_00012A20,
  sub_0014CCA0, sub_00013930, sub_000659C0, and a big cluster in the D3D
  section 0x0018D000-0x00198000.
So it is RUNNING, not blocked on a wait.

Ruled out, each with evidence:
  - Not slow, stalled. 120s changes nothing from 25s.
  - Not a fatal. JSRF_FATAL.ERR is never written any more.
  - Not the suspend/resume handshake. NtSuspendThread/NtResumeThread are
    balanced (~2300 each per 20s) and win32_compat.c implements cooperative
    suspend properly with a safe point at the thunk dispatch.
  - NOT WAITING FOR A BUTTON. RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1 reports port 0 connected and
    pulses A and START once a second; 45 seconds of it changed nothing.

9.4 A REAL GAP THE ABOVE EXPOSED
There is NO KEYBOARD INPUT on POSIX. src/input/xinput_device.c needs an SDL
GameController; without one every port reports ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_CONNECTED.
This build cannot be driven without a controller.

9.5 NEXT, reordered by what actually gates progress
  1. Why the cache build stops after two assets. It is the only thing between
     here and the title having content to draw, and it is not any of 9.3.
     se_sys.dat~ surviving says the second asset's finalise did not complete;
     start there. RECOMP_FILE_BACKTRACE=se_sys will name the caller.

10. THE CACHE LOADER IS NOT FAILING — IT STOPS BEING ASKED
================================================================================
Investigating 9.5 item 1. No code change; findings only.

10.1 THE ASSET LOADER RUNS EXACTLY THREE TIMES
sub_00025DD0 is the asset-open helper (RECOMP_FILE_BACKTRACE=se_sys lands in it
at +0xCF for the Z: cache attempt and +0x152 for the D: fallback). Probing its

    #1  ret 0x00033AD7 (sub_00033A80+0x57)  a0 = a stack buffer
    #2  ret 0x0002C08E (sub_0002C072+0x1C)  a0 = "D:\Media\Font\jetfont.dat"
    #3  ret 0x0002C146 (sub_0002C12D+0x19)  a0 = a runtime-built path (se_sys)
It is NOT looping, NOT retrying and NOT failing. Nothing asks it for a fourth
asset. The stall is upstream of the loader, in whatever decides what to load.

10.2 THERE IS A CACHE STATE MACHINE, AND IT IS NOT THE LIVE PATH
sub_00026170 dispatches on [esi+0x18f8] through a jump table at 0x000261E8:
    state 0 -> sub_00026185  open next asset via sub_00025DD0;
                             returns non-zero -> state 1, zero -> state 3
    state 1 -> sub_000261A7  sub_00025400; non-zero -> [esi+0x18f4] = 1,
                             state = 2; zero -> falls out to sub_000261E2
    state 2 -> sub_000261C9  "mov eax,1 / ret" -- TERMINAL IDLE, does nothing
    state 3 -> sub_000261D0  sub_00026080
State 2 parking for ever would explain the symptom exactly -- but a probe on
sub_00026170 printed NOTHING in 30 seconds. It is never called, and the se_sys
backtrace contains no 0x000261xx frame. Do not spend time on this machine
before establishing it runs at all; it is probably a later phase.

10.3 WHAT THE STALL IS NOT (cumulative, all evidenced)
  - not slow (120s == 25s)          - not a fatal (JSRF_FATAL.ERR never written)

The question is now "what decides to request assets", i.e. the task/state layer

12.2 d3d8_vsh.c DOES NOT DECODE REAL MICROCODE
It looked like the unblock for section 11.4 and it is not. Against the program
captured from JSRF (now recorded in that file and in nv2a-shaders.md):
  - insn[0] as bits 0..31, the way vsh_extract reads: every slot is
    MAC=NOP ILU=NOP. The first uploaded dword is zero in all of them and that

  - words reversed: slot 2 gives ILU opcode 8, which does not exist (0..7), and
    wants c128 and c143 when the title uploads only c0, c1, c60..c62.
Word order, offsets, or both are wrong. It is Windows-only and that path has
not been exercised here, so nothing caught it -- a wrong field yields a
plausible shader rather than a failure. DO NOT BUILD ON IT UNTIL IT PASSES THE
VECTOR. An empirical search for the offsets over five instructions is
underdetermined; too many candidates survive while the high word is zero.

14. THE INPUT PATH, FOLLOWED TO THE HARDWARE  (commit 1698432)
================================================================================
Following 13.5 item 1. The title's input path is the XPP section, and XPP is a
USB stack: it drives the OHCI host controller at 0xFED00000 directly rather
than going through any driver this runtime provides. That is why nothing in
src/input is reachable (13.2) -- the guest was never going to call it.

14.1 TWO REGISTERS THAT PLAIN RAM GOT WRONG  (measured, RECOMP_OHCI_DUMP=1)
Before:
    +0x08 HcCommandStatus = 0x00000001   HostControllerReset STILL SET
    +0x48 HcRhDescriptorA = 0x00001200   NDP = 0 -- ZERO DOWNSTREAM PORTS
    +0x54 HcRhPortStatus  = 0x00000000
    +0x18 HcHCCA          = 0x01452000   the stack really did initialise
HCR is self-clearing on hardware; on RAM the reset never finishes. NDP is
read-only and reports the port count; XPP writes the register for NPS/NOCP and
on RAM that write zeroes NDP too. A root hub with no ports can never have
anything attached.

Both are now held from the NV2A ack tick (xbox_McpxHoldRegisters), which is
where the existing note in that file said such things belong. After:
    +0x08 = 0x00000000    +0x48 = 0x00001202 (NDP=2)    +0x54 = 0x00000000
Two ports is a CHOICE, not a measurement. RECOMP_OHCI_PORTS overrides it.

14.2 THIS DOES NOT ATTACH A CONTROLLER
Port status stays zero, which is an honest "nothing plugged in" instead of the
previous "no ports exist". Game behaviour is UNCHANGED: 12 opens, three cached
files, no JSRF_FATAL.ERR. Do not record this as having unblocked anything.
Giving JSRF a pad means descriptors and control transfers through the HCCA at
0x01452000 -- real device emulation, sized as its own piece of work.

14.3 CORRECTION MADE DURING THIS INVESTIGATION
I inferred mid-way that the ~100k KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel/KfLowerIrql pairs per
20s were USB polling. They are not. sub_001BD5FF is a generic interlocked
read-and-reset helper called from all over the game code, and the OHCI init
sub_001BD14A runs EXACTLY ONCE -- probed and counted in the generated code. The
USB stack is not spinning; it initialised and went quiet.

14.4 INSTRUMENTS ADDED
  RECOMP_OHCI_DUMP=1     root hub register block, once, a few seconds in
  RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN=1   live message-box objects by vtable (section 13.3)
  RECOMP_OHCI_PORTS=n    override the NDP the root hub reports

14.5 NEXT
  1. USB device emulation, if input is the goal: HcHCCA is at 0x01452000 and

     and ConnectStatusChange, then service the control transfers XPP issues.

15. KNOCKING ON THE ROOT HUB  (commit 511e9ea)
================================================================================
Following 14.5 item 1. RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 announces a device on port 1 --
CurrentConnectStatus + ConnectStatusChange, and RootHubStatusChange raised in
HcInterruptStatus. RECOMP_OHCI_DUMP now takes a COUNT, so a reaction is visible
as a change rather than a single reading.

IT DOES NOT ENUMERATE. What that established:

15.1 SOMETHING DOES REACT
Without the probe HcRhPortStatus[0] reads 0x00000000; with it, 0x01450001. The
extra bits are 18, 22 and 24 -- none of which OHCI defines -- and 0x0145xxxx is
heap-shaped (the HCCA is at 0x01452000). Treat this as a reaction, NOT as an
enumeration. Do not record it as success.

15.2 THE ISR STILL DECLINES
HcInterruptStatus holds RHSC for the rest of the run and is never acknowledged.
Nothing accepted the interrupt.

15.3 THE PROBE FIRES TOO EARLY
It waits only for HcControl. At that moment HcInterruptEnable is still 0; XPP
enables RootHubStatusChange later. An announcement made before the stack is
listening is not one. FIX THIS FIRST if resuming: gate on
HcInterruptEnable & 0x40 instead of on HcControl.

15.4 A DIAGNOSTIC THAT HAS BEEN LYING
The device-ISR log line prints en(+0x140) and intr(+0x100) -- NV2A PMC offsets
-- against an OHCI regbase whose interrupt registers are +0x10 and +0x0C. Every
"ISR ... -> FALSE ... en=0 intr=0" line about 0xFED00000 in every log in this
tree has been reporting the wrong registers. It says nothing about USB.

15.5 WHAT ATTACHING A CONTROLLER ACTUALLY NEEDS, IN ORDER
  1. the announcement timed after HcInterruptEnable has RHSC (15.3)
  2. an ISR path that accepts the interrupt (15.2)
  3. service for the control transfers XPP then issues through the HCCA at
     0x01452000 -- device/config/HID descriptors, endpoint and transfer

That is device emulation and a PROJECT, not a patch. It was left scoped rather
than half-built.
```

```txt
This continues CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-03_STARTUP.txt, which remains accurate

==========================================================================
1. WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT IT MEASURABLY BOUGHT
==========================================================================

The previous handover's goal A was the measured allocation failure on

At the end of the run it is cycling NtReadFile / NtAllocateVirtualMemory /

9dc5cdcf2b4abd98a266b99496fa0062bec2c56e30b979a7cb5d033275eed1b3, the same
value as the previous session. No graphics behaviour was changed here.

==========================================================================
2. THE ALLOCATION FAILURE - WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS
==========================================================================

It was not fragmentation, not retained capacity, and not a title asking for
more RAM than the console has. New instrumentation (section 4) reported, at
the first failure:

  live 997 blocks / 47,307,848 bytes; free 0 blocks / 0 bytes

Nothing had ever been returned to the guest heap, because every kernel free
the title calls was routed somewhere that could not release a guest block:

  ExFreePool (ordinal 17) had NO bridge at all. The dispatch table entry was
    commented out, deliberately, because the existing wrapper called the host
    HeapFree on a translated guest pointer -- but the matching allocations
    (bridge_ExAllocatePool / WithTag) come from xbox_HeapAlloc and hand back
    guest VAs, so the correct free is xbox_HeapFree. JSRF calls it.

  NtFreeVirtualMemory (199) went to xbox_NtFreeVirtualMemory, which calls the
    host VirtualFree on a guest address. MEM_RELEASE was silently dropped (the
    POSIX shim returns TRUE for size 0), and MEM_DECOMMIT would have called
    mprotect(PROT_NONE) on live guest RAM. 12,072 calls in the latest run.

  MmFreeContiguousMemory (171) did reach xbox_HeapFree, but the title frees
    through the physical-memory mirror (0x80000000 + address) and the table
    was matched on the raw value, so no block ever matched. All eight frees
    logged in the baseline are 0x81Exxxxx / 0x81Fxxxxx addresses.

Repairing those three exposed a second, separate failure: 13.9 MB free, a
2.8 MB largest free block, and a 349,520-byte page-aligned request failing
anyway. xbox_HeapAlloc split a reused block at the end of the request, so the
remainder started at an arbitrary address -- and every caller that reaches
this heap asks for at least 4 KB alignment, so those remainders were
unallocatable. Splitting on a page boundary fixed it.

Two further allocator defects were repaired at the same time, both of which
would have surfaced later rather than immediately:

  Reuse handed over the whole free block without splitting, so a 16-byte
  request could retire the rest of a 4 MB block permanently.

  Coalescing tested the adjacent table index. Merging leaves a size-0 hole
  behind, and a hole between two adjacent free blocks made them permanently
  un-mergeable. It now skips holes.

Files: src/kernel/kernel_bridge.c, src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.{c,h}.

==========================================================================
3. THE SECOND BLOCKER - UNRESOLVED RETURN PATHS, GENERALISED
==========================================================================

With memory available the title reached Stg10_05 and then took SIGSEGV in
sub_00177FE0 with a garbage object pointer, preceded by four
'epilogue never ran' ABI reports.

That was NOT a use-after-free introduced by the heap repair. Verified: a run
with RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=0xAB, which fills every freed block, produced the
identical fault with the identical bad pointer (0x8508C483, not the poison).
It was new code territory, reached for the first time.

The cause is the same class the previous session repaired for shared
epilogues. sub_0002D240's switch dispatches through 0x0002D438, and its
default case 0x0002D3B3 was still a placeholder stub whose whole body is
`g_esp += 4`. That stub consumes the return address and nothing else, so the
four registers sub_0002D240 pushed stayed on the guest stack.

recover_shared_epilogues.py only repairs stubs that are pure return
sequences. 220 placeholder stubs remained. The new
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/recover_midfunction_entries.py repairs the rest
of the same failure: an address at an instruction boundary inside an already
detected function is real code, and translating it from there through the end
of its owner produces the body it should have had. An address in the gap
between two detected functions is a whole function discovery missed, and is
translated through the start of the next detected function; anything past its
return is unreachable and costs only compiled bytes. A body that jumps
backwards to another undetected entry pulls that entry in too, with a
declaration added to recomp_funcs.h.

  208 of 220 recovered (149 in the first pass, 59 after gap and
  backward-jump support was added), plus 13 entries they reference.
  Manifest: build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/midfunction_entries.json
  Backups: recomp_stubs_unresolved.c.before-midfunction[.N],
           recomp_funcs.h.before-midfunction

  12 were not recovered and are named by their skip reason when the script
  runs: 5 not on an instruction boundary in their owner, 4 incomplete
  translation, 3 past the last detected function. None of them executed in
  the 60-second run. They are the honest remaining list, not a clean bill.

The 13 pulled-in entries have declarations and bodies but no dispatch entry,
because nothing calls them indirectly today. If a later indirect call lands on
one, RECOMP_ICALL will report it unresolved rather than silently misbehaving.

==========================================================================
4. NEW DIAGNOSTICS - USE THESE BEFORE GUESSING
==========================================================================

xbox_HeapReport(const char *why)  [src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c]
  Prints arena bounds, bump high-water, unreached bytes, live and free block
  counts and totals, the largest free block, bytes retained beyond what
  callers requested, and the top owners by live bytes -- each named by kernel
  ordinal and guest return address -- plus the 16 largest live blocks. Called
  automatically on the first allocation failure. This is what turned "the
  heap is full" into "nothing is ever freed", and it names the guest call
  sites: 0x00145A48 (the title's allocator), 0x0014903F, 0x0018E6E9,
  0x00199789 were the four largest.

xbox_HeapSetOwner(ordinal, guest_ra)
  Called by kernel_thunk_dispatch around each bridge so blocks carry that
  attribution. Zero means the runtime itself allocated, not a guest call.

RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE=<n>    narrate the first n frees and reuses (default 64).
RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=<byte> fill freed blocks. Use this before blaming a heap
  repair for a fault: if the bad pointer is not the poison, it did not come
  from a freed block.

[STUB] reports  [tools/recomp/translator.py, and
                 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/announce_unresolved_stubs.py]
  Every unresolved stub now announces itself once when it runs. A stub that
  runs is a return path this build got wrong, and it used to run in silence.
  This is what identified 0x000250C9 and 0x001185B0 after the first recovery
  pass. The generator emits this shape; the script applies it to a generated
  checkout that must not be regenerated, and --remove reverses it.
```

```txt
3 September 2026 - the renderer question, measured

WORKSPACE
/Users/andrewcollard/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Jet Set Radio Future/upstream_xboxrecomp_clean

Work after e97c71c is in the tree and NOT yet committed.

==========================================================================
1. THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT WE EXPECTED
==========================================================================

The screen is black because THE TITLE'S VERTEX BUFFERS ARE EMPTY. Not because
the transform is wrong, not because a shader opcode is missing, and not
because the wrong program is bound. There is nothing to draw.

Sampling a draw at batch 20,000 (RECOMP_VSH_SAMPLE moves the sample point;
batch 1 is always the measured full-screen blit and tells you nothing):

  [VSH] late batch attrs: a0(t2 s4 st32 @01BA2000) a3(t0 s4 st32 @01BA2010)
                          a4(t0 s4 st32 @01BA2014) a9(t2 s2 st32 @01BA2018)
                          reads=1F9B inline=0 idx=0
  [VSH] late batch in0=[0 0 0 0] in3=[0 0 0 0] in9=[0 0 0 1]
  [VSH] late batch bytes: 00 00 00 00 ... (32 bytes, all zero)
  [VSH] array owner: block 0x01BA2000+4096 (asked 128) ordinal 166
                     ra=0x00199789 live, from a reused block

The declaration is coherent: position float4, diffuse and specular UB_D3D,
one float2 texcoord, interleaved at stride 32. The buffer is a 128-byte
MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx allocation from guest 0x00199789 -- exactly four
vertices of 32 bytes, which is a quad. It is empty.

I suspected my own heap work, twice, and both times the measurement said no:

  - RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=0xAB fills freed blocks. The bytes stayed 00, not AB,
    so the array is not sitting in freed memory.
  - RECOMP_HEAP_NO_FREE=1 restores the pre-repair behaviour exactly, where
    nothing is ever reclaimed. The buffer then lands at 0x01EC1000, a fresh
    block that was never recycled, from the same guest call site -- and is
    STILL all zero.

So the title allocates a vertex buffer, points the arrays at it, issues the
draw, and never fills it. That is the thing to explain.

That reading was right, and a 300-second run (claude-long-21) settled it.

JSRF was on its first-boot cache-building screen. The cache COMPLETES:
Cache00-08.tbl, DmCache00-09.tbl, and nine JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE00..08.CMP
markers written a little after the 60-second mark. No JSRF_FATAL.ERR. The
file set stops at 259 files / 117 MB and stays there, and the run has no
fault, no allocation failure, no stack damage and no stub execution over five
minutes. G4 is answered: the cache is not an endless loop.

After it completes the title starts drawing differently, and the empty array
stops being the story. Sampled at batch 120,000:

  [VSH] late batch attrs: a0(t2 s2 st0 @01BA3000) a9(t2 s2 st0 @01BA3018)
                          reads=1F9B inline=12 idx=0
  [VSH] late batch in0=[-0.53125 -0.53125 0 1] in3=[1 1 1 1] in9=[0 0 0 1]

inline=12: the title has switched to INLINE vertex submission, and the values
are real -- a position and a white diffuse, not zeros. So the empty vertex
array in the sample above belongs to the loading phase, and post-cache draws
carry actual data.

THE SCREEN IS STILL BLACK, AND THE STAGE THAT DROPS THE WORK HAS MOVED:

  [VSH]     executed batches=1370379 rejected=0
  [TEXTURE] prepared=456799 rejected=913580
  [TEXTURE] rejected draw 11: combiner / texture program

Two of every three draws are now refused by the FRAGMENT stage, not the
vertex stage, and every one of them for the same reason: the register
combiner / texture program is not the one configuration nv2a_texture_copy
implements. That module reproduces a single measured RGB565 blit and rejects
anything else by design -- which was correct while it was the only verified
path, and is now the thing in the way. The third that do pass are that blit,
whose source surface is itself all zeros.

So the answer to "why is nothing displayed", as a chain of measurements:
the vertex stage is fixed and accepts everything; the fragment stage
implements exactly one program and drops two thirds of the work; and what
survives is a copy of a black surface. All 93 dumped frames are byte-identical
black, SHA-256 9dc5cdcf...5eed1b3, unchanged.

==========================================================================
2. WHAT WAS RULED OUT, AND HOW
==========================================================================

Each of these was a live hypothesis. Each died to a measurement, which is
cheaper than the code that would have implemented the wrong fix.

The vertex programs are not being missed.
  RECOMP_VSH_TRACE=1 reports uploads by subchannel and every distinct program
  slot the title selects:
    upload words by subchannel: 0=13059744 1..7=0
    changed=1399872 dropped=0 loads=272078 starts=77738 constants=2021100
    constant-dropped=0 decodes=19442 unique-hashes=1 load=12 constant-load=2
    distinct START slots 0x00000001, LOAD slots 0x00000001, LOAD >= 32: 0
  Everything arrives on subchannel 0, nothing is dropped, and the title only
  ever loads at slot 0 and starts at slot 0. There is one program, twelve
  instructions, and 19,442 decodes produced one unique hash. The executor is
  not missing a program switch, because there is no program switch.

The pusher is not swallowing the uploads.
  nv2a_pusher.c dispatch() calls nv2a_pb_exec_method for every method when
  RECOMP_PB_EXEC is set. The "[PUSHER] unhandled 0x0B00-0x0B4C" histogram is
  about pgraph_d3d11_method, a different consumer. The two layers were never
  in disagreement; the previous handover's open question is answered no.

Vertex arrays are not DMA-relative in a way we are getting wrong.
  Resolving SET_CONTEXT_DMA_VERTEX_A/B through the same nv2a_dma_resolve the
  texture-copy path uses:
    vertex DMA A: seen=1 handle=0x00000003 resolved=1 base=0x00000000
                  limit=0x07FFAFFF        (B identical)
  Base is zero, so fetch_attr's raw-offset assumption is correct. This one is
  worth recording because the texture path DOES need the resolve, and it
  would have been reasonable to assume the vertex path does too.

The transform constants are not obviously wrong.
    late batch c0..c7: [1 1 1.67772e+07 1] [0.53125 0.53125 0 0]
                       [0 0 0 0] x6
  c0 and c1 are the screen-space scale/offset pair a 2D program uses -- note
  16777216 is 2^24, the depth-range constant -- and the oPos we get back,
  (0.53125 0.53125 0 inf), is literally c1.xy with an infinite w. That is what
  this program does when handed a zero vertex. The constants are consistent
  with the program; the input is not consistent with anything.

    Stubs xbox_HeapDescribe. That target links xbox_vsh, not xbox_kernel.
```

```txt
1. READ THIS FIRST: THE OLD STARTUP BLOCKER HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AND REPAIRED
==========================================================================

The earlier claim that the game had a healthy main loop but loaded only
jetfont.dat and se_sys.dat was incomplete. The loop continued executing with
a corrupted root-object pointer. It was not evidence that startup awaited
input. We reproduced this corruption with the CPU renderer DISABLED.

The first cause was an untranslated shared epilogue at guest 0x0002C11E.
Function discovery had split a switch into separate C functions. Branches to
the common epilogue called a placeholder which only did g_esp += 4. The real
instructions are:

  0002C11E  5E       pop esi
  0002C11F  33C0     xor eax,eax
  0002C121  5D       pop ebp
  0002C122  C3       ret

Skipping those pops left saved registers on the guest stack and the caller
then restored registers from the wrong slots. The error propagated through
sub_00025310 -> sub_00011070 -> sub_000123E0 -> sub_00013A80. Around tick 7,
the main loop changed its root pointer from 0x01053A70 to 0x00002EBE in the
renderer-disabled baseline (0x00002E9E in an earlier renderer-enabled run).

Fixing that one epilogue reached a second broken shared return in the cache
scheduler, then additional omitted switch entries and an exception epilogue.
These are now handled as described below. No artificial loader success,
forced state transition, fake button press or fault suppression was added.

LATEST RESULT: the game proceeds through logo/title/demo requests, mission,
miscellaneous assets, objects, effects, people and stage data. The latest
20-second fresh-HDD run keeps root 0x01053A70 through the last logged tick
30,000. It has ZERO 'epilogue never ran' ESP reports, ZERO unresolved ICALL
reports and no FIRST GUEST FAULT. It still does NOT display a recognisable
screen and is NOT playable.

  xbox_HeapAlloc: out of memory

The same stage-file request then repeats. 'used' here is the bump high-water

3. CODE CHANGES IN THIS STARTUP SESSION
==========================================================================

tools/recomp/shared_epilogue.py  [NEW]
  recover_shared_epilogue() recognises instruction-aligned return sequences
  inside already detected functions. It is bounded to 16 instructions / 64
  bytes and requires a stack-restoring operation followed by a near return.
  Handles register pops, stack cleanup, simple return values/state stores,
  frame teardown, bounded stack loads and the observed FS:[0] restoration.
  Rejects branches, calls, unsupported operations, missing returns and bad
  instruction boundaries. Uses the normal lifter, with a separate instance,
  and bridges EBP through g_seh_ebp. This is targeted recovery, not a complete
  fix for arbitrary overlapping functions or omitted control-flow blocks.

tools/recomp/translator.py  [MODIFIED]
  Before creating unresolved stubs, attempts that recovery. Recovered bodies
  join normal translations, declarations and the sorted dispatch table.
  Reports recovered_epilogues in the returned statistics.

tools/recomp/test_shared_epilogue.py  [NEW]
  Three unittest tests, including a compiled C execution harness using the
  real runtime header. Checks the actual JSRF loader/cache/SEH byte sequences,
  caller stack balance, saved registers, state store, local cleanup, ret N,
  frame teardown, exception-chain restoration, rejection boundaries and
  generation of body/header/dispatch together.

diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/recover_shared_epilogues.py  [NEW]
  Applies the same recovery to exact placeholder bodies in an EXISTING
  generated checkout, preserving unrelated timing patches and observations.
  Recovered 101 epilogues initially, then 10 more after adding the observed
  SEH form: 111 total. Manifest:
    build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/shared_epilogues.json
  Previous generated files are retained beside the patched file under
  .before-shared-epilogues suffixes. Re-running without new recoverable stubs
  is a no-op. Subsequent recovery passes preserve numbered backups.

diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/startup_entries.json  [NEW]
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/recover_startup_entries.py  [NEW]
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/regenerate.sh  [MODIFIED]
  Once returns worked, sub_000304F0 reached an unresolved indirect switch
  target 0x00030592. The XBE table at 0x00030618 contains exactly:
    0003050F, 00030592, 000305B9, 00030601
  Only the first had a dispatch entry. The incremental script verifies the
  original table slots, owner bounds and instruction boundaries, then lifts
  the missing three entry points through existing end 0x00030618. It appends
  bodies to recomp_stubs_unresolved.c and adds declarations/sorted dispatch
  entries. Existing functions remain unchanged. Backups use
  .before-startup-entries suffixes. The manifest also feeds --seed-functions
  in regenerate.sh, so future discovery knows these entries.
  The incremental script is specific to these verified entries, not an
  unrestricted seed-every-pointer tool. Full regeneration was NOT run here.

Our cached upstream/main was older; the GitHub README web cache also lagged.

Most relevant new upstream commit:
  https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp/commit/0655e8e52bb341bed35ae7290672b69870f9ae97
  Guards CPU framebuffer writes against overwriting the loaded XBE image.
  Root upstream issue: surface colour offsets were treated as guest addresses
  while ignoring DMA bases. A dashboard clear overwrote code/data/globals.

That commit is NOT merged or ported here. Our new texture-copy path already
resolves its observed DMA objects and mapped bounds, but the older flat
triangle/clear paths still use raw offsets and lack this image guard. This
is a useful follow-up before trusting newly reached untextured rendering.
It is not the cause of the initial JSRF root corruption: renderer-OFF repro
and the exact missing epilogue establish a different cause.

Other upstream developments: PR 17 adds D3D8 texture resource translation;
PR 18 corrects ReleaseMutex error handling. Neither was merged, and neither
has been established as the current JSRF blocker. JSRF presently drives its
statically linked graphics code into the NV2A path, rather than calling our
D3D8 host wrappers. Upstream's ABI diagnostic, already present in our base,
was immediately useful and is what exposed the silent register/stack damage.

The inspected upstream input module still has no callers of xbox_InputInit /
xbox_InputGetState outside that module and its documentation. There is no
verified drop-in controller fix from this audit.
```

```txt
CLAUDE HANDOVER
Jet Set Radio Future / upstream_xboxrecomp_clean
4 September 2026

Continues, and corrects, CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-04_USB_GFX.txt and

READ THIS FIRST
===============

This session did not fix the stall. It eliminated most of the places it could
be, fixed two real lifter defects and one real gap in the function database,
built seven instruments, and retired three hypotheses that previous handovers
were organised around -- including the one this session was told to pursue.

It also produced four wrong mechanism claims, three of which reached the user
before I caught them. Two required retraction commits. That failure mode is
documented under WRONG TURNS because it is the most transferable thing here:
every one came from asserting a runtime fact from static reading or from a
trace I had not checked the semantics of.

If you read only two sections, read RULED OUT and WRONG TURNS.


WHAT IS FIXED (COMMITTED)
=========================

87ef36d  Cross-block flag merge for destination-writing setters.

  A jcc reached from several blocks could only be resolved when every edge
  agreed on the flag setter, or when they were all cmp/test snapshots of the
  same width. Anything else fell to the `_flags` local, which is initialised
  to zero and never written, so the branch could go only one way.

  A setter that writes its destination leaves ZF = (dest == 0) and SF =
  sign(dest). When every edge did that to the same destination those two bits
  are known whatever the instructions were. MSVC's signed remainder by a power
  of two is exactly that join -- `and eax, 0x800007FF; jns L; dec eax; or eax,
  0xFFFFF800; inc eax; L: jne` -- an `and` meeting an `inc`.

  Answers ZF and SF only. CF and OF genuinely differ between these setters, so
  a branch needing either still falls back.

  tools/recomp/lifter.py, tools/recomp/translator.py,
  tools/recomp/test_lifter_result_flag_merge.py (7 cases).

  Ten sites in JSRF, nine in the WXCI/XB disc driver. sub_001403B0 is
  wxCiReqRd, the sector-read request; it runs the idiom twice, on the read
  length at 0x001404DB and the seek position at 0x001404F1. With the second
  `je` nailed not-taken every read request fell into "E0109152:illegal seek
  position." and returned zero.

  backport_result_flag_merge.py carries it into the preserved generated tree,
  which regeneration does not reproduce because it holds recovered
  mid-function entries. It runs the fixed translator over each affected
  function and copies the statement across, keyed on guest block label,
  mnemonic and branch target -- no hand-written C. --scope also applies the
  older cmp/test merge's ten sites, which this tree had never received.
  Together 110 dead fallbacks -> 80, and the ctest ratchet with them.

8597a08  Recovered indirect-call target 0x0013D840, plus
f76594b  the correction to its reasoning.

  A function whose address is only taken as a data immediate has no call site
  to be detected by. functions.json held 0x0013D810-0x0013D834 then
  0x0013D860, leaving 0x0013D835-0x0013D85F undetected, and the disassembler
  recorded the reference without promoting it ("XREF: 0x0013E42A (data_imm)").
  RECOMP_ICALL printed "Failed to resolve VA 0x0013D840" three times per run.

  It is the bridge from the WXCI error reporter (installed at 0x002615C4) to
  CRI's cvFs print path. Not behaviourally significant -- the chain ends at
  another uninstalled hook at 0x002616D8 -- but a real hole.

  recover_icall_entries.py is the sibling of recover_startup_entries.py: same
  registration into dispatch/header/bodies, but for an address that is unowned
  rather than inside an existing function. Extent is decoded, not declared,
  and a forward conditional keeps the body open so 0x0013D840's `je` over its
  own tail jump does not truncate it before the `ret`. icall_entries.json also
  feeds a full regeneration through --seed-functions.

Neither fix moves the milestone. Both are correct anyway.


RULED OUT, EACH BY MEASUREMENT
==============================

Every one of these has an artifact under
build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/.

Unresolved flag branches.   Of 110 static sites, exactly five execute during a
  boot: 0x001403B0 twice, 0x001569A0, 0x0015D3F0, 0x0015DC20. All five now
  resolve; a run executes zero. Milestone unchanged.
  (claude-flagmerge-00-baseline vs -04-final)

Heap exhaustion.  The all-sites build exhausts the 61.8 MB arena (226 OOMs,
  deterministic, identical across three runs; zero before). It is not the
  cause: title.adx fails identically with and without it. The heap is
  genuinely tight -- 58.9 MB live even in a clean run, ~95% occupancy -- but
  tight is not the blocker. Worth its own goal.
  (claude-cf-all-01 vs claude-cf-resultmerge-01)

The pushbuffer spin.  Sampling puts 89% of the main thread in one loop,
  loc_001914F0 in sub_00191440, the D3D free-space wait, reached through
  sub_00013A80 -> sub_0014D090 -> sub_00198F10. It is where the time goes and
  not where the block is: it drains at ~4.6 units/s with the CPU rasteriser
  and ~1075/s without -- 233x -- and both produce exactly 1341 file opens.
  (claude-pbwait-01 vs claude-pbwait-noexec-02)

Both WXCI cache misses.  wxCiOpen and wxCiGetFileSize both report
  "is not in cache" on title.adx and both fall through to the identical path
  they use when no cache callback is installed (0x00140A94 and 0x00140907
  respectively). The index at 0x00269D80 is empty and that is normal; the
  lookup runs three times in ninety seconds.

cvFs.  Its whole failure vocabulary is now readable and it emits nothing.

The vblank acknowledge.  loc_00193E40 executes once in ninety seconds. The
  write-1-to-clear path and the PMC summary follow-on are correct.

Thread deadlock.  The only dispatcher object the title uses, the D3D device's
  KEVENT at device+0x2430 (guest 0x0019D630), is waited and signalled 1000+
  times each. Nothing is stuck.

The indirect call at 0x0013D840.  Fixed; 3 failures -> 0; nothing changed.

The read path.  ~285 NtReadFile calls, every one delivering its full length,
  up to 1.9 MB in a single call.

The root object's triggers (8f54dba).  +0x50..+0x6C are a latch bank --
  edge-triggered set/reset PAIRS for four persistent booleans (+0x50/+0x54
  drive +0x40, +0x58/+0x5C drive +0x44, and so on), consumed and cleared every
  tick, with 53/21/8/51 static callers spread across the game. "Nothing sets
  them" means nobody requested a change to four flags already at their
  intended value. Measured: 59108 writes in ninety seconds, all to the root at
  0x005E3A70, all sub_00012750 (+0x70) from sub_0001DAA0. Per-frame service.
  Two handovers were organised around this non-observation. Do not return.


THE MILESTONE, AND HOW TO MEASURE IT
====================================

  RECOMP_PATH_TRACE=1, fresh RECOMP_HDD_ROOT, 75-90 s.
  opens          = lines matching \[FILE\] Nt(Open|Create)File
  distinct files = unique Z:\Media\... paths, dropping ~ and directories

As of this session: 1341 opens, 260 distinct files, identical at 45 s, 75 s,
90 s and 150 s. Identical with the rasteriser on or off, with or without the
OOM, with all flag fixes or none, and with the indirect call fixed or broken.

That number, not wall-clock, is the thing to beat. Each run needs its own HDD
(119 MB); reusing one invalidates the comparison.

Do NOT count reads by grepping "NtReadFile" -- reads are not traced by the
[FILE] logging, and the existing per-read line is labelled "[READ] want=".
Use RECOMP_READ_COUNT=1. That mistake nearly became a fifth wrong conclusion.


INSTRUMENTS BUILT THIS SESSION
==============================

All read-only, all env-gated, all self-limiting.

  RECOMP_WXCI_ERRORS       Every CRI middleware diagnostic. sub_0013C890 is
                           the funnel; it copies each message to 0x0027BC20
                           and forwards to a hook at 0x002616D8 JSRF never
                           installs, so cvFsOpen's six messages, cvFsAddDev's
                           three and the WXCI set were all being discarded.
                           Covers the WXCI reporter too, via 0x0013D840.
  RECOMP_PB_WAIT_TRACE     The D3D pushbuffer free-space spin at 0x001914F0.
  RECOMP_CACHE_TRACE       WXCI index hits/misses plus a dump of the 16 mount
                           slots at 0x00269D80.
  RECOMP_EVENT_TRACE       Both sides of every dispatcher object crossing the
                           thunk boundary. NOTE: reports at counts 1, 10,
                           1000, 100000 -- "count=1" means "at least once".
  RECOMP_VBLANK_ACK_TRACE  The acknowledge spin at loc_00193E40.
  RECOMP_READ_REQUESTS     wxCiReqRd entry (sub_001403B0).
  RECOMP_READ_COUNT        Real NtReadFile calls, bytes asked and delivered.

And the technique that mattered most, which needs no code:

  sample <pid> 20 -f out.txt

Guest functions are real C symbols in a -O0 -g3 -fno-omit-frame-pointer
binary, so macOS `sample` gives true guest stacks with call paths. Generated
functions carry NO per-function hook (only 3 traced functions exist), so a
counter-based profiler is not available -- do not plan one. Launch the run in
the background, wait ~50 s for the steady state, then sample.

RECOMP_PEEK="0x261588,0x2615C4,..." prints guest dwords and is the cheapest
way to settle what a pointer actually holds. Use it before reasoning about
one.


WRONG TURNS, AND WHY
====================

Four claims, same failure mode each time: a runtime fact asserted from static
reading or from a trace whose semantics I had not checked.

1. "The WXCI cache miss destroys the file handle." The `rep stosd` at
   0x00140AB1 is conditional on sub_001406D0's return, not the cache result;
   the miss falls through to the ordinary open path. I read the report site
   and not the fall-through target.

2. "Two threads are deadlocked on an unsignalled event." (commit 1ca03a1,
   retracted by ae21723.) Two errors at once: I read "count=1" as "signalled
   once" when the tracer reports at 1/10/1000/100000, and I treated a thread
   sampled inside bridge_KeWaitForSingleObject as blocked when that function
   waits by polling with Sleep(1) -- a thread doing a thousand short
   successful waits lives there.

3. "The recovered thunk returns immediately because its hook is null."
   (8597a08, corrected by f76594b.) RECOMP_PEEK showed 0x00261588 = 0x0013AF10.
   One run would have told me.

4. "1341 opens and one read, so the title never loads data." Caught before
   reporting. Reads are not logged; I had counted the logging.

The rule that would have prevented all four: before stating what the guest
DID, measure it. RECOMP_PEEK for a dword, sample for where time goes, a probe
for a branch. State a mechanism as a hypothesis until a run confirms it, and
say which it is. Read a counter's reporting thresholds before reading its
value.

A second, structural lesson. Three sessions in a row picked a hypothesis from
a static or structural artifact -- a subsystem that looked incomplete, an
audit count, a field that was always zero -- rather than from the stall
itself. Each cost a session. The first thing this session did that worked was
sampling the running process, and it should have been the first thing done.


WHERE TO GO NEXT
================

The loading phase is healthy end to end: files probed, opened, read and
closed; both middleware layers silent; no thread blocked; no allocation
failing once the arena settles; the renderer drawing correctly (frame dumps
show the anti-graffiti screen rendered properly and "Now Loading" still
animating at 90 s).

The last file activity of every boot is opening D:\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\title.adx,
the title screen's music, which is exactly what you would load last before a
title screen. It opens and sizes successfully.

sub_00013A80 is the root object's per-frame service and the loading state is
not in it. Past the latch bank it clears +0x74, calls sub_000123E0, then
branches on +0x94 (which alternates 0/2 per tick); the ==0 arm packs indexed
bytes from 0x00251F5C into +0x28/+0x2C.

The successor question: the loading screen is a CHILD object with its own
update. Find which child owns it, via sub_000123E0, and read that object's
per-tick state. The backtrace frames from the BGM open give the game-side
callers to start from: 0x0013E270 (cvFsOpen), 0x0013E15C, 0x0013D91A.

Worth its own goal, independently: the CPU rasteriser is 233x slower than the
pushbuffer drain rate without it. That is a measured defect nobody is
tracking, and it is why a 90 s run sees so little.

Do NOT spend the next session on: a Windows/CrossOver control run (the MMIO
trap is macOS/AArch64-only, the Windows path decodes x86-64 in a VEH which is
the worst thing to run under translation, and its APU hook does not even reach
AC97 -- Codex reached the same conclusion and was right); a Metal or GPTK
renderer; the remaining 80 dead flag fallbacks (none execute); further USB
work.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-04_STALL_FOUND.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE HANDOVER
Jet Set Radio Future / upstream_xboxrecomp_clean
4 September 2026

Continues CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-04_STALL_ELIMINATION.txt, and answers its
successor question.

State: main at 2e39891, no new commits. No code was changed this session --
this was measurement only. Working tree is exactly as that handover left it
(the Windows-portability and OHCI work, still uncommitted).


READ THIS FIRST
===============

The stall is found. It is not slowness, not the renderer, not I/O, not a
deadlock. The title screen is waiting for the title BGM to buffer, and the CRI
ADX stream never gets a single byte of title.adx.

Every link below was measured in a running process. Nothing here is inferred
from static reading alone. The previous handover's rule was followed and it
paid: two of my intermediate readings were wrong and measurement caught both
(see WRONG TURNS).


THE HEADLINE: IT IS NOT SLOWNESS
================================

The previous handover left the 233x CPU-rasteriser slowdown as a suspect for
"why a 90 s run sees so little". It is not.

  Root per-frame service (sub_00013A80) tick rate, measured:
    with the rasteriser     25,374 ticks in  66 s   (~620/s)
    without the rasteriser 481,812 ticks in  94 s  (~5,100/s)

Half a million iterations of the game's main loop, and the state machine does
not advance one step. The title is stuck, not starved. The rasteriser is still
a real performance defect, but it is not this.

  (claude-tickrate-exec vs claude-tickrate-noexec)


THE WAIT CHAIN, EACH LINK MEASURED
==================================

1. The title-screen object is global id 8 at 0x00E20870, vtable 0x001CAAF8,
   update sub_0004EF90. That update is a 21-entry jump table at 0x001FA008
   indexed by the object's +0x44.

   Measured: +0x44 = 0x14 for the whole run. State 20, handler sub_0004F970.
   It waits for global object id 2 to be destroyed, then tears down its own
   subtree. The object is never marked dead (flags stay 0x00020000 across all
   47 snapshots), so the wait never ends.

2. Global object id 2 is 0x00E1C170, update sub_0007B8D0.

   Measured: +0x48=0, +0x54=0, +0x58=1, identical in all 47 snapshots. That
   path calls sub_001167F0() and requires it to return 2. It returns global
   object id 5's +0xBC.

3. Global object id 5 is 0x00C35CC0, update sub_00116E30 -- the ADX stream
   manager. Four stream slots at +0x68..+0x74, current index at +0x78.

   Measured: +0xBC went 0 -> 1 early and stuck at 1 for the rest of the run.
   sub_00116C30 advances it to 2 only when sub_0013A9A0(stream, 0) >= 0x2000.

4. sub_0013A9A0 reads stream->[0x18], calls its vtable +0x24 (sub_0013F9A0)
   with 1, and halves the result. That returns the decoder's +0x0C.

   Measured, decoder 0x002771B0:  +0x0C (filled) = 0
                                  +0x10 (free)   = 0x4000
                                  +0x20 (cap)    = 0x4000
   The output ring buffer is completely empty. It needs 0x4000.

5. The producer is alive. The CRI ADX server thread is sub_0013B1C0, created
   at 0x0013B330 via CreateThread, and it loops
   { BlockUntilVerticalBlank (sub_0018CE50); 0x0025EFAC++; call group-2 slot 0 }.

   Measured: 0x0025EFAC ran 332 -> 2354 over the run (~30 Hz). Registration is
   correct too: the ADXT_Init gate 0x0022DB20 == 1, and group-2 slot 0 at
   0x00261638 holds 0x00141F10, the ADX server tick. It is being called ~2350
   times and producing nothing.

6. ADXT handle 0 at 0x0027D120 is stuck in PREP.

   Measured: handle+1 = 1 (PREP). sub_0013D470 dispatches PREP to sub_0013CE30,
   which requires the stream's own state byte to be 2.

   The stream is 0x0027C720. Measured: stream+1 went 0 -> 1 and stopped at 1.
   sub_0013BDF0 (the stream server) calls sub_0013B610 for state 1 every tick;
   sub_0013B610 sets state 2 only after reading >= 0x10 bytes from the reader
   at stream->[8].

7. The reader is 0x00277180 -- the same ring-buffer class as the decoder,
   index 0 of the three built by the constructor sub_0013FD60 at
   0x277180 + n*0x30. Its buffer memory is 0x00C3DF80, capacity 0x000D0000
   (851,968 bytes).

   And here the earlier reading of this handover was WRONG. The bytes ARE
   there. Measured at 0x00C3DF80:

       80 00 00 20   ADX magic (sync 0x8000, copyright offset 0x20)
       03 12 04 02   encoding 3, block size 0x12, 4-bit, 2 channels
       00 00 AC 44   0xAC44 = 44100 Hz

   a valid stereo 44.1 kHz ADX header, and the read log agrees:
   "[READ] want=51200 got=51200 st=0x00000000 80 00 00 20".

   What is broken is the BOOKKEEPING, and it is deterministic. Across three
   independent runs the same thing happens at the same point (sample 5 -> 6 of
   the periodic peek, roughly a third of the way into the boot), never to
   change again:

       +0x10 (bytes the WRITER may still take)   0x000D0000 -> 0
       +0x0C (bytes the READER may take)         0        -> 0   (never moves)
       +0x14, +0x18 (both cursors)               0        -> 0   (never move)
       buffer memory at 0x00C3DF80               zero     -> ADX header

   A full-capacity acquire is exactly what produces that: sub_0013F9E0's
   view-0 path sets +0x14 = (0 + avail) % capacity, which wraps back to 0, and
   +0x10 -= avail, which lands on 0.

   So: the stream acquires the ENTIRE input ring buffer as one write block, the
   file read delivers title.adx into it, and the commit that would publish
   those bytes to the reader never happens. The writer has taken everything,
   the reader can see nothing, and both counts sit at zero forever.

   The commit is vtable slot +0x1C (sub_0013FBC0) called with view 0. It moves
   the count into +0x0C. It is never reached for this buffer.


WHAT THE SAMPLE SHOWS (and what it rules out)
=============================================

`sample <pid> 15` on a steady-state run. Four guest threads:

  Thread A  sub_0013B1C0   the ADX server thread. 10,831 of 10,855 samples are
                           inside sub_0018CE50, D3DDevice_BlockUntilVerticalBlank.
                           22 samples do the actual ADX work. It is alive and
                           vblank-paced -- but at ~30 Hz, not 60.
  Thread B  sub_0013B2A0   the CRI worker. 10,853 of 10,855 samples parked in
                           NtSuspendThread -> SuspendThread -> pthread_cond_wait.
                           It suspends itself each iteration and thread A
                           resumes it every vblank.
  Thread C  sub_0013B180   `while (!exit) counter++`. CRI's idle/CPU-load
                           measurement thread. By design -- but it burns a full
                           core here, because guest thread priorities are not
                           honoured. Worth its own goal; not the stall.
  Thread D  sub_0013B230   the second vblank thread (group-2 slot 1, empty).

The sample proves the entire pipeline executes every tick:
  sub_0013B1C0 -> sub_00141E50 -> sub_00141F10 -> sub_0013A9E0
     -> sub_0013DE40 (14/22 samples, the read pump; reaches sub_00140C30 ->
        sub_00140BA0 -> the thread-sync primitives)
     -> sub_0013BDF0 -> sub_0013B610 -> sub_0013F9E0   (the failing acquire)
     -> sub_0013D690, sub_0013D470 -> sub_0013CE30     (the PREP handler)

Ruled out by measurement this session, so do not spend time on them:

  Suspend/Resume is NOT losing wakeups. The worker's own tick counter
  0x0025EFB0 ran 321 -> 1588 in 70 s, in lockstep with thread A's 0x0025EFAC
  (337 -> 1667). The handshake works. (claude-group5-01)

  The ADX server registration is correct. Gate 0x0022DB20 == 1, and group-2
  slot 0 at 0x00261638 holds 0x00141F10. sub_00141E50 is its caller and runs.

  No unresolved indirect calls. Zero "[ICALL] Failed to resolve VA" lines in a
  94 s run.

  0x0013F900, the ring buffer's +0x28 "callback", is `eb fe` -- jmp to itself,
  CRI's fatal-halt stub. It is correctly never called. (It IS an undetected
  entry point -- the dispatch table skips 0x0013F8F0 -> 0x0013F910, and the
  disassembler recorded "XREF: 0x0013F900 (jump), 0x0013FE1B (data_imm)", the
  same shape as the 0x0013D840 hole recovered last session. Harmless, but real,
  and recover_icall_entries.py would close it.)

  The ADXF table at 0x27BD20 (40 entries of 0x40) is entirely zero, so
  sub_0013C070 -- which holds both an acquire and the commits -- never runs for
  this file. Whatever performed the acquire was something else.

  Group 5 (0x00261698..) is empty, so thread B wakes 30 times a second,
  dispatches nothing, and parks again.


THE INSTRUMENT CLOSED IT: LINKS 8-11
====================================

G14's instrument was built and run (RECOMP_RINGBUF_TRACE, RECOMP_ADXF_TRACE,
both in startup_probe.c via instrument_startup.py, both read-only and
env-gated). It named the acquirer in three lines.

8. The acquirer is sub_0013C070, the ADXF read server, at site 0x0013C1C3.

     [RINGBUF] call=3 pc=0013F9E0 ret=0013C1C3 obj=00277180 view=0
               arg=000D0000 filled=00000000 free=000D0000

   It asks for 0x000D0000 -- the whole buffer -- ONCE, and there is never a
   matching commit. Over a whole run the only ring-buffer traffic is:

       34x  acquire view 1  from 0x0013B636   (sub_0013B610, header read)
        1x  acquire view 0  from 0x0013C1C3   (sub_0013C070)   <-- the leak
       31x  release view 1  from 0x0013B64F
        0x  ANY view 0 commit

   This corrects an earlier reading in this handover: sub_0013C070 does run.
   The peek that said its table was empty was wrong (see WRONG TURNS).

9. The ADXF entry is 0x0027BD20, and it is serviced every tick, forever:

     [ADXF] entry=0027BD20 state=01/02/01 buf=00277180 handle=00261118
            vt=0022DB98 done_fn=001405B0 want=000D0000

   state bytes are (+0, +1, +2) = (1, 2, 1). Its caller sub_0013C290 services
   an entry while +0 == 1 and +1 == 2, so the filter matches and the server is
   called tens of thousands of times. +2 == 1 sends it down the completion-poll
   path at loc_0013C088, not the issue-a-read path. It is not stuck because
   nobody calls it; it is stuck because the poll never succeeds.

10. The poll is sub_0013DE70(handle 0x00261118), which returns
    handle->vtable[0x2C](handle->[4]). Measured: vtable 0x0022DB98, slot 0x2C =
    **0x001405B0**. sub_0013C070 requires that to return 1.

11. sub_001405B0 is three instructions of substance:

        wxCiGetStat(req):
            if (req == 0) { report via the 0x2615C4 hook; return 0; }
            return (int8_t)req->[1];

    So the whole title screen hangs on one byte: **the WXCI request status at
    req+1 never becomes 1**, where req = MEM32(0x00261118 + 4).

That is the end of the chain. Everything above it is healthy and provably
running; everything below it is the WXCI/XB disc driver.


WHERE TO GO NEXT
================

One byte: the WXCI request status at req+1 (req = MEM32(0x00261118 + 4)).
sub_0013C070 polls it through sub_001405B0 and needs 1.

The writers of that byte in the WXCI module are sub_001402F0, sub_00140380,
sub_001403B0 (wxCiReqRd) and the four command variants sub_00140E60 /
sub_00140F00 / sub_00140F90 / sub_00140FC0. Each writes the same 1 / 1 / 2
pattern, so the question is which value the request is parked on and which
transition is missing.

Note the neighbourhood. sub_001403B0 is the function the 3 September session
fixed the cross-block flag merge in -- "with the second je nailed not-taken
every read request fell into E0109152:illegal seek position and returned zero".
That fix is in and is why the read now delivers bytes at all. This is the next
defect along the same path, and the WXCI error reporter (sub_00140190, already
covered by RECOMP_WXCI_ERRORS) has twelve diagnostics about exactly this area.

Do first, in this order, because each is cheap:

  1. Run with RECOMP_WXCI_ERRORS=1 and RECOMP_ADXF_TRACE=1 together. The
     driver has been describing its own failures all along; read them at the
     moment the poll fails rather than guessing.
  2. Extend jsrf_adxf_probe to print req = MEM32(handle + 4) and req->[1]
     directly. One line then says which status the request is parked on.
  3. Read the writer that owns that value and find what advances it. If it is
     an interrupt- or DPC-driven completion, the missing piece is in our
     kernel, not the guest.

Do NOT re-open: the renderer, the heap, thread deadlock, the vblank
acknowledge, the flag fallbacks, the root object's latch bank, the pushbuffer
spin, tick rate, Suspend/Resume, or ADX server registration. All measured, all
clear, all consistent with this chain.

Two separate goals this session uncovered, neither of them the stall:
  - sub_0013B180, CRI's idle counter thread, burns a full core because guest
    thread priorities are not honoured.
  - The ADX server thread is vblank-paced at ~30 Hz where hardware gives 60.


WRONG TURNS, AND WHY
====================

Two, both caught by measurement before they reached a conclusion.

1. "A[2] is already zero, so state 20 is not blocked." The peek that said zero
   was sampled early in a run, before global object id 2 was registered. In the
   steady state A[2] = 0x00E1C170. Fixed by measuring the disputed value and
   the object's state in the SAME process rather than across two runs.

2. "The jump-table targets have no labels, so the indirect tail jump fails."
   They are not labels; each of the 21 targets is its own generated function,
   all present in recomp_dispatch.c. Confirmed by measuring: zero
   "[ICALL] Failed to resolve VA" lines in a full run.

A fourth, and it cost two wrong statements in this document before the
instrument caught it. I peeked the ADXF table at 0x0027BD20 and the file table
at 0x00273780, saw zeros, and concluded that sub_0013C070 never runs. The probe
then showed entry 0x0027BD20 live, at that exact address, tens of thousands of
times. RECOMP_PEEK and the in-probe read_word DISAGREE about that region:
peek_addresses uses xbox_GetMemoryOffset() + va, the probe uses
xbox_GpuMemoryRange(va, 4). Nearby addresses (0x0027C720, 0x0027D120) peek
correctly, so this is not a whole-region mapping failure and it is not
explained yet.

  Rule: a probe that reads at the moment the guest itself uses the value beats
  a sampled peek. Where they disagree, believe the probe, and do not conclude
  "this code never runs" from a peek alone -- prove it with a probe at its
  entry, which costs one rebuild.

A third near-miss worth recording: root+0x87E8 also holds 0x14, and it is
tempting to read that as the same state index. It is not -- it is the count of
live registered objects (sub_00012100 increments it per construction). It
reaching 20 and stopping just means 20 objects are alive.


STRUCTURE WORTH KEEPING
=======================

MEM32(0x0022FCE0) IS the root object at 0x005E3A70. They are the same object,
and it is the global manager:

  +0x98    7668 object pointers indexed by GLOBAL OBJECT ID.
           sub_000128C0(i) reads (2802 call sites), sub_00012870 writes
           (one caller: the base constructor sub_00012100), sub_00012890
           reads-and-clears.
  +0x7868  a second array, read by sub_000127E0(i).
  +0x40/44/48/4C  four booleans selecting one of five game modes. All zero for
           the whole boot, so mode 0 runs.
  +0x87DC  scene-graph root (0x0060FF40).
  +0x87E8  live registered-object count. NOT a state index.

Every scene-graph node: +0x00 vtable, +0x04 flags (bit31 = dead, walker skips),
+0x08 ITS OWN GLOBAL ID, +0x28 first child, +0x30 next sibling.

sub_000123E0 broadcasts one virtual method over the whole tree per mode, via
five identical walkers (sub_00011070/112A0/114D0/11700/11930 -> vtable slots
0x04/0x10/0x1C/0x28/0x34) and a second bank for the draw pass (slots
0x08/0x14/0x20/0x2C/0x38). The vtable is five mode-groups of three slots,
spaced 0x0C.

The +8 field is what makes the whole registry legible: the existing
RECOMP_STARTUP_TRACE [STARTUP-OBJECT] line already dumps 32 words per object, so
word[2] names every live object's global id with no new instrument. The full map
for a steady-state boot is in claude-tickrate-noexec/stderr.log.


HOW TO MEASURE THIS CHEAPLY
===========================

Almost everything above came from instruments that already existed.

  RECOMP_STARTUP_TRACE=1 RECOMP_STARTUP_STATE=1
      [STARTUP] prints the root's fields every tick it changes, and a tick
      counter every 2 s -- that is where the tick-rate numbers came from.
      [STARTUP-STATE] object=... dumps ~32 fields of every live scene-graph
      node every 2 s. Nodes 0x00E20870, 0x00E1C170 and 0x00C35CC0 were all
      read straight out of it; no new code.

  RECOMP_PEEK="0xA,0xB,..."       guest dwords, sampled by the pushbuffer
                                  reporter. Budget ~22 addresses (256-char buf).
  RECOMP_PEEK_CHAIN="0xA,0x18"    deref-and-offset, then prints the value at the
                                  end. One run per chain instead of one per level.

Reading the XBE directly is free and avoids a run entirely -- section table at
0x11C/0x120, base 0x10000. That is how the 21-entry jump table at 0x001FA008
and the decoder vtable at 0x0022DB38 were resolved.

A run:
  RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_PEEK="..." \
  RECOMP_HDD_ROOT="$PWD/build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/NAME-hdd" \
  python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_bounded.py NAME --seconds 75

Each run needs its own HDD (119 MB). Delete the -hdd afterwards; the stderr.log
is the evidence and it is small.

===========================

Under build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/ (HDDs already deleted):

  claude-mode-01           the four mode booleans, all zero
  claude-tickrate-exec     620 ticks/s with the rasteriser
  claude-tickrate-noexec   5,100 ticks/s without it; the full object/id map
  claude-conflict-01       A[2] and the object state in one process
  claude-svrthread-01      the ADX server thread tick counter, 332 -> 2354
  claude-adxstm-01         the ADXT handle and stream state bytes
  claude-reader-01         the empty 832 KB input ring buffer

  (claude-loadslot-01, claude-obj5-01, claude-decoder-01, claude-svrtable-01
   were intermediate and their logs are kept too.)

==========

No code changed, so nothing to revalidate. The build was current at session
start and ctest was left untouched at 14/14 by 2e39891.
```
