`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-04_USB.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE HANDOVER -- USB ENUMERATION COMPLETE
Jet Set Radio Future / xboxrecomp
Date: 2026-09-04 (Europe/London)
Continues: CODEX_TO_CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-04.txt


BOTTOM LINE
===========

The controller enumerates. JSRF's XPP driver now completes the whole USB
conversation against an emulated Xbox gamepad -- device descriptor, address
assignment, configuration descriptor, SET_CONFIGURATION, XID descriptor,
capabilities -- and then settles into steadily polling the pad, both by
GET_REPORT on the control pipe and on the interrupt-IN endpoint.

Measured over 40 s (claude-usb-transfer-service-14 and -15, identical):

  one port reset, no re-enumeration
  zero unhandled control requests
  zero guest faults
  ~5000 schedule services, ~125/s, steady to the end of the run
  the title renders throughout (47400 frames presented)

The previous handover's minimum success criterion is met and its stronger one
is met: enumeration reaches a configured controller and the game is reading
reports from the host input backend.

The input chain is verified end to end with real hardware. A DualShock 4 on
USB, run claude-usb-realpad-01: SDL2 opens it, and real presses arrive at the
emulated device correctly decoded --

  buttons=10                 Options -> START
  buttons=04 / 02 / 06       D-pad Left / Down / Down+Left
  A=FF B=FF X=FF Y=FF        Cross / Circle / Square / Triangle

so host backend -> USB device -> OHCI -> XPP -> title all works. The
[USB-PAD] trace in xbox_UsbInterruptIn, gated on RECOMP_OHCI_TRANSFER_TRACE,
is what shows this; it prints when the pressed set changes.

The user-visible milestone -- a button advancing the Stage 12 / Press Start
wait -- is still NOT confirmed, but no longer for want of input. The title
receives the presses and shows no observable reaction: identical stage
sequence, identical pushbuffer profile, with and without a pad. Whether that
is the wrong button, an attract loop that ignores input, or game code above
XPP not consuming it cannot be told apart while draws=0 and there is no
picture to read. That question now belongs to the renderer, not to USB.

Two hosts notes, both macOS rather than code. open_controllers() runs once in
xbox_InputInit and there is no hotplug, so a pad attached after launch is
never seen -- attach first. And on macOS 26 the Games app claims the
controller Home button system-wide; irrelevant here, since the Xbox 20-byte
report has no Guide button at all, but it steals focus.


WHAT WAS BUILT
==============

  src/kernel/xbox_usb_ohci.{c,h}   (new)

An OHCI transfer service and the one USB device behind it. Two halves:

  xbox_OhciServiceList()   walks an ED list, retires the TDs between HeadP and
                           TailP, builds the done queue, publishes it into the
                           HCCA and raises WritebackDoneHead.
  xbox_UsbControlRequest() answers as an Xbox controller (0x045E:0x0289).
  xbox_UsbInterruptIn()    fills the 20-byte pad report.

Both are pure functions over a caller-supplied RAM window and caller-supplied
register values. That is not decoration: the live caller is the MCPX SIGSEGV
handler, so the service must not allocate or lock, and the test drives the
identical code over a plain buffer with no guest at all.

Wiring in src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c:

  - ControlListFilled / BulkListFilled (HcCommandStatus bits 1-2) run the
    service synchronously, then the doorbell bits are cleared as hardware
    clears them when it finds the list empty.
  - A port reset returns the device to the default address.
  - ohci_periodic_tick() runs one HCCA interrupt-table entry per frame off the
    NV2A ack thread, and raises StartOfFrame.

Host input, in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/main.c: usb_pad_state_shim() packs
xbox_InputGetState into the Xbox report layout, installed through
xbox_SetUsbPadStateHook. A hook, so xbox_kernel keeps no link dependency on
xbox_input -- the same arrangement the APU MMIO hook uses.


FIVE BUGS FOUND BY RUNNING IT
=============================

Each was found by a measured run, and each run name below is a real log under
build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/.

1. HcInterruptStatus was not write-1-to-clear.

   As plain memory the driver's acknowledge STORED the bit it meant to retire.
   XPP's ISR ran mask/handle/acknowledge/unmask about eighty times against a
   RootHubStatusChange it could not put down. It also made every later fix
   impossible: a WritebackDoneHead that can never be acknowledged is one
   transfer, then silence. (claude-usb-transfer-service-01)

2. Nothing ever advanced a frame.

   After SET_ADDRESS, XPP enables the StartOfFrame interrupt and counts frames
   to time the 2 ms a device may take before answering at its new address. It
   waited for ever. (claude-usb-transfer-service-02/03)

3. An unacknowledged done queue was being overwritten.

   XPP submits the next transfer from its completion DPC, BEFORE it
   acknowledges the interrupt for the transfer before it. Publishing over that
   loses the first queue outright; the driver then freed descriptors it was
   never told about and faulted dereferencing 0xFFFFFFF0. Hardware keeps
   retiring into HcDoneHead and publishes the lot at the next writeback, which
   is what the service does now. (claude-usb-transfer-service-04)

4. HeadP was left pointing at a failed TD.

   A retired TD is retired whether or not it succeeded: it is unlinked and put
   on the done queue, so HeadP advances past it and only gains the Halted bit.
   Leaving HeadP on it handed the driver the same descriptor from two places.
   (claude-usb-transfer-service-08)

5. One guard window per register, instead of one per event.

   Every mcpx_hw_store drops the mprotect guard, and a guest write landing in
   that window is stored as plain memory with none of the register semantics
   the trap exists to supply. The attach probe used two windows; XPP's ISR
   acknowledged ConnectStatusChange in the gap and its 0x00010000 stored whole,
   wiping CurrentConnectStatus -- the exact failure the port model exists to
   prevent -- and the driver spent the run resetting an empty port. There is
   now mcpx_hw_store_n() for a set of registers belonging to one event.
   (claude-usb-transfer-service-05)

   This one is worth remembering beyond USB. Windows cannot be eliminated while
   the mechanism is mprotect; the rule is to open as few as possible. Any
   future runtime-side register write on a guarded page should batch.


THE ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM OHCI
======================================

A short read does not raise DataUnderrun and does not halt the endpoint.

XPP asks for 0x50 bytes of configuration set and builds exactly ten eight-byte
IN transfer descriptors for it, with bufferRounding set on the last one only.
The modelled device has 32 bytes, so it underruns in the middle of that chain.
Per OHCI that halts the endpoint -- and XPP treats a mid-chain halt as a failed
enumeration, tears the control list down and resets the port, for ever
(claude-usb-transfer-service-10 and -11). Completing the short read cleanly
carries it straight through to SET_CONFIGURATION (claude-usb-exp-a2 and -a3).

Read this as a symptom, not a fix. That XPP asks for exactly 80 bytes and sizes
its TD chain to match is evidence the REAL controller's configuration set is 80
bytes and the 32-byte one in xbox_usb_ohci.c is missing something -- plausibly
the expansion-slot interfaces an Xbox pad carries for memory units. Nothing was
invented to fill the gap: 32 bytes that are right beat 80 that are half
guessed. If a real descriptor dump turns up, replace USB_CONFIG_DESC and this
deviation should go with it. Both places carry a comment saying so.


THE CONVERSATION, AS CAPTURED
=============================

In order, each request issued once the one before it completed:

  80 06 00 01 00 00 08 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(DEVICE), 8 -- the address-0 probe
  00 05 01 00 00 00 00 00   SET_ADDRESS(1)
  80 06 00 02 00 00 50 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(CONFIGURATION), 80
  00 09 01 00 00 00 00 00   SET_CONFIGURATION(1)
  C1 06 00 42 00 00 10 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(XID), 16   -- VENDOR, not class
  C1 01 00 02 00 00 06 00   GET_CAPABILITIES(output), 6
  C1 01 00 01 00 00 14 00   GET_CAPABILITIES(input), 20
  A1 01 00 01 00 00 14 00   GET_REPORT(input), 20     -- CLASS, and repeating

Two of those are worth knowing. The XID descriptor is a VENDOR request
(bmRequestType 0xC1, bits 6:5 = 2), not a class one -- routing it as class
stalls it. And GET_REPORT on the control pipe, not the interrupt endpoint, is
where a button press actually reaches this title; the interrupt endpoint runs
too, but XID polls.

EXACT NEXT STEP
===============

Geometry. Nothing else can be judged until something draws.

The title clears and flips ~45000 times in 40 s and issues ZERO draws. The
pushbuffer sink implements about fifteen methods, written for Burnout 3's 2D
menus (INLINE_ARRAY, five-dword X/Y/U/V/Color vertices). JSRF drives a fully
programmable pipeline, and the top unhandled methods say so exactly:

  0x1800       4.6M    NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT16          indexed vertices
  0x1EA4       1.4M    NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT_LOAD
  0x0B00-0x0B3C 495k each  NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM  vertex shaders

In dependency order, each with an observable stop condition:

  a. Shader upload and constants. nv2a_vsh.c already emits GLSL, which is what
     this host needs. Stop condition: a translated shader compiles.
  b. Vertex array state -- offsets and formats, so the sink knows where the
     vertices are and how they are laid out.
  c. ARRAY_ELEMENT16/32 as an indexed draw. Stop condition: draws > 0.
  d. Textures (nv2a_texture_copy.c exists), then render state.

Aim at one recognisable frame -- the SEGA logo, or the loading screen -- rather
than at "the game renders". Same discipline that worked for USB: one
observable contract at a time, learned from the title rather than the spec.

Extend the NV2A sink rather than routing through the d3d8_gl HLE layer: JSRF
writes pushbuffers directly, 23.9M methods a run, so the HLE path is not where
its geometry goes.

After that, in rough order of likely need: the EP2 OUT rumble endpoint is
accepted and discarded rather than driven; the configuration descriptor
question above; and multiple controller ports, which today is one device on
root-hub port 1.

CORRECTION AND UPDATE -- GRAPHICS. The renderer was never the blocker.

The "EXACT NEXT STEP" above is WRONG and is superseded by this section. It
read draws=0 as "nothing renders" and set out to build a geometry path. That
counter belongs to the D3D11 pushbuffer sink; the CPU executor in
src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c is counted separately, and it draws. None of my runs
had set RECOMP_PB_EXEC, so none of them drew anything. Setting it renders the
title correctly.

  env RECOMP_HDD_ROOT=... RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 \
      RECOMP_FB_DUMP=<dir>/f \
      python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_bounded.py <name> --seconds 45

Run claude-gfx-pbexec-01 produces the CRI/ADX logo and the animated JSRF
"Now Loading" screen, both correct, as <dir>/fNNN.bmp. Over 150 s
(claude-gfx-pbexec-02) the rasteriser reports:

  [VSH] executed batches=... rejected=0        the title's own vertex programs
  [TEXTURE] prepared=... rejected=0
  [GPU] draws 267400 (267400 with coordinates), 3596979 indices
  [GPU] rasterised 3052519 triangles; 0 batches skipped as not screen-space,
        0 triangles fully off-surface

Zero rejected, zero skipped, zero off-surface. Geometry, the vertex-shader
interpreter and texturing all work on the paths this title uses. There is a
window too -- d3d8_gl.c creates one -- so this can be watched live rather than
through BMP dumps.


THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: THE LOAD NEVER COMPLETES
============================================

The title reaches "Now Loading" and stays there. Not slowly -- it stops.

  45 s run:  242 distinct files, 284 reads
  150 s run: 242 distinct files, 284 reads

Identical. File I/O finishes and never resumes, while the game loop keeps
running hard and the loading animation keeps ticking. So this is a stall in
whatever ends the loading state, not a performance problem and not rendering.

What has been ruled out:

  - Not a fatal error. No JSRF_FATAL.ERR on the emulated HDD.
  - Not a missing file. All 253 failures are STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND on
    Z:\ paths, which is the HDD-cache-miss-then-read-from-D:\ pattern; the
    D:\ read succeeds immediately after each one.
  - Not a blocked thread. Two NtWaitForSingleObjectEx INFINITE calls in the
    whole run, both early, neither at the stall.
  - Not audio. The ADX manager/server handshake is healthy: tick advancing,
    flag clear, no adxm_goto_mwidle_border timeout.
  - Not input. Same behaviour with a real pad, with RECOMP_FAKE_PAD and with
    no pad at all.
  - Not rendering. Same 242/284 with and without RECOMP_PB_EXEC.

The guest is busy, not idle: 5.9M kernel calls, dominated by
RtlEnterCriticalSection and RtlLeaveCriticalSection at ~2.4M each. It is
spinning on something it expects to change.

The last file read is an ADX stream header (want=51200 got=51200,
80 00 00 20), so the last thing loaded is music.


NEXT STEP
=========

Find the loading screen's exit condition, with the probe machinery that is
already here -- diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_startup.py adds
read-only observation sites at guest addresses, and that is how the USB device
path was pinned down.

Start from the loading state itself rather than from the file system: the
title decides to leave "Now Loading" somewhere, and the question is which
predicate it is re-testing 2.4M times without ever seeing true. The critical
section traffic gives a thread to follow, and the four stage files it loaded
(Stg10, Stg00, Stg08, Stg12, in that order, every run) give a load-completion
counter to look for.

Do not start building renderer features. Nothing in the pushbuffer sink's
unhandled list is on the critical path -- the CPU executor already handles
what this title draws.
```

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER, 5 SEPTEMBER 2026
The title renders its own screens. The frontier is presentation, not drawing.
================================================================================

Active goals:  JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-05_GAMEPLAY.md
Superseded:    JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-05_PUSHBUFFER_RATE.md,
               JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-04_AUDIO_STALL.md
Commits:       5103862..f37d451 (22 commits), all pushed to origin/main
Tests:         ctest 18/18 in build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/build


WHERE THE PORT IS
=================

It boots, loads its assets, streams its title BGM through the CRI stack, runs
the title screen's state machine to completion, tears it down, builds a
successor scene of ~128 objects, consumes ~260 million dwords of push buffer
continuously with zero bad headers and zero faults over a 110-second run, and
DRAWS ITS OWN SCREENS CORRECTLY.

Two pictures prove that, both captured from the CPU rasteriser's surface:

  - the SEGA anti-graffiti screen, pixel-correct: red spray-can logo, four
    paragraphs of legible text, right scale and colours (132 distinct colours);
  - the JSRF title screen: logo, character graphic, "JSRF" and "JET SET RADIO
    FUTURE(TM)" beneath it, correctly scaled, centred, legible.

It is NOT playable. Nothing has been done on controls (goal 4). Presentation is
partly working: of 46 frames captured at the flip, 19 carry a picture and 27 do
not, and the 27 are not frames the title intended to leave blank.


WHAT WAS FIXED, AND THE EVIDENCE FOR EACH
=========================================

Six fixes landed, each measured before and after. They compound; several were
prerequisites for the next.

1. The empty-list guard (59bf975).
   sub_00014870's `jbe` at 0x00014885 is an empty-list guard whose `cmp` sits
   four instructions earlier. The recompiler split those ten instructions into
   three generated functions chained by fallthrough calls; guest registers
   survive that (they are globals) but the lifter's _fa/_fb flag snapshot does
   not (it is a local). So the guard took the constant-zero `_flags` fallback
   and never fired. The array-remove loop behind it ran with `count - 1`
   underflowed to 0xFFFFFFFF and copied every dword down one slot across guest
   memory -- including the kernel import thunk table at 0x001C3F60, which sent
   every kernel call to the next export along. That is how a call to
   ObReferenceObjectByHandle arrived at ExQueryNonVolatileSetting.
   Fix: backport_empty_list_guard.py, with a --check ctest.

2. The shared-ZF branch (914c76c).
   0x000A13A1's `je` is reached from two different comparisons, so it has no
   condition of its own and the lifter emitted the fallback. Fixed at each
   predecessor. This was the only remaining dead `_flags` fallback that
   executes; RECOMP_UNRESOLVED_FLAGS=1 now reports none at all. 78 latent sites
   remain in the ratchet and none of them run.

3. DMA_GET published from the consumed cursor, not from PUT (e4f9e99).
   nv2a_ack_thread copied PUT into GET every tick. For a title whose push
   buffer nothing executes that is honest; for one whose buffer IS executed it
   tells the producer the ring is free the instant it submits, so it laps the
   parser and overwrites commands mid-read. g_nv2a_pusher_owns_dma_get lets an
   executor take the register over.

4. The ring executed in place, not from a copy (f72ab68).
   The reserve notification is a PATCH. loc_001914A9 writes [esi+0x10] =
   0x00040100 and [esi+0x14] = 5 into a segment already published, and
   loc_001914CD overwrites both words again if the GPU caught up. jsrf_pb_feed
   memcpy'd up to 1 MB and executed the copy, so patches landing afterwards
   were never seen. Measured: [PB-PATCH-LOST] address=005DF9A4 snapshot!=5
   live=5.

5. Consumption in bounded steps with GET republished after each (a2c32a2).
   THE BIG ONE. GET was published once per poll; a poll could cover most of the
   ring, and for all that time the producer saw a GET that had not moved. The
   replay experiment proved it: re-walking the failing window from a copy taken
   at its start parses cleanly to the end, while the live parse died 1,893
   dwords in -- so the ring changed underneath it. Steps are 0x8000 bytes,
   which must exceed the 8 KB largest legal packet.
     bad headers 1 -> 0, invalid 1 -> 0, rejected control flow 2 -> 0
     draws 9,819 (frozen) -> 638,538 and climbing
     triangles 32,535 (frozen) -> 3,266,664 and climbing

6. The framebuffer probe pointed at the surface being drawn (f0dc0dd).
   [FB] summed PCRTC_START. JSRF never programs a scanout, so that register
   pointed at a heap block for this port's whole life -- RECOMP_GUARD_PAGE
   named xbox_HeapAlloc zeroing the very page being summed. Every
   "nonzero=0/153600" line in the history was reading an allocation.

7. Consumption stops at FLIP_STALL (b1dceba).
   Presentation ran after the poll, so the parser walked into the next frame's
   clear before presenting. Blank presents 43/46 -> 27/46.

Codex's parallel work (f79cfa4) was a prerequisite for 4 and 5: the contiguous
allocator returning high CPU addresses so the guest's reconstructed DMA_GET
compares against the right range, and the PGRAPH software-method interrupt
path. Its own caveats are in CODEX_PROGRESS_2026-09-05_PUSHBUFFER.md.


WRONG TURNS, AND WHY -- READ THIS ONE
=====================================

Four claims of mine were withdrawn during the session. Every one came from
inferring off a fragment instead of measuring, and they cost real time.

1. "The draws arrive in world coordinates, so the transform is broken."
   The `[GPU] draws ... input x -4636..4636` range is the PRE-SHADER range by
   construction; draw_primitive says so in its own comment. It describes object
   space and carries no information about the transform.

2. "oPos = (0,0), (2560,0), (0,1920) is a 4x scale defect."
   That is the startup blit's oversized covering triangle, a standard
   technique, and it appears in frames that come out pixel-correct.

3. "The title screen is drawn 4x too large."
   Those captures were taken mid-composition, showing individual UI elements
   before the rest of the frame was drawn. The finished frame is correct.
   Sampling a drawing batch is not sampling a frame.

4. "The framebuffer is black, so the renderer produces nothing."
   The probe was summing a heap allocation. See fix 6.

There was also a heuristic I added and had to back out: a resync that skipped
to PUT on a parse failure, and a "backwards PUT with no jump means a restart"
branch. Both hid the defect instead of explaining it, and the second may have
been producing desyncs of its own (f03d3a1). Do not add heuristic
resynchronisation, forward scanning for a plausible header, or clearing of
stream_fault. The permanence of stream_fault is deliberate: it keeps the one
event per run visible.

  Rule that would have prevented all five: before stating what the guest did,
  name the instrument that showed it. If the answer is "I read the range/the
  sample/the probe line", check what that number actually measures first.


THE OPEN FRONTIER (goal 3c)
===========================

27 of 46 presented frames carry a blank surface, and they are NOT frames the
title meant to leave blank. The discriminator is the triangle count between one
flip capture and the next:

    blank, and >50 triangles drawn since the previous capture : 11
    blank, and <=50 triangles                                 :  0
    with content                                              : 15

Every blank present follows a frame that drew -- about 750 triangles per
capture interval, consistently, with no empty frames anywhere. So work is being
composed, cleared, and then presented.

What has NOT been measured, and is the next thing to do: what the guest emits
between its last draw and its flip. If the clear for frame N+1 precedes the
FLIP_STALL for frame N in this title's command order, the flip is the WRONG
boundary rather than a misapplied one, and the fix is different in kind.
nv2a_pusher_dump_recent(48) already prints the last methods dispatched; call it
at the flip and read the sequence.


INSTRUMENTS ADDED THIS SESSION
==============================

All are env-gated or self-limiting and silent in a healthy run.

  RECOMP_GUARD_PAGE=<guest VA>
      mprotect that page read-only before the guest starts, so the first write
      faults and the report names the writer. This is what identified both
      sub_000147A0 (the runaway array-remove) and xbox_HeapAlloc (the
      framebuffer probe's page). The single most useful thing added.

  RECOMP_PB_REPLAY=1
      Keep a copy of every push-buffer window as it is taken; on a parse
      failure re-walk it with nv2a_pusher_scan_segment (dispatches nothing,
      moves no counters) and report whether the second walk stops at the same
      offset. Same offset = a decoding defect; different = the ring changed.

  RECOMP_FB_DUMP=<prefix> with RECOMP_FB_DUMP_DRAW=<stride>
      Capture the executor's surface after every stride-th drawing batch,
      capped at 24 files. Composed frames rather than report-time snapshots.

  RECOMP_FB_DUMP=<prefix> with RECOMP_FB_DUMP_FLIP=<stride>
      Capture at the flip -- the only moment a frame is finished. Also logs
      [FLIP] capture N at frame M: X triangles since the previous capture,
      which is what separates "intended blank" from "presented after a clear".

  jsrf_title_state_probe   the 21-entry title state machine at 0x001FA008,
                           printing every change plus a heartbeat every 20000
                           unchanged visits. Sampling says where it is; only a
                           trace says whether it is moving.
  jsrf_list_remove_probe   sub_000147A0's arguments, reporting only calls that
                           cannot be right. A regression detector for fix 1.
  jsrf_notify_probe        sub_00193F70's notification index, tallied.
  jsrf_cri_handler_probe   CRI's installed-handler dispatcher.
  [PB-NOPSCAN]             one-shot ring scan for software-method packets.
  [EVENT-SET] caller=      the guest caller on the kernel bridge's event trace.
                           This is what identified the reserve event's
                           signaller: the literal 0x0019D640 appears nowhere,
                           because it is only ever computed as device+0x2440.


STRUCTURE WORTH KEEPING
=======================

The reserve/notification chain, measured end to end and working:

    NO_OPERATION parameter 5
      -> PGRAPH software-method trap (0xFD400704 method, 0xFD400708 data)
      -> guest ISR at 0x0019428C, which reads the index from 0xFD400708
      -> sub_00193F70(device, index): nine-entry switch on index-1,
         table at 0x001941B4
      -> index 5 is the only entry reaching 0x00194144
      -> KeSetEvent(device+0x2440), the event 0x00191510 waits on

  device is 0x0019B200; the reserve event is 0x0019D640; its sibling
  0x0019D630 is the VBLANK event, signalled ~1000 times a run from 0x00193E62
  via sub_0018CE50 (D3DDevice_BlockUntilVerticalBlank).

The render target is 0x005F0000, pitch 1280, clip 640x480, 16bpp. The viewport
the title programs is textbook: scale 320/-240/16777215, offset 320.531/240.531.
On this host the window is fed from that same surface, via
xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource(nv2a_pb_exec_surface), so what is composed
is what is displayed. PCRTC_START is never programmed and must not be trusted.

PFIFO control flow: CALL ((h & 3) == 2) and RETURN (h == 0x00020000) are now
implemented with hardware semantics -- the caller keeps the one-deep stack,
saving the cursor after the call word exactly as the hardware saves DMA_GET.
JSRF uses NEITHER; zero of each in a full run. A real gap, closed, and not the
cause of anything.


A RUN
=====

  RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 \
  RECOMP_HDD_ROOT="$PWD/build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/NAME-hdd" \
  python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_bounded.py NAME --seconds 110

Each run needs its own HDD (119 MB); delete the -hdd afterwards, the stderr.log
is the evidence and it is small. Rebuild with:

  cd build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/build && cmake --build . -j8 && ctest
```

```txt
    -> sub_0019EB2D
    -> sub_001A490D
    -> sub_001A40F5
    -> sub_001A3E58
    -> sub_001A308E

Original guest routine 0x001A308E is a 15-byte DSOUND busy wait:
  test byte ptr [ecx+0x12],1
  je return
  loop:
    test word ptr [ecx+0x12],0x8000
    jne loop
  return

While the main thread stayed in that loop, the DSOUND worker was blocked in
bridge_RtlEnterCriticalSection. Renderer, USB/OHCI, and APU threads remained
alive. Post-freeze kernel-call accounting rose to roughly 484 million calls,
dominated by critical-section/IRQL churn. This identifies a scheduling/completion
deadlock in the guest DSOUND path, not an input or graphics freeze.

The title's real completion path at 0x001A2FB5 tests object+0x12 bit 15. At
0x001A2FBE it clears exactly that bit with:
  and word ptr [esi+0x12],0x7fff
then returns without other object work in this case.

Existing repository evidence independently describes the same spin in:
  JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-05_GAMEPLAY.md
and the harness already contains jsrf_audio_completion_probe.


MINIMAL AUDIO OVERRIDE NOW IMPLEMENTED
======================================
File:
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/jsrf_manual_overrides.c

Added manual function sub_001A308E. If object+0x12 bit 0 says this wait applies,
it clears only bit 15, preserving all other flags, then performs thiscall return
stack adjustment. This mirrors the observed hardware completion transition and
avoids the impossible busy wait while the main execution chain owns progress.

The generated source was regenerated with 0x001A308E excluded as a manual
function. Generated calls now use RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE(... 0x001A308E ...) and the
dispatch table maps 0x001A308E to the manual symbol. Build and link succeeded.

Instrumentation maintenance:
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_startup.py

The removed manual function no longer has a generated loc_001A308E label, and
the three remaining DSOUND probe labels moved from recomp_0009.c to
recomp_0010.c. The instrumentation map was updated accordingly. It installs
84 fixed observation sites successfully.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-10_ANIMATION.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE CORN TUTORIAL: CHARACTERS DRAW BUT DO NOT ANIMATE
=====================================================================
Claude, 10 Sep 2026. Supersedes the animation/missing-character parts of
earlier handovers. Read this before touching the tutorial fault.

Checkpoint used throughout: the opening Corn dialogue,
"This is the GG's Garrage. Hey, where's our pizza?"
Both sides at live=61, 47 ids, +7930/+7934=FFFFFFFF, +7EC4=0.
Run the recomp with RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0 (see below) to see Corn at all.


1. THE ESTABLISHED FAILURE
--------------------------
Per-frame character state is not written. Measured with the same 0x2000 window
and 12 s interval on both sides:

    object            xemu            recomp
    CPlayer id 44     299 dwords      8
    CPlayer id 45     506 dwords      136

Not merely fewer -- different places. In xemu BOTH CPlayers write a contiguous
run at +0x9E8 and +0xCE0..0xD14+ (a 4x4 matrix; confirmed 16 dwords in 5 s).
In the recomp NEITHER does. The only offset written on all four is +0xC94.

User-confirmed by eye: Corn dances in xemu, is static in the recomp, and A does
not advance the dialogue. +0x7EC4 (a tutorial progression marker that xemu's
archived snapshots show going 0 -> 1) never leaves 0 in our runs -- 720 s of
steady state with no change in any of the 47 objects' first 0x50 bytes.


2. THE DIVERGENCE, AND ITS SIGNATURE
------------------------------------
Every per-character identity field is DISTINCT PER CHARACTER in xemu and
IDENTICAL ACROSS BOTH CHARACTERS in the recomp:

    field      xemu            recomp
    +0xE50     23, 25          15, 15
    +0x11C     170, 171        128, 128
    +0xE6C     170, 171        128, 128
    +0x9E4     233, 234        61, 61

This is the shape of both CPlayers being CONSTRUCTED WITH THE SAME CHARACTER
IDENTITY, not of one field being miswritten. Everything downstream follows
faithfully from it.

The downstream mechanics are fully understood and CORRECT in the recomp:

    sub_0009E910 @0x0009EBC3:  +0xE6C := [this+0x11C]        (a plain copy)
    sub_000A0120:              record = 0x2104A0 + idx*96
                               + 0x30 if [this+0xE70] != 0
    sub_000A0260:              return *(record + 0xC)
    sub_0009D030 @0x0009D0AA:  [this+0xE54] := that return value

Verified: the table at 0x002104A0 is XBE-resident and byte-identical between
default.xbe and xemu's runtime memory (all 6144 bytes checked). record[128]+0xC
is genuinely 61; record[170]/[171] are genuinely 233/234. The lookup is right;
the input is wrong.


3. WHAT IS ELIMINATED (do not re-investigate)
---------------------------------------------
Each of these was measured, not argued.

  ID 46's absence          xemu lacks it during the dialogue too; it appears
                           only in the tutorial_done snapshots.
  Draw-list membership     identical across all 47 objects, all three lists.
  eACTFLAG / mask +0x0C    0 differences across all 47.
  m_dwZSort +0x14          0 differences across all 47.
  The id registry          identical 47-id set; ids 233/234 exist in BOTH.
  vtables                  CPlayers are 0x001CCFF8 with flags 0x00805040 on
                           both sides. NOT a vtable or layout fault.
  CActSequence             object id 0, +0x48 = 30 = WaitEndStoryOrVsMission
                           on both sides. The Corn tutorial is a STORY MISSION,
                           not the Tutorial branch (indices 32-35).
  Heap placement           RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0 moved the manager
                           0x040D3A70 -> 0x005E3A70 and changed every garbage
                           value while leaving the garbage COUNT at 106/107 of
                           188 float fields (xemu 33). Placement is not it.
  The +0xE54 bit-0 gate    FALSIFIED. xemu reads +0xE54 = 0 with bit 0 clear on
                           both CPlayers and Corn dances anyway. A four-link
                           causal chain was built on this and is dead. The
                           unexamined assumption was that every `lea [reg+0xce0]`
                           site operates on a CPlayer -- sub_00080340 uses ebx,
                           sub_00094AB0 uses ebp, and neither base was ever tied
                           to that object. A static offset match is not an
                           object identity.
  sub_0007EA00             writes +0x11C from [this+0x10F4] gated on
                           [this+0xE50]==0x1B. Nobody has 27 and +0x10F4 is 0
                           on both sides, so it never ran.

Still UNPROVEN: that the identity divergence causes the missing animation. We
have a confirmed symptom and a confirmed divergence with no demonstrated link.
Do not assert one.


4. THE NEXT STEP
----------------
CPlayer is constructed by sub_0007E830 (one of only two sites storing vtable
0x001CCFF8; the other is sub_00084200), called from sub_00080320. The
constructor takes no identity argument in its prologue, so identity is either
already on the object or applied by the caller.

  a) Instrument sub_00080320 at entry with `this` capture (ONE site) and see
     what it assigns to each CPlayer.
  b) Find what writes +0xE50 -- it is the earliest field showing the signature.
  c) Whatever is found, the decisive test is whether restoring distinct
     identities restores the +0x9E8/+0xCE0 writes. Correlation is not the
     chain.

Also still unanswered, and worth reopening if (a)-(c) stall: WHAT actually
writes +0xCE0 in xemu? Never determined. xemu's GDB write watchpoints do not
trap these writes (proven with a positive control: the block changed 16 dwords
in 5 s while an armed Z2 watchpoint never fired).


5. TOOLING ADDED THIS SESSION
-----------------------------
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/
    xemu_objects.py        GDB-stub object inventory (was in /private/tmp)
    xemu_object_delta.py   per-object mutation rates over an interval
    xemu_index_chain.py    one-pass capture of the +0x9E4 provenance
    xemu_rsp.py            resume-safe RSP helper -- USE THIS, see 6
    compare_objects.py     symbolic differ; resolves pointers to pointee
                           identity so heap-base offsets cannot fake diffs
    func_hit_probe.c       function-entry counters + `this` capture
    instrument_func_hit.py installs/removes them in generated C
  main.c
    jsrf_object_dump()     RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP=<dir>, bounded JSON time series
    [JSRF-GATE]            cheap two-object field sampler in the scene report
    RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0 opt-out (default unchanged)

Captures worth keeping (render-investigation/):
  xemu_corn_opening_v2.json, xemu_corn_opening_64mb.json,
  xemu_index_chain.json, xemu_delta_corn.json, recomp_corn_opening_v2.json
  /tmp/xemu_cplayer_44.bin, _45.bin (0x2000 each -- most questions about xemu
  CPlayer fields can be answered from these WITHOUT a replay)


6. CONSTRAINTS PAID FOR IN RUNS
-------------------------------
  * NEVER probe xemu's stub port with nc. Connecting IS attaching and attaching
    HALTS the VM. A bare `nc -z` froze the guest.
  * Any script that halts xemu must resume it in a `finally`. Three replays were
    lost to scripts that raised between the halt and the continue; the stub then
    refuses new connections (a stale CLOSED socket beside the LISTEN).
  * Do NOT send \x03 after connecting -- the attach already stopped the guest and
    the extra interrupt desynchronises the stream. xemu_rsp.py probes with a
    read first and only interrupts if that fails. Use it.
  * INSTRUMENTATION WEIGHT IS A HAZARD, measured. jsrf_func_arg originally
    linear-scanned 192 entries per call; with nine hot sites the pad poll
    stalled within 10 s (polls=475 flat, pad opened, nonneutral=262). One site
    with a bounded scan ran past 6000 polls to the tutorial. Instrument ONE site
    at a time and keep per-call work cheap. A sudden early poll stall means the
    probe set is too heavy -- it is not the controller.
  * Do NOT instrument mid-function `loc_` labels. Counters at 00094D20/3F/47/5A
    wedged the guest on the SEGA screen (drawOne stuck at 12, polls=1, no GPU
    draws). Function-entry labels are safe.
  * RECOMP_MEM_WATCH CANNOT RUN on this build. Armed on 0x03536C3C it SIGSEGVs
    at t=5 s on guest 0xFFFFFFF8; the identical binary with it unset has zero
    faults and reaches the tutorial. The hook being present in the generated
    recomp_types.h does NOT mean the build tolerates it.
  * "No input" has two distinct fingerprints: polls climbing with nonneutral=0
    means another process holds the pad (xemu was the culprit once); polls
    flatlining means the guest stopped asking.
  * Object-diff window size matters: a 0x400 window said "CPlayers frozen" and
    a 0x2000 window disproved it in the same session.


7. IDEAS AND TOOLS WORTH BUILDING NEXT
--------------------------------------
Ranked by how much time they would have saved today. Roughly fifteen manual
playthroughs to the Corn dialogue were spent this session; that, not analysis,
was the dominant cost.

  (1) xemu SAVE STATES, scripted.  Launch xemu with
        -monitor unix:/tmp/xemu-mon,server,nowait
      and drive `savevm corn` / `loadvm corn` over that socket. Reaching the
      oracle checkpoint becomes seconds instead of a playthrough. This is the
      single highest-value item and it is small. (The user was asked twice to
      save a state manually; automating it removes the need.)

  (2) SCRIPTED INPUT FOR THE RECOMP.  Add RECOMP_INPUT_SCRIPT=<file> feeding
      timestamped pad reports into the OHCI/USB path, recorded from a live run.
      Reaching our own checkpoint then costs no human. Combined with (1) the
      whole paired comparison becomes a single unattended command. This also
      makes the poll-stall reproducible on demand instead of by luck.

  (3) THE SIGNATURE SCANNER.  Today's breakthrough was noticing a pattern:
      fields that are DISTINCT between the two CPlayers in xemu but IDENTICAL
      between them in the recomp. That is mechanically detectable across all
      0x2000 bytes rather than found by eye. Write it: read both objects on both
      sides, and report every offset matching that signature (and its inverse).
      It would have pointed at +0xE50/+0x11C immediately, and it generalises to
      any pair of same-class objects.

  (4) FUNCTION-SCOPED STORE WATCHING.  RECOMP_MEM_WATCH is global -- a call on
      every guest store -- which is why it kills the run. Instead extend
      instrument_func_hit.py to wrap stores only inside chosen functions, so the
      cost is proportional to one function rather than the whole title. That
      turns "which instruction wrote this field" from impossible back into a
      one-run question, which is exactly what blocked us tonight.

  (5) O(1) PROBE STORAGE.  Replace jsrf_func_arg's linear scan with a small
      direct-mapped hash keyed on (va, value). Removes the perturbation class
      that cost several runs and lets more than one site be armed at a time.

  (6) POLL-STALL WATCHDOG.  Detect `polls` flatlining while GPU draws advance,
      print a loud marker, and optionally dump guest thread PCs at that instant.
      The stall is still unexplained after five sessions and is a recurring tax;
      catching it in the act with a stack sample is the obvious missing step.

  (7) AUTO-SYMBOLISATION IN REPORTS.  Pipe every raw sub_XXXXXXXX through
      symbolize.py when printing, so logs name functions where the
      decompilation knows them. Cheap, and would have made several traces
      readable at a glance.

  (8) A SINGLE PAIRED-DIFF COMMAND.  jsrf_diff.py that, given a checkpoint,
      captures both sides and prints the field-level differences -- wrapping
      xemu_objects.py, the recomp dump and compare_objects.py. The pieces exist;
      the glue does not.


8. A NOTE ON METHOD
-------------------
Three hypotheses died today: ID 46, heap placement, and the +0xE54 gate. The
third had a complete four-link causal chain and survived until someone finally
read the field in xemu. The lesson is the one already in CLAUDE.md, but it
recurred in a new form: a static offset match (`lea [reg+0xce0]`) was treated as
an object identity without ever proving the base register held that object.
Before building a chain, check that each link's BASE is the object you think it
is -- not just that the offset matches.


9. FACILITIES THIS PROJECT ALREADY HAS THAT WE DID NOT USE
----------------------------------------------------------
Asked at the end of the session whether xboxrecomp was being leveraged fully.
It was not. 196 RECOMP_* switches exist; enumerate them before building
anything (`grep -rhoE 'RECOMP_[A-Z0-9_]+' src diagnostics templates tools`).

  --trace-functions FILE   THE BIG MISS. tools/recomp/__main__.py takes a file
                           of addresses and emits trace calls for exactly those
                           functions, backed by src/kernel/recomp_trace.c, with
                           RECOMP_TRACE_ARGS (argument capture),
                           RECOMP_TRACE_BUDGET (a cap -- the perturbation
                           control whose absence cost runs this session),
                           RECOMP_TRACE_PROFILE, _ESP, _DEREF, _ENTER, _EXIT.
                           func_hit_probe.c + instrument_func_hit.py are a
                           hand-rolled, worse version of this. The one real
                           argument for hand-instrumenting is that
                           --trace-functions needs a REGENERATION, which this
                           tree warns is not bit-stable and has a SIGBUS
                           history -- but that trade should be made knowingly.

  RECOMP_HEAP_POISON       Would have settled the "uninitialised object fields"
                           thread directly. We instead ran the whole
                           reserve-space experiment to falsify it.
  RECOMP_PEEK / _CHAIN     Guest memory peeking; probably replaces the ad-hoc
                           lldb `memory read --outfile` reads used all session.
  RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN       Aimed at dialogue. "A does not advance the dialogue"
                           is half the reported symptom and was never probed.
  RECOMP_WATCHDOG_SECS     Relevant to the poll stall.
  RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH/_ALL Kernel-side watching, unexplored.
  RECOMP_MEM_WATCH_MIRRORS NOT A SWITCH -- corrected 11 Sep. It is a
                           compile-time `#define 28u` in recomp_mem_watch.c with
                           no env binding, used only to bound one mirror loop
                           that normalize_ram skips for in-range addresses. It
                           cannot reduce the watch's cost.
                           Also checked: MEM32(addr) is literally
                           *(volatile uint32_t*)XBOX_PTR(addr), identical to the
                           watch-DISABLED store path, so enabling the watch
                           changes no store semantics or masking. The cost is
                           purely the per-store function call.
                           Two further reasons the watch is the wrong tool here:
                           it takes a FIXED guest VA, and CPlayer addresses are
                           not stable across runs (0x3626B50 in one fake-pad
                           run, 0x36284A0 in the next).
  RECOMP_ICALL_FEEDBACK    Indirect-call resolution, unused here.
  RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE/_REPORT/_NO_FREE   Allocation history, unused.

  RECOMP_FAKE_PAD          EXISTS but is explicitly diagnostic: it pulses A and
                           START once a second and "cannot steer anything". So
                           scripted input to reach a checkpoint unattended is
                           still genuinely missing (idea 7.2 stands).

Revision to section 7: ideas (4) function-scoped store watching and (5) O(1)
probe storage are largely SUPERSEDED by --trace-functions, which is already
selective and already budgeted. Build (1) xemu save states and (2) scripted
input first; then reach for --trace-functions instead of extending the
hand-rolled probes.

On Burnout 3 (../burnout3-research): its docs are forward-looking planning for
a different title -- RenderWare .rws formats, kernel imports, recompilation
strategy options -- not debugging findings. JSRF does touch RenderWare (the
64 MB wrap mirrors in xbox_memory_layout.c exist for its memory walker), but
the current fault is in JSRF's own CActBase/CPlayer identity assignment,
upstream of any rendering engine. No clues for this bug. It would only become
relevant if the missing +0xCE0 writes turn out to be skinning matrices.


10. SIGNATURE SCAN RESULTS (diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/signature_scan.py)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Built and run against the saved captures, no game needed:
  /tmp/xemu_cplayer_{44,45}.bin  vs  /tmp/recomp_cplayer_{44,45}.bin
(the recomp pair is sliced out of the chr_1.bin character-region capture).

2048 dwords per object compared. Four classes:

  IDENTITY-LOST    23 offsets   distinct in xemu, IDENTICAL here
  IDENTITY-GAINED  90 offsets   identical in xemu, distinct here
  BOTH-DISTINCT  1112 offsets   healthy per-character data
  VALUE-DIFF      317 offsets

**The 1112 matters as much as the 23.** Our two CPlayers differ in over a
thousand places, so this is NOT "the same object registered twice" or two
copies of one character. Only specific identity fields collapse to one value.

IDENTITY-LOST, excluding pointer-valued noise -- the causal candidates:

    offset   xemu (44 / 45)        recomp (44 / 45)
    +0x011C  170 / 171             128 / 128     character slot
    +0x09E4  233 / 234             61 / 61       derived index
    +0x09E8  0.390 / 0.800 (f)     0 / 0         per-frame animated value
    +0x0D68  11.69 / 11.12 (f)     5.61 / 5.61
    +0x0E50  23 / 25               15 / 15
    +0x0E58  12 / 3                11 / 11
    +0x0E6C  170 / 171             128 / 128
    +0x0E80  39.5 / 99.5 (f)       0.5 / 0.5     (sub_0009D030 does
                                                  `lea ebx,[esi+0xE80]`)

The remaining entries (+0x11A8 upward) are sparse per-frame floats, nonzero in
xemu for one character or the other and zero in both here -- consistent with
animation simply not running, i.e. consequences rather than causes.

So the identity cluster is SMALL and TIGHT: +0x011C, +0x0E50, +0x0E58, +0x0E6C,
+0x0E80, +0x0D68. Chase whichever is written earliest.

IDENTITY-GAINED (90) is a separate finding: contiguous regions
(+0x0178..+0x0244, +0x0368..+0x0418 and more) read ZERO in xemu on both
characters and hold garbage here, in values shaped like packed 16-bit pairs.
This is the "uninitialised fields" pattern from earlier in the session, now
quantified and localised. Untested idea: run with RECOMP_HEAP_POISON and see
whether these offsets carry the poison pattern -- that would prove the guest
never writes them, which the reserve-space experiment could not.

The scanner is generic: give it any two same-class objects from each side.
It would have pointed at +0x0E50/+0x011C on day one instead of by eye.


11. RECOMP_FAKE_PAD RESULT (negative, useful)
---------------------------------------------
`RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1` DOES drive the title unattended -- it got past the intro
into a scene load without any human input -- but it landed at live=161/123, a
different scene from the tutorial's 61/47, and `polls` flatlined at 124 with
nonneutral=0. Consistent with its own comment: it pulses A and START and
"cannot steer anything".

So it cannot reach the Corn checkpoint, and scripted input (idea 7.2) is still
needed. But it is a usable no-human smoke test for anything that only needs the
title or an arbitrary scene.

Also learned: RECOMP_PEEK takes FIXED guest VAs, so an address list computed for
one scene prints garbage in another. Recompute the addresses per scene, or peek
the manager root and derive.


12. AUTONOMOUS SESSION (fake pad + O(1) probe): THE BIG UNLOCKS
---------------------------------------------------------------
(a) THE IDENTITY COLLAPSE IS GENERAL, NOT TUTORIAL-SPECIFIC.
    RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1 reaches gameplay unattended with 3-4 CPlayers. All of
    them read:
        +0x11C=128  +0xE50=15  +0xE58=11  +0xE6C=128  +0x9E4=61
    identical across every CPlayer, in an ordinary gameplay scene.
    **Debugging this no longer requires the Corn checkpoint or a human.**
    That is the single most useful thing found today.

(b) THE PROBE IS NOW O(1). jsrf_func_hit uses a 1024-slot direct-mapped table
    (open addressing on va>>4) instead of a linear scan. **113 sites armed at
    once ran with no destabilisation** -- against nine sites stalling the guest
    in ten seconds with the old scan. This makes "which of N candidates runs?"
    a single experiment instead of N.

(c) THE FUNNEL, using (a) and (b):
        186 store sites writing +0x11C
     -> 112 containing functions
     ->  16 that actually execute       (96 never run at all)
     ->  13 called with a CPlayer `this`
     ->   5 that also write +0xE50
     ->   4 after excluding the clearing pass

    **SHORTLIST FOR THE IDENTITY SETTER:**
        sub_00091930  sub_00092100  sub_00098100  sub_000A0610
    all called at initialisation frequency (1-2 calls per CPlayer).

(d) sub_000836F0 IS THE CLEARING PASS, not the setter. Called exactly once per
    CPlayer, it writes the whole identity cluster:
        0x00083726  mov [esi+0x11C], ebx     ; ebx = 0 (xor ebx,ebx at 0x8370F)
        0x0008372C  mov [esi+0xE6C], ebx     ; 0
        0x000837E6  mov [esi+0xE50], edx     ; edx = descriptor[+0x24]
        0x00083AA7  mov [esi+0xE58], 3
        0x00083AD9  mov [esi+0xE80], ebx
    Its descriptor argument (arg1) IS distinct per CPlayer -- captured live at
    0x018FBA54 and 0x018FBA88, 0x34 apart, i.e. consecutive 52-byte records --
    and descriptor[+0x24] AT CALL TIME varies (0 and 0x18). Since the object
    ends up with +0xE50=15 and +0x11C=128, both values must come from a LATER
    write. So the descriptor path is not the fault.

(e) HEAP POISON. RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=0xAB fills freed blocks. Of the 97 dwords
    in the IDENTITY-GAINED regions, **0 held the poison pattern** on any of the
    three CPlayers. Caveat: poison only marks FREED blocks, so this rules out
    recycled-and-poisoned memory as the source but does not prove the fields
    were written.

NEW INSTALLER OPTIONS (diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_func_hit.py):
    --va-file FILE        VAs one per line (zsh does not word-split an
                          expanded argument list, which silently mangles a
                          long --va sequence)
    --stackarg VA:OFF     record the dword at [esp+OFF] on entry -- a
                          stack-passed argument
    --derefarg VA:OFF:F   record [[esp+OFF]+F] on entry -- a FIELD of a
                          pointer argument, sampled AT CALL TIME. Reading the
                          block later is not equivalent: it may have been
                          reused by then, which cost one experiment here.

NEXT: arm --arg or --derefarg on the four shortlisted functions and see which
one writes a nonzero +0x11C / +0xE50 for a CPlayer, and from what source. All
four are reachable unattended with RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1, so this needs no human.


13. CORRECTION (11 Sep): +0x11C IS A MUTABLE STATE INDEX, NOT AN IDENTITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Captured with the new --ecxpair option, which records `this` AND the field
together (either alone is ambiguous):

    sub_00098100  this=036274A0 (CPlayer)  +0x11C = 0x6A (106)
    sub_00098100  this=036274A0 (CPlayer)  +0x11C = 0x7E (126)
    sub_00098100  this=03630880 (CPlayer)  +0x11C = 4

Both objects confirmed CPlayers from the same run's object dump. So +0x11C
takes 4, 106, 126 and 128 at different moments and sub_00098100 actively
changes it (106 -> 126). It is a **state/animation index**, not a fixed
character identity.

**This corrects section 12 and the memory note.** "Both CPlayers read
+0x11C=128" was a SINGLE-INSTANT SNAPSHOT of a field that moves, not a
permanent collapse. Two objects sharing a value at one instant is not evidence
of shared identity.

**And it is a methodological warning about signature_scan.py:** it compares one
instant per side. For any MUTABLE field, "distinct in xemu, identical here" can
be sampling coincidence. The scan's output is a list of CANDIDATES, and each
one must be re-checked over time before it is believed. Fields that survive
that check are real; the rest are noise. Use --ecxpair (or a dump time series)
to classify a candidate as static or mutable BEFORE building on it.

What survives, and fits the symptom better: ours sit at **128** while xemu's sit
at **170/171**. That is consistent with our characters being stuck in a DEFAULT
state rather than being the wrong character -- and with the user's observation
that "the player appears briefly". A stuck state index would also explain the
missing per-frame +0xCE0 writes without any identity being wrong.

NEXT, and it is now a different question: not "who assigns identity" but
**"why does the state index stop advancing"**. sub_00098100 is the function
observed advancing it (106 -> 126) and is called on CPlayers. Instrument its
callers, and compare the state-index TIME SERIES between xemu and the recomp
rather than single samples -- the recomp reaching 128 and stopping, against
xemu moving through a range, would be the real measurement.


14. THE FAULT IS TUTORIAL-SPECIFIC. THE ANIMATION MACHINERY WORKS.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Two measurements on 11 Sep, both unattended via RECOMP_FAKE_PAD.

(a) +0x11C IS NOT STUCK. A 31-sample series, 3 s apart, with the state index
    added to jsrf_object_dump:

      CPlayer 44: 13 distinct values -- 0,17,28,32,48,56,68,90,91,115,126,150,152
      CPlayer 45: 12 distinct values -- 17,24,28,36,44,52,56,58,60,68,76,106

    It cycles continuously, and **128 never appears in either series**. So
    "the recomp reaches 128 and stops" is FALSE. The 128 readings came from a
    different scene state (the tutorial dialogue), plausibly a legitimate
    idle/talking state. Comparing a single instant of a fast-moving field
    across two runs that are not in identical states shows a difference by
    construction. **The +0x11C divergence was sampling noise.**

(b) **THE TRANSFORM BLOCK MOVES IN GAMEPLAY.** Two live reads 10 s apart, four
    CPlayers:

      id 44 @ 03626C10  +0xCE0 16/16 dwords changed   object  319 dwords
      id 45 @ 0361E910  +0xCE0 16/16 dwords changed   object 1124 dwords
      id 46 @ 0362F010  +0xCE0 16/16, +0x9E8 2/2      object  773 dwords
      id 47 @ 0363E010  +0xCE0 16/16, +0x9E8 2/2      object 1579 dwords

    Against the Corn tutorial, where the same measurement gave 8 and 136 dwords
    with the +0xCE0 block untouched on both CPlayers.

**So the recomp animates characters correctly in ordinary gameplay.** The
missing animation is SCENE-SPECIFIC to the Corn tutorial, where xemu animates
and we do not.

This retires the whole line of inquiry from sections 2, 12 and 13: identity
assignment, the descriptor path, the state index, sub_000836F0, and the
four-way setter shortlist were all chasing a general animation fault that does
not exist. The machinery is fine; something about the tutorial state suppresses
it for those particular objects.

### The question now

What is different about the Corn tutorial that stops animation there, when the
same code animates four CPlayers in gameplay?

Candidates, in the order they are cheapest to test:
  * The tutorial CPlayers may be driven as cutscene/scripted actors rather than
    by the normal per-frame path. Compare WHICH functions are entered with a
    CPlayer `this` in the tutorial versus in gameplay -- the O(1) probe can arm
    a hundred sites, so one run of each and a set-difference answers it.
  * +0x7EC4 never leaves 0 in our tutorial while xemu's archived snapshots show
    0 -> 1. That progression marker is still unexplained and is tutorial-scoped.
  * The dialogue never advances on A. RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN is unexplored and is
    aimed exactly at this.

### Method note, third occurrence

A snapshot of a mutable quantity is not a fact about that quantity. The +0xE54
gate, the +0x11C identity and the signature scan's candidate list were all
built on single-instant comparisons. **Measure rates and series; compare
snapshots only for fields first shown to be static.**


15. PLAN FROM HERE (written 11 Sep, after the tutorial-specific finding)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The question is now: **what suppresses character animation in the Corn tutorial
when the same code animates four CPlayers in ordinary gameplay?**

Ordered by evidence-per-hour, with the human cost of each stated.

STEP 1 -- THE DIFFERENTIAL ENTRY SET.  *One tutorial playthrough; gameplay half
unattended.*  Arm the O(1) probe on a broad set of candidate functions with
`--ecxpair VA:0` (records `this`), run once in gameplay via RECOMP_FAKE_PAD and
once in the tutorial, and set-difference the functions entered with a CPlayer
`this`. Functions present in gameplay and ABSENT in the tutorial are the
suppressed path; the first one that stops is the target.
This is the single most direct attack and it is only possible because the probe
is now O(1) -- 113 sites ran with no destabilisation, so a few hundred is
plausible. Start with the known per-frame path (sub_00094AB0, sub_00080340,
sub_000606C0, sub_00060730, sub_000651E0, sub_00060930) plus the 13 functions
already observed with a CPlayer `this`.

STEP 2 -- RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE.  *Unattended.*  `jsrf_trigger_probe` observes
"the only direct writers of the root object's transient command fields" -- i.e.
scene/mode transition requests, distinguished by object and return address.
That is precisely the shape of "the tutorial is in a state gameplay is not".
It also bears on `CActMan +0x7EC4` never leaving 0 while xemu goes 0 -> 1.
Needs its probe installed (see instrument_startup.py).

STEP 3 -- RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN.  *Unattended to reach a scene; tutorial needs a
run.*  Aimed at dialogue, and "A does not advance the dialogue" is half the
reported symptom and has never been probed directly.

STEP 4 -- RECOMP_EVENT_TRACE.  *Unattended.*  Pairs kernel event signals with
waits, deduplicated by object, and reports "a wait that never returns ... once".
If the tutorial is blocked on an event that is never signalled, this names it.
RECOMP_SCHED_TRACE is the sibling for the thread side.

STEP 5 -- INFRASTRUCTURE, still the biggest multiplier.
  (a) xemu save states via `-monitor unix:/tmp/xemu-mon,server,nowait` and
      savevm/loadvm. The oracle checkpoint becomes seconds. ~15 playthroughs
      were spent this session.
  (b) Scripted input for the recomp. RECOMP_FAKE_PAD gets to gameplay but
      "cannot steer", so it cannot reach the tutorial. A timestamped pad-report
      replay would make BOTH halves of step 1 unattended.

NOT WORTH DOING: extending the identity/descriptor line (retired, section 14);
RECOMP_MEM_WATCH (unusable, and it takes a fixed VA while CPlayer addresses
move between runs); RECOMP_MEM_WATCH_MIRRORS (not a switch).

### Are we leveraging xboxrecomp fully? Better, still no.

Used for the first time today: RECOMP_FAKE_PAD (reaches gameplay with no
human -- the biggest workflow win of the session), RECOMP_HEAP_POISON,
RECOMP_PEEK.

Still unused, and four of them aim straight at the current question:
  RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE   scene/mode transition requests      <- step 2
  RECOMP_EVENT_TRACE     signal/wait pairing                 <- step 4
  RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN     dialogue                            <- step 3
  RECOMP_SCHED_TRACE     thread scheduling
  RECOMP_TREE_TRACE      object-tree traversal
  RECOMP_RESOURCE_TRACE / RECOMP_STARTUP_STATE / RECOMP_STARTUP_TRACE
  RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH / _ALL
  RECOMP_ICALL_FEEDBACK  (and the memory note that its merge step is manual)
  --trace-functions FILE with RECOMP_TRACE_ARGS / _BUDGET / _PROFILE
                         -- still the proper version of the hand-rolled probe,
                         but it needs a regeneration this tree warns about.

The pattern worth naming: the runtime's SWITCHES have been used reasonably, the
TRANSLATOR has not been used at all beyond hand-patching its output. And three
of the unused switches (trigger/event/dialog) were written for exactly the kind
of fault now in front of us.


16. STEP 1 GAMEPLAY HALF DONE; FOUR SWITCHES UNBLOCKED
-------------------------------------------------------
### Why TRIGGER/TREE/RESOURCE/STARTUP had never been used

`instrument_startup.py` refused to install ANYTHING: it asserts a per-site
label count and **5 of its 84 sites had drifted** against this generated tree
(`loc_0014F801` and `loc_0014FA19` want 2 found 1; `loc_001A2FBE`,
`loc_001A25CA`, `loc_001A3A8E` want 1 found 0). One stale assert blocked four
switches, which is very likely why they were recorded as "unexplored" rather
than tried.

Fixed with `--skip-mismatched`: each site is still validated individually, the
79 that match are installed, and the 5 skipped are named. Not a loosening of the
guarantee -- nothing is installed at a site that did not validate.

    python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_startup.py --skip-mismatched
    -> Installed 79 fixed observation sites in 7 generated files
    -> Installed 107 unresolved-flag execution sites in 12 generated files
    -> skipped 5 stale site(s): <named>

### They work

  RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE
    [TRIGGER-WRITE] call=N root_call=0 pc=00012750 ret=0001DAE7
                    object=005E3A70 root=00000000 arg=00000000
    Repeated writes to the manager root's transient command field, all with
    arg=0, from one site. In the tutorial this is where a scene/mode transition
    request would appear -- and `+0x7EC4` never leaving 0 is exactly that shape.

  RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN
    [DIALOG] scanning guest RAM for vtable 0x001CC660
    [DIALOG] object 0x0006F244 [+0x98]="" -- 1 object
    It finds the dialogue object by vtable and prints its string. Run this AT
    THE CORN DIALOGUE: the text and the object's state are then directly
    readable, which is the most direct probe yet of "A does not advance".

  RECOMP_TREE_TRACE printed nothing in gameplay (sites may be among the five
    skipped, or it is scene-gated). Untested rather than negative.

### Step 1, gameplay half -- DONE (unattended)

`render-investigation/cplayer_functions_gameplay.txt`: the 17 functions entered
with a CPlayer `this` in settled gameplay (live=161), captured with
`--ecxpair VA:0`, which records (`this`, vtable) so the class is identified
without correlating against a dump:

    00080340 000836F0 0008D040 0008E5A0 00091640 00091930 00092100 00098100
    000982B0 0009A170 0009AA70 0009D030 0009E910 000A0260 000A0610 000A08B0
    000A0F10

**Absent even in gameplay: 00094AB0, 000606C0, 00060730, 000651E0, 00060930.**
None of them ever takes a CPlayer `this`. That is independent confirmation that
the +0xE54/+0xCE0 chain of section 2 was built on functions that never touch a
CPlayer at all.

RECOMP_SCHED_TRACE also works and looks healthy in gameplay: waits report
`woken` climbing with `timed-out=0`.

### What remains, and it needs one playthrough

Run the SAME armed build at the Corn tutorial and diff:

    comm -13 <tutorial set> <gameplay set>   -> present in gameplay, absent in
                                                the tutorial = the suppressed path

with RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN=1 and RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE=1 in the same run, so the
dialogue object's state and any transition request are captured at the same
instant. That is one human run for three measurements.


17. THE SUPPRESSED REGION: CPlayer +0x0000..+0x09F4
----------------------------------------------------
Measured 11 Sep, same build, same 10 s interval, two scenes.

The tutorial run had progressed further than any before it: `+0x7EC4 = 1`
(matching xemu's `snap_tutorial_terminal`), and the dialogue DID advance on A.
So the tutorial is not stuck. **The characters still do not animate:**

    tutorial  id 44 @ 03536B20  +0xCE0  0/16 dwords   object   8 dwords
    tutorial  id 45 @ 03542D00  +0xCE0  0/16 dwords   object 137 dwords
    gameplay  id 44..47         +0xCE0 16/16 dwords   object 319/1124/773/1579

The tutorial figures (8, 137) reproduce the original Corn-dialogue reading
(8, 136) exactly, in a different run and a later tutorial stage. The fault is
stable and scene-scoped, and it is NOT the progression stall -- progression
worked here and animation still did not.

### Which regions move, per scene

    move in GAMEPLAY, never in the tutorial : 1645 dwords, +0x0000..+0x09F4
                                              (one near-contiguous sweep;
                                               +0x0444..+0x09CC alone is 355)
    move in BOTH                            :  139 dwords, all ABOVE +0xC94
                                              (+0xC94, +0x11CC, +0x1248..,
                                               +0x147C, +0x1628..)
    move only in the tutorial               :    5 dwords

So the tutorial updates only the object's HIGH region and never touches the low
~2.5 KB. `+0x9E8` -- one of the two fields xemu writes per frame on both
CPlayers -- sits inside the suppressed sweep, at its very top edge.

**The target is therefore: what writes CPlayer +0x0000..+0x09F4 每 frame in
gameplay and not in the tutorial?**

### Candidates from the entry-set differential

Entered with a CPlayer `this` in gameplay but NOT at the tutorial:

    sub_00091640   sub_00091930   sub_00092100   sub_000A0610

Nothing is entered in the tutorial that is not also entered in gameplay, so the
tutorial path is a strict subset. Treat this list as SUGGESTIVE only: those four
fire just 1-63 times in gameplay, so their absence over one window is weak
evidence. Confirm with a longer tutorial window before acting.
Three of the four (00091930, 00092100, 000A0610) were independently on the
earlier "+0xE50 writers called with a CPlayer" shortlist, which is mild
corroboration that they are per-character behaviour drivers.

### Reproduction

    python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_func_hit.py \
        --va 00012580 --ecxpair 00080340:0 ... (see /tmp/anim_path.txt list)
    RECOMP_FUNC_HIT_TRACE=1 RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN=1 RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0 ...
    gameplay half: add RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1 (no human)
    tutorial half: real pad, and do NOT install instrument_startup.py -- its
                   107 unresolved-flag sites take `polls` to ZERO (the guest
                   never asks at all) and read exactly like a dead controller.


18. PLAN, REVISED 11 Sep AFTER THE REGION FINDING
--------------------------------------------------
State: two SEPARATE faults are now distinguished.
  A. Animation suppressed in the tutorial -- STABLE, reproduced across runs
     and tutorial stages (8/137 dwords vs 16/16 in gameplay).
  B. Tutorial progression stalling (+0x7EC4 stuck at 0) -- INTERMITTENT; it
     did NOT occur in the last run, and animation was still dead. Do not
     conflate them.

### Why the current candidate list is insufficient

The four tutorial-absent functions write only ~14 distinct offsets between them
(0x118-0x134, 0x1A4, 0x9D0, 0x9DC). The suppressed sweep is **1645 dwords**.
They cannot explain it.

And static store analysis cannot find the real writer: a 355-dword contiguous
block (+0x0444..+0x09CC) is a block copy or an indexed loop, not the
`mov [reg+disp]` form a disassembly grep matches. **Do not spend more time
grepping for stores.** The writer has to be found at runtime.

### STEP 1 (decisive) -- the oracle at the same point
Two GDB reads 10 s apart on xemu's CPlayers AT THE CORN TUTORIAL, then diff the
changed-offset regions exactly as section 17 does for the recomp.
  * xemu writes +0x0000..+0x09F4 there -> confirms the low region is what we
    fail to write, in the oracle, at the same scene. The comparison stops being
    "our gameplay vs our tutorial" and becomes a true differential.
  * xemu does NOT write it -> the low sweep is a gameplay-only behaviour and
    section 17's framing is wrong; go back to +0xCE0 alone.
Cost: xemu with `-s` plus one playthrough. Use xemu_rsp.py. This is the highest
value measurement available and it has never been taken.

### STEP 2 -- widen the entry differential
The armed set (23 sites) was chosen before the region was known and is too
narrow. Arm several hundred sites -- affordable now the probe is O(1), proven
at 113 -- covering the functions that plausibly touch a CPlayer per frame, and
re-run both halves. The writer of a 1645-dword sweep is NOT in the current set.
Gameplay half is unattended (RECOMP_FAKE_PAD); tutorial half needs one run.
Remember: do NOT install instrument_startup.py for the tutorial half.

### STEP 3 -- infrastructure, to stop paying a playthrough per experiment
  (a) xemu save states: `-monitor unix:/tmp/xemu-mon,server,nowait` +
      savevm/loadvm. Makes STEP 1 repeatable in seconds.
  (b) Scripted pad input for the recomp, so the tutorial half of STEP 2 needs
      no human either. RECOMP_FAKE_PAD reaches gameplay but cannot steer.
Roughly twenty playthroughs have been spent across this investigation.

### STEP 4 -- fault B, separately
+0x7EC4 stuck at 0, and the pad-poll stall. Both intermittent, both distinct
from fault A. RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE is installed and working for the first one
(watch the root transient command writes at pc=00012750), but it rides on
instrument_startup.py, which cannot be used in a run that needs input. Resolve
that conflict before attacking B -- e.g. install only the trigger sites.

### Not worth doing
More static store grepping (per above); the identity/descriptor line (retired);
RECOMP_MEM_WATCH (unusable, fixed VA); mid-function loc_ probes (wedge the
guest); the four-candidate list as a target in itself.


19. SECTION 17 CORRECTED -- THE REAL DIFFERENTIAL, LIKE FOR LIKE
------------------------------------------------------------------
The oracle measurement of STEP 1 was taken (xemu_region_delta.py, new) and it
**overturned section 17**, exactly as that step was designed to be able to.

    xemu at the Corn tutorial, 10 s:
      CPlayer 44:   2 dwords changed,  +0xCE0  0/16,  low region 0
      CPlayer 45: 449 dwords changed,  +0xCE0 16/16,  low region 1 (just +0x9E8)

**xemu does NOT write +0x0000..+0x09F4 at the tutorial either.** That sweep is
gameplay-only behaviour in both implementations, so "the suppressed low 2.5 KB"
was an artefact of comparing our gameplay against our tutorial. Section 17's
target was wrong. Compare like with like: same scene, both sides.

**And id 44 is near-static in xemu too** (2 dwords, against our 8). So id 44 is
not the animating character; **id 45 is**. Any framing built on "both CPlayers
are frozen" was wrong about half its subject.

### The actual divergence, CPlayer 45, tutorial, 10 s

    xemu 449 dwords | recomp 137 dwords | shared 119

    IN XEMU, NOT IN THE RECOMP -- 330 dwords, structured:
      +0x09E8                     1
      +0x0CE0..+0x0DE4           66      <- the transform block; FOUR TIMES the
                                            16 dwords previously measured
      +0x0E80                     1
      +0x11D4..+0x120C      4 x 3        <- 3-dword groups = vectors
      +0x12C0..+0x140C      4 x 15
      +0x1484..+0x14D4      5+ x 3

    IN THE RECOMP, NOT IN XEMU -- 18 dwords: +0x1C44..+0x1C64, +0x1CA0..+0x1CC0
    IN BOTH -- 119 dwords: +0xC94, +0x11CC, +0x147C, +0x1628.. upward

A large matrix block plus many 3-float vector groups is the shape of SKELETAL
ANIMATION -- bone matrices and per-bone transforms. The recomp drives the
shared 119 dwords (whatever that is: state, timers, the +0x1628 block) but
never produces the 330.

### Why this is the right target now

It is a single object (id 45), a single scene, both sides measured with the same
tool over the same interval, and the difference is 330 specific dwords in
identifiable structures rather than "animation does not work". The earlier
+0xCE0 16-dword figure was a windowing artefact: the real block is +0xCE0..
+0xDE4, 66 dwords.

### Next

  1. Widen the recomp-side window to +0x2000 and confirm the 330 are absent over
     a longer interval, not merely slower.
  2. Find what writes +0xCE0..+0xDE4 on id 45 in xemu. Static grep is useless
     for a 66-dword block (block copy / indexed loop), and xemu's GDB
     watchpoints do not trap these writes (proven with a positive control).
     So: widen the O(1) entry differential (STEP 2) and look for a function
     entered with id 45's `this` in xemu-like conditions but not ours -- or
     bracket it by arming every function that the shared-119 writer calls.
  3. Re-check whether id 44 SHOULD animate at all. If xemu leaves it near-static
     at this dialogue, "Corn is still" may be correct behaviour for that object,
     and the whole user-visible symptom may be about id 45 alone.


20. ID 44 IS STATIC BY DESIGN. THE FAULT IS ONE OBJECT: ID 45.
---------------------------------------------------------------
A 30 s xemu sample at the Corn dialogue (against the 10 s one):

    CPlayer 44:   2 dwords changed in 30 s -- the SAME two as in 10 s
                  (+0x0C94, +0x134C). +0xCE0 0/16.
    CPlayer 45: 506 dwords in 30 s, same structure as in 10 s.

**xemu's id 44 does not animate at this dialogue.** It is static by design, and
our id 44 (8 dwords) is therefore NOT divergent. Corn is **id 45**.

So the entire user-visible fault reduces to: **CPlayer id 45 is missing 330
dwords of structured animation writes per interval** -- the +0xCE0..+0xDE4
66-dword block, four 15-dword groups at +0x12C0..+0x140C, and a series of
3-dword vector groups. Everything else about both objects matches in kind.

Note the offsets touched by id 45 SATURATE quickly: the 10 s and 30 s samples
name the same runs with the same counts. So this is a fixed working set written
every frame, not a slowly growing one -- which means a recomp-side longer window
will not reveal "slower", only "absent". That check is now cheap and conclusive.

### What this retires

  * "Both CPlayers are frozen" -- half of it was correct behaviour.
  * Anything measured on id 44 as evidence of the fault, including the 8-vs-2
    dword comparison and the +0x11C / +0xE50 / +0xE58 readings taken on it.
  * The +0x0000..+0x09F4 region (section 17, already corrected).

### The remaining question, stated exactly

What writes CPlayer id 45's +0xCE0..+0xDE4 (66 dwords), +0x12C0..+0x140C
(4 x 15) and the 3-dword vector groups every frame, in xemu at the Corn
dialogue and in our own GAMEPLAY, but not in our tutorial?

Constraints on answering it, all established:
  * static grep cannot see it (block copy / indexed loop, not mov [reg+disp]);
  * xemu GDB write watchpoints do not trap these writes (positive control:
    the block changed 16 dwords in 5 s while an armed Z2 never fired);
  * RECOMP_MEM_WATCH cannot run (SIGSEGV at t=5 s, A/B proven) and takes a
    fixed VA while CPlayer addresses move between runs;
  * the 23-site entry differential did not contain the writer.

So: widen the O(1) entry differential substantially (it is proven at 113 sites
and is O(1) per call), comparing our GAMEPLAY against our TUTORIAL for id 45
specifically -- gameplay writes the block, the tutorial does not, and both are
the same binary, so the function that appears in one and not the other is the
target. The gameplay half needs no human.


21. THE VIDEO'S MECHANISM, AND WHAT IT REFRAMES
------------------------------------------------
Source: Video Notes/nJWHf-uUIBU.{srt,_slides.md} -- the JSRF-Decompilation
author's own walkthrough of the exec phase. Two passages matter.

  "with three methods, exec, postexec, and draw, for each of the five modes,
   there's a total of 15 virtual methods on the game object class. The modes
   are controlled by booleans on the game class, and while multiple modes can
   be set at once, only one actually has its methods run that frame, in
   accordance with some precedence rules."

  "...making everything stop during freeze cam moments, because most objects
   don't do anything in their freeze cam exec methods, SO THE PLAYER
   CHARACTER'S POSITION AND ANIMATION WON'T GET UPDATED, for example."

The second sentence describes our exact symptom, and the five modes are
coveredPause > Event (a cutscene, "called an event internally") > FreezeCam >
UncoveredPause > Default. The Corn tutorial is a cutscene.

### Tested, and the simple form is FALSE

CActMan +0x30..+0x9C, xemu vs recomp, both at the Corn dialogue
(`snap_corn_talk.bin` against `mgr_1.bin`):

  * the mode booleans +0x38..+0x48 are **all zero and identical on both sides**
  * `+0x94 m_DrawMode` 0 on both, `+0x74 m_bSkipDraw` 0 on both
  * the only differences are frame counters (+0x7C 0x3C vs 0x16, +0x84 0x8EEE
    vs 0x8EF0, +0x88 0x65 vs 0x66) and +0x98, the id-array base (different heap)

So both sides are in **Default** mode and the flags are not divergent. This
independently reconfirms the earlier session's "the Corn cutscene reads ALL
ZERO, identical to normal gameplay".

### What it reframes -- the right next measurement

The flags being equal does NOT mean the same virtual method runs. The
precedence rules select ONE of the 15 slots, and an earlier handover already
recorded the draw-side shape: "the object vtable dispatch uses +24/+18/+30/+3C/
+0C according to manager +40/+44/+48/+4C, in that precedence". If our
*selection* lands on a different slot despite identical flags -- a dispatch
index bug rather than a state bug -- the object would be walked, would pass
every filter, and would run a method that does nothing. That is consistent with
EVERY measurement so far: identical object state, identical draw lists,
identical flags, and no animation.

**So: instrument the exec dispatch and record WHICH virtual slot is invoked on
CPlayer id 45 per frame, in the tutorial versus in gameplay.** Same binary, one
object, and the answer is a small integer. If the slot differs between the two
scenes while the mode flags are identical, the precedence computation is the
bug. If the slot is the same, mode selection is exonerated entirely and the
difference is inside the method.

This is a better-posed question than the 545-site entry differential, and it
supersedes it: the entry differential asks "which function stopped being
called", this asks "which function was called instead", which is the same
information with a hundredth of the noise.


22. EXEC-MODE MEASUREMENT (partial) AND THE STALL AS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The five mode walkers are NAMED in the decompilation's symboltable.tsv, so the
active mode can be counted directly instead of inferred from flags:

    0x00011070 CActBase::recursiveExec0Default
    0x000112A0 CActBase::recursiveExec0Event
    0x000114D0 CActBase::recursiveExec0CoveredPause
    0x00011700 CActBase::recursiveExec0FreezeCam
    0x00011930 CActBase::recursiveExec0UncoveredPause
    0x00011D00..0x00011F80  the recursiveExec1* (postexec) set
```
