```txt
    0x000123E0 CActMan::ActionExec (the driver)

### Measured

  GAMEPLAY:   Exec0Default 33916, Exec1Default 33917, ActionExec 3028
              **every other walker: never called**
  NEW GAME MENU: Exec0Default 10020, Exec1Default 10000, others never called

So Default mode runs exclusively in both, and flags -> walker correspondence is
confirmed (the flags were all zero in both).

### The tutorial half is STILL UNMEASURED

Three consecutive real-pad runs were lost to the poll stall. Strong inference,
NOT measurement: the CActMan mode booleans at the Corn tutorial are all zero and
byte-identical to xemu (section 21), and all-zero demonstrably selects Default
in two other scenes -- so the tutorial almost certainly runs Default too, which
would EXONERATE mode selection entirely and place the fault inside the Default
exec method for CPlayer id 45. **Confirm it before relying on it.**

### The stall is now the binding constraint

Rate, correctly filtered: most "stalled" rows in a naive survey are FAKE_PAD
runs, where the real poll counter legitimately does not climb because the fake
pad substitutes. Among REAL-pad runs it is roughly **4 failures in 14**, and it
landed on three in a row here.

Its user-visible effect is exactly "the game stops responding": the guest ceases
calling the pad read, so the menu or tutorial ignores input. That is why a run
looks like a dead controller.

**Sampled live while stalled** (new evidence): the guest is NOT spinning in a
tight loop and is NOT blocked. It runs the whole frame loop -- `recursiveExec0Default`
(0x00011070) appears in the sample -- while never reaching the pad read. Hot
frames: `sub_0013B180` (hottest, unnamed), `XapiThreadStartup` (0x00147EBB),
and a spread across 0x0019xxxx-0x001Axxxx (XDK/CRT, unnamed in the decomp).
This refines the older note that it "spins in guest code": it does not spin, it
simply stops taking the branch that polls.

Next for the stall: `xbox_InputGetState` (src/input/xinput_device.c:301) is the
host function that increments the counter. Record the GUEST RETURN ADDRESS on
every call; when the count flatlines, the last caller is known, and its callers
can then be armed with the O(1) probe to find which one stopped running. That
is a small, targeted change and it is the first approach that does not depend
on RECOMP_MEM_WATCH (unusable) or on catching the stall by luck.


23. THE PAD-POLL STALL: MECHANISM FOUND AND A FIX UNDER TEST
--------------------------------------------------------------
### It reproduces WITHOUT a human -- the key that unlocked it

`RECOMP_FAKE_PAD` does NOT bypass the USB path. `g_pad_polls++` is at
`xinput_device.c:305`, and the fake-pad branch is at :307, i.e. AFTER the
counter. The counter is reached only from `usb_gamepad_report()`
(`src/usb/usb_gamepad.c:168`), which runs when the guest requests a report over
USB. **So flat `polls` in a FAKE_PAD run is the same stall**, not an artefact.
Six such rows were dismissed as "expected" earlier in this session; that was
wrong, and correcting it made the bug reproducible on demand for the first time
in five sessions. It reproduced unattended on the first attempt (flat at 957).

### The mechanism

With `RECOMP_OHCI_TRACE`, at the stall:

    OHCI register writes stop dead at log line 1702; the stall begins at 1909;
    the log runs to 11389 with NO further OHCI write of any kind.

The last writes are a truncated service cycle:

    #397 HcCommandStatus    <= 0x00000006   ControlListFilled|BulkListFilled
    #398 HcInterruptEnable  <= 0x80000000   MIE on
    #399 HcInterruptDisable <= 0x80000000   MIE off
    #400 HcInterruptStatus  <= 0x00000002   ack WritebackDoneHead
         ... nothing, ever again

**`ohci_raise()` was edge triggered.** It sets the status bit and then returns
early when `!(enable & INTR_MIE)` -- without calling the ISR. `case
HcInterruptEnable:` merely OR'd the mask and returned, re-evaluating nothing.
Real OHCI is LEVEL triggered: a pending status bit re-asserts the line the
moment the driver unmasks it.

So: the driver masks MIE for the length of its ISR; a transfer completes inside
that window; WDH is recorded but never delivered; the driver unmasks and waits
for an interrupt that has already happened; it never refills the schedule; the
gamepad's interrupt endpoint is never polled again. Intermittent precisely
because it needs a completion to land inside the mask window.

### The fix (src/usb/ohci.c)

`ohci_deliver_pending()` -- deliver any interrupt that is pending AND now
unmasked -- called from the `HcInterruptEnable` write (the mask just changed)
and from the `HcInterruptStatus` ack (a second source may have arrived while
the first was being serviced). Kept separate from `ohci_raise()` because the
triggers differ; neither may call the ISR while MIE is clear.

### THE FIX IS NOT CONFIRMED -- three runs, one pass, two failures

    baseline (no fix):        flat at polls=957 after 4 reports
    run 1, both paths hooked: polls 3632 -> 9825 over 8 reports, no stall
    run 2, both paths hooked: polls=0 for the WHOLE run -- never polled
    run 3, unmask path only:  climbed to 3117 then FLATLINED (stalled later,
                              not eliminated)

**So the fix does not reliably remove the stall.** Run 2's total failure was
plausibly self-inflicted: `ohci_deliver_pending()` was also called from the
`HcInterruptStatus` ack, and that write happens INSIDE the driver's ISR, so it
re-entered the ISR. That call has been removed; only the `HcInterruptEnable`
(unmask) trigger remains, which is the one the trace actually justifies.
Run 3 still stalled, so either there is a second cause or the level-triggered
delivery is implemented incompletely.

Beware a crude pass/fail test: comparing only first vs last poll count called
run 3 "OK" when its last three reports were identical. **Check the TAIL for a
flatline, not the endpoints.**

Note also that `grep -c OHCI-W` reads 400 in both stalled and healthy runs --
that is a trace cap, not a signal; do not use it as one.

### What is still solid, regardless of the fix

  * The stall reproduces UNATTENDED under RECOMP_FAKE_PAD (the counter sits
    before the fake-pad branch, so the fake pad does not bypass the USB path).
    That alone converts this from a bug caught by luck into one that can be
    iterated on, and it is the most useful thing learned about it in five
    sessions.
  * At the stall the guest stops writing OHCI registers ENTIRELY, mid service
    cycle, after an ack with MIE masked -- and never writes another.
  * `ohci_raise()` genuinely is edge triggered and genuinely drops interrupts
    raised while masked; real OHCI is level triggered. That is a real defect
    whether or not it is THE defect here.

### Next for the stall

Instrument rather than patch: log every ohci_raise() that returns early because
the source was masked, with the source bits and the current mask. If the stall
is preceded by a dropped WDH, the mechanism is confirmed and the fix is merely
wrong in its details. If no raise is dropped before the stall, the level-trigger
theory is dead and the guest is stopping for another reason.


24. THE STALL: BOTH INTERRUPT THEORIES DEAD, AND WHY
-----------------------------------------------------
Instrumented rather than patched further (`RECOMP_OHCI_DROP_TRACE`, opt-in,
read-only, in `ohci_raise`): a counter for raises that reach no ISR, and -- the
part that mattered -- a POSITIVE CONTROL counting raises that do.

    stalled run (polls flat at 1767):  OHCI-RAISE 0   OHCI-DROP 0
    healthy run (polls -> 14329, reached gameplay):  OHCI-RAISE 0   OHCI-DROP 0

**`ohci_raise()` is never called at all, in healthy and stalled runs alike.**
No interrupt is ever dropped because none is ever raised. The positive control
is what makes that readable: without it, "0 drops" would have been filed as
"no masking race", which is the opposite of the truth.

Dead as a result:
  * the level-trigger theory (nothing is dropped);
  * the worker-exit theory -- the "delivered 200 times ... stopping" guard has
    never fired in any run, and no `[OHCI0]` message appears at all, including
    the "operational ... device arriving on port 1" line. The interrupt worker
    never reaches the operational state in ANY run, healthy or not.

So the gamepad is polled entirely through the guest kicking the schedule
itself (`usb_gamepad_report` at ohci.c:427, reached from TD processing), and
the interrupt path is unused end to end. **The stall is the guest ceasing to
drive the schedule, not a missed interrupt.**

The level-triggered delivery was written, tested and then REVERTED: it did not
fix the stall, one run carrying it never polled at all, and the measurement
above shows it addresses a path that never executes. What remains in the file
is the opt-in tracing only (+83 lines, no behavioural change). Re-adding
level-triggered delivery would be defensible correctness work, but it must not
be described as a fix for this.

### Where the stall investigation actually got to

  * It REPRODUCES UNATTENDED under RECOMP_FAKE_PAD -- the counter sits before
    the fake-pad branch, so the fake pad does not bypass the USB path. This is
    the single most useful thing learned about it in five sessions: it is now
    iterable without a human, at roughly a 50% hit rate per run.
  * At the stall the guest stops writing OHCI registers entirely, mid service
    cycle, and never writes another.
  * A live sample shows the guest still running its whole frame loop
    (recursiveExec0Default appears) -- it is not spinning and not blocked, it
    simply stops taking the branch that drives USB.

### Next for the stall

The question is now guest-side: what stops calling the USB service path? Since
it reproduces unattended, arm the O(1) probe on the guest functions around the
last OHCI register write and bisect upward -- the same differential method that
worked for the animation thread, now affordable because no human is needed per
iteration.


25. PLAN (11 Sep, after both interrupt theories died)
------------------------------------------------------
Two independent faults remain. **Do the stall first** -- not because it is more
important, but because it is now the only one that can be iterated without a
human, and it is what costs a tutorial run its value.

## THREAD B -- the pad-poll stall (unattended, do this first)

  B1. PUT A GUEST PC ON THE OHCI REGISTER TRACE.
      `[OHCI-W]` already logs every register write. The MMIO handler runs on
      the guest thread, so the guest PC / return address is available there.
      Add it. At the stall the LAST write then names the exact guest code that
      was driving USB, instead of only naming the register.
      One line of instrumentation; reproduces unattended at ~50% per run.

  B2. BISECT UPWARD FROM THAT PC with the O(1) probe.
      Arm the containing function and its callers with `--ecxpair VA:0`,
      reproduce, and find which one stops being entered. This is the same
      differential that worked on the animation thread, and it is affordable
      now only because no human is needed per iteration.

  B3. Compare the answer against xemu's behaviour at the same moment if it is
      still ambiguous. xemu drives the same guest driver, so "which function
      stops" has a ground truth.

  What NOT to do: anything in the interrupt path. `ohci_raise()` is never
  called in healthy or stalled runs (section 24), the worker never reaches
  operational in either, and the level-triggered change was tried and reverted.

## THREAD A -- id 45's missing animation writes (needs a human per run)

  A1. CONFIRM THE TUTORIAL RUNS Exec0Default. Gameplay and the new-game menu
      both run Default exclusively (33916 / 10020 calls, every other walker
      zero). The tutorial's mode booleans are byte-identical to xemu's and
      all-zero, which selects Default elsewhere -- so this is strong inference
      but NOT measured. One run with the twelve exec-mode counters settles it.
      If Default runs, mode selection is exonerated and the fault is inside the
      Default exec method for id 45.

  A2. FIND THE WRITER of id 45's +0xCE0..+0xDE4 (66 dwords), +0x12C0..+0x140C
      (4 x 15) and the 3-dword vector groups. Constraints already established:
      static grep cannot see it (block copy / indexed loop); xemu watchpoints
      do not trap it; RECOMP_MEM_WATCH cannot run. So: the widened O(1) entry
      differential, gameplay vs tutorial, same binary, filtered to calls whose
      `this` is id 45. The 545-site band 0x90000-0xAFFFF is already installed
      and its gameplay half is captured
      (`render-investigation/cplayer_functions_gameplay.txt`, 176 of 550 ran).
      Only the tutorial half is missing.

  A3. Do NOT chase: id 44 (static by design in xemu too), +0x11C (a mutable
      state index, not identity), the descriptor path, +0xE54, the low 2.5 KB
      region, or the four-candidate setter shortlist. All measured dead.

## THREAD C -- infrastructure, if either thread drags

  xemu save states (`-monitor unix:/tmp/xemu-mon,server,nowait` + savevm/loadvm)
  and scripted pad input. Around twenty playthroughs have gone into this
  investigation; A1 and A2 each cost one, and B now costs none.

## Sequencing

  B1+B2 unattended -> if the stall is fixed, A1 and A2 become reliable, and
  they are then two runs rather than two runs plus however many the stall eats.


26. THE "PAD-POLL STALL" IS THE GAME BEING PAUSED
---------------------------------------------------
Caught by SAMPLING, not instrumentation -- necessarily, because the probe set
needed to observe the stall is heavy enough to precipitate it (1118 sites froze
it at 30 polls, 578 sites at 253; the same build with no probes ran to 8790).
A sampling profiler has no per-call cost, so it is the only unperturbed
observer available for this bug.

One run, two samples, zero instrumentation:

    healthy (polls=1166): sub_00011070 and sub_00011D00 present
    stalled (polls=8790): both ABSENT; sub_000114D0 present, 13 samples

From the decompilation's symbol table:

    0x00011070  CActBase::recursiveExec0Default        <- healthy only
    0x00011D00  CActBase::recursiveExec1Default        <- healthy only
    0x000114D0  CActBase::recursiveExec0CoveredPause   <- STALLED only

Read live from the stalled process:

    CActMan +0x3C = 1      +0x40 = 1

and an earlier handover already recorded "Pause sets +0x3C and +0x40 to 1".

**So the guest is in COVERED PAUSE.** It is not stalled, not deadlocked and not
missing an interrupt: it is paused, and in covered-pause mode most objects do
nothing by design -- which is exactly why the pad stops being polled, the
characters stop moving and the title looks hung. The video says this outright:
"making everything stop ... so the player character's position and animation
won't get updated".

### The unattended reproduction was self-inflicted

`RECOMP_FAKE_PAD` "pulses A and START for 150 ms once a second"
(src/input/xinput_device.c, its own comment). **START opens the pause menu.**
So every FAKE_PAD run that "stalled" was the fake pad pausing the game, and the
delighted claim in section 23 that the stall "reproduces unattended" is wrong:
what reproduces unattended is a synthetic START press.

This invalidates, as evidence about the stall:
  * "it reproduces unattended at ~50% per run" (section 23/24) -- that was
    START being pressed, not a bug;
  * the FAKE_PAD rows in the poll-rate survey (section 22) -- already flagged
    as suspect there for the wrong reason;
  * "OHCI-RAISE 0 in healthy AND stalled runs" remains TRUE and still kills the
    interrupt theories, but the "stalled" run in that comparison was a paused
    run, so it says less than it appeared to.

### What is still genuinely open

Whether the REAL-pad stalls are the same thing. Four of ~14 real-pad runs
flatlined, and the user was not knowingly pausing. Two possibilities:
  a) a stray START reaches the guest (a controller mapping or a spurious USB
     report) -- check `+0x3C`/`+0x40` the moment a real-pad run flatlines;
  b) something else sets the pause booleans.
Either way the question is now "what sets +0x3C/+0x40", not "what breaks USB".

### Method note, fourth occurrence

An unattended reproduction that is produced BY the harness is not a
reproduction of the bug. The fake pad's own comment said it presses START; that
was read in section 11 and its consequence not followed through.


27. TWO PHENOMENA, NOW SEPARABLE IN ONE LINE
----------------------------------------------
Two harness changes, both small, both aimed at never repeating section 26's
misdiagnosis.

  A1  `RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=a` (or `=noStart`) presses A WITHOUT START.
      The default is unchanged (A+START) so older notes still apply. START
      opens the pause menu, so any unattended run that must keep running needs
      this form. src/input/xinput_device.c.

  A2  `[JSRF-PAUSE] +3C=.. +40=..` printed every report, with an explicit
      "<== PAUSED (covered pause)" when both are set.
      diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/main.c.

### And they immediately separated two different failures

First run with `RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=a`:

    polls = 0 for the whole run   -- the guest never requested a USB report
    +3C = 0, +40 = 0              -- NOT paused
    scene reached live=141        -- a scene loaded regardless

So there are at least TWO things that have been reported as "controller not
working", and they are now distinguishable at a glance:

  (1) PAUSE. `polls` stops climbing, +3C/+40 = 1, recursiveExec0CoveredPause
      runs instead of Default. Caused by a START press -- synthetic in every
      FAKE_PAD run to date. **Not a bug.**

  (2) polls = 0. The guest never polls at all and is NOT paused. A genuine
      defect, and the one worth chasing. Note the title still advances through
      menus and loads a scene without any input, which is why it can look like
      it is "working" while ignoring the pad entirely.

Every prior "stall" observation in this document needs re-reading against that
split. The real-pad flatlines (4 of ~14) were never checked for pause state and
could be either.

### Next

  * Re-run the real-pad case with A2 live: one look at [JSRF-PAUSE] when it
    flatlines says which of (1) or (2) it is. No new tooling.
  * For (2): the guest reaches a scene without ever polling, so the question is
    what normally starts the poll loop and why it never starts. Sampling is the
    right observer (the probe set needed to watch it precipitates failures --
    1118 sites froze a run at 30 polls, 578 at 253, zero probes ran to 8790).
  * The animation thread (id 45's missing +0xCE0 writes) is untouched by any of
    this and remains the actual objective.


28. THE GENUINE INPUT BUG, ISOLATED AND REPRODUCIBLE UNATTENDED
----------------------------------------------------------------
### The fake pad now boots the game without pausing it

The game needs START to get past "Press Start" and through the menus, so a pad
that never sends START cannot reach gameplay at all -- `RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=a` is
useless for that and the first attempt at a fix was wrong. START is also the
PAUSE button. Resolved by making it a time window:

    RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1        START for the first 90 s, then A only   [default]
    RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=<n>      as above with an n-second window
    RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=a        never send START
    RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=always   old behaviour -- always START, and it WILL pause

The chosen mode is announced at startup (`[PAD] fake pad: ...`).

### With that, the real bug reproduces unattended and is unambiguous

    [PAD] fake pad: START for the opening window only
    polls climbed to 1220   -- so START worked and the game started
    then flat at 1220 for five reports
    [JSRF-PAUSE] +3C=00000000 +40=00000000   -- NOT paused
    scene live=145

Sampled at that moment (no instrumentation, so no perturbation):

    recursiveExec0Default  15 samples   } running normally
    recursiveExec1Default  12 samples   }
    Event / CoveredPause / FreezeCam / UncoveredPause   0 samples

**So the guest is in Default mode, executing its frame loop, and simply stops
requesting USB reports.** Not paused, not deadlocked, not in a cutscene mode.

Top guest frames at the stall:

    sub_0005E9B0 55   sub_00191440 48   sub_000B3E10 46   sub_001993A0 45
    sub_000163D0 26   sub_00159650 24   sub_00191530 21   sub_00047690 20

`sub_000163D0` matches the frame recorded in
[[jsrf-corn-tutorial-input-poll-stall]] from an earlier session, so this is the
same long-standing bug, now with a clean unattended reproduction and the pause
confound removed.

### Next

Take a HEALTHY sample and a STALLED sample in the same run (the sampler script
does this) and diff the frame sets, exactly as section 26 did -- but now the
"stalled" side is the genuine bug rather than a paused game. The frames present
when healthy and absent when stalled are the poll path that stops. Sampling is
mandatory here: 1118 probe sites froze a run at 30 polls, 578 at 253, and zero
probes ran to 8790.

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-10_XEMU_REFERENCE.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER — THE xemu REFERENCE, AND EIGHT HYPOTHESES IT KILLED
Date: 2026-09-10 (Europe/London)
From: Claude

PURPOSE
=======
This session built a ground-truth reference rig against xemu and pointed it at
the recomp. The headline is not a fix. It is that the audio investigation is
closed, and that eight renderer hypotheses -- several of them mine, stated with
more confidence than they deserved -- died on measurement without a single line
being patched around them.

Read the "WHAT NOT TO RE-DERIVE" section before forming a theory. Most of the
obvious ones are already spent.


THE RIG
=======
xemu 0.8.136 is configured for the *US* ISO, the same title we target, so it is
a legitimate oracle. Three instruments, none requiring changes to the host:

  Audio, sample-exact:
    SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER=disk
    SDL_AUDIO_DISK_OUTPUT_FILE=<path>
    SDL_AUDIO_DISK_TIMESCALE=1
  Writes raw S16LE / 48000 / stereo straight from the APU. TIMESCALE is a
  direct multiplier, NOT a percentage: the plausible-looking 100 runs it ~100x
  too slowly. This takes audio off the speakers for that run.
  `-audiodev wav` does NOT work -- xemu exits with "no default audio driver
  available", because APU output goes through SDL, not QEMU audiodev.

  Method traces, gated:
    -monitor unix:/tmp/xemu-mon,server,nowait
    printf 'trace-event nv2a_pgraph_method on\n' | nc -U /tmp/xemu-mon
  Two seconds is 40 MB / 544k methods. Leaving it on from boot is ~10 GB, so
  gate it at the monitor rather than at launch. Same for mcpx_apu_method.

  Live state diff:
    scratchpad/mode_finder.py -- snapshot the game object over the GDB stub
    (-s, port 1234) in two states, filter noise with a same-state pair.
  6 noisy dwords out of 8704 across a state change. Excellent signal. This is
  the most reusable thing built today.

Video capture is `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -i "3:"`. Wrap xemu AND ffmpeg in
`caffeinate -dimsu` or the Mac locks mid-run and wastes the take.


REFERENCE NUMBERS (US ISO)
==========================
Boot -> title:
  chime 0.5-8.5 s; then EXACTLY 40 s of all-zero samples; music from 49.3 s,
  sustained. RMS ~-21 dBFS, peak ~10100/32767 (~-10 dBFS). JSRF's mix sits
  about 10 dB below full scale -- worth knowing before "our audio is quiet".
  12 voices, handles 0x40-0x4B.

Voice lifecycle, and it is scene-dependent -- do not generalise either row:
                 VOICE_ON  VOICE_OFF  VOICE_RELEASE  SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE  handles
  boot -> title       40          3            72                59   0x40-0x4B
  gameplay            61         60             0                61   0-10,68-70

Draw rates, both counting one per BEGIN_END pair:
  xemu, tutorial start          102 draws/frame   strip 2002 fan 425 quad 24
  xemu, past the Corn cutscene  150 draws/frame   strip 2739 fan 420
  ours, stuck tutorial          200 draws/frame
xemu itself swings 102 -> 150 between two scenes of one level, so our 200 is
inside scene variance. There is NO established draw-rate divergence.


WHAT WAS SETTLED
================
The audio investigation is closed. Commit bc4a9b5 deferred its real test to
gameplay, where one-shot voices retire. Measured there:

  [APU-VOICE] on=13 off=8 release=0 idle_trap=11 fe_methods=17613
              set_current_voice=5633

idle_trap is 11, not 0 -- the trap fires. release=0 beside off=8 matches xemu's
gameplay profile exactly (xemu: 0 releases, 60 offs). set_current_voice=5633
against xemu's 8608 is the same order of magnitude. An earlier reading of 12
that looked like a three-orders-of-magnitude routing gap was a title-screen
artifact and nothing more.

One real change is in the tree (src/apu/apu_vp.c, uncommitted): a
g_apu_voice_release_count, incremented in NV1BA0_PIO_VOICE_RELEASE and reported
as release=. It exists because off= increments only inside voice_off(), which is
reachable only from VOICE_OFF, and at boot/title JSRF releases 72 voices against
3 offs. off=0 would have read identically had all 72 been released. Built clean,
27/27 ctest.


WHAT NOT TO RE-DERIVE
=====================
Each of these was proposed, tested, and killed. None was patched around.

  APU/audio front end broken
    -> idle_trap=11, off=8, release=0 at gameplay, matching xemu.

  The executor discards transform and texture state
    -> WRONG, and this one is a trap worth naming. The executor's "unhandled"
       list shows SET_MODEL_VIEW_MATRIX and SET_TEXTURE_OFFSET/FORMAT with
       hundreds of thousands of hits. But nv2a_pb_exec.c:1729 stores EVERY
       aligned method below 0x2000 into s_methods[] *before* the switch runs,
       and s_methods[] is exactly what nv2a_ff_vertex() and
       nv2a_texture_copy_prepare() read. note_unhandled() only counts; it is a
       label meaning "no explicit case", not "dropped". CLAUDE.md already warns
       about the D3D11 sink's method list. The executor's list is the same trap
       wearing a different hat. The tell was that textures visibly work.

  A corrupted matrix in guest RAM
    -> RECOMP_FIND_NAN reports "none in RAM" at every scan. Its own message is
       the useful part: the NaNs are computed into registers, not stored.

  Entities destroyed / Corn's object killed
    -> 67 live registered, 67 walked, ZERO marked dead, at the frozen tutorial.

  Geometry culled by us
    -> 0 batches skipped as not screen-space, 0 triangles fully off-surface.

  Batches rejected wholesale
    -> 640 rejects out of 665738 batches (0.1%).

  A missing depth clear (xemu clears 2x/frame, we count 1)
    -> counter artifact. clear_surface() performs the Z clear at
       nv2a_pb_exec.c:845-851, BEFORE the early return at :854 that skips only
       the colour fill and the s_gpu.clears++ increment. Behaviour correct.

  Cutscenes never enter "event" mode, so event-mode draw methods never run
    -> FALSIFIED by positive control. Diffed the game object across three
       states in xemu. Pause sets +0x3C and +0x40 to 1 -- so the offsets, the
       object and the method are all sound. The Corn cutscene reads ALL ZERO,
       identical to normal gameplay. Cutscenes are not driven through the mode
       booleans, and all-zero is the NORMAL reading, not a symptom.

That last one deserves a note. docs and memory have recorded the mode flags as
"all zero for the whole boot" since 2026-09-04, phrased in a way that invites
suspicion. That phrasing is what cost a session's hypothesis. All-zero is
correct outside of pause.


COUNTERS IN THIS TREE THAT LIE
==============================
Four found misleading in one day. Read a counter's trigger before its value.

  off=            blind to VOICE_RELEASE (now paired with release=)
  [PUSHER] draws= always 0 by construction (already in CLAUDE.md)
  [GPU] unhandled= "no explicit case", not "value dropped"
  [FB] sum=/same   probes a fixed address; reads a retired surface as all-zero
                   while the live surface has moved (double buffering)
  [GPU] clears=    does not count depth-only clears


THE FOUR USER-VISIBLE FAULTS, WITH WHAT IS KNOWN
================================================
1. Intro title cards: wrong colour, no fade in/out.
   The architecture video describes this exact draw path and it is small: the
   opening object "paints the whole screen in appropriate color, black or
   white, sets the active texture to whatever logo or legal notice is supposed
   to be on screen, and renders it". A fullscreen quad plus a texture plus an
   alpha ramp. Both symptoms -- wrong colour AND absent fade -- are consistent
   with one blend/alpha fault. We hold exact reference frames for every card in
   scratchpad/xemu_ref/run3/reference_av.mp4.

2. Playback speed slow.
   Ours measured 15.2 fps at the tutorial (152 flips / 10 s). JSRF targets 30,
   so roughly half speed. NOTE: the xemu figures of 10.5-12 fps in this document
   were taken while the pgraph trace or the GDB stub was active and are NOT a
   fair baseline for xemu's true speed. Take a clean xemu fps measurement before
   concluding anything about relative performance.
   The APU thread is not the bottleneck: elapsed=740.3s slept=738.1s.

3. Sound glitchy and choppy. This is measured and it is a delivery fault, not
   a mixing fault:
     [APU-SDL2] max_submit_gap=71.0 ms gaps_over_cushion=22
     [APU-PACE] starved=15 empty=5 min_queued=0 bytes (0.0 ms)
     [APU-SDL2] depth buckets: 0=5 <1=10 1-2=89 2-4=38393 4-8=98375 8+=1838
   The queue ran completely dry 5 times and 22 submit gaps exceeded the
   cushion, the worst at 71 ms. Generation is fine -- gen_hz=47983 against a
   48000 target. So the mixer produces correct audio at the correct rate and
   then fails to hand it over on time. That is a scheduling problem, and it is
   very likely the same stall that costs the frame rate in (2).

4. Tutorial does not render or work properly: no player, Corn vanishes, text
   glitchy. Everything in WHAT NOT TO RE-DERIVE was aimed at this and missed.


THE STRONGEST UNTESTED LEAD
===========================
From the decompilation author's architecture video:

  "There are a few other trees on linked lists used by the draw phase as well,
   not to mention every game object has a few flags that determine how it's
   used in the draw phase."

The 67-node walk that found zero dead objects traversed the EXEC tree. The draw
phase uses different structures, and nobody has looked at them. A character can
be perfectly alive in the exec tree and absent from the draw lists, which would
present exactly as observed: world renders, characters do not, nothing is
culled, nothing is rejected, every method arrives.

mode_finder.py is the tool: diff the game object between a frame where a
character is visible and one where it is not.


SUGGESTED ORDER
===============
Take (1) first. It is isolated, its draw path is documented, it is reproducible
without reaching gameplay, and we hold frame-exact reference for it. A blend or
alpha fault found there plausibly explains the glitchy tutorial text too, and it
is the only one of the four that can be iterated in ten-second runs.

Then (3), because it is measured, bounded, and probably shares a root cause with
(2). Then (2) with a clean xemu baseline. Then (4), via the draw-phase trees.


NOT DONE
========
  - No fix was implemented for any of the four faults.
  - No commit was created; four files are modified in the working tree
    (main.c, apu_core.c, apu_sdl2.c from earlier sessions; apu_vp.c from this
    one).
  - No generated code was regenerated; the verified archived gen was used
    throughout (hashes checked against RESTORE_MANIFEST.txt).
  - The 449 "oPos is not finite" batch rejects, a count that climbs steadily
    through a run, remain unexplained. Too few to hide the characters, but real.
```

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE WINDOWS CRASH, ROOT-CAUSED
Date: 2026-09-11 (Europe/London), late night
From: Claude.

Supersedes the Windows sections of JSRF_PLAN_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_GRAPHICS.md,
which is retracted at the top of its own file, and every account of the
0xFFFFFF00 crash written earlier today.


0. THE ONE-LINE VERSION
=======================
0xFFFFFF00 is a cleared Z24S8 depth pixel. Our own NV2A executor was painting
1.2 MB of it over the title's .data on every clear, because the depth surface
resolves to guest 0x00248000 -- inside the loaded image. Windows no longer
crashes. The surface ADDRESS is still wrong and that is the open work.


1. WHAT LANDED (all committed, tree clean)
==========================================
  2e0e921  nv2a_range_hits_image: refuse surface writes over the image
  0a9ef37  restore the documented ICALL caller + ring logging
  e74721e  instrument_block_writes.py + recomp_mem_watch_guest_block
  87f82d4  stop the missing-bridge warning accusing void functions
  79b5821  point the .text checksum probe at real .text
  dafa70c  PGRAPH software-method notify on Windows (guard, raise, handler)
  db7d9e4  KeConnectInterrupt race fix + RECOMP_TEXT_CHECKSUM
  a8afcf5  read the two D3D allocators

Instruments now available, all opt-in:
  RECOMP_STORE_WATCH=<va>:<len>   host page guard, reports the faulting HOST PC
  RECOMP_MEM_WATCH=<va>:<len>     guest macro stores (79,114 of them)
  RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH=<va>        samples either side of every bridge call
  RECOMP_TEXT_CHECKSUM=1          .text pages, ring window + control half
  RECOMP_DUMP_VA=<va>[,<va>...]   guest dwords once, at load
  RECOMP_D3D_ALLOC_TRACE=1        the two contiguous allocators, path probe
  RECOMP_PB_NOTIFY_TRACE=1        software methods the parser decodes
  instrument_block_writes.py      1571 lifted rep movs/stos, into a gen COPY
  instrument_d3d_alloc.py         12 sites down both D3D allocators

Symbolising a Windows crash: the mingw .exe keeps symbols and is based at
0x140000000, so
    x86_64-w64-mingw32-addr2line -f -e jsrf_first_fault.exe <rip>
resolves any frame from Wine's backtrace or from a STORE-WATCH host_pc. Saved
Wine reports are in docs/jsrf/artifacts/.


2. STATE OF THE TWO HOSTS
=========================
macOS   unchanged throughout. 2.7M pusher methods, ~1880 flips, 61.8 Hz,
        notifies completing, zero image refusals, ctest 21/27 (the five
        backport-presence failures and the ratchet this gen has always had).

Windows boots, all four vectors, APU + ADX, PGRAPH notifies raised AND
        acknowledged, no crash, runs minutes instead of dying inside 60s.
        Renders nothing yet, and never will until it has a framebuffer path --
        xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource and the event-pump hook are still
        POSIX-only in main.c, so the CrossOver window is black by construction.
        Judge it by counters.

Current Windows boundary: a PGRAPH software method with parameter=2 is raised
and never acknowledged --
    [PB-NOTIFY] waiting parameter=2 raised=1 pmc=00001000 intr=00100000 fifo=00000000
so PGRAPH_ERROR is set, PMC's PGRAPH bit is set, and the guest has not restored
FIFO access. parameter=9 notifies complete normally, six of them. That asymmetry
is the next thread to pull.


3. THE OPEN ROOT CAUSE
======================
Three symptoms, one shape: this host hands the title addresses that collide
with its own image.

    depth surface   guest 0x00248000, 0x12C000 bytes   (inside .data)
    framebuffer     fb=0x001B2000 vs macOS 0x0071E000  (inside DSOUND)
    push ring       physical 0x1000 vs macOS 0x56D000  (would be .text)

The D3D contiguous allocators are NOT the cause -- measured identical on both
hosts, same sizes, same descriptors, same thunk, zero failures either side
(CLAUDE_PROGRESS_2026-09-11_ALLOCATORS_EXONERATED.md). So the divergence is
downstream of them, in whatever computes surface and ring addresses from what
those allocations returned. Start by logging the colour/depth surface offsets
and their DMA objects on both hosts and diffing; the REFUSED line already gives
the Windows half.


4. RULES THIS SESSION PAID FOR
==============================
  - A guarded page must not share a lock with a device handler. Sharing
    g_nv2a_pcrtc_lock stalled two runs, which reads as "the guard prevented the
    corruption" and means "the guard wedged the title".
  - Before believing a watch reported nothing, check the run reached the code
    that writes. Two zeroes here were runs that stopped early.
  - [HEAP] lines are capped at 64 (RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE). Counting them is not
    counting allocations; that is what made "ordinal 166 is never called on
    Windows" survive every test while being false.
  - g_xbox_code_lo..hi is NOT .text. This XBE flags .rdata and .data
    executable, so that range is mostly data; use g_xbox_text_lo/hi.
  - The memory watch sees only RECOMP_MEM_WRITE stores: not block copies (now
    separately instrumented), and not the runtime's own device writes, which is
    what this crash turned out to be.
  - docs/pipeline/06-debugging.md prescribes the ICALL caller address and the
    target ring for exactly this class of crash. Our build had dropped both.
    Consult the documented method before building a new instrument.


5. HYPOTHESES CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT -- DO NOT RE-RUN
====================================================
  .text corruption by the push ring (16/16 pages clean, both hosts, with the
    probe corrected to measure real .text)
  the KeConnectInterrupt race (fixed; crash unchanged)
  concurrent guest DPCs (interlock tried; crash unchanged; reverted)
  the OHCI memset(out,0xFF,len) (run without RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH; identical)
  unbridged ordinals leaking stack (1, 46 and 144 all have correct arg sizes;
    the warning that said otherwise was itself the bug)
  guest block copies (positive control passing, then zero hits)
  kernel bridge calls (RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH, zero hits)
  the D3D contiguous allocators (identical call for call on both hosts)
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_ORACLE.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE WINDOWS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE
Date: 2026-09-11 (Europe/London), afternoon/evening
From: Claude. Read alongside HANDOVER_TO_CODEX_2026-09-11_INPUT_AND_APU.txt,
      which this does not replace: that one is about input, this one is about
      building a second host to debug against.


0. THE STATE, IN ONE PARAGRAPH
==============================
There is now a Windows build of the JSRF harness. It cross-compiles with
mingw-w64, runs under CrossOver 25 on Apple Silicon, boots, loads the XBE,
brings up the kernel and APU, executes guest code, and delivers device
interrupts at 62 Hz. It does NOT reach the title: DirectSound init fails and
runs an error path, so the sound engine never starts and nothing downstream
does either. macOS remains the only build that plays. Four real bugs were found
and fixed getting this far, three of them in code shared with macOS. Everything
is uncommitted; both toolchains build clean; the macOS build is verified
unregressed at gameplay counters.


1. WHY BOTHER
=============
The premise was a differential oracle, not a second playable runtime: one
source tree, one gen tree, two hosts. A fault that reproduces on both is
guest-side (the recompiler, the device models); one that appears only on macOS
is in our Metal/SDL/AArch64 code. The macOS build had reached the point where
several open questions -- the input stall, the tutorial divergence -- could not
be told apart from runtime bugs by any single-host measurement.

That premise is why this was NOT forked into a Windows-only tree, and should
not be. The value of every comparison below rests on both binaries coming from
one tree and one gen. A fork makes every future difference ambiguous, and the
three shared-code bugs found here would have become Windows-local patches with
macOS keeping the latent versions.


2. THE FEASIBILITY GATE (scratchpad/wine-gate, preserved)
=========================================================
Two questions decided whether any of this was possible. Both were answered with
a 150-line test program before a line of the harness was built.

(a) Can the guest address space be mapped? Wine reserves the low address space:
    everything below 0x00800000 returns ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS, so the 1:1 map
    at XBOX_BASE_ADDRESS is impossible. It is also not required -- XBOX_PTR is
    (uint32_t)addr + g_xbox_mem_offset and the apertures are placed the same
    way, so the whole 4 GB guest space relocates as one block. Reserving 4 GB
    succeeds; the runtime later mapped guest RAM at 0x02000000 and ran.

(b) Does a guarded MMIO page still trap usefully under translation? YES, and
    this was the surprise. Faulting address exact, Rip readable, the x86-64
    store decoded (41 C7 04 24 EF BE AD DE = mov [r12], 0xDEADBEEF),
    EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION resumed correctly, and the guarded RAM did not
    take the store. No traps lost across four threads.

    Cost: 27.2 us per trapped store vs 3.5 us native, 7.8x. That sounds fatal
    and is not: the only recorded JSRF figure is 43,707 faults in a 45 s
    title-screen run, ~971/s, against 36,807/s sustained single-threaded under
    Wine. ~38x headroom, and it would survive gameplay trapping ten times
    harder than the title screen.

DO NOT re-measure these. They are settled.


3. WHAT THE PORT ACTUALLY COST
==============================
Far less than expected, and the surprise is where the work was.

  Generated C, 1,310,876 lines across 13 files:      0 errors.
  Runtime libraries, 49 files:                       3 errors in 2 files.
  Harness (main.c + 4 probes + recomp_manual.c):     4 errors in 1 file.

Every Windows import lib is present in mingw-w64 13.0.0 -- d3d11, dxgi, dxguid,
d3dcompiler, xinput, xaudio2_8, bcrypt, winmm, ole32, mfplat/mfreadwrite/
mfuuid/mf. There is no SEH anywhere (__try/__except appear only inside
comments). #pragma comment(lib,...) is ignored by GCC and CMake already links
those. The harness already carried an if(MINGW) block and GCC-style flags.

3,301 lines are POSIX-only and ALREADY excluded by CMake on Windows --
win32_compat.c (1653), d3d8_gl.c (1340), nv2a_metal.m (278), fb_window_stub.c
(30). A "Windows-only version" would delete code that never compiles anyway.

The blockers were not portability gaps. They were latent Windows-path bugs
introduced during macOS work: a duplicate TLS definition, a variable declared
inside a !_WIN32 guard and used outside it, two APU globals never added to the
Windows list, and -- the one that matters -- the [PAD-POLL] counters, which did
not exist on Windows AT ALL. A Windows build would have silently reported
polls=0, which is one of the two input failure signatures under investigation.
That is why they are wired to the real XInput path rather than stubbed: a
counter that cannot move is worse than no counter.


4. THE FOUR BUGS, AND WHAT THEY COST TO FIND
============================================
(a) GP/EP REGISTER BLOCKS HAD NO STORAGE.  apu_core.c's dispatch carried the
    comment "GP (0x30000) and EP (0x50000) regions ignored for now": writes
    dropped, reads returning 0. The guest brings the EP DSP out of reset with a
    READ-MODIFY-WRITE of EPRST at 0x5FFFC, so reading back 0 turned |= 1 into a
    write of 0 and the DSP stayed in reset. Storage already existed
    (d->gp.regs, d->ep.regs), simply unwired. After the fix Windows writes
    0x5FFFC = 1, byte-identical to macOS.

(b) INTERRUPT DELIVERY REQUIRED THE GUEST TO BLOCK.  bridge_device_irq_poll and
    its siblings had exactly one caller: inside the guest's blocking wait. That
    is enough for a guest that waits and nothing at all for a guest that SPINS,
    and JSRF's audio bring-up spins. RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD (opt-in, default off)
    runs the same three pumps on their own thread, the way ohci_thread already
    does. Deadlines went 0 -> 1865.

    It needs a guest stack: bridge_run_isr pushes onto g_esp without
    establishing one, because every previous caller already had the guest's.
    XBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT is 0 by default, so the build directory is
    configured with -DXBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT=4. That is a memory-layout change
    and is deliberately confined to the Windows build dir.

(c) PCRTC_INTR_0 HAD NO WRITE-1-TO-CLEAR ON WINDOWS.  NV_PCRTC_INTR_0 is
    write-1-to-clear in hardware, and the vblank handshake depends on it:
    bridge_vblank_poll will not raise another vblank while the last is pending,
    and the ISR clears pending by writing a 1. Against plain RAM that write
    SETS the bit. Measured: 1859 of 1865 deadlines skipped, nothing ever
    delivered. The VEH now guards that page and does the same work the AArch64
    trap does. Result: delivered=2797 at 62.3 Hz, unacked_skips=0.

    NOTE THE MISTAKE, it is the one this tree keeps paying for: the first
    version guarded the page but handled only ONE address on it, so the
    title's write to 0xFD600140 -- same page, different register -- fell
    through and killed the process. A page guard must complete every store on
    the page, not just the interesting one.

(d) Windows traps NV2A not at all otherwise. The VEH covers only
    0xFE800000..0xFE880000. src/nv2a/nv2a_mmio_hook.c contains a complete
    Windows VEH handler that is called from nothing but the README, and
    src/usb/ohci.c is dead code entirely -- the live controller is
    src/kernel/xbox_usb_ohci.c, which is why ohci.c can reference an
    xbox_AllocThreadTib that is defined nowhere and still link.


5. THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS EXPERIMENT
============================================
MACOS NEVER EXERCISES THE APU MODEL'S READ PATH.

The macOS trap protects the APU aperture PROT_READ, so only writes fault. Every
guest APU register read there is an ordinary load against the aperture RAM,
which the write handler stores through. The guest reads back only what it
itself wrote; mcpx_apu_read is never consulted. Windows is the first host ever
to reach it, and it failed on the second register it touched.

That is why Windows found (a) and macOS structurally could not. The model's
read side is unvalidated on the platform this effort has been debugging, and
that is worth knowing independently of whether the Windows build ever boots.


6. WHERE IT STOPS NOW, NAMED -- AND A RETRACTION OF THE FIRST ANSWER
====================================================================
Both hosts were run against the SAME gen tree, instrumented with
instrument_func_hit.py (no regeneration) on all 410 DSOUND-band functions. Only
2 of 410 skipped: sub_001A1769 and sub_001A308E, exactly the pair
jsrf_manual_overrides.c replaces -- confirmation the override path is live on
Windows too.

RETRACT THIS FIRST: an earlier pass reported "Windows enters 23 DSOUND
functions macOS never enters", and concluded the title was running an error /
cleanup path. THAT WAS AN ARTEFACT. The hit tables were extracted with `tail
-N`, which truncated the macOS table (245 functions) far more than the Windows
one (56). With the FULL tables there are ZERO Windows-only functions.

The corrected picture is simpler and much more useful:

    Windows executes a strict SUBSET of what macOS executes -- 56 of the
    245 DSOUND functions macOS reaches. It is not taking an error path.
    It stops partway through the same sequence.

Counting could not have shown that; it took ordering. func_hit_probe.c now
records the first 384 site entries in CALL ORDER (FUNC_SEQ_MAX / [FUNC-SEQ]),
and the two hosts line up exactly:

    185 calls byte-identical, then at call #186:
        MAC:  ... 001A1B7C -> 001A6D5C -> 001A1B7C -> 001A1BAF ...
        WIN:  ... 001A1B7C -> 001A72E0        (the ISR: the guest stopped)

So the guest stalls between the RETURN of call #185 and entry to sub_001A6D5C.

What those are:
  - sub_001A1B7C is a scoped IRQL raise, not a lock. It reads fs:[0x24],
    compares against DISPATCH_LEVEL, and if below it calls through the thunk
    at 0x1C40D4 -- which is kernel thunk slot 93, ordinal 160, KfRaiseIrql
    (read straight out of the XBE: .rdata VA 0x001C3F60 / raw 0x001B4000).
    Both hosts call it; fs:[0x24] reads 0 on both because our kernel keeps IRQL
    in g_current_irql and never writes the TIB field.
  - sub_001A6D5C calls sub_001A1B7C itself as its first action, which is why
    001A1B7C appears on both sides of it in the macOS order.

And the visible consequence, one line of the boot log apart:

    MAC: KeConnectInterrupt vector 3, vector 1, vector 6, vector 5
                                             (vector 5 routine = 0x001A2681)
    WIN: KeConnectInterrupt vector 3, vector 1, vector 6   -- and nothing more

macOS connects a FOURTH interrupt that Windows never reaches. That is
downstream of the stall, not its cause, but it is the cheapest one-line check
that a future fix has actually worked.

Separately and consistently: the 63 APU register writes Windows DOES make are
byte-identical to macOS's first 63, same registers, same values, differing only
in heap addresses. The recompiled guest is not host-sensitive here.


6c. THE ANSWER MOVED TWICE AS THE INSTRUMENT WIDENED -- READ THIS FIRST
=======================================================================
Section 6 above says the divergence is in DSOUND. THAT IS WRONG, and the way it
was wrong is the most useful thing in this file.

With only the 410 DSOUND functions armed, the first ordered divergence looked
like DSOUND. Arming the other SDK bands as well -- D3D (267), XPP (231),
MMATRIX (46), XGRPH (10), 554 more sites -- moved it EARLIER, into D3D. The
audio stall was downstream the whole time. An ordered divergence is only ever
as early as your instrumentation reaches; it is a CEILING on where the fault
is, never a location, until arming more sites stops moving it.

IT MOVED A THIRD TIME. Arming the render-state driver band as well (0x00150000
-0x00158000 plus the direct push-helper callers, 342 more sites) moved the
divergence from step 259 to step 150:

    both: ... 0019701F  001949E2  00197058  001945D6  0019701F  001912A0
    MAC :  00190F90      (the calibrated delay -- macOS polls)
    WIN :  00194480

Three widenings, three different answers -- DSOUND, then D3D step 259, then
step 150. Treat the number below as the best CEILING to date and nothing more.
The deciding code is still in uninstrumented game .text, which is 10,941
functions; the SDK bands and the render-state band together are under 1,000.

The step-259 comparison, superseded but kept because the shape is instructive:

    258 steps identical, then at step 259:
      both: ... 0018F010  0018E960  0018EB80  0018E960  0018EEF0  0018E960
      MAC :  0018EF40   then 0018E960 0018EFA0 0018E960 0018EC80 0018E960 ...
      WIN :  00194480   then 00192A80 0018F3B0 0018ED90 001919C0 ...

The alternating "setter, 0018E960, setter, 0018E960" is a D3D state-setting
loop -- 0018E960 sits beside sub_0018E930, the fastcall push primitive
CODEX_HANDOVER.txt section (x) documents, and 0018EB80 is the function func_id
identified as D3DDevice_SetFogState. macOS iterates further through that loop;
Windows leaves it early for 00194480. The next question is what ends the loop.

TWO ANALYSIS TRAPS, both of which produced a confident wrong answer here:

  - A positional diff of two call sequences is invalid when a poll takes a
    different number of spins. sub_00190F90 is a calibrated delay loop (load
    400, decrement, return); macOS calls it 5 times and Windows 28, and
    Windows then CONTINUES NORMALLY. That is a slower poll, not a stall, but
    it offsets everything after it and makes a positional diff report a false
    divergence 80 steps too early. Collapse consecutive repeats first.
  - The [FUNC-SEQ] ring is GLOBAL ACROSS THREADS. ISR entries interleave with
    the main thread, so 0x00193C50 (the vblank ISR) shows up mid-sequence and
    reads as a divergence when it is only the IRQ thread preempting. Filter
    the three ISR entry points -- 00193C50, 001A72E0, 001C288F -- before
    diffing. A per-thread ring would be better and is not written.

And the count comparison behind section 6 was ALSO wrong for a third reason:
the hit tables were extracted with `tail -N`, truncating macOS's 245-entry
table against Windows' 56. There are ZERO Windows-only functions; Windows
executes a strict SUBSET. Take the last contiguous run of [FUNC-HIT] lines,
never a fixed tail.


6b. WHAT THE CALLER HUNT ESTABLISHED (and three dead ends)
=========================================================
All the functions in question are reached through vtables; not one has a direct
caller in the generated C. DSOUND is COM-shaped, so static caller analysis
cannot bracket this. Do not repeat that search.

Three dead ends, recorded so they are not re-run:

  - fs:[0x24] (IRQL) reads 0 on BOTH hosts, so the IRQL test inside
    sub_001A1B7C cannot be the divergence.
  - g_current_irql is XBOX_THREAD_LOCAL, so RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD running ISRs on
    the shared primary TIB does NOT leak IRQL into the main guest thread. That
    was a real worry about a change made today; it is not happening.
  - ordinal 161 (KfLowerIrql) called from 0x001A1BC0 is just the matching
    lower. Nothing further in it.

7. WHAT TO DO NEXT
==================
DO NOT simply widen again and believe the result. Three widenings moved the
answer three times, and there is no reason to think a fourth would be the last:
game .text is 10,941 functions against the ~1,000 armed so far, and CLAUDE.md's
own warning about instrumentation weight destabilising this title makes arming
all of them a poor trade.

Two better options than another round of bisection-by-widening:

  1. Read the branch directly. At the current ceiling the guest is at
     sub_001912A0 -- which writes GPU register [dev+0x2268]+0x100410 with bit
     16 set and then spins -- and macOS goes on to poll (sub_00190F90) while
     Windows leaves for sub_00194480. Read sub_001912A0's caller and see what
     it tests. That is one function, not ten thousand counters.

  2. Fix the instrument instead. [FUNC-SEQ] is a GLOBAL ring, so it interleaves
     threads and has to be hand-filtered; and it records entries, so a call
     tree is flattened and a "next entry" is not a "next step". A per-thread
     ring with a depth counter would make these comparisons mean what they
     appear to mean, and would have prevented two of the three wrong answers
     in this file.

Success is checkable in one line: macOS connects a fourth interrupt,
KeConnectInterrupt vector 5 routine 0x001A2681. When Windows does that too, the
stall is gone.

Get an ORDERED trace, not more counts. instrument_func_hit.py installs bounded
entry counters into a COPY of an existing gen tree and validates every anchor
before writing, so a missed label leaves the tree untouched -- but it counts,
and counting has now taken this as far as it goes.

Do NOT reach for a regeneration first; the archived gen is what both hosts ran
and regeneration is not bit-stable.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS FILE: the archived gen is the AS-FOUND
tree, not a pristine one. It already carried 8 jsrf_func_hit sites from an
earlier session (which is why 0005F590 and 00067220 show up in the macOS hits
despite only the DSOUND band being armed here). It is still the right baseline
-- it is what the macOS build has been running -- but it is not clean, and a
future comparison that assumes it is will be wrong.


8. RETRACTIONS -- THINGS THIS SESSION GOT WRONG
===============================================
(a) "Windows writes zeros to the VP configuration block." FALSE, and it was an
    instrument artefact. The Windows RECOMP_APU_TRACE prints
    mcpx_apu_mmio_read(offset) -- the value read BACK from the model -- not the
    value written. VP registers the model does not store read back as 0, so
    correct writes displayed as zeros. Read a counter's trigger before
    trusting it; this tree says so for a reason. RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE (new,
    in mcpx_apu_mmio_write, works on both hosts, prints the written value and
    the issuing guest function) replaces it for cross-host work.

(b) "The model's read path is the cause of the stall." FALSE. Only five
    registers are ever read on Windows -- FECTL, SECTL, IEN, 0x1510, 0x20010 --
    and all five round-trip correctly. XGSCNT returning a live host clock is
    real but irrelevant: the guest never reads it.

(c) "The two d3d8_gl symbols are link blockers." FALSE, both call sites are
    already #if !defined(_WIN32) guarded. Inspection error.

(d) Several early sweeps reported 35 compile errors. That was a shell bug --
    zsh does not word-split unquoted parameter expansion, so $INC reached gcc
    as a single argument. Use ${=INC}. The real number was 7.

(e) The black CrossOver window is NOT a symptom and never was. The guest
    framebuffer is never connected to it (xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource
    and the event-pump hook are both POSIX-only in main.c), so it can only be a
    black unresponsive rectangle no matter how far the title gets. The D3D8
    probe is now opt-in on Windows (RECOMP_D3D8_PROBE) so no window appears and
    there is nothing to misread. This build's output is the counters on stderr.

===========================
Uncommitted, 447 insertions across 8 files:
  src/apu/apu_core.c          GP/EP storage; RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE at the funnel
  src/apu/apu.h               trace PC provider declaration

plain memory, the guest's writes go nowhere the model can see, and it
```

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE MISSING FIFTH VOICE IS THE MUSIC, AND IT IS NOT A DSOUND BUG
Date: 2026-09-12 (Europe/London)
From: Claude.

Supersedes the audio half of CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_WINDOWS_RENDERS_FOR_REAL.txt.
That handover's sections 0, 1 and 5 (the contiguous alias, the three closed
items, the known-bad shortcuts) all still stand. Its section 2 -- "the new
leading edge: the APU front end" -- is answered here, and the answer is that
the front end was never the place to look.

Long form: docs/jsrf/progress/CLAUDE_PROGRESS_2026-09-12_STREAM_NEVER_STARTS.md


0. THE ONE-LINE ANSWER
======================
Voice 0x44 is the ADX streaming voice -- the music. On Windows the guest never
opens D:\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\, so no ADX stream ever leaves status 0, so CRI never
polls a play cursor, so DirectSound is never asked for the fifth voice. Every
link below that is healthy on both hosts and was never the bug.


1. THE CHAIN, MEASURED END TO END
=================================
    D:\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\ opened
      -> ADX stream slot 0, byte [slot+1]: 0 -> 1 -> 3
        -> sub_0013EF00 reaches sub_0013ECE0          (needs (stat >> 1) & 1)
          -> call [[slot+0x38]+0x20]  ==  sub_001417B0
            -> sub_0019F1F4                           (GetCurrentPosition)
              -> sub_0019ECA3 -> sub_001A43DA -> sub_001A3570
                -> SET_CURRENT_VOICE 0x44             -> on=5

Windows never takes the first step. macOS takes it at about 30 s: the two
D:\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\ opens are at log lines 6119 and 6123 and the 0 -> 1
transition at line 6130.


2. THE FOUR LEVELS AND THEIR NUMBERS
====================================
All paired runs: one gen tree, one instrumented build cross-compiled for both
hosts from the same sources, same scene.

(a) THE DSOUND FATAL LATCH IS NOT IT. RECOMP_DSOUND_FATAL=1.

0x001BA04C is read at 48 sites across DSOUND's API surface and written at
exactly one, 0x001A2317 inside the vtable thunk sub_001A230D; every reader
returns E_FAIL when it is set, and nothing clears it. It is a perfect single
gate above both missing writers. It is also never set:

    macOS    [1BA04C]=00000000 all run, 001A230D: 0 calls, blocked=0
    Windows  [1BA04C]=00000000 all run, 001A230D: 0 calls, blocked=0

What that run did establish is where the two hosts part:

    site        what                       macOS   Windows
    0019F1F4    thunk -> ECA3 -> ... -> 3570 1604         0
    0019ECA3    gate above 001A43DA          1604         0
    0019F214    thunk -> EDCE -> 49A7         204        63
    0019EDCE    gate above 001A49A7           204        63

The first 63 calls through the second chain are IDENTICAL on both hosts, from
the same caller 0x0016CDB1. The first chain Windows never enters.

(b) WHAT sub_0019F1F4 IS. Its macOS caller is 0x001417EA, outside DSOUND.
sub_001417B0 divides the returned cursor by a frame size:
IDirectSoundBuffer::GetCurrentPosition, polled at about 20 Hz. That identifies
the fifth voice as the streaming voice.

(c) CRI'S DIRECTSOUND DRIVER IS NEVER ENTERED. RECOMP_CRI_DSOUND=1.

    site        what                        macOS   Windows
    00143240    diagnostic funnel               0         0
    001417B0    GetCurrentPosition caller     664+        0
    00141560    sibling                         1         0

macOS's handle is the static 0x00272900, [+4]=1, [+8]=80954B60 -- and
80954B60 is exactly the `this` entering sub_0019F1F4. Windows reports no
E1225 because it never reaches the check.

(d) CRI'S STREAM SERVER IS IDENTICAL, AND ONE BYTE DIFFERS.
RECOMP_CRI_SERVER=1. Sixteen slots of 0xA4 bytes at 0x0027B1C0.

    macOS    4 slots in use from tick 1, none gated, ticks=2682 calls=10728
    Windows  4 slots in use from tick 3, none gated, ticks=3809 calls=15236

Windows runs the per-stream body MORE than macOS. The +0x8C gate inside
sub_0013EF00 is never taken on either host. The difference is byte [slot+1]:

    macOS    slot 0: stat 0 -> 1 (tick 906) -> 3 (tick 931); 3 polls the cursor
    Windows  all four slots: stat 0 for the whole run

sub_0013ECE0 runs 1533 times on macOS and zero times on Windows. Its vtable
dispatch [[slot+0x38]+0x20] resolves on macOS to vtable=0x0022DC80 ->
0x001417B0, closing the chain.


3. THE CONFOUND, RULED OUT
==========================
"Windows has not got there yet" would explain all of it. It does not hold:

  * the same Z:\Media\* directories in near-identical proportions
    (Event 79/76, TalkEvent 79/76, Stage 66/66, Mission 52/52, SE 43/38,
    Effect 32/32, Enemy 24/24, StgObj 20/20)
  * the same four stream slots created within three server ticks on both
  * Windows healthy elsewhere: 2577 textures prepared / 0 rejected,

4. WHERE TO START
=================
    WHAT OPENS D:\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\, AND WHY DOES IT NOT RUN ON WINDOWS?

Not DSOUND, not the APU, not the front end. Leads, in the order I would take
them:

  * Instrument the open itself. It is two NtOpenFile calls on D:\ and the only
    D:\ subpath in either log, so it is trivially greppable and its caller
    names the requester directly.
  * 0x0027B1C0 is referenced from six sites. sub_0013E550 (called by
    sub_0013F290) is the slot lookup; sub_0013E440 and sub_0013F470 have no
    static callers and are reached indirectly.
  * byte [slot+1] is written from about a dozen sites in
    0x0013Bxxx..0x0013Cxxx. CONFIRM THE OBJECT before trusting any of them --
    several of those sites are a different structure's +1.
  * The transition to watch is 0 -> 1. On macOS it lands within eleven log
    lines of the directory open, so the two are almost certainly the same
    event.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_THE_IDLE_LOOP_FREEZE.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- A FRESH NEW GAME FREEZES IN CActMan::Idle, AND THE TRANSLATOR
                 WORK OF 12 SEP IS NOT WHY
Date: 2026-09-12 (Europe/London), late evening
From: Claude.

Supersedes nothing outright. It adds a new top-level fault, and it corrects
four readings made during this session -- three of them mine, made in the same
way, and section 4 exists so the next session does not repeat them.


0. THE ONE-LINE ANSWER
======================
Selecting New Game loads a complete stage and then freezes with a black screen.
The guest is in CActMan::Idle() taking its second branch -- `readInput();
Sleep(0x10);` forever -- which is the branch the title runs when it has decided
something is fatally wrong. It is deterministic (1408 file opens, live=56,
every run), the guest is otherwise healthy, and it reproduces bit-identically
on the pre-change gen tree, so nothing committed today caused it.


1. WHAT LANDED TODAY (three commits, all pushed)
================================================
a459a6d  Switch arms recognised and dropped.
    Interior seeds are switch cases, not secondary entries. 143 of 175 kept
    seeds, and 870 of the 895 previously dropped, are entries in a table
    dispatched by `jmp [reg*4 + disp32]`. The loop was self-sustaining: an arm
    is only reachable through its table, so a run observes it, icall_targets
    seeds it as a function start, that start truncates the owner to end at the
    dispatching jump, and a truncated owner is exactly what stops
    _analyze_switch_table resolving the table.
        kept interior seeds 175 -> 35;  resolved switches 293 -> 354;
        unresolved indirect tails 678 -> 615;  functions 9,397 -> 9,129.

12954cb  The ABI check records HOW a target was reached.
    RECOMP_ITAIL is an indirect TAIL JUMP routed through RECOMP_ABI_CALL, so a
    shared epilogue reached that way reads as a violation every time -- false
    by construction. 'C' direct, 'I' indirect call, 'T' tail jump; dedup key is
    the pair.
        ABI offenders 131 -> 9:  C=4, I=0, T=5.
    Five of the nine are one shared epilogue (0x0007E575..5AA). Three of the
    four C rows are the CRT at 0x17CAB0/0x17D1F8/0x17D231, two saying
    "esp(epilogue never ran)" -- the __SEH_prolog/__chkstk signature already
    called expected on 12 Sep. sub_00011D00, recursiveExec1Default, the one
    offender in the exec tree, is GONE.
    regenerate.sh now sets RECOMP_SEED_INTERIOR=1.

289f21f  Two further defects, both found by subagents, both making the OWNER
         wrong rather than the arm.
    (a) THE FIRST ARM. MSVC makes case 0 the dispatch's own fall-through, so a
        switch's first arm sits exactly on a boundary of its own making:
        interior to nothing, and every later arm in that table is then judged
        against an owner that BEGINS after the dispatch site. Of 422 resynced
        tables, 137 have the dispatcher ending at the jump and 133 are
        truncated this way. resync_jump_tables was never at fault -- the raw
        FF24 scan and the engine agree on all 422, none missed either way.
    (b) THE TAIL CALL. functions.json is healthy (largest body 11,124 bytes).
        The runaway is at the one call site passing next_func=None, where
        `upper` becomes the whole 1.5 MB .text and every forward tail call
        looks internal. p99.9 4,639 -> 270,906. In 83 of 83 worst escalations
        the culprit is an unconditional jmp to an address already in
        functions.json. The veto fires ZERO times under the clamped builder.
        Cost of leaving it: 45 of 1,142 interior-seed verdicts were decided by
        an owner extent above 11 KB.

    310 tests green, including 8 in test_function_end.py that had been failing
    since c621ffe (its fixture predates _forced_bounds).


2. THE FREEZE -- WHAT IS ESTABLISHED
====================================
    // Address: 0x00013F80   Status: matching   (JSRF-Decompilation)
    int CActMan::Idle() {
        if (this->m_InitState >= 0) while (true) {
            if (!this->m_bFatal) this->IdleSub();
            else { readInput(); Sleep(0x10); }
        } else return -1;
    }

Our generated C matches that structure exactly:

    loc_00013F90:
        eax = MEM32(esi + 0x24);                     // m_bFatal
        if (TEST_NZ(_fa, _fb)) goto loc_00013FA0;    // != 0 -> freeze branch
        call sub_00013A80;                           // else IdleSub()
        goto loc_00013F90;
    loc_00013FA0:
        call sub_000659C0;   // readInput
        push 0x10; call sub_00145CA6;                // Sleep(0x10)
        goto loc_00013F90;

/usr/bin/sample against the live pid, TWO separate processes, at the stall:

    sub_00013F80 + 724 -> sub_00145CA6 (Sleep)      2676 / 3450 samples
    sub_00013F80 + 576 -> sub_000659C0 (readInput)    53 /   62 samples
    sub_00013A80       (IdleSub)                       0 /    0 samples

So MEM32(esi + 0x24) is nonzero and the freeze branch is running. m_bFatal is
at CActMan+0x24: derived from the decompilation's struct layout and confirmed
independently by sub_00012770's body, which writes [ecx+0x24] = 1.

Also measured at the stall:
  * deterministic: 1408 NtOpenFile, 264 distinct files, live=56, EVERY run
  * a complete stage loads: Stage, StgObj, Effect, Sounds\SE, Disp\map,
    Player, Disp\charicon
  * the guest is healthy: frame loop running, Exec0Default climbing, no errors
  * 446 indirect targets resolved, ZERO unresolved
  * NOT today's translator work: the pre-change tree (gen.dropcontrol, built at
    scratchpad/build-control) stalls with the same 1408 / live=56
  * NOT slowness: removing JSRF_ABI_CHECK_ALL changed nothing, and the file
    count was bit-identical
  * Z_ADX\BGM IS opened (4x) -- the step the Windows oracle never reached

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: what sets the flag. CActMan::Fatal() at 0x00012770 is
instrumented and NEVER CALLED. Only ELEVEN sites in the whole image write 1 to
[reg+0x24]; ten remain:

    0x0001B5C0 (x2)  0x00027F70  0x0007AF90  0x0008B3E0 (x2)
    0x00156AB0       0x0017C069  0x0019F39C

Probes on seven of them are installed and record `this`. At the stall none had
`this` = the CActMan. That set is where the next session starts.


3. THE OTHER REAL RESULT -- PAD_INJECT KILLS THE POLL STALL
===========================================================
    USB schedule:  polls FROZEN at 971,  nonneutral 116,  15 transitions
    PAD_INJECT=1:  polls 13,379+,        nonneutral 1,969, 482 transitions

The stall is in USB DELIVERY, not in the guest. RECOMP_PAD_INJECT writes the
report straight into the title's own copies at 60 Hz and the schedule stops
mattering. Unattended runs of arbitrary length are now possible.
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/play_tutorial.sh is the human-driven harness;
it sets PAD_INJECT, the scene markers and the exec-mode counters.


4. FOUR WRONG READINGS, ALL THE SAME MISTAKE
============================================
Read this section before trusting any counter in this tree. Every one of these
was "a number that looked like an answer", and each cost a cycle.

  (1) "nonneutral=0 proves the poll stall."  It proved RECOMP_USB was unset, so
      the OHCI model was never enabled. An absence with no positive control.

  (2) "[ADX] flag=0 means the stream is stuck in PREP."  flag is MEM32(0x25EFA4),
      the ADX server's WAKE flag, and 0 is the HEALTHY value -- the server
      clears it each pass. main.c says so five lines above the print. The
      successful 79M-triangle run shows flag=0 throughout.

  (3) "CActMan::Fatal() must be what sets m_bFatal."  The decompilation covers
      0.38% of the binary and marks that function `unimplemented`. It is never
      called. The generated C -- which has no coverage problem -- names eleven
      writers.

  (4) "m_bFatal=0, so the freeze branch is not running."  jsrf_scene_report
      accepted 0x040FFF40 as the root because it only RANGE-checked the pointer.
      The root literal moves between runs but its low 16 bits are invariant at
      0x3A70 (the xemu rig's README says so outright). Every field printed from
      that pointer was read from the wrong object. NOW FIXED in main.c: the
      pointer is rejected unless low16 matches, and it says so when it rejects.

Also worth recording, because it wasted your time rather than mine: RECOMP_FAKE_PAD
REPLACES the real pad rather than merging with it, so an unattended run started
while a human has the window silently eats every press. Check `pgrep -x
jsrf_first_fault` before launching -- twice today two instances fought over the
controller, and once a "the task finished" notification raced a run that had
70 seconds left.

============================================
Mostly yes, but not from a standing start, and the first task is what buys the
rest.

THE BLOCKER ON AUTONOMY: reaching the freeze needs New Game selected. The

live=133 and 1342 opens but never New Game's live=56 / 1408. Every measurement

    RECOMP_PAD_SCRIPT="2.0:START 3.0:A 4.0:A 6.0:A ..." -- a timed sequence
    rather than a pulse. fake_pad_start() already has the shape; this replaces

TASK 2 -- NAME THE WRITER OF m_bFatal

    freeze, find the one entered with this = the CActMan (low16 0x3A70). Then

TASK 3 -- REGENERATE AND MEASURE 289f21f
    Owed from section 5. Mechanical.

TASK 4 -- THE 36 REAL FUNCTION STARTS
    Of the 155 remaining carves: 28 are switch arms of the 133-table family,
    86 are interior addresses of one compiler function, 36 are REAL function
    starts (all 16-aligned, all reached only by a tail jmp, 30 preceded by NOP
    padding or a ret), 5 are phantoms from decodes that ran past a ret into
    data. _pass_tail_jump_targets misses the 36 for a measured reason: 41 of
    43 jump sites fail `if insn.address >= body_end` because the jmp sits in a
    tail_jump_alias fragment or a gap, and aliases do not exist when that pass
    runs; one more fails because that pass never calls engine.decode_at on the
    target, unlike _pass_call_targets. Both guards are narrow and testable.

WHAT SIX HOURS WOULD REALISTICALLY COVER: task 1 (~1h, including the unattended
verification), task 2 (~1h once task 1 lands), task 3 (~1h, mostly waiting on
regenerate.sh and one run), task 4 (~2h with tests). That leaves an hour of
slack, which will be needed: rebuilds are minutes each and this title punishes
heavy instrumentation -- 578 probe sites froze the guest at 253 polls where an
unprobed run reached 8,790.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT GO WRONG: doing task 2 before task 1. Every hour spent
without a scripted repro is an hour of a human pressing START, and section 4 is
what happens when the cost of a measurement tempts you into inferring one
instead.
```
