`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_TLS_IS_THE_BOTTLENECK.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE BIGGEST COST IS THE TLS LOOKUP, AND THE TOOLCHAIN CHOOSES IT
Date: 2026-09-12 (Europe/London), late
From: Claude.

Follows CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_WINDOWS_REACHES_GAMEPLAY.txt, which stands.
That one said both hosts reach gameplay and Windows is ~5x slower. This one
says why BOTH hosts are slow, which is a different and larger question.


0. THE MEASUREMENT
==================
Profiled macOS with RECOMP_METAL unset -- the same CPU path Windows runs,
natively, where `sample` works:

    _tlv_get_addr                      ~5250 of the main guest thread's 7021
    combine                             3022
    nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth    2029
    sub_0013B180 (guest, ADX)           1933
    texel                               1055

ABOUT 75% OF THE MAIN GUEST THREAD IS THE THREAD-LOCAL LOOKUP. More than the
rasteriser, the combiner and the ADX decoder together.

The generated code is `#define eax g_eax` over a thread-local register set, so
every guest register read and write is one TLS access.


1. IT IS A TOOLCHAIN ARTEFACT, NOT UPSTREAM'S DESIGN
====================================================
Upstream declares the registers exactly as we do, RECOMP_TLS, with _MSC_VER
checked first, and upstream's README requires Visual Studio 2022 and supports
Windows+MSVC+D3D11 or Linux+GCC+OpenGL. On MSVC, __declspec(thread) is a
TEB-relative load and costs nothing.

We run neither supported configuration:

    Windows   mingw-w64 defines __GNUC__, so it takes __thread, and GCC
              implements __thread on that target with EMULATED TLS --
              __emutls_get_address(), a real call per access. 145 emutls
              symbols in the exe.
    macOS     Darwin has no ELF TLS models. __thread always goes through the
              tlv descriptor and _tlv_get_addr in libdyld, and -ftls-model= is
              silently a no-op. There is no flag that fixes this.


2. CLANG FIXES THE WINDOWS HALF, AND NEEDS NO WINDOWS MACHINE
=============================================================
Same mingw sysroot, same headers, same libraries, same source. Only the
compiler changes:

    x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc   ->  __emutls_get_address, __emutls_v.g_eax
    clang --target=x86_64-w64-windows-gnu  ->  _tls_index   (native, TEB)

Verified on the real build, not a toy: tools/windows/clang-mingw.cmake
produces jsrf_first_fault.exe with 145 -> 0 emutls symbols.

Three things clang's driver does not do that GCC's does, all handled in that
toolchain file:
  * it drives the host ld -- point -fuse-ld at x86_64-w64-mingw32-ld
  * it does not add libgcc's directory -- -L .../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/<v>
  * it links no default libraries -- winpthread (for clock_gettime64, which
    mingw's pthread_time.h inlines a call to) and the usual Win32 import libs,
    and they must go in CMAKE_C_STANDARD_LIBRARIES so they land AFTER the
    objects, not in the linker flags where the archives are scanned too early.


3. WHERE IT STOPS, AND IT IS ONE CONTAINED BUG
==============================================
The clang exe builds and runs the whole memory layout, then dies on the first
guest fault:

    HOST FAULT ADDRESS 0x0000000100C00130   (the AC97 codec status register)
    LAST INSTRUMENTED GUEST FUNCTION sub_00000000   (none -- still in init)

xbox_memory_layout.c does, long after the AC97 page is guarded read-only:

    *(volatile uint32_t *)((char *)g_mcpx_memory + MCPX_AC97_CODEC_STATUS)
        |= MCPX_AC97_CODEC_READY;

That is a read-modify-write against a guarded page. The VEH decoder in
xbox_Nv2aHandleWin32Fault completes PLAIN STORES ONLY -- 0x89, 0xC7, 0x88,
0xC6. GCC spells the |= as load / or / store, so the store decodes and the
handler completes it. Clang emits `or [mem], imm`, which the decoder rejects,
returns 0, and the process dies.

So the guard has always been compiler-dependent; GCC merely happened to spell
it in the one form the decoder knows.

THE FIX IS THE DECODER, NOT THE CALL SITE. Moving the write earlier does not
help -- tried, and it only moves the fault, because the AC97 guard goes up at
xbox_memory_layout.c:2040 and this write is at ~3500. Add the read-modify-write
forms (0x81 /1 and 0x83 /1 for OR, and whatever else the codebase actually
emits) to the decoder, computing the new value from the current one and then
completing it with the existing store path. The undecoded counter added in
commit 996f84c will tell you if anything else is being silently rejected --
that counter is why this was findable at all.


4. WHAT THIS IS WORTH
=====================
If the ~75% figure carries, removing the TLS lookup is worth roughly a 3-4x on
the guest thread, on BOTH hosts, and it is larger than the GPU-rasteriser gap
of the previous handover. Order of work:

  1. Extend the VEH decoder (section 3). Small, and it unblocks the clang
     Windows build, which is native TLS for free.
  2. Measure the clang build against the GCC baseline: 203 loops @30s,
     421 @60s, 782 @90s. That is the A/B for the whole hypothesis.
  3. macOS needs a different fix -- there is no fast __thread on Darwin. The
     real answer is to stop doing a lookup per access: hand each generated
     function a register-context pointer on entry and index through it. That is
     a translator change or a mechanical edit of the gen tree, and it is the
     single largest measured win available.

RECOMP_TLS is now overridable by the build (-DRECOMP_TLS=) for bounding
experiments. Plain globals crash, as they must -- guest threads share the
register set -- so the profile stays the measurement.

TRIED AND REVERTED, so nobody pays for it twice: keying RECOMP_TLS on _WIN32 so
mingw-gcc takes __declspec(thread). emutls drops 145 -> 16 but the title exits
through HalReturnToFirmware within sixteen file opens. Native PE TLS wants its
directory and per-thread init; gcc's mingw path does not give the harness that.
Clang is the better route and is already proven to emit native TLS.


5. BUILD IT
===========
  cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build> \
    -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=tools/windows/clang-mingw.cmake \
    -DRECOMP_GEN_DIR=<gen> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DXBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT=4"

tools/windows/gcc-mingw.cmake is the working GCC toolchain, kept so the two can
be compared without reconstructing either.

```

```txt
3. WHERE WINDOWS ACTUALLY STOPS -- WHAT I HAVE
==============================================

    sub_0004C400   595 calls   1185 bytes, no static callers, calls sub_00117140
    sub_000585E0    39 calls   11124 bytes -- a very large update body,
                               called by 0x0005B3F0 and 0x0005B570
    sub_00067220  2373 calls   called by 0x0005F590
    sub_0004EF90     3 calls   the title state machine, 0x12 -> 0x13 -> 0x14

sub_000585E0 at eleven kilobytes is the most promising ladder rung: something
that large running 39 times on one host and never on the other is a whole
subsystem, not a branch.

The two CRI functions with game-side callers are sub_0013AA60 and sub_0013AEB0
(tiny setters, `[this+0x6C] = al` and similar), called from sub_00116AB0,
sub_00117060, sub_00117140 and sub_001171F0 -- the game's BGM entry points.
sub_00117140 has nine call sites spread across the game. That is the boundary
where game code enters CRI, and it is never crossed on Windows.


4. HOW TO CARRY THIS ON
=======================
Arm func_hit over the scene/mission band and bisect downward from
sub_000585E0's callers (0x0005B3F0, 0x0005B570) and sub_0005F590. The installer
handles hundreds of sites at once and needs no regeneration:

    python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_func_hit.py \
        --va-file <file of VAs> --skip-mismatched
    python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_func_hit.py \
        --remove --va-file <same file> --skip-mismatched

RECOMP_FUNC_HIT_TRACE=1 at run time. The gen tree in build-macos is currently
left with 556 sites armed (CRI + sound manager + the 17 CPlayer markers).

**Put the gameplay marker in every future Windows/macOS comparison, first,
before reading any other counter.** Every audio conclusion in the last two
handovers would have been caught by that one check.

Read-only and opt-in, installed by instrument_startup.py, all reporting

7. THE WINDOWS BUILD CAN SHOW ITS OUTPUT: RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1
============================================================
CORRECTS every handover from 2026-09-11 onward, which said the CrossOver
window is always black and is not a symptom, and told you to judge runs by the
stderr counters. That was true of ONE route and wrong as a general claim, and
it cost this project every Windows run it has ever done: none of them had a
picture.

The route those handovers describe -- xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource plus
the event-pump hook -- really is inside `#if !defined(_WIN32)` in main.c, so
the D3D8 layer's window really is a black rectangle on this host.

But there is a SECOND presenter, and it is the Windows-only one.
src/video/fb_present.c is a plain GDI window that reads the guest framebuffer
out of guest RAM and blits it -- deliberately not going through the D3D8
layer, so that it shows whatever the guest actually wrote. Its whole body is
`#if defined(_WIN32)`; POSIX gets the stub at the bottom of the file. It is
wired into AvSetDisplayMode already (kernel_bridge.c calls
xbox_FramebufferWindowSet then xbox_FramebufferWindowStart), it is linked into
jsrf_first_fault.exe, and `x86_64-w64-mingw32-nm` finds both symbols in the
binary.

It is off unless RECOMP_FB_WINDOW is set, and nothing in this project had ever
set it.

    set RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1

and the run prints

    [FBWIN] framebuffer window open (640x480)

Measured 2026-09-12: the window shows the SMILEBIT "Created by" logo and then
advances through the boot sequence, changing continuously. The Windows build
renders, presents, and can be watched.

Two consequences:

  * "Judge Windows runs by the stderr counters" is no longer the only option,
    and several of this project's hardest arguments -- whether the frame is
    real, which screen it is on, whether it is advancing -- are now one
    screenshot.
  * The framebuffer nonzero counts in the logs were never the right instrument
    for "what is on screen". Use the window.

RECOMP_FB_VA pins the window to one guest address instead of following the
surface being drawn, which separates "the read path is broken" from "the title
rendered black".
```

```txt
0. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS
========================
Given 672 seconds instead of 110, the Windows build:

    t=671.9  [TITLE-STATE] 0x12 -> 0x13 -> 0x14      at main loop 2408
             opens \Device\CdRom0\Media\Z_ADX\BGM\title.adx

IN GUEST TIME THE TWO HOSTS AGREE ALMOST EXACTLY: 2408 against 2400-2900. The
divergence that three handovers chased was entirely wall-clock.


1. EVERY AUDIO FINDING OF THE LAST TWO DAYS IS RETIRED
======================================================
on=4 against on=5, fe_methods 177 against 4369, set_current_voice 12 against

opened", "sub_0019F1F4 is called 1604 times on macOS and never on Windows" --
all of it was a 90-to-110 second run measured against a 90 second run that had
already reached gameplay at t=30. There was never an audio bug, never a DSOUND
bug, and never a content-loading bug.

Windows now reports on=5, fe_methods=1945, set_current_voice=582 and climbing,
through the exact chain the earlier handover named:

    BGM opened -> ADX slot 0 byte[+1] 0->1->3 -> sub_0013ECE0
      -> [[slot+0x38]+0x20] = sub_001417B0 -> sub_0019F1F4 -> ... -> voice 0x44

That chain is correct and is now confirmed on BOTH hosts. Only the conclusion
drawn from its absence was wrong.

Still genuinely closed, because they were measured on both hosts directly:
  * the DSOUND fatal latch 0x001BA04C -- zero on both, latch never fires
  * the byte [this+0x12] & 3 gate at 0x001A43F0
  * "two adjacent methods on one object" -- they are DirectSound API thunks


2. THE REAL NUMBER
==================
The guest main loop, sub_000123E0, measured on both hosts at equal elapsed
time:

    macOS    36.1 iterations/s   (70/s during the title, ~9.5/s in gameplay)
    Windows   7.4 iterations/s   (~2-5/s during the title)

About 5x on the loop, and about 22x on the whole boot in wall clock, because
macOS's early phase is much faster than its later one.

That is Windows x86-64 under CrossOver on Apple Silicon: recompiled C ->
x86-64 -> binary-translated to ARM64. On a native x86-64 PC -- which is what
upstream xboxrecomp targets -- that layer does not exist. NOT MEASURED here;
there is no native PC in this setup. It is the obvious hypothesis and it is
cheap for anyone with a PC to test.

RULE, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERED THIS WEEK:

    NEVER COMPARE THE TWO HOSTS AT EQUAL WALL-CLOCK TIME.
    COMPARE AT EQUAL GUEST MAIN-LOOP COUNT.

`[FUNC-HIT] 000123E0 calls=N` armed by instrument_func_hit.py is the clock.
A Windows run needs 600+ seconds to reach what macOS reaches in 30.


3. THE WINDOWS BUILD HAS A PICTURE: RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1
======================================================
Also corrected today, see commit 0d45c25. src/video/fb_present.c is a
Windows-only GDI presenter, wired into AvSetDisplayMode, linked into the exe,
and never switched on by anything in this project. Set RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1 and
the run prints

    [FBWIN] framebuffer window open (640x480)

and shows the boot logos, the title, and gameplay.

KNOWN ARTIFACT, do not chase it as a rendering bug: the image tears along a
clean diagonal, one half at a time. The blit loop is a bare 16 ms timer that
reads guest RAM with no flip, lock, vsync or double buffer -- so at 62 Hz
against a guest drawing at 2-7 Hz it lands mid-draw nearly every time, and a
fullscreen image is two triangles. Complete frames are produced: 50 samples in
one run read 153600/153600. Worth fixing by blitting on the guest's flip,
which would also make the window admissible as evidence.


4. THE BIGGER HALF OF THE SLOWDOWN: WINDOWS HAS NO GPU RASTERISER
=================================================================
CORRECTS section 2's implication that a native PC would fix the speed. It
would remove the translation penalty and leave the larger problem standing.

    macOS    [METAL] native raster pipeline ready: Apple M1 Max
             128,425 batches native, 0 software fallbacks     -- 100% GPU
    Windows  0 batches native; 6,625,275 triangles through raster_triangle()
                                                             -- 100% CPU

In src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c the entire accelerated path is

    #ifdef __APPLE__
        if (s_copy.active && getenv("RECOMP_METAL")) {
            int triangles = nv2a_metal_draw(...);
            if (triangles >= 0) goto batch_complete;      /* GPU */
        }
    #endif
        switch (s_gpu.prim) { ...                          /* CPU fallback */

so every triangle on Windows is scalar software rasterisation, and then that
software rasteriser is itself binary-translated. The D3D11 sink that would be
the Windows equivalent handles nothing at all: unhandled=15,078,354 of
15,078,354 methods.

Observed directly in the window: the city intro draws layer by layer at about
four seconds a frame. That is the software rasteriser completing one batch at
a time, with the unsynced presenter blitting between batches.

So the order of expected value is:
  1. GIVE WINDOWS A GPU BACKEND. The D3D11 sink already exists and is already
     initialised; it just implements no methods. The Metal path is the
     structural model -- one entry point that takes the prepared batch state
     and returns a triangle count or -1 to fall back.
  2. Only then test a native x86-64 PC. Both effects are real and they
     multiply; neither alone makes the intro run.
  3. The diagnostic logging is unconditional and heavy -- [FILE], [PATH] and
     [KERNEL] print on every call with an fflush. Windows emits ~25 log lines
     per guest loop iteration against macOS's 4.3.
  4. The VEH trap now has per-page fault counters (commit 996f84c); a run with
     them says how much of the remainder is the MMIO guard. That number has
     never existed on this host.

DO NOT read [TEXTURE] prepared=N rejected=M as a rejection RATE, and do not
compare it across hosts. `batches` counts batches and `rejected` counts a
mixture of rejected triangles and rejected draws, so the two are different
units; and macOS's Metal path reaches `goto batch_complete` before the site
that increments `rejected`, so macOS reports ~28 where Windows reports
439,082 for the same work. Windows's own figure is about 6% of the triangles
it rasterises.


5. RUNS BEHIND THIS
===================
  render-investigation/win-fbwindow-1   the 720 s Windows run, everything in
                                        section 0 is from its stderr
  render-investigation/mac-threshold-1  macOS with RECOMP_REPORT_MS=2000, which
                                        pins the title crossover to a loop count
  render-investigation/win-bisect-1,
  render-investigation/mac-bisect-1     the 583-site func_hit sweep behind the
                                        loop-rate figures
```

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE WINDOWS ORACLE RENDERS, AND ITS THREE OPEN ITEMS ARE SHUT
Date: 2026-09-12 (Europe/London), early hours
From: Claude.

Supersedes CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_RENDERS.txt. All three

0. WHAT CHANGED
===============
Physical offset N and XBOX_CONTIG_BASE + N did not name the same bytes on
Windows. The contiguous window was VirtualAlloc'd storage aliasing nothing, so
every block the guest filled through 0x80XXXXXX was invisible to a GPU
resolving the low offset -- and the separate bump arena that followed from it
climbed through the guest's own stacks and heap.

xbox_EnablePhysicalHeapAlias now has a Windows implementation (6fb8734). The
window is rebuilt at the end of layout init as committed storage below the
heap, a view of the RAM section across it, and committed storage above;
xbox_ContiguousAlloc then takes from the heap. RECOMP_PHYSICAL_HEAP_ALIAS=0
opts out and falls back to the floored arena.

The framebuffer has pixels. Every Windows run before this reported
nonzero=0/153600 for its whole life. A 260 s run now changes continuously,
repeatedly covering the full frame, with 5,108 texture copies and zero
rejected -- against roughly half rejected in every earlier run.


1. THE THREE ITEMS, ANSWERED
============================
(a) WHY SUBMISSION STOPS AFTER ~600 DRAWS. It does not any more. The 260 s run
    was still submitting when it was stopped: texture copies climbing linearly
    to 5,108, framebuffer changing at t=259, no fault, no outstanding notify
    deadlock. Judge this by the CPU executor's counters, NOT by
    "[PUSHER] draws=0" -- that line reads 0 on both hosts and CLAUDE.md already
    lists it as a known-bad shortcut.

(b) THE 0xBC60 VOICE LINK. Gone, and the absence is controlled. The walker's
    own throughput counter says it ran:

        baseline   [APU-VOICE] processed=16559     + 8 out-of-range reports
        aliased    [APU-VOICE] processed=1521632   + 0 out-of-range reports

    36x more voices walked and not one bad handle. The 8 in the baseline was
    the print cap, not a frequency; the list was being truncated every frame
    ("stopping this list"), which is why so few were processed. The garbage
    link was the arena writing over the voice list.

(c) A RING THAT HAS NEVER WRAPPED TO ITS BASE. Not a fault. macOS -- which
    renders, presents and reaches gameplay -- reports the same:

        win baseline 1    win aliased 0    macOS 0

    The healthy reference host never wraps to base either, so this says nothing
    about Windows. Item closed; do not spend a session on it.


2. THE NEW LEADING EDGE: THE APU FRONT END
==========================================
Rendering is fixed; audio submission is not, and it is now the clearest
remaining divergence. Same scene, same build:

        macOS    on=5 fe_methods=4369 set_current_voice=1390 processed=480096
        Windows  on=4 fe_methods=177  set_current_voice=12   processed=1521632

Windows walks three times as many voices and submits a twenty-fifth of the
front-end methods. Those two counters are the right ones and live in
src/apu/apu_vp.c, which both hosts compile: fe_methods and set_current_voice
localise a failure to the guest's submission loop rather than to MMIO routing,
and both are nonzero here, so the routing works and the loop runs short. The
register traffic confirms it -- RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE shows Windows configuring
voice handles 0x40..0x43 once and then stopping, where macOS keeps
re-submitting.

CORRECTION, AND A WARNING ABOUT THIS EXACT REPORT. An earlier draft of this
handover said Windows "generates no audio frames at all", citing
[APU-PACE] batches=0 frames=0 and [APU-SDL2] prime=0. That was wrong, and it
was wrong in the way CLAUDE.md warns about. macOS uses the SDL2 backend and
Windows uses XAudio2; apu_sdl2.c compiles to stubs under _WIN32, so every
g_apu_sdl_* counter on that host is a variable with NO PRODUCER. Those zeros
are a definition. Whether Windows produces audio was, at that point, simply
unmeasured.

[APU-OUT] now reports the backend that is actually live and its own numbers --
submits offered, buffers landed, sample frames, and which of the three silent
early returns in xa2_submit_samples swallowed the rest. Read that line, not
the SDL2 block, when the host is Windows. It labels itself on both:

    Windows  [APU-OUT] backend=XAudio2 submits=15017 submitted=13104
             frames=3354624 gen_hz=41890 drops: inactive=0 full=1913 failed=0
    macOS    [APU-OUT] backend=SDL2 (XAudio2 counters below are inactive)
             submits=0 ... and [APU-PACE] batches=7500 frames=1920000 gen_hz=48006

So WINDOWS IS PRODUCING AUDIO -- 13,104 buffers and 3.35M sample frames in
90 s, with the only drops being ordinary back-pressure (the device queue full).
It runs at about 87% of nominal against macOS's 48 kHz, which is worth
understanding but is a different question from silence.

What is thin is the CONTENT, and that is where the front-end divergence lands:
four voices started against five, and voice configuration that stops after the
first pass. Chase that, not the output stage.

Note also [APU-PACE] subframes/se, which DO have a producer on both hosts and
are nearly equal (14976 vs 15040 at t=10 s). The APU core runs at the same rate
on both; it is the front-end submission and the output reporting that differ.

DO NOT TRUST [APUREG]'s "from sub_XXXXXXXX". It was the harness's thread-local
last-instrumented-function, which is whatever ran most recently on that thread
and not the writer. It confidently named sub_001664D0 for a burst of voice
configuration; sub_001664D0 is a 37-byte refcount release, `lock xadd [ecx+8]`
then maybe a vtable call, and it touches no MMIO at all. The macOS attribution
(sub_00147EBB) was equally wrong. The field is now printed as "guest~" to mark
it as a hint.

Use host_pc= instead. It is the faulting store itself, and

    x86_64-w64-mingw32-addr2line -f -e jsrf_first_fault.exe <host_pc>

resolves it exactly, which is the method 06-debugging.md prescribes. Both hosts
now record it (POSIX from the sigaction context, Windows from the VEH).

With it, every APU register write on Windows resolves into the statically
linked DSOUND -- nineteen distinct functions, all in sub_001A2xxx..sub_001A6xxx:

    sub_001A5E19 sub_001A5742 sub_001A368A sub_001A5671 sub_001A6160
    sub_001A5CD7 sub_001A586B sub_001A40F5 sub_001A3E58 sub_001A52F7
    sub_001A4E12 sub_001A5B82 sub_001A5B27 sub_001A5AF0 sub_001A5AB9
    sub_001A53AA sub_001A268D sub_001A22BC sub_001A2285

That is the submission loop, named. The macOS list, taken the same way (dladdr
resolves it inline there), has 21 entries and Windows's 19 are a strict subset.
The two that macOS has and Windows never reaches:

    sub_001A3570   (87 configurations in 55 s)
    sub_001A49A7   (1)

Both do the same thing: SET_CURRENT_VOICE to handle 0x44, VOICE_LOCK, release.
**They are the only two functions that touch voice 0x44**, and that is the
whole of on=5 against on=4. The fifth voice is never configured on Windows
because neither function runs.

One level up, sub_001A3570 has a single caller, sub_001A43DA, which gates it:

    0x001A43F0  mov al, byte ptr [esi + 0x12]
    0x001A43F3  and al, 3
    0x001A43F5  cmp al, 3
    0x001A43F7  jne 0x1a4484          ; skip sub_001A3570

The gate is NOT what fails. RECOMP_DSOUND_GATE=1 probes that branch:

    macOS    this=80954C64 dword+0x10=0303FFFF byte+0x12&3=3 CONFIGURES
    Windows  (no lines at all)

sub_001A43DA is never reached on Windows. Controlled: the env var was set,
other probes in the same generated file fired in the same run (9 [NOTIFY],
9 [RESERVE]), and the run reached 1,802 texture copies -- so the silence is the
measurement, not a dead instrument.

Next level up, and where to start:

    sub_001A43DA  called by sub_0019ECA3, sub_001A464B, sub_001A46F0
    sub_001A49A7  called by sub_0019EDCE
    sub_0019ECA3  called by sub_0019ECF8, sub_0019F1F4
    sub_0019EDCE  called by sub_0019F214

Note sub_0019F1F4 and sub_0019F214 are 32 bytes apart -- adjacent methods on
the same object, one feeding each missing writer. A single gate above both is
the likely shape. Probe those two entries next.

Worth knowing while reading it: the DSOUND object macOS gates on lives at
0x80954C64, inside the contiguous window. That window aliased the guest's own
stacks and heap on this host until today (section 0), so any conclusion about
DSOUND state drawn from a run older than commit 6fb8734 is unsafe.

Start with the submission loop, and start by reading what increments each
counter -- including the ones that look like they already answered.


3. BUILD AND RUN
================
Unchanged from the previous handover -- cross-compile with the mingw toolchain,
build ONLY the jsrf_first_fault target, drive it from a .bat inside the
CX_BOTTLE. RECOMP_AC97_READY=1 is still mandatory.

New switches:
  RECOMP_PHYSICAL_HEAP_ALIAS=0   fall back to the old two-pool arena
  RECOMP_CONTIG_VERIFY=1         compare both views of a surface where the
                                 model resolves it; POSIX is its positive
                                 control and must report "match"
  RECOMP_TEXTURE_SLOT=<index>    one texture-cache slot's whole life, uncapped

RECOMP_CONTIG_FROM_HEAP is gone. It existed for one session, removed the crash
by making the window inert, and was never a fix.


4. DO NOT RE-RUN THESE
======================
  the 0xBC60 voice link           (b) above, with a positive control
  the ~600-draw submission stall  (a) above, 260 s and still going
  the ring that never wraps       (c) above, macOS does the same
  RECOMP_STORE_WATCH on a page a bulk copy touches -- the first toucher of the
    texture-cache page is a lifted rep stosd, the VEH decoder completes single
    stores only, and the run dies inside ntdll before reaching the writer


5. WHAT I WOULD NOT DO
======================
Do not read [PUSHER] clears/flips/draws or the D3D11 sink's unhandled-method
list as evidence about Windows rendering. On the aliased run they are
0/0/0 and 100% unhandled while the framebuffer is demonstrably changing --
the drawing goes through the CPU executor, counted separately. CLAUDE.md lists
both as known-bad shortcuts and this run is another instance.

Do not treat the triangle total as progress. It fell from 22.2M to 5,108 when
the alias landed, and that was the improvement: the large figure was a software
rasteriser sweeping blank memory as fast as it could.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_COMISS_NAN_FROZE_THE_TUTORIAL.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE, 13 Sep 2026
SOLVED: COMISS ON NaN. CORN ANIMATES.

Supersedes both CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_THE_SECOND_WRITER.txt and
CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_E6C_IS_ZEROED_EVERY_FRAME.txt, which are the two
earlier stations on the way to this.


0. THE BUG, IN ONE PARAGRAPH
============================
x86 `comiss` sets ZF, PF and CF ALL AT ONCE when either operand is NaN. The
lifter emitted the unsigned conditions as the plain C operators, and C
disagrees in both directions: `a == b` is false for NaN where ZF is set, and
`a != b` is true for NaN where ZF is clear. JSRF's ray-plane intersection
sub_0014C100 ends `comiss xmm0, xmm7` / `je -> return 0`, and is handed a
movement segment that is zero-length whenever a character stands still, which
normalises to NaN. On hardware the branch is taken and the test reports no
intersection. For us it fell through and reported a HIT, with a NaN
intersection point. CSysDeathWarpManager therefore death-warped both CPlayers
on every frame of the Corn tutorial, and that read -- for two days -- as
"the characters do not animate".

    tools/recomp/lifter.py, the comiss/ucomiss condition mapping.
    Regression test: tools/recomp/test_lifter_comiss.py (144 suite tests pass).


1. THE CHAIN
============
    zero-length movement segment (standing still in a cutscene)
      -> normalise gives 0/0 = NaN
      -> comiss xmm0, xmm7 ; je     in sub_0014C100
      -> x86: ZF=1 unordered -> je TAKEN -> "no hit"       <- xemu
      -> ours: NaN == 0.0f false -> fall through -> "HIT"  <- the bug
      -> warp-hit branch at 0x00024BA0 writes the record at CPlayer+0x3C8:
             +0x38 := 1        (warp pending)
             +0x3C := kind     (2)
             +0x40 := the intersection point  (NaN,NaN,NaN -- the tell)
      -> exec virtual sub_00080340 at 0x000806A8 sees [+0x3C8]+0x38 != 0 and
         copies +0x3CC := [[this+0x3C8]+0x3C] = 2
      -> its 3-way dispatch at 0x00080716 sends 2 -> sub_00092750
      -> sub_00092750 sets state(+0xE50) := 15 and anim(+0x11C) := 128,
         the respawn animation, EVERY FRAME
      -> that defeats the idempotence guard at 0x000A7EBD in sub_000A76E0,
         which skips only when the state already equals 23
      -> so sub_0009B2D0 / sub_0009B3E0 re-enter the dialogue state every frame
         and set +0xE6C := 0, which is the engine's "restart this clip"
      -> sub_0009E910 therefore always takes its "animation changed" branch
      -> the clip is re-armed before it can advance; the pose is evaluated at
         the same phase forever and the transform block never changes.


2. BEFORE AND AFTER, MEASURED
=============================
Same beat, root live=61/62, seq=30. xemu column is 8 samples 1.5 s apart with
the pose block hashed each time as a positive control.

                    before            xemu              after the fix
    +0x3CC          2                 0                 (unread; guard skips)
    +0xE50          15                23 / 25           23 / 25
    +0x11C          128               170 / 171         170 / 171
    +0xE6C          0 at entry        170 / 171         170 / 171  == +0x11C
    frame           0.5, parked       advancing         25 -> 72.5, 1 -> 48.5
    blend           0.0555556 (1/18)  --                1
    pose block      identical x16     8 distinct of 8   MOVED every report

The record diff is what cracked it. The POSITIONS were bit-identical to xemu
(43CBFC57, 43F4F608), so the geometry input was never wrong; only +0x38..+0x4C
differed, and those are written by exactly one branch.


3. WHAT THE EARLIER HANDOVERS GOT WRONG, AND THE LESSON
=======================================================
  * "A second writer exists that runs on hardware and never runs here."
    False. sub_0009E910 runs, 3290+ calls per 10 s window, and writes +0xCE0.
    That conclusion came from diffing 64-byte blocks on two samples 3 s apart:
    the blocks straddle the 12-byte entries, and two samples inside the frozen
    window cannot see that the pose moved for ~30 s first.

  * "The +0xE50 state band is not the problem -- xemu is IDENTICAL."
    The VALUE matched. The WRITE RATE did not. A field rewritten every frame
    reads exactly like one written once, so comparing values against the oracle
    crossed the true culprit off the list. THIS IS THE LESSON: when comparing
    against xemu, compare how often a field is written, not just what it holds.
    Branch counters at the reading site cost nothing and would have caught it.

  * Do not derive a function's extent by measuring to the next NAMED symbol.
    The decompilation names 1332 of ~8868 functions, so the gaps contain real
    unnamed functions; that method reports CPlayer::talk as 2112 bytes and
    claims 477 shredded functions, and both figures are artifacts.

  * Vtable/seed shredding is NOT implicated here. sub_0009E910 does have a
    function carved out of its interior at 0x000A000D, but its generated C
    contains the whole tail; the carved one is an unreferenced duplicate.
    Binary-wide, 1596 of 1604 overlapping pairs are tail_jump_alias, i.e.
    shared-epilogue aliasing.


4. STILL OPEN
=============
  * REGENERATE. The fix is in the lifter; the running proof was a hand-patch of
    the single `je` in the gen tree. Every one of the 54 comiss/ucomiss sites
    needs the corrected emission, and `jp`/`jnp` were returning hardcoded 0/1,
    which silently discarded every NaN test made through the parity flag.

  * ARM vs x86 DEFAULT NaN. Ours is 0x7FC00000, hardware's is 0xFFC00000 --
    opposite sign bits. Visible in the record at +0x10..+0x18. NOT the cause of
    this bug, but it will bite anything that tests a NaN's sign.

  * OUR HEAP RETURNS DIRTY MEMORY where the Xbox's was zeroed. After the fix
    +0x3CC reads as garbage (402717546) because the guard now correctly skips
    the copy and nothing else initialises it. Harmless only because it is read
    solely on the path that has just written it.

  * THE TITLE STALL IS UNRELATED AND STILL THERE. Roughly half of unattended
    runs never leave the title (live=127..165, seq stuck at 12). The CLEAN
    binary does it too. See the previous handover's section 6: read the poll=
    count in [PAD-SCRIPT] lines before blaming a probe, check CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE
    is Debug, and check `ps -A -o %cpu,command -r` before blaming load.
    The attract demo runs at ~54 polls/s against a healthy ~177, which is why
    a human at the pad also experiences it as "input not registering".

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_E6C_IS_ZEROED_EVERY_FRAME.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE, 13 Sep 2026
TWO STATE-ENTRY PATHS FIGHT EVERY FRAME. THAT IS WHY CORN DOES NOT ANIMATE.

Supersedes CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_THE_SECOND_WRITER.txt, whose
central question was built on a premise that does not survive measurement.


0. THE CHAIN, END TO END
========================
There is no missing writer. sub_0009E910 runs here (3290+ calls per 10 s
window) and does write CPlayer +0xCE0. The character freezes because two
state-entry paths both claim the player on every frame:

  A. sub_000A76E0 guards on the state and enters state 23 / 25:
         0x000A7EBD  cmp [eax+0xE50], 0x17     ; already in state 23?
         0x000A7EC4  je  ...                   ; yes -> skip
         0x000A7ECC  call sub_0009B2D0         ; no  -> enter it
     sub_0009B2D0 (id 44) / sub_0009B3E0 (id 45) set state := 0x17 / 0x19,
     set anim from a table, and set +0xE6C := 0. Zeroing +0xE6C is CORRECT
     here -- it is how the engine says "restart this clip".

  B. sub_00080340, the CPlayer exec virtual, runs every frame and dispatches
     on [esi+0x3CC]:
         0x00080716  mov eax, [esi+0x3CC]
                     == 0 -> 0x8073A
                     == 1 -> sub_00092690
                     == 2 -> sub_00092750
     sub_00092750 sets [esi+0x11C] := 0x80 (anim 128) and
     [esi+0xE50] := 0x0F (state 15) -- EXACTLY the frozen values we observe.
     It is the ONLY site in the whole .text that writes 15 to +0xE50.

So each frame: A sets state 23/25 and zeroes +0xE6C; B overwrites state with
15; next frame A's guard sees 15 != 0x17, fires again, and zeroes +0xE6C
again. sub_0009E910 therefore always takes its "animation changed" branch, the
animation timing is reset before it can advance, and the pose is evaluated at
the same phase forever.

THE ORACLE HAS ANSWERED. xemu at the same beat (root live=61, seq=30), eight
samples 1.5 s apart, with the pose block hashed each time as a positive control:

                      ours (frozen)        xemu (animating)
    +0x3CC            2                    0        (8/8)
    +0xE50            15                   23 / 25  (8/8)
    +0x11C            128                  170 / 171 (8/8)
    +0xE6C            0 at entry           170 / 171  == +0x11C
    pose block        identical x16        8 distinct of 8 samples

The control passes -- xemu's pose really is moving -- so the stable e50 there is
meaningful. On hardware +0xE6C EQUALS +0x11C, which is the "same animation"
branch our build never takes.

AND THE SELECTOR IS NOT COMPUTED, IT IS COPIED, under a guard:

    0x000806A8  mov eax, [esi+0x3C8]     ; a record, not a class instance
    0x000806AE  cmp [eax+0x38], ebp      ; ebp = 0
    0x000806B1  je  0x80741              ; [+0x38]==0 -> skip the copy AND the
                                         ;   dispatch at 0x00080716 entirely
    0x000806B7  mov ecx, [eax+0x3C]
    0x000806BA  mov [esi+0x3CC], ecx     ; +0x3CC := [[this+0x3C8]+0x3C]

xemu at the tutorial: [+0x3C8]+0x38 = 0 and +0x3C = 0 for BOTH players, so the
branch is taken, nothing is copied, +0x3CC stays 0, sub_00092750 never runs.
id 44 also reads +0xE58 = 12 = 0xC there -- the value sub_0009B2D0 writes --
so path A ran ONCE and stuck, which is the intended behaviour.

Ours latched +0x3CC = 2 earlier in the run, at a moment when [+0x38] was
nonzero: Codex's probe caught exactly that ("pending=1 kind=2"), and the
report-time probe reads pend=0 kind=2 afterwards. So the copy fired once on a
state hardware never presents, and +0x3CC is sticky thereafter.

THE ONE QUESTION IS NOW: why does [[CPlayer+0x3C8]+0x3C] ever hold 2 here when
it is 0 on hardware -- and why is [+0x38] ever nonzero? The record at +0x3C8 is
not a vtable object; on xemu it reads as floats plus links:

    +00 43CBFC57  +08 43F4F608        (~407.97, ~489.92 -- a position)
    +10 FFC00000 x3                   (sentinel)
    +20 43CBFC57  +28 43F4F608        (the same pair repeated)
    +30 001EC05C  +34 03C13F30        (a static descriptor, and a link to the
                                       OTHER player's record)
    +38 00000000  +3C 00000000        (the guard and the selector source)

So this is a small linked record carrying a position and a static descriptor
pointer, and the fault is in whatever fills it. Dump the same 0x50 bytes on our
side and diff -- that is the next measurement, and it needs no oracle.


1. WHAT THE PREVIOUS HANDOVER GOT WRONG, AND WHY
================================================
It asked "what writes CPlayer +0xCE0 on hardware and never in our build?" and
concluded a second, separate writer exists that we never reach. It reached that
by diffing 64-byte blocks on two samples 3 s apart and finding 0CC0..0DC0
unchanged on our side.

Two flaws:

  * 64-byte blocks straddle the 12-byte entries. One moving float inside a
    block of static neighbours is invisible; the method can report "this region
    does not move" about a region that does.
  * Two samples is not a time series. The block DOES move here -- for about two
    report intervals after the tutorial loads -- and then freezes. Sampling
    twice inside the frozen window says "never moves".

Measured instead with a hash of +0xCE0..+0xDDC taken per report and compared
against the previous report (RECOMP_ANIMATION_STATE, main.c, host-side, no
guest cost). Verdict sequence for both tutorial CPlayers:

    new-object -> MOVED -> MOVED -> static x16   (hash identical throughout)

Also note the registry rebinds: the tutorial constructs NEW CPlayers, so ids
44/45 name different objects before and after. Compare the self pointer or a
rebind reads as movement.


2. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT
==================================
O(1) counters at sub_0009E910 entry, gated on own_id (+0x8) in {44,45},
counting which way `cmp [esi+0x11C], [esi+0xE6C]` goes.

Intro, animating correctly:

    id44 same=2011 changed=37 | id45 same=2009 changed=39     (~54:1)

Corn tutorial, frozen:

    id44 same=184 changed=328  ... 840 ... 1352 ... 4424
    id45 same=185 changed=327  ... 839 ... 1351 ... 4423
    seen id=45 anim=128 prev=0 state=15 frame=0.5 blend=0.0555556

`same` STOPS INCREMENTING ALTOGETHER at 184/185. `changed` rises by exactly
512 per report -- every call. And `prev=0` at entry while the report-time
sample of the same field reads 128, because sub_0009E910 sets it itself at
0x0009EBD6. So the zeroing happens between calls, every frame.

0.0555556 is 1/18: an accumulator reset to zero and advanced exactly one step.


3. THE ZEROING STORE, IDENTIFIED
================================
O(1) counters on all four explicit stores of zero to +0xE6C, gated on
own_id (+0x8) in {44,45}. At the Corn tutorial:

    [E6C-ZERO] pc=0009B2FB id=44 hits=1025 1537 2049 2561 3073 3585
    [E6C-ZERO] pc=0009B40B id=45 hits=1025 1537 2049 2561 3073 3585

512 per report each -- the SAME rate as the "changed" branch counter, and one
per player per frame. The other two candidates (0x0007FF9A, 0x0008372C) do not
fire at the tutorial. So these two stores account for all of it.

0x0009B2FB is in sub_0009B2D0 and 0x0009B40B is in sub_0009B3E0. Both are
small complete functions ending in a real `ret`, not carved fragments. The
decompilation names 0x0009B2D0 `CPlayer::talk`, which fits a dialogue scene --
but that name comes from nearest-preceding-symbol attribution and is NOT
proven; the measurement above is what matters, not the name.

4. WHAT IS NOW EXCLUDED, WITH EVIDENCE
======================================
  * NOT a missing writer. sub_0009E910 runs, 3290+ calls per window.
  * NOT vtable truncation on this path. sub_0009E910 does have a function
    carved out of its interior at 0x000A000D (tail_jump_alias), but its
    generated C contains the whole tail -- loc_000A0003, loc_000A0008, and the
    stores at 0xA000F/0xA0015. The carved function is an unreferenced
    duplicate. Binary-wide there are 1604 overlapping function pairs and 1596
    of the interior ones are tail_jump_alias, i.e. shared-epilogue aliasing,
    not lost code.
  * NOT the jump table at 0xA00BC. 15 targets emitted plus a RECOMP_ITAIL
    fallback; nothing is dropped.
  * NOT a stuck resource load. [[this+0x3C8]+0x38] reads 0 at the tutorial in
    every sample; an earlier reading of 1 was transient.


5. THE PROBES, AND HOW TO RE-RUN THEM
=====================================
Host-side, no guest cost, in main.c behind RECOMP_ANIMATION_STATE:
  [ANIMATION-STATE]  the field band for ids 44/45, sampled outside execution
  [ANIM-BLOCK]       pose hash + MOVED/static/new-object + consecutive runs
  [ANIM-DELTA]       which of the 21 entries moved, and the largest delta

Guest-side, O(1), in a COPY of the gen tree at gen.claude-anim:
  [ANIM-BRANCH]      the entry compare, per id, every 1024 qualifying calls
  [E6C-ZERO]         each of the four zeroing stores, per id

Build and run:

    cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build> \
        -DRECOMP_GEN_DIR=<gen tree> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
    JSRF_BIN=<build>/jsrf_first_fault RECOMP_ANIMATION_STATE=1 \
        diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_scripted.sh <name> \
        @diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/pad/new_game.pad 200


6. THE HARNESS IS ABOUT 50% RELIABLE, AND IT IS NOT PROBE WEIGHT
================================================================
Six runs today stalled at the title (live=127..165, seq stuck at 12
WaitEndTitle). THE CLEAN, UNINSTRUMENTED BINARY STALLS TOO -- that control is
what stops you blaming the probe, and the previous handover's author spent
three runs making exactly that mistake.

Three separable causes, in the order they are cheap to check:

  * READ THE POLL RATE FIRST. Every [PAD-SCRIPT] line carries poll=, which is a
    frame-rate proxy already in every log. Differenced against a good run at
    the same t= it separates the cases in one line:
        t=15  good 1991  bad 2003     (not yet diverged)
        t=39  good 6238  bad 3470     (~61 polls/s vs ~177)
  * CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE. The known-good build/ is Debug. A build dir configured
    without -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug gets an EMPTY build type, different
    optimisation, and stalled the title at only 8% below baseline poll rate.
    grep it out of CMakeCache.txt before trusting any A/B.
  * CPU starvation. The repo is inside iCloud Drive, so copying a gen tree or
    linking a binary wakes cloudd, bird, mds and managedcorespotlightd; load
    average hit 34 that way. uptime alone misleads -- read
    `ps -A -o %cpu,command -r | head`.

There is also a genuine feedback loop once the first menu window is missed: the
title's attract demo loads a full scene (live rises to 127-165), the guest drops
to ~50 polls/s, and the wall-clock pad schedule desynchronises for good. Do not
"fix" this by starting the schedule later -- tried, it is worse, because the
repetition in new_game.pad is the robustness. Loop the whole run instead and
keep the first attempt that reports seq 30.
```

```txt
CLAUDE, 13 Sep 2026 (late night)
THE APU WAS ADDRESSING HALF THE MACHINE. THE MUSIC GAP IS FIXED. THE INTRO IS
STILL AUDIBLY BROKEN AND FOUR OF MY METRICS SAY IT IS FINE.

Supersedes CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_THE_RESAMPLER_AND_FIVE_NON_FIXES.txt and

0. STATE OF PLAY
================
HEAD d449575, pushed to origin/main. tools/recomp 160/160. ctest 21/23, the two
failures deliberate (05e0465).

The default build dir IS the optimised one now, and every log opens with

    [BUILD] title compiled -O2, binary <path>
    [APU] DMA wrap mask 07FFFFFF (128 MB of guest RAM)

A log without those lines predates them; re-take its numbers rather than trust
them. play.sh and measure.sh refuse a binary older than the sources
(JSRF_ALLOW_STALE=1 overrides).

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/measure.sh <name> [seconds] [padfile]
    pad/intro.pad    presses NOTHING -- the only way to capture the intro
    pad/measure.pad  reach the tutorial and stop pressing
    pad/still.pad + pad/moving.pad   identical to t=47, then one holds the stick


1. FIXED TODAY, WITH EVIDENCE
=============================
  * **The APU masked every DMA to 64 MB while the map is 128 MB.** Seven
    accessors in apu_shim.h carried a hardcoded 0x03FFFFFF. An APU read above
    64 MB did not fault; it folded into the wrong half and returned whatever was
    there. JSRF's voice buffers resolve to 0x041E57B0, 0x042E5A10, 0x045CF010 --
    all legal in a 128 MB map, all silently wrapped. Voice 68 played only
    because its buffer happens to live at 0x00B30004.

    This was the ~300 ms music gap at the track change. The title covers the
    change with a second voice (on70 at 42730 ms, off68 at 42762, off70 at
    43024, on68 at 43034 -- only ~10 ms uncovered by design), and that cover
    voice was fetching zeros. Measured: voice 70 energy 0.0 with 432/433 frames
    silent -> 3017.4 with 0/411 silent; worst gap 304 ms -> 14 ms, against
    xemu's whole-run worst of 16 ms. (2d21ce2)

    NOT an xemu artifact -- an EXTRACTION artifact. xemu reads through QEMU's
    real address_space_memory and has no mask at all. The constant appeared when
    that address space became a flat pointer. The category to watch is "what got
    hardcoded when a QEMU abstraction became a raw pointer".

  * **The voice resampler discarded its rate.** `(void)rate;` under a comment
    claiming nearest-neighbour resampling that did not exist. JSRF runs voices
    at 48000, 44100 and 22050 Hz concurrently, so the 22 kHz voice played 2.177x
    too fast. Linear interpolation now, carrying fractional phase across frames;
    unity rate keeps its old path bit-identical. RECOMP_NO_RESAMPLE=1 A/Bs it:
    0 deltas >12000 with it on, 137 with it off. (f464df9)

  * **Vblank ran 4% fast for the life of the port.** BRIDGE_VBLANK_PERIOD_MS was
    16 under a comment saying 60 Hz; 1000/16 is 62.5. A fractional macro does not
    fix it -- both operands are DWORD, so `now + 16.683` truncates every call.
    bridge_vblank_step_ms carries the remainder. Measured 62.3 -> 59.7 Hz against
    59.94. Frame rate unchanged; correctness, not speed. (cfd07a3)

  * **MmQueryStatistics reported 64 MB unconditionally**, silently defeating
    RECOMP_TOTAL_RAM_MB. (c2afab2)

  * getenv was half the pushbuffer executor's CPU (855308c); five C tests did
    not LINK and ctest called that "Not Run" (81eaf21); the default build dir was
    the -O0 tree while every measurement used another binary (2f7c741).


2. THE OPEN BUG, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT ONE
============================================
**The intro audio is audibly broken and every sample-level metric says it is
fine.** The user's words: ours "super glitchy", xemu's "perfect".

Ours and xemu's 30-second attract clips, aligned on the music's first note:

    peak 9882 / 10183   d50 527 / 535   d99 2404 / 2520   dmax 7050 / 6667
    deltas >2k 37460 / 45762    >4k 267 / 374    gaps 1 / 1

Statistically indistinguishable, OURS WITH FEWER LARGE JUMPS. One sounds broken.

**The live candidate: the buffer wrap.** Voice 68's bounds are incoherent in
every capture taken today:

    ba=00001004 cbo=0     ebo=16383
    ba=00001004 cbo=14740 ebo=32
    ba=00001004 cbo=13711 ebo=32      (different run)

The cursor sits thousands of samples past the declared end of a LOOPING buffer.
voice_get_samples runs `for (; sample_count < requested && cbo <= ebo; cbo++)`
and then `if (cbo >= ebo) { if (loop) cbo = lbo; }` with lbo=0 -- so that state
produces zero samples, snaps the cursor to 0, and the next call plays samples
0..32, which is 0.69 ms, before snapping back. A voice stuck there replays a
fragment forever, and every sample of it is valid music.

**That is why the statistics cannot see it: the defect is in WHICH samples get
played, not in the samples.**

THE EXPERIMENT IS BUILT AND NOT YET RUN. RECOMP_VOICE_RATES now counts per voice
`loopbacks` and `starved_loops` -- wraps that produced NOTHING first. A healthy
stream wraps after playing a bufferful; a stuttering one wraps on an empty
buffer. Run measure.sh with pad/intro.pad and read voice 68's line. If
starved_loops is large, it is confirmed, and the next question is who is
supposed to advance ebo (the guest writes it through NV_PAVS_VOICE_PAR_NEXT --
check we are not dropping or mis-decoding that write).


3. HOW TO MEASURE THIS, BECAUSE I GOT IT WRONG FOUR TIMES
=========================================================
Four metrics of mine called an audibly broken capture clean. Each looked
reasonable. Do not rebuild them and believe them.

  * **Delta distributions** (|x[k]-x[k-1]|). Found the resampler bug honestly,
    then said the intro was fine. A replayed buffer has normal deltas.
  * **Silence-gap detection** with |sample|<64. That threshold fires on every
    zero crossing: 8830 of 8850 "silence runs" in one window were ONE SAMPLE
    long, and I reported "550 of 551 discontinuities are near silence" from it.
    It meant "near a zero crossing", which is true of nearly all audio.
  * **Autocorrelation for echo.** Measures tonality. It scored the tutorial
    HIGHER than the intro (0.520 vs 0.016) because sustained notes look like
    echoes.
  * **Log-frequency spectral alignment** for pitch. Flat -- 0.512 down to 0.495
    across ratios 0.88 to 1.00. No peak. Reported as inconclusive, correctly,
    but only after I nearly read a "-12.2% pitch error" out of noise.

  And one dump that produced pure fiction: printing guest[ba] for a voice
  descriptor. BA is NOT an address -- it is a linear offset through the
  VPSGEADDR scatter-gather table. Printed raw it gave a tidy story about voices
  pointing into low memory and into the game's own code. Translate with
  get_data_ptr or do not print.

  **What DID work: the user's ears, and structural counters.** Per-voice output
  energy found the silent cover voice in one run. The loopback counter above is
  the same shape. Count events in the mechanism; do not characterise the output.


4. THINGS THAT MEASURED AS NOTHING

All committed saying so. Do not re-derive.

  * **Skipping unstored VSH units**: vsh 16.07 -> 14.25 ms/frame, frame time
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-13_THE_BLACK_SCREEN_WAS_OURS.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- THE BLACK SCREEN WAS A LOST `pop esi`, AND THE TITLE NOW
                 REACHES THE CORN TUTORIAL UNATTENDED
Date: 2026-09-13 (Europe/London), morning
From: Claude.

Supersedes CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_THE_IDLE_LOOP_FREEZE.txt on its central
claim. That handover's task list was right and its diagnosis was not.


0. THE ONE-LINE ANSWER
======================
Nothing ever set m_bFatal. CActMan::Idle's `this` was a CODE ADDRESS, because
a switch dispatcher's arms were never translated and the arm's `pop esi` never
ran. Three translator fixes later the title reaches the Corn tutorial with
nobody at the machine, zero ABI violations, rendering and presenting.


1. WHAT LANDED (three commits on main)
======================================
68569e8  RECOMP_PAD_SCRIPT -- a timed press schedule.
    "12:START 13.5:START 15:A", or @file. t is measured from xbox_InputInit,
    not the first poll. MERGES with a live controller rather than replacing it,
    and reports port 0 connected with no hardware attached.
    run_scripted.sh drives it; JSRF_BIN selects the binary.

b8abfea  RECOMP_SEQ_TRACE -- the title's own top-level state, by name.
    CActSequence::m_dwNextMethod at +0x48, dispatched through the 64-entry
    table at guest 0x0020D2B8. All 64 names come from the decompilation and are
    CHECKED against the live table on the first poll; a mismatch suppresses the
    names rather than lying. One host thread, 100 Hz, prints on change only.

d013f03  A function must contain its own switch arms.
    Two defects, both stopping a dispatcher absorbing its arms. See section 3.


2. THE FREEZE, AND WHY 12 SEP GOT IT WRONG
==========================================
12 Sep concluded "so m_bFatal is set" from /usr/bin/sample finding the guest in
CActMan::Idle's readInput/Sleep arm. The sample was right. The inference was
not: the arm runs when MEM32(esi+0x24) is nonzero, and esi was not the object.

Probes on BOTH arms, the healthy one as the positive control:

    00013F97 this=040D3A70 field=00000000 calls=2792   healthy
    00013FA0 this=00013B24 field=6AF88B00 calls=6385   freeze

0x00013B24 is the return address pushed for the call at 0x00013B1F. With
RECOMP_ABI_CHECK armed the cascade falls out in one run, innermost first:

    [ABI/I] sub_0006D770: esp(epilogue never ran)
    [ABI/C] sub_00011070: esi 0492E2F0 -> 0001108A
    [ABI/C] sub_000123E0: esi 040D3A70 -> 000124C3
    [ABI/C] sub_00013A80: esi 040D3A70 -> 00013B24

THE LESSON, and it is the same one as 12 Sep's section 4: a counter that says
"the flag is set" is only as good as the pointer it was read through. The fix
was to probe both branches and record `this`, not the field.


3. THE TRANSLATOR DEFECTS
=========================
(a) LATER ARMS OF A CARVED RUN. 289f21f drops a switch's first arm. That alone
    leaves the dispatcher ending at the jump, so arm 1 is owned by arm 0, arm 2
    by arm 1, and the dispatch is outside every one of those owners. New test:
    walking back from the arm to the function holding the dispatch, everything
    crossed is an entry of the SAME table. Asked in the classifier AND in the
    interior gate -- a seed the gate turns away is never classified.
        switch_arm drops 533 -> 1333; carves 35 -> 17, all 17 16-aligned.

(b) STALE ALIAS EXTENTS. Every pass recording an alias extent runs before
    _pass_demote_interior_seeds rebuilds the function set. A body is
    re-measured only when its end is PROVABLY wrong: it contains a
    `jmp [reg*4+table]`, the table resolves, and arms lie outside the body
    dispatching them. A function cannot end at its own switch and exclude its
    own cases -- and while it does, _analyze_switch_table refuses the table
    (it needs func_start <= arm < func_end), so the arms are never translated.

THREE THINGS I GOT WRONG IN (b), each settled by measurement:
  * The clamp counted ALIASES as boundaries. An alias is an alternate ENTRY
    into a body, not a boundary -- _build_alias_entries overlaps them
    deliberately. Cost: 198 of 200 dispatches lost their arms.
  * With no clamp at all the walk ran away, exactly as 289f21f documents:
    49 of 124 bodies crossed a real start and became overlapping duplicates.
  * The trigger looked only at the body's LAST instruction. A body cut AFTER
    its dispatch and still short of its arms is skipped entirely. That left
    156 of 161 cases untouched, sub_00114A80 among them.


4. WHERE THE TITLE IS NOW
=========================
Unattended, one schedule, no human:

    logos -> title -> New Game -> Corn tutorial (live=61), HELD for 250 s
    ABI violations reaching the tutorial:  4 -> 0
    dispatches whose arms fall outside:  276 -> 154
    framebuffer: presenting ~202,000 nonzero, changing
    +7930/+7934 = FFFFFFFF (in-tutorial marker), m_bFatal=0, not paused

sub_0006D770  22 -> 488 bytes    sub_0007E550  37 -> 314
sub_000F8B10  68 -> 1408         sub_00114A80  692 -> 1296

CONTROL PRESERVED, read-only, with CONTROL_README.txt:
    gen.freeze-repro/          pre-regeneration tree
    jsrf_first_fault.CONTROL   its binary
    build-ab/                  its build dir


5. THE OPEN ITEM
================
The tutorial does not advance. It holds live=61 (cutscene) and never reaches
65 (gameplay). On screen the prompt reads "Press the" and stops; the strings in
the XBE are COMPLETE ('Press the A Button!' at 0x001D2758), so the truncation
is in rendering or in a progressive reveal, not the data. Dialogue DOES advance
-- a scripted A every 8 s walked through several lines -- so input reaches the
tutorial. 13,876 nonneutral polls with a human on the pad did not move it.

THAT MEASUREMENT IS NOW DONE, and it came back CLEAN.

JSRF_STARTUP_ABI_CHECK arms ONLY recomp_0000.c, so every violation seen earlier
in another chunk was an INDIRECT call caught by the armed kernel layer, and
direct-call clobbers outside chunk 0 had been invisible all session. Rebuilt
with JSRF_ABI_CHECK_ALL=ON and run to the tutorial, the whole path reports FOUR
violations and all four are the CRT signatures already called expected on
12 Sep:

    sub_0017CAB0  esp delta -6032          __chkstk's stack probe
    sub_0017D1F8  esp(epilogue never ran)  __SEH_prolog
    sub_0017D231  ebx esi edi, esp +140    __SEH_epilog
    sub_001816B0  ebx, esp +20             icall targets all FE0000xx

So there is NO unexplained register clobber left on the path to the tutorial.
The 154 remaining dispatches whose arms fall outside their body are either not
executed here or do not clobber. Do not spend the next session on them
expecting the tutorial to move.

AND THE GUEST IS NOT HUNG. Kernel calls climb 913,139 -> 921,107 between two
reports and the pusher keeps acking (12,896 -> 13,055). The frame loop runs and
re-presents the same image. This is a state the title will not leave, not a
stall in our translation.

SO THE TUTORIAL IS A GAME-LOGIC OR RENDERING PROBLEM, and it is very likely the
one already on file: the CPlayer animation gate (Corn is object id 45, id 44 is
static by design) and the 17x update asymmetry between the two CPlayers. Those
leads were recorded when reaching the tutorial cost a human playthrough. They
are now reachable unattended, in about 50 seconds, with one schedule.


6. RULES PAID FOR THIS SESSION
==============================
  * A predicate over a function body must consider the WHOLE body. I reasoned
    from the last instruction twice and was wrong twice.
  * An A/B is only an A/B if one variable moved. I attributed a dead title
    screen to the gen tree when the controller had been unplugged at the same
    moment; the correlation held over five runs and was still a coincidence.
  * "Only real starts clamp" is not a heuristic, it is the definition of an
    alias. Deriving it from the concept would have been faster than the 198/200
    measurement that eventually forced it.


7. THE TUTORIAL STALL, TRACED (added later the same day)
========================================================
Reaching the tutorial unattended made this cheap, so it was worked properly.
Every measurement below had a control run against the untouched binary first
and was REJECTED if progression to the tutorial differed. Three were.

WHAT THE FRAME IS DOING
    Corn's exec virtual keeps being dispatched -- 2550, 2815, 3081, 3348 over
    successive reports -- so this is not an update-selection gate above
    CPlayer. 16 of 27 registered objects change every report, both CPlayers
    among them, and the changing set is identical each time. "Corn is frozen"
    was wrong; only the state indices and the pose blocks are pinned.

THE STRUCTURE, from the binary rather than from memory
    CPlayer vtable      0x001CCFF8
    slot 1 (exec)       sub_00080340       <- what the walker dispatches
    slots 4,7,8,10,11,13,14 = 0x00011C90   <- every non-Default mode IS a nop

THE TWO PREDICATES, both inside sub_00080340
    0x00080340:  eax = [this+0xE50]
                 if (eax <  0x14) <timer path>
                 if (eax <= 0x1A) skip          <- taken, every frame
    0x00080407:  eax = [this+0x2D0]
                 if ([eax+0x38] == 0) goto 0x0008066E
                                                <- taken, every frame; jumps
                    past +0xCB0, +0xCA4, +0x13C.. and the +0xCE0 loop

    Measured from the first frame the tutorial scene exists:
        id=44  e50=23  r2d0=04839950  r38=0
        id=45  e50=25  r2d0=04846280  r38=0
    The resource pointer is VALID; the field inside it is zero and stays zero.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ABSENT, at 64-byte resolution
    id 44 changes exactly blocks 0C80 and 1340 -- which is where xemu's
    reference puts its only two moving dwords (+0xC94, +0x134C). The control
    behaves correctly, so the instrument is not dead.
    id 45 changes 0C80, 11C0, 1440, 1600..17C0 and NOT 0CC0..0DC0, NOT
    12C0..13C0, NOT 1480..14C0 -- the +0x0CE0..+0x0DE4, +0x12C0.. and
    +0x1484.. groups the 11 Sep xemu differential named. Positive control for
    the absence: 0C80 moves on the same object, 96 bytes below a block that
    never does.

WHAT THE SKIPPED LOOP IS, and why the first reading was too strong
    sub_0014C340 is a three-float VECTOR ADD, not a copy:
        for (i = 0; i < 21; i++)
            (this+0xCE0 + i*12).xyz += ([this+0x2D0]+0x3C).xyz;
    So +0xCE0..+0xDDC is 21 positions translated by ONE delta, and [res+0x38]
    gates whether the delta is applied. Zero there is consistent with "this
    character is not moving", which in a cutscene may be CORRECT. The pose gate
    is therefore probably a SYMPTOM of the parked state, not a second defect.

THE STATE BAND
    +0xE50 in 0x14..0x1A is written by one contiguous family, and nothing else
    writes those values:
        sub_0009C4D0 0x14   sub_0009C550 0x15   sub_0009C600 0x16
        sub_0009B2D0 0x17   sub_0009B350 0x18   sub_0009B3E0 0x19
        sub_0009B4B0 0x1A
    The 0x17 and 0x19 setters -- the two parked values -- are both called from
    sub_000A76E0, a 3000-byte function at .rdata vtable slot 0x001CD574, i.e. a
    virtual on a class OTHER than CPlayer. +0x11C reads 170/171 for ids 44/45,
    the same pair recorded on 10 Sep.

NEXT, AND IT IS A REFERENCE QUESTION NOT A STATIC ONE
    Ask xemu what +0xE50 is for Corn at the same moment.
      * If xemu also shows 25, the state is right and the fault is in what the
        state's handler does -- keep going down from sub_000A76E0.
      * If xemu shows something outside 0x14..0x1A, the fault is in how the
        state was chosen, and the 0x09/0x0A family is where it should have
        gone instead.
    +0xE50 is now a cheap proven marker readable from the existing hook at
    0x00011083, so this is one run per side.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately not answered: whether Draw is called for Corn. It
needs a second walker hook, which the one-probe discipline ruled out. The
vector-add reading makes a pure render fault unlikely, but that is an inference.

INSTRUMENT NOTES, because two of these cost runs
  * jsrf_func_arg does a LINEAR SCAN of up to 384 entries per call. At two hot
    CPlayer sites it perturbed the guest enough that the title stopped
    responding. jsrf_func_hit is a direct-mapped O(1) increment; prefer it.
  * RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP writes a JSON file per report. At any cadence fast
    enough to bracket the stall the I/O stalls the title (live=157, not 61 --
    twice). Its 128-file cap was also spent before the tutorial loaded, on
    EMPTY dumps, because it carried its own bare-range root check instead of
    the low-16 rule. Both fixed, but for "what is still changing" use
    RECOMP_OBJECT_ACTIVITY / RECOMP_OBJECT_BLOCKS, which write nothing.


8. G1 ANSWERED BY XEMU, AND IT KILLS THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS
===========================================================
xemu, US ISO, at the Corn tutorial on the "This is the GG's Garage" beat, read
through the GDB stub with diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/xemu_cplayer_state.py.

FIELD FOR FIELD, XEMU IS IDENTICAL TO US:

                  ours                        xemu
    scene         live=61 seq=30              live=61 seq=30
    id 44         e50=23 s11c=AA r38=0        e50=23 s11c=AA r38=0
    id 45         e50=25 s11c=AB r38=0        e50=25 s11c=AB r38=0

and static across three samples over six seconds on BOTH sides -- while Corn is
visibly animating in xemu (two screenshots, different arm poses).

So both of the predicates found in section 7 are CORRECT BEHAVIOUR:
  * +0xE50 parked in 0x14..0x1A is what the real console does here.
  * [[this+0x2D0]+0x38] == 0, skipping the sub_00080340 pose writes, is what
    the real console does here.
Neither is the fault. The 0x14..0x1A band and sub_000A76E0 are exonerated, and
the plan in JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-13 branch one is dead.

WHERE THE ANIMATION ACTUALLY COMES FROM, same beat, 64-byte blocks, 3 s apart:

    xemu id=45   30/96 changed: 09C0 0C80 0CC0 0D00 0D40 0D80 0DC0 0E80
                                11C0 1200 12C0 1300 1340 1380 13C0 1400
                                1440 1480 14C0 1540 1580 15C0 1600 1640
                                1680 16C0 1700 1740 ...
    ours id=45   10/96 changed: 0C80 11C0 1440 1600 1640 1680 16C0 1700
                                1780 17C0
    xemu id=44   26/96 changed (including 0CC0..0DC0)
    ours id=44    5/96 changed: 0C80 1240 1280 12C0 1340

xemu writes +0x0CE0..+0x0DC0 -- the transform block -- WITH r38 == 0 and e50 in
the skip band. The loop at 0x000804A1 is therefore correctly skipped on both
sides, and A SECOND, SEPARATE WRITER OF +0xCE0 EXISTS THAT RUNS IN XEMU AND
NEVER RUNS IN OURS. Both CPlayers animate there; neither does here.

That second writer is the target. It is not reachable by grepping for a literal
"+ 0xCE0" -- section 7 already showed no RECOMP_MEM_WRITE32 targets it, and the
known 0x804A1 loop writes through a computed pointer via sub_0014C340.

HOW I BROKE THE ORACLE, so the next session does not
    A GDB write watchpoint (Z2) on Corn's +0xCE0 was accepted with OK and then
    never trapped in 20 s. Reading registers while the guest was running
    desynchronised the stream, and the stub then refused new connections --
    exactly the failure xemu_rsp.py's own docstring warns about in its first
    paragraph. The port stays LISTENing with a dead peer; xemu must be
    restarted and the tutorial replayed.

    Do not send `g` or any register read unless a stop reply has actually been
    received. Probe with a memory read first, and if a watchpoint does not trap
    within a few seconds, remove it with z2 BEFORE touching anything else.
    Better: the block-delta method above needs no watchpoints at all and got
    the whole answer.
```

```txt
2. FIXED, WITH EVIDENCE
=======================
  * **A refused blend was deleting whole draws.** prepare_texture_copy accepted
    only ZERO/ONE/SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, because the factor was one
    scalar and DST_COLOR is per-channel. JSRF asks for DST_COLOR/ZERO, a
    multiply blend; a refusal there is not a degraded draw, nv2a_pb_exec.c:2117
    returns and the batch reaches NEITHER sink. **6034 draws deleted in a 150 s
    run**, onset the moment the tutorial scene loads. Now per-channel in all
    three sinks behind one predicate. Measured: rejected 6034 -> 0 over 733,909
    draws. (ac38c32)

  * **The floor was culled by an inverted winding.** area() runs on positions
    the guest already perspective-divided, and dividing by a negative w negates
    x and y, so a triangle with an ODD number of vertices behind the camera
    arrives wound backwards. Large ground quads near the camera straddle; small
    objects on them do not, which is exactly what the screen showed. Census over
    106M triangles: 1,908,636 straddling, of which **955,965 culled** -- the
    entire half that faces the viewer. Correction is a parity of sign bits
    (the product overflows; w reaches 1e31). (d6230da)

  * **The depth policy was at the wrong stage and the wrong way round.** We
    clamped z into a hardcoded range in the VERTEX shader. The range is right --
    SET_CLIP_MIN/MAX captured live read 0 and 16777215 -- but clamping before
    the perspective multiply corrupts the endpoint the clipper interpolates
    from, and NV097_SET_ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL asks for CULL, not clamp: ZCLAMP_EN is
    a FOUR-BIT field at 0xF0, and JSRF writes 1, so 1 & 0xF0 == 0 == CULL. Read
    as bit 0 it looks like CLAMP and means the opposite. Now: no vertex clamp,
    depth clamp always on, cull-or-clamp per fragment in guest z units, which is
    what xemu does. RECOMP_LEGACY_ZCLAMP=1 A/Bs it. (d6230da)

  * **Crash reports name the crash now.** 37 of 277 archived runs end in a
    guest fault (13%) and none could say where -- LAST INSTRUMENTED GUEST
    FUNCTION reports the tracer's last sighting, which on a worker-thread fault
    is the thread trampoline. dladdr on HOST PC/LR fixes it; 9100 of 9140
    generated sub_* are external symbols. First real fault after the change
    named itself immediately. (680c753)

  * **Housekeeping.** Four backports the lifter outgrew retired (two KEPT and
    still failing on purpose -- they are two of the four reachable dead
    branches); ratchet regated on the reachable count (4, was an unpassable 76);
    in/out/wbinvd now say they are deliberately ignored. 153 -> 160 tests.
    (05e0465)

  * **A regeneration landed**, merging the runtime icall dump. Translation
    "failed": 0. Verified to live=157 with 0 crashes and 0 blend rejects.

4. WHAT IS LEFT, IN THE ORDER I WOULD TAKE IT
=============================================
**(1) SPEED -- and the first move is a config change, not code.**

    CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=Debug
    CMAKE_C_FLAGS_DEBUG:STRING=-g

The whole title, all 1.3M lines of generated C included, is compiled at -O0.
Measured on this machine at 640x480: the RGB565 convert loop is 1.038 ms at -O0
and 0.201 ms at -O2 (5.2x); the depth loop 1.264 -> 0.203 (7.5x). Memory already
lists an unset CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE as one of three causes of the title stall, so
this has regressed before. Do this FIRST and re-measure everything after it --
several numbers in this file are -O0 numbers.

**(2) The Metal vertex/index ring, uncommitted in the tree.** Replaces 304,980
per-batch MTLBuffer allocations (measured 4.88 us at 16 KB, 8.17 us at 64 KB)
with bump allocation from 8 x 2 MiB slabs, ~6 ns per reservation. Safety against
in-flight GPU work is an atomic in-flight count per slab plus a condvar on wrap,
and it was stress-tested over 20,000 real command buffers with a positive
control that reproduces corruption when the pin is removed. **It has never been
run in the game.** Build it, run it, and read RECOMP_METAL_RING_AUDIT.

**(3) The 13% crash is a USB use-after-free, not a pool bug.** 0x27DBC0 is a
virtual-minus-physical BIAS and is legitimately 0 on this host every run --
kernel_bridge.c:1930 returns the VA unchanged, so EAX=0 carries no information.
The fault operand is 0xFFFFFFF0, the guest's own free-list poison: sub_001C2403
ORs -1 into descriptor +8 on free. This is the Xbox OHCI driver (XBE section
XPP), and we are dereferencing a freed USB descriptor. Our own source already
records the same fault address at xbox_usb_ohci.c:645. Prime suspect:
xbox_OhciServiceList writes guest descriptor memory (td[2], ed[2]) from TWO
threads with no mutual exclusion -- ohci_periodic_tick on the ack thread
(xbox_memory_layout.c:810) and mcpx_trap_handler on the guest thread (:1324,
:1330). Fix is a dedicated OHCI lock across both call sites -- NOT mcpx_lock,
see the APU-lock-inversion lesson. Test: 30 boots, 13% -> 0.
**The user's intermittent controller stalls are very likely the same bug.**

**(4) Black bars and a grey ellipse** in the attract/title scenes. Real, in the
framebuffer, unexplained, predate today's fixes.

**(5) `oPos is not finite`** kills whole batches -- 52 of 166k. VSH_REJECT drops
the entire batch while the sinks already drop non-finite vertices per triangle,
so the batch-level kill is stricter than it needs to be -- but the NaN is a
producer bug, so find the producer first.

**(6) Sub-pixel viewport offset.** SET_VIEWPORT_OFFSET.x reads 320.531 on a
640-wide surface; our inverse transform assumes exactly 320. We never handle
SET_VIEWPORT_SCALE/OFFSET at all. Half a pixel, but it is free information we
are throwing away.

  * `s_gpu.tris_drawn` counts triangles SUBMITTED, after CPU culling and before

    draws refused by prepare_texture_copy; `[VSH] executed batches=N rejected=M`

    nothing; RECOMP_PB_EXEC_TOP raises the cut.
  * `symbolize.py callers` does not follow tail-jmp thunks, so it will tell you
    a function has no caller when it has one. That is how I convinced myself an
```
