```txt
1. THE METHOD, AGAIN, BECAUSE IT CAUGHT A WHOLE DAY'S WRONG CONCLUSION
======================================================================
**Read what increments a counter before you difference it.** The previous
session's z-clipping finding rested on an A/B of `s_gpu.tris_drawn` with
RECOMP_METAL_DEPTH_CLAMP on and off, 18.46M against 15.26M. That counter is
`nv2a_metal_draw`'s return value, `n/3` -- triangles assembled and culled,
computed BEFORE the render encoder is created. The clip mode is set on the
encoder afterwards. The counter cannot respond to it, at all. The two numbers
differed because the two runs got different distances into the title.

This is the third counter in this project to lie in the same way, and the rule
in CLAUDE.md already said so. It is cheap to check and it was not checked.

The second half of the method: **when you think geometry is being dropped,
count the drops at every stage, and split each bucket by whether the geometry
had any business being drawn.** A raw drop count is meaningless -- most
dropped triangles are supposed to be dropped.


2. RETRACTED, WITH THE MEASUREMENT THAT DID IT
==============================================
`RECOMP_METAL_CLIP_AUDIT=1` (new, opt-in, read-only, in nv2a_metal.m)
recomputes on the CPU exactly the clip position the vertex shader emits and
applies exactly Metal's volume to it. Over 37.7M triangles at the Corn
tutorial:

    discarded by the far plane                           0
    discarded while fully on screen with every w > 0     0

Both zero. The far plane CANNOT fire: the shader clamps z into [0,16777215]
and only then multiplies by w, so 0 <= z*w <= w holds identically for w > 0.
For w > 0 the side planes reduce to "every vertex beyond one screen edge",
which is correct culling. Every discard the audit finds has w < 0 -- geometry
behind the camera, which the guest's own perspective divide mirrors through
the viewport origin, so it lands on screen looking legitimate. Discarding it
is right, and recovering it is all RECOMP_METAL_DEPTH_CLAMP ever did: it drew
mirrored garbage over large areas, which is why it halved the frame rate.

The clamp switch stays, off, as the positive control for this class of claim.

Two more figures the audit settles, so nobody spends a day on them:
  * 14.5% of assembled triangles have ZERO AREA -- but 98.9% of those have a
    duplicate vertex. Triangle-strip stitching. Supposed to vanish. (xemu
    ground truth agrees JSRF is strip-dominated: 2002 strips vs 0 plain
    triangle lists at the tutorial.)
  * 42.5% backface culled, with front_cw on 113.0M of 113.1M. Ordinary. And
    front_ccw occurs ONLY when culling is off -- exactly equal counts, every
    report -- so the winding plumbing is not misread.


3. FIXED: THE DRAWS THAT WERE BEING DELETED
===========================================
`prepare_texture_copy` accepted four blend factors: ZERO, ONE, SRC_ALPHA,
ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA. The factor was modelled as one scalar float, and
DST_COLOR is per-channel, so it could not be expressed and was refused.

JSRF asks for **DST_COLOR/ZERO**, a multiply blend. A refusal there is not a
degraded draw. prepare_texture_copy returns an error, nv2a_pb_exec.c:2117
returns, and the batch reaches NEITHER Metal NOR the CPU rasteriser. It is
deleted. Measured before the fix: **6034 draws in a 150 s run**, onset the
exact moment the tutorial scene loads, recurring about once a frame, count
rising monotonically (0,0,0,0,27,134,410,692,1039,1802,4200,5542,5828,6034).

A deleted draw is a whole flat piece of scene that never gets painted. That is
the reported symptom, and it had nothing to do with clipping.

Fixed: per-channel factors in all three sinks -- the Metal fragment shader, the
CPU rasteriser, and the D3D11 blend state which supports them natively -- gated
by one shared predicate, `nv2a_texture_copy_blend_factor_supported`, so the
three cannot drift apart. The destination-ALPHA factors stay refused and the
comment says why: the Metal surface keeps its 24-bit depth in the alpha
channel, so there is no destination alpha there to read. Adding them means
giving that path a real alpha channel first.

Also removed from all three: a silent `default:` that returned ONE_MINUS_SRC
_ALPHA for any factor it did not recognise. An unreachable factor now
contributes nothing rather than quietly rendering as something else.

MEASURED AFTER: the same state logs without REFUSED; rejected falls 6034 -> 0
across 733,909 draws; the run reaches live=161 with no fault. Confirmed again
on two further runs, 370,790 and 389,792 draws, rejected=0 on both.

**NOT VERIFIED VISUALLY.** Nobody has looked at the screen since the fix. Those
6034 draws per run now paint something that was previously invisible, and a
multiply blend that is subtly wrong will look like a dark overlay rather than
like nothing. That is the first thing to check.


4. FIXED: A CRASH REPORT THAT COULD NOT NAME THE CRASH
======================================================
37 of 277 archived runs end in a guest fault -- **13%** -- and none of the
reports say where. Two sites dominate LAST INSTRUMENTED GUEST FUNCTION:

    19  sub_00147EBB   XapiThreadStartup(DWORD, DWORD)
    15  sub_00177FE0   Controller::AddRef(Controller *this)

The first is not a crashing function. It is the thread entry trampoline, and
that line reports the most recent function the TRACER saw, which on a
worker-thread fault is many frames above the code that died. GUEST EIP/BLOCK
reads `unavailable` on all of them and GUEST REGISTERS is the main thread's
globals, not the faulting thread's.

`describe_host_address()` now runs dladdr on HOST PC and HOST LR. 9100 of the
9140 generated sub_* are external symbols, so a fault in translated code gets
a name and an offset. Caveats are in the comment: dladdr returns the nearest
PRECEDING symbol (a four-digit offset means the name is a neighbour, not the
answer), and _DARWIN_C_SOURCE must precede the include or it compiles and then
fails at the call.

Verified standalone, NOT yet on a real fault -- three runs afterwards did not
crash, which at 13% is the likely outcome and is not evidence either way.

WHAT THE FAULT ADDRESSES SAY, for whoever picks this up (guest base
0x300000000):

    20x  0x3FFFFFFxx   guest 0xFFFFFFxx. A small NEGATIVE value used as a
                       pointer: EAX=FFFFFFB4 (-76) read at +10, ESI=FFFFFFF0
                       (-16) read at +8. The `NULL - offset` shape of an
                       unterminated list walk or an unchecked lookup.
    13x  0x385.. 0x38B..  guest 0x8xxxxxxx, the physical-window alias range.

Get one crash with the new report and it should name the function directly.
```

```txt
    cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build>
    cmake --build <build> -j 6

To measure rather than play, there is a new script:

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/measure.sh <name> [seconds] [padfile]
    JSRF_BIN=<path> ... to A/B two binaries

Build dirs left behind, all current, all with the same source:
    build-O2   the default, -O2 title          <- use this
    build-O0   -O0 title, identical otherwise  <- the control for section 1
    build/     the old Debug tree, untouched, still the archived-baseline build


1. THE RETRACTION, FIRST
========================
The previous handover's item (1) was "SPEED -- and the first move is a config
change, not code", on the grounds that the whole program including the runtime
was compiled at -O0, with the RGB565 convert loop measured 5.2x faster at -O2
and the depth loop 7.5x.

**The premise is wrong, and it was checkable in thirty seconds.** Every runtime
library sets its own -O2 in target_compile_options -- xbox_vsh, xbox_kernel,
xbox_apu, xbox_nv2a, platform -- and target options come after
CMAKE_C_FLAGS_<CONFIG> on the command line, so they win. Those libraries have
been at -O2 in the Debug tree all along. Read it out of a configured tree:

    grep -h '^C_FLAGS =' <build>/xboxrecomp/src/*/CMakeFiles/*.dir/flags.make

The RGB565 and depth loops live in xbox_vsh and xbox_kernel. They were ALREADY
optimised in the shipped build. The microbenchmark that produced 5.2x and 7.5x
was timing code nobody ships at -O0. CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE reaches exactly one
library in this project, xbox_video, the FMV player.

What WAS at -O0 is the recompiled title itself, whose flags are set explicitly
and ignore the build type. That is now -O2 (section 2). It did not make the
game faster either, and section 3 says what does.


2. -O2 ON THE TITLE: WHAT IT DID AND DID NOT BUY
=================================================
JSRF_OPT_LEVEL in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/CMakeLists.txt, default -O2,
set it to -O0 to get the bring-up build back. -g and frame pointers stay on --
the crash reporter symbolises host PC/LR through dladdr and walks the frame
chain, and that is the only thing that can name a worker-thread fault.
RelWithDebInfo deliberately carries no -DNDEBUG: the APU model is xemu's and is
held together by assert(), and deleting every bounds check is a semantic change
wearing an optimisation's clothes.

DID buy: the binary drops 42.7 MB -> 29.7 MB, and _tlv_get_addr -- recorded in
recomp_types.h as "the biggest single cost in the program on BOTH hosts", about
75% of the main guest thread's samples at -O0 -- falls to 22 samples out of
~37,000 in a profile. The compiler CSEs the thread-local address per function,
which is what the reverted register-context rewrite was trying to do by hand.
That also retroactively explains why that rewrite measured 30.55s vs 30.69s:
the TLS lookup was never the bottleneck, so removing it changed nothing.

DID NOT buy: any frame time. Scene-matched, -O0 and -O2 are identical within
noise. Same source, same schedule, 210 s each, comparing only windows in the
same scene:

    scene     -O0 flips/window   p50      -O2 flips/window   p50
    live=131       118.0        89.5 ms        114.0        93.5 ms
    live=133       108.5        95.0 ms        104.0        99.2 ms
    live=137       106.5        89.2 ms        105.0        90.2 ms

**Do not read the first measurement I took as evidence.** With a 150 s budget
the -O2 build reached the Corn tutorial and the -O0 build did not, and its
cumulative flip count was 28% higher. Both facts are real and neither is about
speed: they are the run-to-run depth variance the previous handover already
warned about ("296k draws and live=61 on one run, 733k and live=161 on the
next, same binary"). Match the scene or measure nothing.

I kept -O2 anyway -- smaller, no measured regression, and the CPU efficiency
will matter once section 3 is fixed -- but it is not the win, and anyone
reporting it as one has not matched scenes.


3. WHERE THE TIME ACTUALLY GOES
===============================
12 s `sample` of the -O2 build sitting in the Corn tutorial (live=61):

    __psynch_cvwait              44037
    __semwait_signal             42129
    __workq_kernreturn           40463
    mach_msg2_trap               26256
    semaphore_wait_trap          26010
    sub_0013B180                  8670   <- the only large compute entry
    semaphore_wait_signal_trap    8633
    swtch_pri                     7040
    nv2a_vsh_execute              2198
    write_dest                     747
    __findenv_locked               638
    nv2a_metal_draw                496

**The program is blocked, not computing.** Roughly 195,000 samples of waiting
against maybe 14,000 of work. Every CPU-side optimisation on the previous
handover's list is optimising the 7%.

**sub_0013B180 is the guest busy-waiting.** It is a tight loop that reads
MEM32(0x0025EFC0), increments a spin counter at MEM32(0x0025EFA8), and loops
until the flag goes nonzero (recomp_0004.c around line 149933). It is reached
from sub_00147EBB, which the decompilation names XapiThreadStartup -- so this
is a guest worker thread spinning on a flag somebody else is supposed to set.
It is the single largest consumer of guest CPU in the program, by 4x.

That is the thread to pull. The question is not "how do we make the spin
cheaper" -- it is **who sets 0x0025EFC0, and why are we slow to do it**. On a
733 MHz Xbox this spin was presumably short. RECOMP_MEM_WRITE32 already carries
the address, so a watch on 0x0025EFC0 should name the writer directly; note the
mem-watch caveats in memory before trusting silence from it.


4. WHAT CHANGED, WITH EVIDENCE
==============================
  * **There is a frame-time instrument now.** Every performance claim in this
    project has been made in seconds of boot, total draws or controller polls,
    and none of them is what a player feels. `[FRAME]` reports flips, mean,
    p50/p90/p99/max and a count of frames over 33 ms, measured at NV097_FLIP_
    STALL -- the guest's own frame boundary -- and `[FRAME-WIN]` reports the
    same for the window since the last report. Use FRAME-WIN. A JSRF run is
    three or four workloads in sequence and a cumulative percentile blends
    however much of each that run happened to reach, which is the same trap as
    comparing two runs' draw totals. 500 us bins, 2 KB of statics, one
    clock_gettime per frame; cheaper than the [FB] line that already checksums
    the whole framebuffer once a second, so it is unconditional.

  * **The Metal vertex/index ring is no longer unrun.** Two 150 s runs, both
    ending at live=61, no ring against ring:

        flips 4085 -> 4275      mean 36.71 -> 35.08 ms
        p50   50.5 -> 48.5      p90  52.5 -> 50.5    p99 126.5 -> 118.0
        max  174.8 -> 123.3 ms  (-29%)
        audio: starved 1 -> 0, empty 1 -> 0, min_queued 0 -> 7168 bytes

    RECOMP_METAL_RING_AUDIT at 150 s: 111,207 reservations, 0 fallbacks to a
    private allocation, 4058 wraps of which **0 had to wait**. The safety
    machinery never engages -- the GPU is always finished with a slab long
    before we come round to it again. Modest on the mean, real on the tail, and
    it is the run where the audio underrun disappeared.

  * **getenv was half the pushbuffer executor's CPU.** nv2a_pb_exec_method
    called getenv("RECOMP_PB_EXEC_VERBOSE") once per pushbuffer METHOD;
    draw_primitive and capture_draw did the same per draw; bridge_vblank_poll
    and bridge_run_isr read RECOMP_PGRAPH_ISR_TRACE unconditionally. getenv
    takes a lock and walks the environment linearly on macOS. In the first
    profile __findenv_locked cost 444 samples against 320 for the ENTIRE vertex
    shader interpreter and 60 for nv2a_metal_draw. Now cached, in the idiom the
    rest of those files already used. This is justified by the profile, not by
    a frame-rate A/B -- at the sample sizes I could afford the frame numbers
    could not resolve it.

  * **The uninitialised ebp is fixed in the translator.** 4901 generated
    functions declared `uint32_t ebp;` and then pushed it before assigning it,
    to save the caller's frame. Reading an indeterminate value is UB, harmless
    at -O0 and not something to rely on at -O2. Now emitted as `= 0`. **This
    needs a regeneration to take effect; the gen tree in build-macos still has
    the old form.** Nothing observed was traced to it -- it is closed on
    principle because we now ship -O2.


5. TWO THINGS THE TEST SUITE WAS HIDING
=======================================
Both found by building ALL targets, which nobody had done -- the habit is
`--target jsrf_first_fault`, and that never builds the tests.

  * **Five C test targets did not link**, and had not for some time:
    g_apu_trap_host_pc is defined in xbox_apu and referenced by
    mcpx_trap_handler in xbox_kernel, and the small tests link xbox_kernel
    alone. ctest reported them "Not Run", which reads like a skip. That is a
    real dependency, now declared: xbox_kernel PUBLIC xbox_apu.

  * **jsrf_texture_copy was asserting the blend set we widened yesterday.**
    ac38c32 deliberately widened the accepted blend factors to the eight
    per-channel ones (refusing DST_COLOR was deleting 6034 draws), and the test
    still said SRC_COLOR must be refused. It went on "passing" for a day
    because the binary was stale. Now it pins both halves -- an accepted factor
    and a refused one -- and names why the destination-alpha factors stay
    refused (the Metal surface keeps 24-bit depth in its alpha channel).


6. THE TWO PIPELINE GAPS, BOTH CONFIRMED, BOTH WORTH LESS THAN THEY LOOK
========================================================================
  * **Flat dispatch was genuinely never enabled, and enabling it buys nothing
    here.** recomp_dispatch_init() has been generated for this title all along
    and the only caller in the tree is templates/new-game/src/main.c, which
    this harness is not built from -- so every indirect call went through a
    ~13-compare binary search, under a render chain that is entirely
    vtable-dispatched. It looked like free speed. It is not: a 12 s profile
    taken with RECOMP_FLAT_DISPATCH=0, so every indirect call used the search,
    **does not contain recomp_lookup at all**, anywhere above the 5-sample cut.
    8,923 functions is not 45,000. Wired up, measured, and left OFF
    (RECOMP_FLAT_DISPATCH=1 enables it): no measured upside, 13.6 MiB, and one
    run with it on ended in a SIGSEGV that cannot be attributed either way at
    n=1 against a 13% background fault rate.

  * **tools.abi_analysis is skipped by regenerate.sh, and running it would
    change comments.** Confirmed: the pipeline runs tools.disasm, tools.func_id
    and tools.recomp only, tools/abi_analysis/output does not exist, and
    tools.recomp prints a WARNING and proceeds with an empty abi_db. But follow
    what the data actually feeds. In translator.py the ABI fields land in the
    doc comment and nowhere else -- ret_type and param_str are hardcoded
    "void", every translated function is void(void) by design, and arguments go
    through the simulated guest stack. lifter.py's _build_call_args, the one
    function that would turn estimated_params into real arguments, is **defined
    and never called**. The single codegen effect is that a function classified
    ebp_frame would stop emitting `ebp = g_seh_ebp`, which _func_has_prologue
    already gates -- so the realistic outcomes are "no change" and "a
    disagreement removes an inheritance we need". It cannot be a speedup.
    Worth running once to fix the comments (the generated headers currently say
    `Frame: fpo_leaf` for functions that plainly have an ebp prologue, which
    will mislead somebody), and only after diffing the generated C to confirm
    the diff is comments-only.


7. WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT
=======================
**(1) Find who sets 0x0025EFC0.** Section 3. Everything else is the 7%.

**(2) The sync traffic the ring audit exposed.** Over 150 s: 13,817
nv2a_metal_sync calls, 7,172 colour read-backs, 4,716 depth read-backs and
7,169 surface re-uploads. That is a GPU->CPU->GPU round trip roughly twice per
frame, on the thread the guest is waiting on, and it fits the profile's shape
far better than anything CPU-side. Measure before designing.

**(3) The OHCI use-after-free**, unchanged from the previous handover and still
the best explanation for both the 13% fault rate and the intermittent
controller stalls. Confirm ownership before adding a lock, and do NOT reuse
mcpx_lock -- see the APU lock-inversion note.

**(4) A real crash study.** 13% is not something two runs can attribute. Any
claim that a change causes or fixes a crash needs ~20 runs per arm; I did not
have the machine time, which is why flat dispatch is off rather than blamed.

**(5) Black bars and grey ellipse, oPos NaN, sub-pixel viewport offset** --
all unchanged from the previous handover, all still open.


8. TRAPS ADDED THIS SESSION
===========================
  * **Cumulative [FRAME] percentiles blend scenes.** Use [FRAME-WIN] and read
    the live= in force for that window. diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault has no
    analysis script for this; I did it with a throwaway that joins FRAME-WIN
    lines to the preceding JSRF-SCENE line, which is ten lines of python and
    worth writing properly if this gets used twice more.
  * **`cmake --build --target jsrf_first_fault` never builds the tests.** Two
    real defects hid behind that for a day. Build all targets before believing
    ctest.
  * **ctest "Not Run" is a LINK FAILURE, not a skip.** It looks benign in the
    summary line.
  * **measure.pad stops pressing at t=47 on purpose.** new_game.pad keeps
    firing to t=71, and past the title START is PAUSE -- so for timing runs the
    tail has to come off or two runs end up in two different places. The cost
    is that an unlucky run never leaves the menus at all; that shows up as
    live!=61 and the run is discarded, not compared.
  * **A 150 s run reaches the tutorial maybe three times in four**, same
    binary. Budget for discards.
  * **getenv is not free and this codebase calls it from hot paths.** Four
    sites fixed here; `grep -rn getenv src/ | wc -l` still returns plenty, and
    the ones inside `static int on = -1` guards are fine. Check the guard
    before assuming a site is cached.
```

```txt
0. STATE OF PLAY
================
HEAD da2f4c0. origin/main is far behind; nothing has been pushed today.
tools/recomp 160/160. ctest 21/23, the two failures deliberate (05e0465).

**The default build dir is now the optimised one.** build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/
build is RelWithDebInfo with the title at -O2, so play.sh and measure.sh no
longer launch the -O0 tree. Every log now opens with

    [BUILD] title compiled -O2, binary <path>

A log WITHOUT that line predates the stamp, and any performance number in it
should be re-taken rather than trusted. play.sh and measure.sh also refuse a
binary older than the sources (JSRF_ALLOW_STALE=1 overrides).

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/measure.sh <name> [seconds] [padfile]
    pad/still.pad + pad/moving.pad   -- identical to t=47, then one holds the stick
    pad/measure.pad                  -- reach the tutorial and stop pressing


1. WHAT IS ACTUALLY FIXED
=========================
  * **The music glitch was the voice resampler.** voice_resample() took a
    playback rate and discarded it -- `(void)rate;` under a comment claiming
    nearest-neighbour resampling that did not exist. JSRF plays concurrent
    voices at 48000 (rate 1.0), 44100 (1.0885) and 22050 Hz (2.1770), so the
    22 kHz voice played 2.177x too fast. Linear interpolation now, carrying
    fractional phase across frames; unity rate keeps its old path bit-identical,
    so four of six voices are untouched by construction. Measured, same binary,
    voice 69 alive at t=35-38 in both arms:

        resampling on          0 deltas >12000, dmax 8365, over 154.7 s
        RECOMP_NO_RESAMPLE=1   137 deltas >12000 in seconds 35/36/37, dmax 16641

    dmax 8365 is BELOW the 8462 that an xemu capture's whole run never exceeds,
    so our audio now sits inside the reference envelope. (f464df9)

  * **Vblank ran 4% fast for the life of the port.** BRIDGE_VBLANK_PERIOD_MS was
    16 under a comment saying 60 Hz; 1000/16 is 62.5. Not jitter -- the archived
    62.3 Hz measurement tracks the nominal constant to 0.4%. A fractional macro
    does NOT fix it: next_vblank and now are both DWORD, so `now + 16.683`
    truncates back to 16 every call. bridge_vblank_step_ms carries the remainder
    and returns a 16/17 sequence averaging 16683 us. Measured 62.3 -> 59.7 Hz
    against a 59.94 target. Frame rate unchanged; this is correctness, not
    speed. (cfd07a3, ba244a3)

  * **getenv was half the pushbuffer executor's CPU.** nv2a_pb_exec_method called
    it once per METHOD; __findenv_locked cost 444 samples against 320 for the
    entire vertex shader interpreter. Cached, in the idiom those files already
    used elsewhere. (855308c)

  * **Five C tests did not LINK**, and ctest reports that as "Not Run", which
    reads like a skip. xbox_kernel needed xbox_apu declared. And
    jsrf_texture_copy was asserting the blend set ac38c32 deliberately widened
    the day before, passing only because nobody rebuilt it. 16/23 -> 21/23.
    (81eaf21)

  * **The reference rig can capture audio alone now**, and survives an absolute
    outdir -- "$PWD/$OUT" silently produced "$PWD//tmp/..." and xemu exited
    before writing a sample while the script reported success. (6853538)


2. FIVE THINGS THAT MEASURED AS NOTHING
=======================================
Each of these looked obviously right. Each is committed saying plainly that it
is not a speedup. Do not re-derive them.

  * **-O2 on the recompiled title.** Scene-matched, -O0 and -O2 are identical
    within noise: live=131 118.0 vs 114.0 flips/window, live=133 108.5 vs 104.0,
    live=137 106.5 vs 105.0. It kills _tlv_get_addr (75% of guest samples -> 22)
    and shrinks the binary 42.7 -> 29.7 MB, and buys no frame time. Kept anyway.
    The handover before this one said the whole runtime was at -O0; that was
    WRONG -- every runtime library sets its own -O2 in target_compile_options.
    (b1f0531)

  * **Flat dispatch.** recomp_dispatch_init() was genuinely never called by this
    harness -- the only caller in the tree is upstream's template. Wired up, then
    profiled with RECOMP_FLAT_DISPATCH=0 so every indirect call used the binary
    search: recomp_lookup does not appear in the profile AT ALL. 8,923 functions
    is not Half-Life 2's 45,000. Left OFF. (c5b3908)

  * **Skipping unstored VSH units.** vsh 16.07 -> 14.25 ms per frame, frame time
    39.8 -> 39.8. The 1.8 ms reappeared as `rest`. (dc4a79e)

  * **The per-vertex diagnostic range.** draw_primitive ran a SECOND fetch_vertex
    over every vertex of every draw to compute a bounding box for one report
    line. Now opt-in (RECOMP_VERTEX_RANGE=1). rest 15.96 -> 15.12 ms, mean 68.5
    -> 68.4. (068b6f6)

  * **Zero-filling a starved voice.** Real placement improvement, no behaviour
    change: short=0 and dry=0 on every voice over 154 s, dropouts unchanged at
    88 vs 85. (85a9177, corrected by c2c003e)


3. RETRACTIONS
==============
  * **"voice_process mixes stack residue."** It does not. The line after the
    declaration is `memset(samples, 0, sizeof(samples))`, present since the
    original import. I read the declaration and not the line beneath it. A short
    return has always truncated to silence. (c2c003e)
  * **"550 of 551 discontinuities are within 5 ms of silence."** An artifact of
    my own detector: the silence test was |sample|<64, which fires on every zero
    crossing, and 8830 of 8850 "silence runs" were ONE SAMPLE long. The
    follow-up guess that the burst was near-Nyquist noise is also dead -- a
    roughness metric put a clean window HIGHER than the burst.
  * **"The spinners are idle-priority CPU-measuring threads."** Traced: the
    guest gives them ABOVE_NORMAL (+1), and gives IDLE (-16) to the worker that
    blocks properly. (e2c0e45)
  * **Black bars in the title animation are a defect.** The user says they are
    intentional graphical elements. Stop looking. The grey ellipse reported
    alongside them is NOT yet confirmed either way.


4. AUDITS THAT SAID "DO NOT"
============================
  * **xbox_dsound is dead code for JSRF and must stay that way.** The title
    statically links Microsoft's DSOUND.lib into the XBE (section 2, 116 KB) and
    that recompiled guest code drives the MCPX registers directly -- 14,677 APU
    writes in 154 s. xbox_DirectSoundCreate has no callers. And our xbox_dsound
    is itself a stub ("accept all method calls silently", "deferred to a later
    phase"), so switching to it would delete all audio. (6384659)

  * **nv2a_core.c is unwired scaffolding, and wiring it is not justified yet.**
    nv2a_init_standalone has never been called by anything. Most of it is
    complementary, not duplicated -- it is the MMIO register-block model
    (PMC/PBUS/PTIMER/PFB/PCRTC/PRAMDAC/PVIDEO/PFIFO) we do not have, and its
    pgraph_method is a stub that renders nothing, so nv2a_pb_exec.c's 3354 lines
    were not redundant. The one real overlap is the interrupt path, where its
    computed PMC summary is better than our store-and-mask. Declined because
    unacked_skips=0 and not_ready=0 across six runs -- the race it would prevent
    is not happening -- and because making the model authoritative needs NV2A
    register READ traps, which are currently ordinary loads. (53f36d2)

  * **Library usage, measured at the linker:** xbox_kernel 23/25 objects,
    xbox_apu 6/6, xbox_vsh 4/5, xbox_nv2a 2/6, xbox_video 2/3, xbox_dsound 0/1.
    video_player.c is unused on macOS BY DESIGN -- it is Media Foundation behind
    #if defined(_WIN32). If the intro animation is an FMV, it is not being
    decoded on this host at all, which may bear on how the intro behaves here.


5. THE TWO OPEN DEFECTS
=======================
**(1) Audio dropouts at a music track change.** 85 gaps >=3 ms in 155 s against
xemu's 37, worst ~300 ms against xemu's 16 ms. The big gap sits EXACTLY between
`off68` at t=42 and `on68` at t=43 -- the guest stopping its own music voice,
with voice 70 briefly covering. Delivery is provably healthy throughout: 48,003
frames/s, starved=0, empty=0, queue never below two device buffers.

  The live lead, from an upstream audit: apu_dsp.c:31-54 documents a DirectSound
  -> GP "command doorbell" where DSOUND writes a command word and spins until the
  DSP writes ZERO back, and our GP is a passthrough stub so it never does.
  RECOMP_APU_DSP_ACK=<addr> clears such words once per APU frame; it is set for
  Wreckless and has never been set for JSRF. NOT yet shown to be our bug --
  check whether the track change touches GPSADDR/GPFADDR/EPSADDR/EPFADDR or
  writes a doorbell word before believing it.

  Settling this needs xemu driven to the SAME transition, which the rig cannot
  do unattended. Keystroke automation for capture_reference.sh (osascript, which
  it already uses for focus) is the blocking task.

**(2) 25 fps against a 30 fps target.** Stage breakdown at live=61, ~40 ms/frame:
vsh 14.25, submit 9.47, sync 1.44, rest 14.67, 101 batches. GPU sync is NOT the
problem, which retires a guess made from the ring audit's counters.

  Two independent reductions in pusher-thread work moved the frame rate by zero
  (section 2), so the pusher is not the critical path. A profile puts
  sub_0013B180 -- a guest busy-wait -- at 1611 samples where a whole thread's
  count is 1606. RECOMP_PEEK over a run: the flag 0x0025EFC0 reads 0 for the
  ENTIRE run, its spin counter 0x0025EFA8 climbs past 1.1 BILLION, and
  0x0025EFC4 never sets either.

  But the spinners are LOAD-BEARING: RECOMP_SKIP_SPIN_THREADS=1 leaves the
  handles intact and lets their bodies exit, and the title then stops at live=20
  and never advances, twice, reproducibly. So they cannot be deleted or starved,
  and "a core is busy" is not by itself the defect. (da2f4c0)

  The lifter was checked and exonerated: the original XBE bytes at 0x0013B180
  really do contain a call-free spin.


6. TRAPS ADDED TODAY
====================
  * **Upstream's threading docs are STALE.** kernel-replacement.md,
    gap-analysis.md and 05-runtime.md all say "single-threaded", "stubbed", "no
    real threading". The code spawns real threads and honours CREATE_SUSPENDED.
    Believing those docs would send you the wrong way entirely.
  * **Thread priority is a no-op on POSIX.** SetThreadPriority records the value
    and returns ("real RT priorities need privileges; tracked only"), so all
    42,762 KeSetBasePriorityThread calls do nothing and the guest's four-level
    ordering (+2/+1/0/-16) is flat. A real defect, unfixed, and NOT the spin
    cause.
  * **Scene-match or measure nothing.** A 150 s run reaches the tutorial about
    three times in four. Compare [FRAME-WIN] windows at the same live=, never
    cumulative totals.
  * **Write the positive control before believing an absence.** Two of today's
    wrong turns were absences without one.
  * **`cmake --build --target jsrf_first_fault` never builds the tests.**
```

```txt
Unit tests: `/usr/bin/python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/recomp -t . -p 'test_*.py'`
-- 153, all passing. ctest is 11 of 27 failing and ALL 11 predate this session;
six are backport_* checks made obsolete by their own fixes moving into the
lifter, five are "Not Run".


1. THE METHOD, WHICH FOUND EVERYTHING
=====================================
Every bug this session had ONE SHAPE: an x86 behaviour emitted as the nearest C
construct where C differs at a single edge, or emitted as nothing at all.
Ordinary inputs pass either way, so tests and casual play never see it.

And ONE TELL: **split every population by REACHABILITY before reading its
count.** Raw counts here are dominated by functions nothing calls -- data swept
as code -- and the raw number sends you to the wrong component:

    dead branches        104 -> 90 total  BUT  18 -> 4 reachable
    unimplemented insns  176 -> 164 total BUT  12 -> 3 reachable

Both totals barely moved. Both reachable counts fell by about 78%. A change
that looks like noise in the total is the whole of the work.


2. FIXED, WITH EVIDENCE
=======================
  * `comiss` on NaN (55 sites). x86 sets ZF/PF/CF together; C's `==` is false
    and `!=` is true. This froze the Corn tutorial for two days: a ray-plane
    test reported a HIT on the zero-length movement segment a standing
    character produces, so CSysDeathWarpManager death-warped both CPlayers
    every frame of a cutscene.
  * `cvtss2si` emitted as truncation when it rounds; float->int of NaN/inf/range
    was UB where x86 yields 0x80000000.
  * Variable shift counts unmasked (339 sites). ROL32/ROR32 undefined at count 0.
  * Flag dataflow swept once in address order, so any join whose predecessor sat
    at a HIGHER address was abandoned before the merge was ever called.
  * Width-mismatched snapshot joins refused outright, when ZF is still knowable.
  * `rcl`/`rcr` emitted as NOTHING, inside MSVC's 64-bit shift -- the low word
    was never shifted.
  * `stmxcsr` emitted as nothing, so a rounding-mode check read stale memory.

  * Overlapping functions are NOT truncation. All 1599 pairs checked: in every
    one the outer body emits code covering the interior range.

  * THE BUILD TREE IS OUT OF iCLOUD. `build-macos` is a symlink to
    /Users/andrewcollard/jsrf-build. Boot variance went from a 16-second range
    to 0.2 s and the title stall went from ~50% to roughly 1 in 3.


3. WHAT IS LEFT
===============
  * 3 reachable unimplemented: `in`, `wbinvd`, `out`, one each. Probably
    ignorable on this host, but they should SAY so rather than be comments that
    read like ordinary output.
  * 4 reachable dead branches. Two need OF across a join, which no merge answers.
  * The ratchet is 76 against a tree at 90, so it cannot pass and teaches
    nothing. `audit_unresolved_flags.py` now prints the reachability split;
    decide which number it should gate on.
  * Six `backport_*` tests fail because their fixes moved into the lifter.
    `jsrf_challenge_flag_merge` started passing by itself. Retire them.
  * The disassembler is where the 161 + 86 unreachable items live. One finding,
    not two hundred: the linear sweep walks into data.


4. THE OPEN RENDERING BUG, AND A DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS NOT THE FIX
===============================================================
Reported: background geometry vanishes in WHOLE FLAT CHUNKS as the camera
moves. Characters are fine.

Measured clean, so these are excluded: 70M triangles rasterised, 0 batches
skipped as not screen-space, 0 triangles off-surface, 0 Metal software
fallbacks, 0 texture rejects. Geometry reaches the rasteriser.

The Metal path is a SOFTWARE rasteriser: it takes already-transformed
screen-space vertices and does its own depth test in the fragment shader
against a 24-bit Z packed into the surface's ALPHA channel. There is no depth
attachment. But Metal still clips to 0 <= z <= w by default, so any triangle
whose z leaves [0,1] is discarded before the shader can judge it.

`RECOMP_METAL_DEPTH_CLAMP=1` turns that clipping off. A/B in ONE binary:

    clamp off:  11980 polls, 15.26M triangles
    clamp on:    6085 polls, 18.46M triangles

So geometry IS being z-clipped -- 20% more of it survives -- but clamping
HALVES the frame rate, because geometry past the far plane is squashed onto it
and rasterised over large areas. It is therefore a diagnostic, left OPT-IN and
OFF by default. Do not ship it.

THE REAL QUESTION: why does z leave [0,1] for geometry the title expects to be
visible? That is upstream, in whatever produces the screen-space z in
nv2a_pb_exec.c. Start there, not in the Metal file.

Also unexplained and possibly related: `[VSH] rejected=59  oPos is not finite`.
59 batches with NaN vertex positions. The count is STATIC across reports, so it
happens early and stops -- not the ongoing clipping, but NaN reaching geometry
is exactly what cost two days this morning.


5. TRAPS, EACH PAID FOR TODAY
=============================
  * **START skips the logos.** So `8 WaitDestructLogos -> 12 WaitEndTitle` is
    NOT a boot duration, it is when a press landed. Retuning new_game.pad to
    fire "after the logos end" REMOVES the skip: two retunes scored 1/2 and 1/3
    against 7/7 for the untouched file. Leave that file alone.
  * **live=70 is PAUSED** (61 cutscene, 65 gameplay). A frozen pose plus
    m_bFatal=1 was a human pressing START, not a regression -- three "clean"
    runs and one "bad" one is not a bisect when the build AND the input history
    both differ. Ask what was pressed.
  * **PAD-TRACE proves our side, not delivery.** It observes the state the
    guest is about to be given. RECOMP_PAD_INJECT then writes it into the
    title's own copy; check the [PAD-INJECT] line says it found one.
  * A repeated sweep must not touch the Lifter's reporting dictionaries.
    Unguarded, `unimplemented` counted 538 where the truth was 176.
  * `timeout` does not exist on macOS. Five runs reported "stalled" having
    never started.
```

```txt
0. STATE OF PLAY
================
HEAD a3c4676. ctest 21/23, the two failures deliberate (05e0465).

    RECOMP_VOICE_FRESH=1          ring-freshness probe (implies VOICE_RATES)
    RECOMP_ADX_RATE=1             the guest's own sound-server pass rate
    RECOMP_WAIT_POLL_US=N         wait poll interval, default 1000
    RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED=1 keep the SE rendering while the FE is trapped
                                  -- BUILT, OFF, AND NEVER HEARD. See section 3.

Nothing in this handover about audio quality or frame rate was established by a
scripted run. All of it came from a person playing with a controller, or from

1. THE HEADLINE: 60 FPS, AND WE ARE AT 12
==========================================
xemu 0.8.136, US ISO, traced with nv2a_pgraph_flip_stall -- the same event our
own [FRAME] counter is built on, so no conversion:

    xemu, in-engine attract (character, HUD, city, dialogue)   59.2 - 60.1 fps
    ours, the same attract scene                               11.7 - 14.3 fps
    ours, gameplay at Dogenzaka Hill                                  31.3 fps

11018 flips traced. **JSRF is a 60 fps title.** The "25 fps against a 30 fps
target" line in three handovers has NOTHING measured behind it and understates
the gap by 2x -- 5x at the attract.

This is why the user said it "looks slow" rather than choppy. 31.3 fps against a
59.8 Hz vblank, frame time pinned at 31.9-33.5 ms = two vblank periods: a 60 Hz
title missing 16.67 ms and dropping to every other refresh. Titles of this era
advance simulation a fixed step per frame, so half the frame rate is half the
game speed. The world literally moves at half pace.

Where the 32 ms goes at gameplay:

    vsh 7.52 | submit 8.41 | sync 0.98 | REST (guest CPU) 15.03 | total 31.94

Read that last column before attacking this as a renderer problem. The guest-CPU
half is as large as all the graphics work combined, and 16.67 ms is the budget
for the whole frame.

    xemu -trace enable=nv2a_pgraph_flip_stall,file=/tmp/xemu-flip.trace

~60 events/s, so straight to a file: no FIFO, no monitor gating. No timestamps
-- count lines over an interval you timed yourself.


2. THE AUDIO CHAIN, AS FAR AS IT IS KNOWN
==========================================
The intro replays ~23% of voice 68's 16384-sample music ring, in unbroken runs
of 100-163 ms. Every sample of it is valid music, which is why five separate
characterisations of the output called it clean.

  * CRI's renderer moves at most 1024 samples per server pass (guest
    0x0013E965), so 44100 Hz needs >= 43.1 passes/s.
  * The server (guest thread body 0x0013B1C0) waits on the D3D vblank event at
    59.94 Hz. That looks like 2x headroom. It is 39%.
  * MEASURED 33.4 passes/s, pinned, at 88 fps and at 12 fps alike, with CRI's
    own underrun counter (0x002615AC) flat ZERO -- it always had data; the pass
    rate is the ceiling.
  * bridge_KeWaitForSingleObject is not a wait. It is a poll loop ending in
    Sleep(1) on a 16.67 ms budget.

Confirmed independently: correlation of our attract clip against xemu's, per
window, 0.449 -> 0.904 at 1 s when the poll was shortened. Short windows were
already ~0.99 both ways; the samples were always right.


3. THE TRAP STORM, WHICH IS PROBABLY THE BIGGER ONE
====================================================
The user, playing with a controller, reported a sustained effect -- the grind --
fading in and out. That is not the ring replay. It is this:

    real play        on=109  off=103  idle_trap=22371   48% of APU frames skipped
    every scripted   on=5    off=0    idle_trap=0        0%
    run ever taken

~217 traps per voice retirement. The voice-list walk restarts from the top each
frame and re-traps the SAME dead voice until the guest services it; each trap
costs ~11 APU frames (~7 ms) with the sound engine down. A sustained sound is
the obvious victim -- percussive music hides the same chopping.

Two defects, both addressed behind RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED (edbd87d):
  * se_frame was skipped while the FRONT END was trapped. FE (method
    processing) and SE (voice rendering) are separate units; if a trapped FE
    stopped the SE, every voice retirement would glitch audio on a stock Xbox.
  * the walk abandoned the whole VP frame at the first idle voice, so one dead
    voice silenced every voice behind it in every list.

IT IS OFF AND HAS NEVER BEEN HEARD. ctest passes but no test in this tree
retires a voice. It needs a controller, a grind, and [APU-FRAME] trapped= read
beside [APU-VOICE] idle_trap=.


4. THE HARNESS CANNOT SEE ANY OF THIS
======================================
This is the most important section and it is a process finding, not a bug.

**Every pad schedule in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/pad/ parks the player.**
measure.pad reaches gameplay and stops pressing. So nothing skates, nothing
grinds, no sound effect starts or finishes, and no voice EVER retires:
on=5 off=0 idle_trap=0 in every scripted run in this tree's history.

Consequences, all real:
  * the trap storm in section 3 was invisible for the life of the project;
  * a change was shipped as a default on intro-only numbers and took gameplay
    audio out entirely (section 5);
  * "gameplay is clean" was asserted from live=61 and is false at live=161.

A pad schedule that actually plays -- moves, jumps, grinds, sprays -- is worth
more than any probe in this repo. Until it exists, ANY audio or performance
conclusion from a scripted run is provisional, and should say so.


5. RETRACTIONS
==============
Five, all mine, all from generalising one run.

  * "The buffer wrap is the candidate" -- DEAD. Voice 68 wraps 82 times in

  * "Voice bounds are incoherent" -- an artifact. voice_desc_dump runs at the
    TOP of the VOICE_ON case, ~50 lines before that case resets CBO.
  * "Gameplay is clean" -- scene-specific. live=61 freezes its stale count;

  * "The frame collapse is caused by the music" -- no. [STAGE] shows draws going

  * **"The wait poll fix is a measured win"** (8440c9c) -- REVERTED in 3d00122.
    100 us raised the intro's server passes 36.8 -> 44.9 and halved the replay,

6. TRAPS, PAID FOR
==================
  * **Correlating audio over ONE long window cannot distinguish "different
    music" from "same music, broken continuity".** Both read near zero. Ours and
```

```txt
THE HARNESS NOW REACHES GAMEPLAY WITHOUT A HUMAN. SIX RANKED GAPS ARE CLOSED.
THE THING THAT COST THE MOST TIME WAS A STALE ARTIFACT, AND THE AUDIO
"REGRESSION" I SPENT AN HOUR ON WAS THE MAC'S AUDIO DAEMON.

Supersedes CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-14_THE_RENDERER_IS_FINE_AND_THE_HARNESS_IS_NOT.txt.

0. STATE OF PLAY
================
Tree dirty, nothing committed by me beyond what is described here.
ctest 24/26 -- the 2 failures are the same deliberate pair as before (05e0465).
Was 21/23; three tests added, all passing.

The title was REGENERATED and REBUILT this session. That matters (section 2).

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/pad/gameplay.pad     skates, jumps, sprays

1. WHAT GOT DONE, AGAINST THE OLD RANKED LIST
==============================================
All of ACCURACY_GAPS.md's "suggested order" items 1, 2 and 4, plus §8:

  * BUILD FLAGS (§4). -fwrapv on the title; -fno-strict-aliasing TREE-WIDE, not
    just on generated code -- kernel_bridge.c, xbox_memory_layout.c and the two
    nv2a pushbuffer files reach guest memory through the same MEM8/16/32/MEMF
    macros. -w replaced by -Wall minus four generator-inherent classes, NOT
    dropped: dropping it outright is 11318 unused-label and 742 unused-variable,
    which nobody reads. Measured yield of the chosen set over the whole gen
    tree: 440 -Wuninitialized and 11 -Wmacro-redefined, and nothing else.
  * KeSynchronizeExecution (§6) and NtProtectVirtualMemory (§7) bridged.
    CONFIRMED LIVE by a run first -- both appear as "[KERNEL] WARNING: no bridge

Three of those sections were WRONG in ways worth knowing; see ACCURACY_GAPS.md,
which now records each correction inline. Briefly: §5's "172 callers" is 432
calls across 129 functions and there are only SIX fist/fistp sites in the whole
image; §8's claim was true of `add` only, because `sub` already went through a
reconstruction that is SF!=OF at 32 bits; §6's "returns STATUS_SUCCESS" is a
BOOLEAN export, so the guest got a fabricated FALSE, not a success.


2. THE MOST EXPENSIVE BUG WAS NOT A BUG, IT WAS A STALE ARTIFACT
=================================================================
Dropping -w surfaced 440 `PUSH32(esp, ebp)` reading an indeterminate `ebp`.
Real: at -O2 that is poison the compiler may propagate, not stack residue.

But translator.py ALREADY FIXED IT, in b1f0531, at 18:44 on 13 Sep. The gen
tree in build-macos was generated at 16:59 the same day -- one hour and
forty-five minutes earlier. So the fix existed, and every binary measured since
carried all 440 anyway, because nobody regenerated.

REGENERATING CLEARED THEM: 496 declarations now `uint32_t ebp = 0;`, zero
uninitialised, zero -Wuninitialized from the generated title in the build log.

THE LESSON IS THE PROCESS ONE. A translator fix does nothing until the title is
regenerated, and nothing in the build tells you the gen tree is older than the
tool that produced it. If you change tools/recomp, regenerate, or you are
testing yesterday.


3. THE HARNESS NOW REACHES GAMEPLAY
====================================
gameplay.pad + play_scripted.sh. MEASURED: 1408 NtOpenFile, i.e. New Game, with
nobody at the machine. Previously only a human had ever got there.

play_scripted.sh exists because neither existing script could measure gameplay:
play.sh is light but has no schedule; run_scripted.sh has a schedule but turns
on four heavy probes at once, and heavy probes provoke the input-poll stall, so
the measurement measures the probes. This is the first with both.

It prints THREE verdicts, deliberately separate, because conflating them is how
the first version of this lied to me:

    AUDIO   did the host audio device even open      (section 5)
    SCENE   1342 opens = title plateau, 1408 = New Game
    PLAYED  [APU-VOICE] off=, which must be well clear of 0

FIRST VERSION FAILED INSTRUCTIVELY, and this is the part to keep. It ran the
full 250 s, fired 186 of 193 events, retired one voice -- and never left the
attract screen. off=1 read as "it played" until the open count was checked. The
cause: it copied moving.pad's boot prefix, which stops pressing START at t=45.5
and therefore gambles on hitting one window, and logo length varies by ten
seconds or more between runs. gameplay.pad now uses new_game.pad's full measured
prefix and starts play at t=80, clear of the last START.

WHAT DECIDES WHETHER IT ARRIVES: not known, and the audio device is NOT it.
Across nine runs the boot reaches New Game roughly two times in five. Always
read the SCENE verdict before using a run; a title-plateau run produces a full
log, a full pad trace and plausible audio counters, and means nothing.

I got this wrong three times in a row and the sequence is the useful part:

    1 run    "the one success had a dead audio device"   a hunch
    2 v 2    forced off twice reached New Game, live     written up as a
             device twice did not                        CLEAN SEPARATION
    n = 6    forced off 2 of 4, live device 0 of 2       no evidence at all

0/2 against 2/4 is what one ~40% rate looks like. Anything built on the middle
row -- including "force audio off for non-audio runs" -- was resting on nothing.

THE LEAD THAT DID COME OUT OF IT came from diffing a successful boot against a
failed one instead of running more of them. Both reach the 1342 plateau at
t=36-37, so the failure is NOT slow booting. The difference is the A press: in
the good run the A at t=47 moved it 1342 -> 1344 -> 1408, i.e. that A selected
New Game; in the bad run the A presses at t=39, 47, 55, 63 and 71 each did
nothing. So a group's START,START may be moving off the menu before the group's
own A lands. gameplay.pad now fires bare A presses after the groups stop. One
run, one success, against a baseline that already lands two in five -- untested,
not fixed.

DENSER INPUT IS NOT THE FIX, and this was tried: groups every 4 s to t=118
instead of every 8 s to t=71 still gave 1342. That is the documented masher
plateau, and this project's notes already said not to retune those timings.

TWO CONFOUNDS THAT LOOK LIKE HEALTHY RUNS, both now gated in play_scripted.sh:
  * INPUT-POLL STALL. One run fired 128 of 202 events with a SEVENTY-SIX SECOND
    window in which the guest polled nothing -- while its mean poll interval,
    18.7 ms, matched a healthy run's 18.9 ms, and the schedule still ran to
    completion. No counter we print could see it. The gate reports the largest
    gap between pad events.
  * COREAUDIO FAILING THE DEVICE. Wedges repeatedly on this machine, including
    mid-session, and makes a run's audio figures void while se= stays healthy.

STILL NOT DONE: the schedule reaches gameplay and then does LITTLE. Best run is
on=22 off=16 idle_trap=19, trapped=184, against a human's on=109 off=103
idle_trap=22371. Whether that is the Corn tutorial gating the player or the
synthetic pad not driving him is UNSETTLED. That is the next job.


4. THE PARSER TRAP THAT WAS DOCUMENTED BACKWARDS
=================================================
Overlapping STICK events on the SAME AXIS do not hand over. xinput_device.c:743
writes a scripted deflection only while the axis is still near neutral:

    if (ev->lx && st->Gamepad.sThumbLX > -4096 && st->Gamepad.sThumbLX < 4096)

so an overlapping event finds the axis at 30000 and is REFUSED; the first event
in FILE ORDER wins until it expires. (The guard is deliberate -- it is what lets
a live controller take over a scripted run.)

moving.pad's header asserted the OPPOSITE, that a later event replaces an
earlier one. It reached the right behaviour anyway because its segments happen
to be adjacent rather than overlapping. Header corrected; test_pad_schedule.py
now asserts it, along with the event-count limit and the post-t=48 START rule
(new_game.pad carries an explicit waiver comment for the one real exception).


5. THE AUDIO "REGRESSION" WAS THE MAC. I LOST AN HOUR TO IT; YOU SHOULD NOT
===========================================================================
A gameplay run read [APU-PACE] gen_hz=0 batches=0 frames=0 against the previous
binary's 46086 / 44571 / 11410176. The sound engine still reported se=405138
rendered subframes, so `se=` looked perfectly healthy.

I called it a regression and suspected the new KeSynchronizeExecution bridge,
which is on the two audio interrupt vectors. WRONG, twice:

  1. The comparison was CROSS-SCENE. The baseline never left the title; the new
     run reached gameplay. This tree's own rule says scene-match before
     believing a number, and I did not.
  2. The actual cause was one line further up the log:

         [APU-SDL] output open failed: CoreAudio error (AudioQueueStart): -66681

     The host audio device never opened. apu_sdl2_init() failed, the APU fell
     back to a waveOut path that does nothing on macOS, and every audio figure
     in the run was void.

PROVED it was the host, not us, by reproducing it in a standalone 12-line SDL2
program linking none of this code -- same error, same minute. It did NOT clear
on its own or after killing every jsrf process. Fix: `sudo killall coreaudiod`.

play_scripted.sh now prints this as the FIRST verdict, before any audio number.

I briefly gated both new bridges behind env switches on the strength of the
wrong diagnosis, then reverted it once the cause was known: the switches were
justified by a measurement error, and leaving them in would have left a false
claim in a comment in kernel_bridge.c. Both ordinals are routed unconditionally.


6. WHAT ctest CANNOT SEE
=========================
The suite passed 24/26 throughout the whole audio episode. NO TEST IN THIS TREE
GENERATES AN AUDIO OUTPUT BATCH, so a total audio failure is invisible to it --
just as no test retires a voice, which is why the trap storm survived so long.
If you want audio regressions caught, that is the gap to close.

9. THE CONTROLLER WAS NEVER THE BUG, AND ORDINAL 153 WAS
=========================================================
Added late on 14 Sep, after a hand-played session and two read-only reviews.

"CONTROLLER INPUT NOT WORKING" IS THE GUEST'S USB DRIVER DYING. The XPP driver
stops submitting transfers, permanently, at a different moment every run.
Measure it with kernel ordinal 175 (MmLockUnlockBufferPages), already in every
log's histogram:

    reached New Game    ord175 = 12963 23022 27676 30174 72421 72737 73945 74150 74603
    stuck at the title  ord175 = 234 1100 5130 6684 10614

234 transfers in a 300 s run is enumeration and nothing else. That run was
never going to accept a button, however many were pressed.

DO NOT TRUST [PAD-TRACE] OR nonneutral= AS PROOF A PRESS REACHED THE GUEST.
With RECOMP_PAD_INJECT=1 our own host thread calls xbox_InputGetState at 50 Hz,
so a completely deaf guest still produces a healthy-looking trace. Healthy runs
poll at ~172/s, dead ones at EXACTLY 50/s -- the injector alone. This single
instrument produced three confident wrong claims in one session and has been
misleading this project since 10 Sep. "START works but A does not" was the same
illusion: one 20-byte report, one writer, no threshold anywhere -- the STARTs
landed before the driver died and the A presses after it.

ORDINAL 153 WAS THE REGRESSION, MEASURED THREE WAYS:

    yesterday's binary, no 153 bridge   3/3 New Game   ord175 74603 74150 73945
    today WITH 153 on                   1/3 New Game   ord175 27676 10614  5130
    today with 153 off (new default)    3/3 New Game   ord175 30174 72421 72737

Turning it off restores both the success rate and the transfer rate to within
2% of yesterday, and no 153-off run has produced an ADX stall. Three
hand-played sessions froze during a rail grind with it on; none has been played
with it off.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT THE ONE THE BRIDGE'S COMMENT FEARED. Both guest call sites
are inside DPC bodies, so its bounded spin and g_in_isr code never execute --
which makes g_sync_exec_unsynchronised vacuous, and reading "unsynchronised=0"
as "the interlock was always acquired" was wrong. What it really does is switch
on ~41 previously-dead DSOUND functions: the only instruction in the image that
sets a bit in the DSOUND state word [this+0x6FC] is inside the routine the
bridge calls. They run inside bridge_run_isr -> bridge_run_dpc, holding
g_vblank_delivery_active -- the same interlock bridge_device_irq_poll needs, and
that pump is the ONLY thing that runs the guest's USB ISR on vector 1.

So the freeze, the dying controller and the depressed transfer rate are ONE
fault: the interrupt-delivery interlock doubles as the IRQL model, so any guest
ISR or DPC body blocks interrupt delivery process-wide. FIXING THAT IS THE REAL
WORK; defaulting 153 off is a retreat, and it is marked as one in the code.

STILL UNEXPLAINED: verify153-1 reached New Game with ord175=30174, a 2.4x
depression with a healthy outcome, while runs 2 and 3 sat at ~72500. n=1, not
theorised about.

ALSO CORRECTED: RECOMP_USB=1 does nothing on macOS (src/usb/ohci.c has no
callers), so the 11 Sep elimination of both interrupt theories rested on dead
counters and is VOID. The lifter-regression hypothesis is dead too -- the same
binary succeeded and failed 20 minutes apart, and the and/or/xor + jbe/ja idiom
changed today occurs ZERO times in this image.
```

```txt
CLAUDE, 14 Sep 2026 (early)
THE INTRO STUTTER IS OURS: A 1 ms POLL IN KeWaitForSingleObject STARVES CRI'S
SOUND SERVER. HALF FIXED, MEASURED BOTH WAYS, AND THE REST IS NAMED.

0. STATE OF PLAY

    RECOMP_VOICE_FRESH=1   ring-freshness probe (implies RECOMP_VOICE_RATES)
    RECOMP_ADX_RATE=1      the guest's own sound-server pass rate
    RECOMP_WAIT_POLL_US=N  the wait poll interval; =1000 restores the old build


1. WHAT THE GLITCH IS
=====================
About a quarter of the intro's music was the previous lap of voice 68's
16384-sample ring, replayed, in unbroken runs of 100-163 ms, ~2.7 times a
second. Every sample of it is valid decoded music.

The chain, every link measured:

  * CRI's renderer moves at most 1024 samples per server pass (clamp at guest
    0x0013E965), so 44100 Hz needs >= 43.1 passes/s.
  * The server is a guest thread (body 0x0013B1C0) waiting on the D3D vblank
    event at 59.94 Hz. That looks like 2x headroom. It is 39%.
  * MEASURED 33.4 passes/s, pinned, at 88 fps and at 12 fps alike, with CRI's
    own consecutive-underrun counter (0x002615AC) flat ZERO -- the renderer
    always had data; the pass rate was the ceiling.
  * bridge_KeWaitForSingleObject is not a wait. It is a poll loop ending in
    Sleep(1) -> nanosleep, late under load, on a 16.67 ms budget. A cycle that
    overruns one vblank period catches the next one and the rate halves.


2. THE FIX, AND WHAT IT LEAVES
==============================
Default wait poll 1000 -> 100 us (8440c9c). Same scene, 70 s each:

              server passes/s   guest writes   ring stale   frame rate
   1000 us         36.8            71-75%       25-29%      11.6/11.7/14.1
    100 us         44.9              86%          14%       11.6/11.9/14.2

Cost side empty: frame times identical window for window, scene gets as far
(live=137 vs 134), vblank delivery slightly BETTER (59.9 Hz vs 59.6).

Confirmed independently against xemu, correlation of our attract clip with the
oracle's:

    window    before    after
    100 ms     0.971    0.980
    400 ms     0.883    0.965
    1000 ms    0.449    0.904
    2000 ms    0.281    0.634

Short windows were already ~0.99 both ways -- the samples were always right.

NOT FINISHED. 14-17% of the ring is still replayed and the 2 s correlation is
0.634. At 44.9 passes/s the server still sometimes crosses a vblank period.
Next lever: the wait is still a poll against a deadline tracked in whole
milliseconds (next_vblank, GetTickCount), so sub-ms wake needs that clock
reworked -- or a real wakeup when the event is set.

=========================================

  * "Voice bounds are incoherent": an artifact. voice_desc_dump runs at the TOP

4. HOW TO COMPARE AUDIO WITH xemu, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS WAY LIES
===============================================================
The previous session's A/B declared our clip and xemu's "statistically
indistinguishable" and concluded the samples were fine. Both halves were wrong,
from one method error.

  * Correlation over ONE long window cannot separate "different music" from
    "same music, broken continuity". Both come back near zero. Ours and xemu's
    read 0.09 over six seconds and 0.98-0.99 from 5 ms to 400 ms. SWEEP THE
    WINDOW LENGTH -- the length at which it collapses IS the defect's period.
  * A coarse ratio grid steps straight over a rate error and reports no match,
    which reads exactly like a finding. A 6 s window decorrelates at 0.15%.
  * CONTROL EVERY CORRELATOR AGAINST ITSELF, in the same run, at every window
    length. r=1.000 self-match is the only thing that separates "no match" from
    "broken instrument". This caught one of mine.
  * Envelope agreement is not content agreement. Per-second RMS tracked for four
    seconds while the waveforms had already diverged.

Scripts (scratchpad, not committed): winsweep.py, track.py, match.py, ratesearch.py
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-15_A_METAL_RENDERER_AND_FOUR_COUNTERS_THAT_LIED.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE, 15 Sep 2026 (evening/night)
A METAL RENDERER THAT LETS THE HARDWARE DO THE WORK, AND FOUR COUNTERS THAT LIED

Supersedes CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-15_THE_CONTROL_ARM_WAS_NEVER_A_CONTROL.txt
for everything about the renderer, the crash attribution, and what `vsh` is.
Its APU sections stand.

~20 commits, ctest 30/30, metal_hw_check PASS, nothing pushed since 76fa9f5.


0. THE ONE PARAGRAPH VERSION
=============================
There is now a second Metal backend behind RECOMP_METAL_HW: real depth and
stencil attachments, hardware blend/depth/stencil, combiners still in the
shader. It is 9.6% faster (ranges do not overlap, arms verified distinct) and
MORE correct -- depth 2000x closer to the oracle. A true RGB565 colour
attachment (RECOMP_METAL_565) takes 16 bytes a pixel to 2 and is mid-A/B.
Both default OFF pending a person playing them. Separately: `vsh` is not the
vertex shader, the crash is one instruction in recompiled DirectSound with a
trigger you can drive, and the USB driver was never stalling.


1. THE RENDERER, AND WHY THE OLD ONE WAS SLOW
==============================================
One decision explains the whole shape of the old backend: 24-bit depth was
packed into the colour attachment's ALPHA. Its own comment says so -- "so there
is no destination alpha". With alpha spent, hardware blending is unavailable;
blending moves into the fragment shader; depth and stencil follow; the shader
then needs raster_order_group(0) on both attachments, which SERIALISES every
overdrawn pixel; and the attachment must be RGBA32Float, sixteen bytes a pixel
for a surface the guest thinks is two.

RECOMP_METAL_HW undoes that cascade. Separate Depth32Float and Stencil8
attachments -- measured on this host first: all three candidate formats accept
MTLStorageModeShared and direct replaceRegion/getBytes on Apple Silicon, so no
blit encoder is needed. Pipeline and depth/stencil objects cached on guest
state, because Metal bakes blending into the pipeline and it cannot be set per
draw. Untranslatable state REJECTS the draw rather than falling back, because
depth ownership has to be exclusive -- see section 2.

MEASURED, arms verified distinct (hw draws=0 against 742443, zero refusals):

    RECOMP_METAL_HW=0   31.56  31.78  34.62 ms   (mean 32.65, n=3)
    RECOMP_METAL_HW=1   28.83  30.20        ms   (mean 29.52, n=2)
    clear                9.61 / 10.25 / 11.12  ->  5.76 ms

submit and vsh did not move, which is right -- this touches neither. A clear's
cost is mostly waiting for the GPU to drain, and without the raster order group
there is less outstanding to wait for.

The vertex stage needed NO change: vs() already emits o.p.z = z*p.w with
z = guest_z/16777215, so after the hardware divide the rasteriser holds exactly
the guest's normalised depth.


2. THREE BUGS IN IT, AND HOW EACH WAS FOUND
============================================
None by reading. All three by metal_hw_check.sh.

  * fs_hw returned float4(c.rgb, 1). The blend unit takes SRC_ALPHA from that,
    where the shader took it from c.a -- so every alpha-blended draw went
    opaque. 23096 of 65536 pixels.
  * DEPTH OWNERSHIP. Letting draws choose per-draw put one quantity in two
    stores on different schedules. Every differing pixel read software
    0x000000 against hardware 0xFFFFFF: the attachment still held its uploaded
    value because the draws that wrote depth had quietly used the other path.
    Untranslatable state now rejects the draw.
  * DEFAULTS MUST MATCH THE REFERENCE, NOT IMPROVE ON IT. An unrecognised
    compare is now ALWAYS and an unrecognised stencil op KEEP, because that is
    what cmpf()'s "default: return true" and stop()'s "default: return old"
    already do. Reachable: metal_batch_test sets depth_func=4, a D3D-style
    value the NV2A never emits.

AND THE GATE ITSELF WAS WRONG. It demanded the two Metal paths be
byte-identical, assuming the old one was the reference. Both approximate the
software rasteriser, and against that oracle the new path is 2000x closer on
depth. A byte-identical rule fails the more accurate renderer FOR being more
accurate. It now scores both against the oracle.


3. THE COLOUR FORMAT, WHERE I WAS WRONG TWICE   <-- READ BEFORE TOUCHING IT
===========================================================================
I wrote, and committed twice, that the software rasteriser prefers a float
attachment because float keeps blend intermediates exact.

IT KEEPS NOTHING EXACT. nv2a_texture_copy.c:691-711 reads its blend destination
out of guest RAM with unpack565() and stores RGB565 back after every pixel of
every draw. It is a framebuffer-precision blender and always was. xemu is the
same on both backends -- GL_RGB565 and VK_FORMAT_R5G6B5_UNORM_PACK16, a true
two-byte attachment. Our own nv2a_d3d11.c:972 uses R8G8B8A8.

So float is the one format NOBODY models, being the only one that never
requantises between draws. If intermediate precision drove the ranking, RGBA8
would be closest to the oracle and float furthest; it is the exact inverse, so
that ranking measures double rounding at the readback boundary.

Scored by MAGNITUDE (the test reports worst-step now; a bare count cannot be
acted on, and this project admitted the D3D11 sink under "within one RGB565
channel step" with 48% of pixels differing):

    RGBA32Float      1 of 65536 pixels, worst 1 step
    RGBA16Unorm     24, worst 1
    RGBA8Unorm    5705, worst 1
    B5G6R5Unorm    697, worst 1     <- and it is 2 bytes a pixel

All conform. RECOMP_METAL_565 uses B5G6R5 and deletes both per-pixel conversion
loops from the sync path -- upload and readback become 16-bit row copies.

NO CHANNEL SWAP. Metal's format is NAMED B5G6R5Unorm, which reads as
blue-in-the-high-bits. It is not: packed names run from the least significant
bit up, so it already IS the guest's layout. A swap written on the other
reading scored 38060 pixels wrong at up to 27 steps.

A/B mid-flight at handover: 565=0 gave 30.61-33.55 (n=3), 565=1 gave 27.43
(n=1, two runs lost to the crash). Pool the two rounds before concluding.


4. FOUR COUNTERS THAT LIED, ONE PER HOUR
=========================================
This is the section to read if you read nothing else.

  * `vsh` IS NOT THE VERTEX SHADER. The timer brackets all of
    prepare_vertices(). Proof: with the reuse cache on, a HIT -- which skips
    the attribute fetch AND the whole shader, doing nothing but one copy --
    still costs 93% of a full transform. The cost is the 256-byte write into
    s_outputs, float[4096][16][4], one megabyte. NINE of those sixteen slots
    are dead. RECOMP_VSH_NARROW_OUTPUTS copies the seven live ones and is
    built, unmeasured, and the biggest column on the board.
    THE MSL EMITTER IS AIMED AT ARITHMETIC THAT IS ~7% OF THE COST.
  * `ord175` READ AS A USB STALL. Three crashed runs showed 4709/3578 against
    a healthy 32547 and I wrote up "the USB driver had stalled". Normalised by
    duration: 117.7, 119.4, 120.5 transfers per second. Identical. They were
    30-40 s runs that crashed. ab_score.py reports usb=N/s now.
  * `[VBLANK] over N ms` READ AS A CRASH TIME. Every fault appeared to land at
    exactly 30 s or 40 s, which looked deterministic. It is the REPORT CADENCE:
    that line only prints at a periodic report. Pad events give the real clock.
  * (yesterday's, still true) `trapped=` counts frames where the engine was
    switched OFF, and NtOpenFile measures the disc cache build.

Every one was fixed by finding an instrument with the right resolution, never
by reasoning harder about the wrong one.


5. THE CRASH HAS ONE INSTRUCTION AND A TRIGGER
===============================================
All 11 faults recorded today:

    HOST PC:            sub_001A2E2E +0x670
    HOST FAULT ADDRESS: guest 0xFFFFFFBE

0x1A2E2E is inside DSOUND (0x19E340 + 116060), so this is recompiled
DirectSound. STATUS.md already had 20 of 33 faults attributed to that handler
with a register fingerprint and a call chain -- better evidence than I
rediscovered. What is new:

  * ACCURACY_GAPS said "OHCI path" and STATUS said DirectSound. Corrected.
  * IT IS NOT A NULL OBJECT. STATUS says the handler "dereferences a voice
    object that is NULL". A NULL object read at [obj+0xBE] faults at 0xBE.
    This faults at 0xFFFFFFBE, every time -- the top of the address space,
    which is what a pointer computed from a SENTINEL looks like. 0xFFFF is the
    voice list's own terminator. That points at the LINK VALUE, not the
    object lookup.
  * IT HAS A TRIGGER. Every crash lands immediately after an `A` press on the
    title menu -- t=31.00, t=31.01, t=39.00 against a schedule with A at 31.0
    and 39.0. That is the menu-to-mission transition starting audio, which
    matches STATUS's independently measured t=43-50 s. It is reproducible on
    demand rather than a 12% lottery.

sub_001A2E2E reads the guest's software previous/next links and updates the
hardware list -- the same correspondence as the trap storm, where our regs[top]
and the guest's software list disagree about the head. The two may be one
defect. Not proven.

DO NOT suppress a trap or forcibly unlink a voice. Standing instruction from
the audio-lifecycle note and still right.


6. WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT
========================
  1. Pool the two 565 A/B rounds and decide that switch.
  2. RECOMP_VSH_NARROW_OUTPUTS. Biggest column, built, needs no code, never
     measured -- its A/B was killed at n=1.
  3. EARLY-Z. fs_hw calls discard_fragment() for the z-range cull and the alpha
     test, which disables early-Z for EVERY draw, so the depth unit cannot
     reject fragments before shading. A second pipeline variant without the
     discards, selected when neither is active, may be the largest remaining
     win given this title's overdraw. Small change.
  4. THE METAL PRESENTER. The frame still ends Metal -> CPU readback -> two
     conversions -> glTexImage2D -> GL quad. Two GPU APIs and a full CPU round
     trip, every frame. Deletes one of ~4.8 syncs. Uncosted and possibly the
     biggest item here.
  5. The sub_001A2E2E probe, now that it has a trigger: dump the software
     prev/next links on entry.
  6. Before any upstream PR: the caches are 16 entries sized from "JSRF uses
     three", and nv2a_metal.m:1739 refuses target_bpp != 2. Both are limits
     that should be evidence-driven rather than title-shaped. The translation
     layer itself (nv2a_metal_state.c) has zero title knowledge and is ready.

BOOT ATTRITION IS THE TAX ON ALL OF THIS. Roughly one run in four of every A/B
is lost to the section 5 crash, which is why three trials is the floor and why
some arms still land at n=1.
```

```txt
3. THE OPEN QUESTION IN SECTION 3 WAS MALFORMED   <-- READ THIS FIRST
======================================================================
The last handover put it as: "WHY regs[top] IS STALE IS NOT ESTABLISHED."

It is not stale. The chain it belongs to was:

    the guest writes link(v) = v as its "not in any list" sentinel before
    re-ONing v; our regs[top] still names v; VOICE_ON stores link(v) = v

Classify only the ON that FIRST self-links each voice -- the later ones are the
absorbing state re-counted -- across all four instrumented runs. Sixteen
cycle-forming inserts. In NOT ONE did link(v) hold the sentinel: twelve pointed
at another voice, four at the FFFF terminator, which is the last element of a
list and not absence from one. The sentinel reading comes from counting all 358
self-linking ONs, where it is 343 of them, i.e. from counting the consequence.

What the log shows, end to end, 20260915-122828-human-gameplay, 3D list:

    9417  [VOICE-LINK]   voice=4 link=0004->0001      ON 4   head 1 -> 4
    9444  [VOICE-RELINK] voice=4 ours=0001 now=FFFF at=walk
    9510  [VOICE-LINK]   voice=4 link=FFFF->0004 SELF-LINK

At 9444 the guest rewrites link(4) to FFFF as it removes voices 1 and 3 from
BEHIND voice 4 -- so it is maintaining the list correctly and treating 4 as the
live head, exactly as we do. Then it ONs voice 4 again. regs[top] is 4 because
voice 4 IS the head. No head write is missing and no handshake failed.

THE PRODUCER IS A VOICE_ON FOR A VOICE ALREADY AT THE HEAD OF ITS LIST, which
is an ordinary thing for DirectSound to do with a buffer whose voice has stopped
but has not yet been taken out of the hardware list.

The remaining unexplained part is small and sharp, and it is the next thing to
measure: our regs[top] names v at the re-ON and the guest's own software list
evidently does not, or RemoveIdleVoice would have written TVL when it took v
out. WHERE THE TWO VIEWS PART COMPANY is the question. It is not "why is the
head stale" and it is not "does our insert match xemu" -- that was answered
last session and the answer is yes.

This also removes the argument that made the self-link guard safe. "Terminating
cannot lose a reachable voice" rested on the guest having already written
link(v) = v. At formation link(v) held a real successor and OUR INSERT
OVERWROTE IT, so terminating drops whatever the guest still had behind v.
Looping drops the same tail and pins the walk as well, so the guard is not
worse -- but neither is lossless, and both losses come from the insert
overwriting a live link.

    on = getenv("RECOMP_APU_SELFLINK_END") != NULL;

so =0 ENABLED the guard, which is the opposite of what its own comment eight

5. THE TWO A/Bs, AND WHY NEITHER DEFAULT MOVED
===============================================
RECOMP_METAL_BATCH -- ten boots, four usable runs per arm, scored only inside

                    per frame, mean of 4      range
      clear         10.75 -> 8.88 ms     9.49-11.47 v 8.70-9.24   NO OVERLAP
      submit         8.09 -> 7.73 ms     7.63-8.29  v 7.60-7.83
      vsh           10.55 -> 11.25 ms    9.14-11.54 v 10.67-12.65
      whole frame   33.53 -> 32.27 ms    30.23-35.13 v 31.49-33.77

The win is real, localised and about 2.2 ms/frame off clear+submit. `clear` is
the only column that separates, which makes sense: a clear reaches the GPU
through nv2a_metal_sync(), so its cost is a drain, and batching changes how much
is outstanding when the drain happens. WHOLE-FRAME TIME DOES NOT SEPARATE,
because vsh -- the CPU vertex interpreter, which batching does not touch --
varies 3.5 ms run to run and swamps it.

Default stays OFF and none of that bears on why. The gate is the SEGA-screen
hang: one interactive session, never reproduced, seventeen scripted boots now
and it was in none of them -- which is the evidence it already had. A PERSON
RUNNING RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=1 INTERACTIVELY IS THE ONLY THING THAT CLOSES IT.

RECOMP_APU_SELFLINK_END -- six boots, five usable, arms verified distinct:

                      guard OFF (n=2)      guard ON (n=3)
    idle traps         19706  18891         18957  18883  18344
    halted frames       6350   5809          2286   1564   1457
    engine duty        98.43% 98.57%        99.44% 99.61% 99.64%
    longest trap run      47     47            87     55     55  frames
    frame time         36.74  31.95 ms      36.44  35.31  34.07 ms

THE TRAP STORM IS UNCHANGED -- raises overlap, and the busiest voice's share of
them swings 70-98% inside the OFF arm alone. Yesterday's verdict was right and
now has something behind it.

Two things moved in opposite directions and neither decides it. Duty separates,
98.5% against 99.6%, which is dropped subframes falling from ~6100 to ~1700 a
run; but it is entirely the halted-frame count, `halted` is the GUEST writing
FECTL, and the path from this switch to that count is not established. Against
it, the guest takes LONGER to service each trap -- longest trapped run 31 ms to
37-58 ms. Default stays off. What would decide it is the mechanism behind
`halted`, not more runs of this A/B.


6. A FIX THAT IS NOT A FIX FOR ANYTHING YOU ARE CHASING
========================================================
CVL and NVL are one cursor and both have to hold still. Hardware stalls the walk
on a trap with CVL naming the idle voice and NVL its successor, and
RemoveIdleVoice repairs the pair to steer an in-progress walk through the voice
it is removing.

Holding only CVL was enough while the frame thread idled on TRAPPED -- nothing
then ran to move NVL either. Since RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED became the
default the walk is re-entered every 1500th of a second while the guest still
owes a service, and it was rewriting NVL at every voice behind the trapped one
and then resetting CVL from TVL at the top of the next frame, discarding the one
value the guest was told to read.

Now separated: the local rendering cursor always starts at the head, so the
duty-cycle win is untouched, and the guest-visible pair does not move until the
guest clears the trap. With coalescing off, a raise that replaces an outstanding
one moves the pair, so FEDECPARAM and CVL cannot name different voices.

THIS IS NOT THE STORM'S FIX AND IS NOT OFFERED AS ONE. The storm is measured in
runs that predate both this and the local cursor. It is the handshake the guest
is entitled to, and it was intact before yesterday.


7. MY RETRACTIONS AND NEAR-MISSES
==================================
  * "ON is faster and the ranges DO NOT OVERLAP (5.8%)." My own summariser
    printed that for one run against one run. A single run has a range of zero
    width. Caught before reporting it, and the tool now refuses below n=2.
  * "The self-link is a legitimate one-element list, so the guard models
    hardware." Written, then weakened: the same finding that supports it shows
    our insert destroys a live link, so terminating drops a tail. Both readings
    are in section 3 and the default did not move on either.
  * I assumed the previous session's "indistinguishable" was a statistical
    weakness. It was a mechanical one -- the control arm enabled the thing it
    controlled for -- and the tell was printed in every report of every run.

One process note: do not edit src/**.c|h|m while an A/B is running. The
staleness guard will refuse the next run and abort the whole thing. Docs, .sh
and .py are safe; ab_switch.sh itself is not, because sh reads a script
incrementally.
```
