```txt
CLAUDE, 15 Sep 2026 (afternoon)
THE SOUND ENGINE WAS SWITCHED OFF, AND THE HARNESS WAS WATCHING THE WRONG SCREEN

Supersedes CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-14_THE_INSTRUMENTS_LIE.txt for
everything about the APU voice list, the idle-voice trap storm, and how a
scripted run is scored. 13 commits, ctest 29/29 (the suite gained

Two of today's findings came from a person looking at the game window and
sending a screenshot. Both overturned a conclusion I had already written down.
That is the third session running where that has happened and it is now the
most reliable instrument in this project.


0. THE ONE PARAGRAPH VERSION
=============================
The sound engine was running on 63.6% of APU frames because `trapped=` does not
count traps -- it counts frames where the engine is SWITCHED OFF waiting for one
to be serviced. RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED fixes that (98.6%) but costs 125,000
guest interrupts, so a second change coalesces a trap that is already
outstanding and gives 92% of them back. Both are now default-on and the gate on
them -- "heard at gameplay, with a controller" -- IS STILL OPEN. Separately:
every scripted run in this tree has been landing in the VS Battle menu, because
gameplay.pad fires six bare A presses after a selection is already made; and the
NtOpenFile gate everything was scored on was timing the DISC CACHE BUILD, not
the scene.


1. WHAT IS COMMITTED
=====================
Sound (the deliverable):
  * RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED default ON. 63.6% -> 98.6% engine duty.
  * RECOMP_APU_TRAP_COALESCE default ON, new. Do not re-raise SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE
    while FEMETHMODE is already TRAPPED.
  * RECOMP_APU_SELFLINK_END, new, default OFF -- see section 5, it is not a fix.
  * [APU-TRAP], [APU-SELFLINK], [APU-LINK], [VOICE-TOP], [VOICE-RELINK],
    [APU-FE-UNKNOWN] counters.

Harness (the thing that had been invalidating measurements):
  * pad/gameplay_nobarrage.pad -- reaches a real mission unattended.
  * RECOMP_SEQ_REPORT -- the scene marker. play_scripted.sh scores on it.

Renderer (not wired in):
  * src/nv2a/nv2a_vsh_msl.c, full opcode coverage, two tests.

Notes: CLAUDE_PROGRESS_2026-09-15_VOICE_LIST_SELF_LINK.md,
CLAUDE_PROGRESS_2026-09-15_THE_FONT_IS_NOT_BROKEN.md, and a parallel session's
2026-09-15-audio-lifecycle.md.


2. THE SOUND FIX, AND WHY THE TWO HALVES ARE INSEPARABLE
=========================================================
Read the counter's trigger first, as always. `trapped=` in [APU-FRAME] is
incremented in mcpx_apu_frame_thread when FEMETHMODE == TRAPPED, i.e. on frames
where the sound engine is SKIPPED. It was never a measure of how many traps were
raised. 67 raises/s x 11 subframes of dwell = 49% of frames, which is the ~50%
that has been in ACCURACY_GAPS as "the engine is down about half the time".

Two matched pairs each, 240 s, same binary, arms alternated:

    SE_WHILE_TRAPPED off   duty 63.8% 63.5%   trapped 113408 114048   raises ~10300
    SE_WHILE_TRAPPED on    duty 99.1% 98.8%   trapped      0      0   raises ~125000

    coalesce off (SE on)   raises 112716 120791   duty 98.9% 98.5%
    coalesce on  (SE on)   raises   9455  12138   duty 98.8% 98.6%

The engine had been throttling its own trap rate BY SWITCHING ITSELF OFF. Turn
it back on and the raise count explodes twelvefold, and every raise is an
interrupt into the DirectSound ISR that 20 of the 33 recorded faults land in.
Shipping the first without the second would have traded a duty-cycle defect for
a crash-rate one. Zero faults across all four coalesce arms, which is
reassuring and is not the same as evidence at n=4.

Validated at a mission the scene marker confirms is state 30: duty 98.6%,
trapped=0, suppressed=95721.

THE GATE IS OPEN. The comment beside the switch said "no default until it has
been heard at gameplay, with a controller". I changed the default on counters
and rewrote the comment to say the gate is still open rather than delete it. A
person has to listen to a sustained sound -- the grind is the documented tell,
because an engine down a third of the time makes a continuous sound fade in and
out. RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED=0 reverts in the same binary.


3. WHAT IS STILL BROKEN UNDERNEATH IT   <-- THE REAL OPEN QUESTION
===================================================================
The fix restores the engine's frames. It does not explain why the traps happen.

Measured, end to end, in one gameplay run carrying every counter: voice 3
self-links (link(3) = 3) and voice 3 is the voice raising the storm -- two
independent instruments naming the same handle. Same voice, same 3D list, in two
separate gameplay runs on two different binaries.

The chain: the guest writes link(v) = v as its "not in any list" sentinel before
re-ONing v; our regs[top] still names v; VOICE_ON stores link(v) = regs[top] = v;
the walk meets a one-entry cycle on a dead voice and traps.

WHY regs[top] IS STALE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. That is the open question.

What the xemu comparison settled (read against xemu master and the XDK
DirectSound driver source, mcpvoice.cpp):
  * Our VOICE_ON is byte-for-byte xemu's. git log -S on the TOP write finds only
    the initial import. KEEP IT -- CMcpxVoiceClient never writes TVL on the
    insert path and its own debug validation asserts dwTVL equals its head
    voice, so conditioning that write away breaks every head insertion.
  * The driver source independently confirms all three guest behaviours the
    differential shadow caught: TVL = next for a head removal, predecessor
    relink otherwise, then point the voice at itself. Nothing the guest did was
    anomalous.
  * xemu has no cycle detection either, and accepts guest TVL writes verbatim.

So the divergence is OURS and it is in the walk, not the insert. Two local
changes:
  1. xemu finishes the walk and stalls the next frame on TRAPPED. We return
     mid-walk on a local cursor. RemoveIdleVoice repairs CVL AND NVL to steer an
     in-progress hardware walk through the voice being removed -- and a mid-walk
     removal is exactly what [VOICE-RELINK] voice=70 ... at=walk caught. The
     guest computes those repairs from registers our walk no longer honours.
  2. xemu raises the trap for every inactive voice it meets; we raise one per
     frame per list and hold (trap_held).

CHASE 1. It is the only candidate with a mechanism behind it.


4. THE HARNESS WAS MEASURING THE WRONG SCREEN, FOR EVERYTHING
==============================================================
gameplay.pad reuses new_game.pad's eight START/START/A groups -- documented to
reach the Corn tutorial -- and then adds

    76.0:A  80.0:A  84.0:A  88.0:A  92.0:A  96.0:A

after a selection has already been made. Those six presses walk the menu into VS
Battle. A person looked at the window and said "selected vs mode"; that is how
this was found, after three instrumented runs and a frame-rate A/B had been
taken there.

pad/gameplay_nobarrage.pad drops the barrage and keeps everything else. Verified
by the scene marker to reach state 30, a running mission, unattended. That is
the first scripted run in this repository to do so.

AND THE GATE EVERYTHING WAS SCORED ON WAS MEASURING SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY.
NtOpenFile 1342/1408 was the DISC CACHE BUILD, not the scene. The 1410-open run
wrote Media/Cache into the staged HDD -- the directory is dated 11:11, the minute
that run ended -- and every HDD staged since carries a complete cache plus
JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE.CMP, so StartBuildCache is skipped and the count collapses to
131 in EVERY scene. File logging stops at t = 79-81 s in all runs, minutes before
either scene is reached. play_scripted.sh was printing "SCENE: NEVER LEFT THE
TITLE" for a screenshot-confirmed gameplay run.

The marker that works was already in the tree and switched off in every run:
RECOMP_SEQ_TRACE reads CActSequence::m_dwNextMethod, which the sequence methods
write themselves. RECOMP_SEQ_REPORT now prints it once per report.

    12 = WaitEndTitle      58 = WaitEndVsMenu      30 = WaitEndStoryOrVsMission

Verified, not trusted: the 64-entry table at 0x0020D2B8 was dumped out of
default.xbe and matches jsrf_seq_tab entry for entry, and the disassembly shows
the VS chain writing its own successor. Validated against a falsifiable control
-- a run with no pad schedule at all must read 12, and did.

Two things it will NOT tell you: state 30 means a mission action object exists,
so the loading screen, the opening cutscene and the pause menu are all inside
it; and character select and stage select are the same state.


5. THE FIX THAT WASN'T, AND WHY IT IS STILL IN THE TREE
========================================================
RECOMP_APU_SELFLINK_END treats link(v) == v as end-of-list in the walk. That is
the driver's own convention -- SetupVoiceProcessor writes it for all 256 voices
at boot -- so it is correct on its own terms, and an unbounded self-cycle is a
defect regardless (the walk's only protection is a 256-iteration cap, so a
self-linked ACTIVE voice would render 256 times in a subframe).

It is not the trap storm fix. It fired 47,293 times in 240 s and left trapped at
50.3%, indistinguishable. Terminating the cycle cannot help: the self-linked
voice is still the HEAD of its list and still inactive, so the walk begins on a
dead voice and traps whether or not it then loops. I fixed the loop and left the
trap.

DEFAULT OFF, because shipping it on would be patching around a gate before a run
proved which value was wrong.


6. TEXT RENDERING: THERE IS NO DEFECT
======================================
Reported as glyph substitution from three screenshots -- DDD1 for 0001, Spra§
for Spray, %SOU for $SOU. Every wrong character was a clean valid glyph of the
same font, which is the shape of an indexing fault.

It is the shipped art. Decoded the assets and looked at them: the HUD sprite
sheet's zero is a heavy filled square with a triangular notch cut from its
upper-left corner, jetfont's y has a flat horizontal descender instead of a
tail, and jetfont's $ carries two rectangular counters either side of a blocky
S. At gameplay size those read as D, § and %.

The fact that should have stopped me sooner was already in hand: the errors are
selective INSIDE ONE STRING drawn by ONE call. "Spra§ Cans" has a correct 'a'
before the bad glyph and C-a-n-s after it. A fault in a shared index or UV
computation moves every character, not one.

decode_norm_asset.py is kept -- it turns any Media/**/*.dat into PNGs and writes
down the NORM/MULT container format. The trap in it, which costs an hour to
rediscover, is that nested containers use offsets relative to their own base.


7. SPEED: WHAT THE FRAME IS ACTUALLY MADE OF
=============================================
From a 20-minute human play session, [METAL] sync:

    443,738 ms draining the GPU     125,914 ms reading back and converting

78% drain, 22% readback. The code's own comment says what that means: a resident
clear could remove the second only, and if the drain is nearly all of it the
available win is pipelining. RECOMP_METAL_BATCH is exactly that lever, is
already measured (69.2 ms per-draw against 46.5 ms batched, 25 alternating
replays of one captured frame, distributions not overlapping), and is off for a
SAFETY reason, not a performance one: one interactive session got stuck on the
SEGA screen and twelve scripted boots could not reproduce it.

An A/B of it at a scene-verified mission was IN FLIGHT when this was written, in
measure/batch_gameplay_*. It reports boot success (scene marker) and frame time
per arm. Read it before doing anything else on speed.

Larger and structural: NV2A vertex programs are INTERPRETED ON THE CPU on this
host -- nv2a_vsh_execute, ~7.5 ms of a ~32 ms frame -- while the D3D11 path emits
HLSL. src/nv2a/nv2a_vsh_msl.c is a complete MSL emitter with tests and is
DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED IN. Three things break the moment vertex work moves to
the GPU: triangle() assembles and culls on the CPU from the shader's own output
and would lose oPos; prepare_vertices' VSH_REJECT paths vanish, so batches now
dropped start drawing while their reject counters read zero (which looks like an
improvement); and s_outputs/s_colors feed texture interpolation, the software
rasteriser and the draw captures, all of which would silently read zeros. The
cheapest next step is a compute kernel over the same inputs compared against the
interpreter across all 16 outputs -- the shape vsh_reference_test.c already uses.


8. MY RETRACTIONS TODAY
========================
Listed because the pattern is the useful part, as last session's was.

  * "The text rendering is a new defect." It is the game's own art. I had
    already written down the fact that kills the theory -- correct characters
    either side of a wrong one -- and built on top of it anyway.
  * "The self-link guard is the fix." It fires 47,293 times and moves nothing.
  * "The guest never writes the list head." Asserted off a t=30 s sample taken
    before any voice churn, when the only writes were three init writes to FFFF.
    It writes it 33-36 times a run.
  * "The INHERIT branch's arithmetic produces the self-link." Real code, never
    executed: on_inherit=0 across 596 ONs. The counter caught the true producer
    only because it was written as a READBACK of the outcome instead of as the
    condition I expected.
  * "Stale FEAV from a store lost through the guarded page." antecedent_sets
    tracked on exactly at every report of every run.
  * "opens=131 proves those runs never reached gameplay." The gameplay run
    reports 131 too. The menu diagnosis was right and rests on a screenshot.

Two process errors worth not repeating:
  * I rebuilt the binary underneath a running A/B, which silently changed a
    default halfway through the arms. Restarted it.
  * I ran `git add -A` in a tree where a parallel agent was working and swept an
    in-progress draft of nv2a_vsh_msl.c into an APU commit. Fixed forward.
    Stage paths, not the tree, when anything else is writing here.


9. WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT
========================
  1. LISTEN to it. The sound gate is a person's ears and nothing else closes it.
  2. Read measure/batch_gameplay_* and decide RECOMP_METAL_BATCH's default. It

  3. Section 3: why regs[top] is stale. Honour CVL/NVL in the walk so the

     on a pre-cached HDD and it currently reports the opposite of the truth.
```

```txt
3 September 2026 - startup, memory, return paths, and where the renderer
actually stops

WORKSPACE
/Users/andrewcollard/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Jet Set Radio Future/upstream_xboxrecomp_clean

Host macOS arm64. Branch main. This continues your
CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-03_STARTUP.txt, which is still accurate about
everything before this session.

UNLIKE PREVIOUS HANDOVERS, THE TREE IS COMMITTED AND PUSHED. origin is
andeecollard/upstream_xboxrecomp_clean. Three commits, in order:

  9645601  Nothing was ever freed, and every return path that lied about it
  e97c71c  Every batch was refused for one reason, and it was not the reason
           we assumed
  879fa2f  The vertex buffers were empty, and then the fragment stage ate the
           rest

9645601 also landed your uncommitted graphics/pushbuffer/startup work, because
the build does not stand up without it. build-macos is still gitignored, so
the hand-patched generated tree is NOT in the repo -- see section 6.

Companion documents, all in the repo now:
  JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-03_RENDERER.md         the current goal list
  CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-03_HEAP.txt       memory and return paths, in detail
  CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-03_RENDERER.txt   the renderer measurements, in detail
This document is the summary of both plus what I would do next.

==========================================================================
1. WHERE THE TITLE GETS TO NOW
==========================================================================

A 300-second fresh-HDD run (render-investigation/claude-long-21):

  no guest fault, no allocation failure, no 'epilogue never ran',
  no unresolved stub executed, root pointer stable throughout
  290 distinct asset paths
  259 files / 117 MB written to the emulated HDD
  Cache00-08.tbl, DmCache00-09.tbl, and nine
  JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE00..08.CMP markers
  no JSRF_FATAL.ERR

The first-boot cache BUILDS AND COMPLETES. Against your seh-04 baseline that
was 38,840 allocation failures, ~30 asset paths and 27 files / 15 MB.

Still no picture: 93 dumped frames, all byte-identical black, SHA-256
9dc5cdcf2b4abd98a266b99496fa0062bec2c56e30b979a7cb5d033275eed1b3 -- the same
value as your runs. No renderer behaviour was added this session beyond one
vertex format; everything else was measurement.

==========================================================================
2. THE STAGE-LOAD ALLOCATION FAILURE - IT WAS NOT FRAGMENTATION
==========================================================================

Your goal A. The number in the message was a bump high-water mark, so I added
accounting that says what is live. At the first failure:

  live 997 blocks / 47,307,848 bytes; free 0 blocks / 0 bytes

Nothing had ever been returned to the guest heap. Three separate causes, all
in how kernel frees were routed:

  ExFreePool (ordinal 17) had NO BRIDGE. The dispatch entry was commented out
  on purpose -- the note in kernel_bridge.c says each of that group needs its
  memory model checked, and it was right to stop: the existing wrapper called
  the host HeapFree on a translated guest pointer. But bridge_ExAllocatePool
  takes its block from xbox_HeapAlloc and returns a guest VA, so the free
  belongs to the same allocator. Bridged now.

  NtFreeVirtualMemory (199) went to the host VirtualFree on a guest address.
  MEM_RELEASE was silently dropped -- the POSIX shim returns TRUE for size 0
  -- and MEM_DECOMMIT would have mprotect(PROT_NONE)'d live guest RAM. 12,072
  calls per 60s run. Now MEM_RELEASE goes to xbox_HeapFree and MEM_DECOMMIT
  is a no-op, mirroring the MEM_COMMIT no-op on the allocate side.

  MmFreeContiguousMemory (171) did reach xbox_HeapFree, but the title frees
  through the physical mirror (0x80000000 + address) and the table matched on
  the raw value. Every free in your logs is 0x81Exxxxx and matched nothing.
  xbox_HeapFree and xbox_HeapBlockSize canonicalise the alias now.

Repairing those exposed a second failure: 13.9 MB free, a 2.8 MB largest free
block, and a 349,520-byte page-aligned request failing anyway. Reuse split a
block at the end of the request, so remainders started at arbitrary addresses,
and every caller that reaches this heap wants page alignment. Splits are now
page-aligned. Two more defects went with it: reuse handed over whole blocks
without splitting at all, and coalescing tested the adjacent table index, so a
size-0 hole from an earlier merge made two adjacent free blocks permanently
un-mergeable.

Your note that a stale comment claims no reuse: the comment is gone, and
jsrf_heap_alloc is a new ctest that drives the real allocator against a live
memory layout and checks each of these behaviours.

==========================================================================
3. THE SECOND BLOCKER - YOUR SHARED-EPILOGUE BUG, ONE CLASS WIDER
==========================================================================

With memory available the title reached Stg10_05 and took SIGSEGV. I suspected
my own frees; RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=0xAB fills every freed block and the fault
was identical with the bad pointer 0x8508C483, not the poison. New code.

It was your bug again. sub_0002D240 dispatches through the table at 0x0002D438
and its default case 0x0002D3B3 was still a stub whose whole body is
`g_esp += 4`. 220 such stubs remained after recover_shared_epilogues.py, which
by design only repairs pure return sequences.

diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/recover_midfunction_entries.py repairs 208 of
them, on the same principle you used for the mission entries but general:

  - an address on an instruction boundary inside an already detected function
    is real code, translated from there through the end of its owner
  - an address in the gap between two detected functions is a whole function
    discovery missed, translated through the next detected start; anything
    past its return is unreachable and costs only compiled bytes
  - a body that jumps backwards to another undetected entry pulls that entry
    in too, with a declaration added to recomp_funcs.h

149 in the first pass, 59 more once gap and backward-jump support existed,
plus 13 entries they reference. The 12 that remain are printed with their
reason when the script runs (5 not on an instruction boundary, 4 incomplete
translation, 3 past the last detected function) and none of them executed.

And a stub that runs now SAYS SO, once, both in tools/recomp/translator.py for
fresh generation and via announce_unresolved_stubs.py for an existing
checkout. That silence is how 0x000250C9 and 0x001185B0 survived a whole
recovery pass. --remove reverses it.

==========================================================================
4. WHY THE SCREEN IS BLACK - MEASURED, NOT ARGUED
==========================================================================

Your goal B asked for the first distinct rejection with its reason before
implementing more graphics. Here it is, and then the next one behind it.

prepare_vertices had five ways to refuse a batch and one counter, which is why
"38,472 rejected" stayed unexplained. Split apart, the answer was unanimous:

  [VSH]  70228  vertex attribute could not be fetched (first detail 3)
  [VSH] attribute 3 unfetchable: type=0 size=4 stride=32 offset=0x01BA2010

Type 0 is UB_D3D, a packed D3DCOLOR stored B,G,R,A, and fetch_attr decoded
only F and UB_OGL. It cannot share the UB_OGL case, which is presumably why it
was left out. Seven lines; rejections went 70,228 to zero.

That did not change a pixel, and the useful part is what it exposed:

  [VSH]     executed batches=1370379 rejected=0
  [TEXTURE] prepared=456799 rejected=913580
  [TEXTURE] rejected draw 11: combiner / texture program

TWO OF EVERY THREE DRAWS ARE NOW REFUSED BY THE FRAGMENT STAGE, all with the
same reason. nv2a_texture_copy implements one measured RGB565 blit
configuration and rejects every other combiner program by design -- correct
while it was the only verified path, and now the thing in the way. The third
that pass are that blit, whose source surface is all zeros.

Four hypotheses died to measurements on the way, and they are worth knowing so
you do not re-run them:

  The executor is NOT missing a program switch. RECOMP_VSH_TRACE reports
  distinct START and LOAD slots as 0x00000001 and 0x00000001, LOAD >= 32: 0,
  with unique-hashes=1 over 19,442 decodes. One twelve-instruction program,
  always slot 0. There is no switch to miss.

  The pusher is NOT swallowing uploads. dispatch() calls nv2a_pb_exec_method
  for every method under RECOMP_PB_EXEC. The "[PUSHER] unhandled" histogram
  belongs to pgraph_d3d11_method, a different sink; its label now says so.

  Vertex arrays are NOT DMA-relative in a way we get wrong. Resolving
  SET_CONTEXT_DMA_VERTEX_A/B through your nv2a_dma_resolve gives base=0,
  limit=0x07FFAFFF for both. fetch_attr's raw offset is correct. I record this
  because the texture path does need the resolve and assuming the vertex path
  does too is reasonable and wrong.

  A loading-phase draw reads an all-zero vertex array from a block marked
  "from a reused block", which is exactly what recycling live memory looks
  like. It is not. RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=0xAB left the bytes 00, not AB;
  RECOMP_HEAP_NO_FREE=1 restores the pre-repair heap and the buffer moves to a
  never-recycled block from the same guest call site and is still all zero.
  The title allocates 128 bytes -- four vertices at stride 32, a quad -- and
  never fills it, because it is on its loading screen. After the cache
  completes it switches to inline submission with real values:
  in0=[-0.53125 -0.53125 0 1] in3=[1 1 1 1] inline=12.

==========================================================================
5. DIAGNOSTICS I ADDED - PLEASE USE THESE BEFORE REASONING
==========================================================================

xbox_HeapReport(why)            arena, bump high-water, live/free counts and
                                totals, largest free block, retained-beyond-
                                request, top owners by live bytes named by
                                kernel ordinal and guest return address, and
                                the 16 largest live blocks. Fires on the first
                                allocation failure. This is what turned "the
                                heap is full" into "nothing is ever freed".
xbox_HeapDescribe(va, buf, n)   who owns an address: extent, requested size,
                                owning ordinal and guest ra, live/free, and
                                whether it came from a reused block.
RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE=<n>           narrate the first n frees and reuses (dflt 64)
RECOMP_HEAP_POISON=<byte>       fill freed blocks. Use before blaming the heap
                                for a fault: if the bad pointer is not the
                                poison, it did not come from freed memory.
RECOMP_HEAP_NO_FREE=1           disable reclamation entirely, restoring the
                                pre-repair build. Exhausts the heap; that is
                                the point. The only honest A/B for a suspected
                                use-after-free.
RECOMP_VSH_SAMPLE=<batch>       late-batch sample, default 20000. Batch 1 is
                                always the measured blit and tells you
                                nothing. Prints attribute declarations, the
                                constants, the values handed to the program,
                                raw bytes behind the position array, resolved
                                vertex DMA contexts, and the owning heap block.
RECOMP_VSH_TRACE=1              uploads by subchannel, changed/dropped,
                                loads/starts/modes, constants, decodes,
                                unique program hashes, and distinct START and
                                LOAD slot bitmaps.
[VSH] reject histogram          prints with the periodic [VSH] line; the first
                                failure of each kind names the record.
[STUB] reports                  every unresolved stub announces itself once.
```

```txt
   tools/recomp/lifter.py had no case for FCMOVcc. It fell through to the
   generic x87 handler and became a bare comment, so the conditional move was
   never emitted. Only four x87 instructions in the whole generated tree were
   untranslated -- two harmless fnclex and these two -- and both are on the
   startup path.

   sub_0014C870 is fminf and sub_0014C850 is fmaxf. With the move gone, the
   trailing fxch/fstp discard the wrong operand and both return their SECOND
   argument. The colour packer sub_000A4CF0 clamps every channel with
   fminf(c, 1.0f) then fmaxf(c, 0.0f) and writes the result back, so it stored
   0.0f into all four channels and packed a colour of 0. sub_00024400 renders
   nothing unless +0xBC & 0xFF000000, so the fade never drew and the startup
   script never advanced.

   Your lead was close but inverted: the interpolator did step. The packer
   zeroed it on the way out. Entry/exit observation showed 18 calls in 35s
   before the fix and 45,000+ after, with 242 distinct alpha values.

3. G9 is heap exhaustion, and enlarging the arena does not fix it.

   The title still writes a zero-byte Z:\Media\Cache\JSRF_FATAL.ERR and raises
   its own disc-error dialog. That is the title's error path, not a guest
   fault -- nothing crashes.

   Three measured corrections recovered 6.4 MB. It changed nothing that
   matters. See "THE ARENA IS NOT THE PROBLEM" below before doing any more
   work on memory sizing.


WHAT I CHANGED
==============

G8 -- the FCMOVcc fix

  tools/recomp/lifter.py
    FCMOVCC_TO_JCC maps the eight FCMOVcc forms to the jcc testing the same
    EFLAGS bits. _make_fcmovcc_cond reuses the existing _make_condition
    machinery. lift_basic_block emits
        if (cond) { fp_top() = fp_st(i); }
    The source is operands[-1]: capstone reports FCMOVcc with both operands,
    and reading operands[0] would move st(0) onto itself -- the same silent
    no-op fxch st(i) once had. When no flag setter is tracked the generic
    handler now says UNTRANSLATED CONDITIONAL MOVE rather than a bare
    /* FPU: ... */, which reads as handled.

  tools/recomp/test_lifter_fcmov.py   (new)
    5 tests, 8 subtests. Both conditions, all eight forms, st(i) source
    selection, the untracked-flags message, and the whole fmin sequence in
    order.

  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/backport_fcmov.py   (new)
    The checked-out generated tree predates the lifter fix and JSRF is not
    regenerated here, so this rewrites exactly the two statements. Idempotent.
    --check is read-only and is wired up as the jsrf_fcmov_backport ctest, so a
    regeneration that loses the fix fails rather than silently reverting the
    milestone. If you do regenerate, run it; it will report "already fixed".

G9 -- the allocator

  src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c
    - Reuse now reaches an aligned start INSIDE a free block and carves the
      leading fragment off as its own free block. Once a misaligned block is
      usable the trailing split only has to respect the caller's alignment.
      ExAllocatePoolWithTag went from 706 blocks / 3,126,516 bytes holding
      400,660 bytes of requests -- 87% padding -- to 844 blocks / 435,808.
      Total slack 4,581,336 -> 1,936,552.
    - heap_absorb_frontier folds the untouched tail of the arena into the free
      block that ends at it. The two described the same arena and were only
      ever consulted separately. "unreached" at failure went 905,028 -> 0.
    - Reporting: per-owner slack, per-export alloc/free tallies, and the
      failing caller's ordinal and return address on the out-of-memory line.

  src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.h
    - XBOX_STACK_SIZE 8 MB -> 6 MB. Painting the region and scanning for the
      lowest touched word puts the main stack's high-water at 3 KB across a
      full 70-second startup; the worker slices in the bottom 4 MB are
      untouched. 6 MB keeps the slices' 4 MB for the tick-driven model and
      leaves 2 MB for a main-loop title against a measured 3 KB.
    - g_xbox_low_base. The fixed low block (primary TLS, kernel data exports,
      TLS/PRCB stand-ins) sat at 0x00700000 to clear any XBE. JSRF's image is
      11 sections ending at 0x00288620. The 4.5 MB between them was dead
      address space charged to the arena. It is now derived from the loaded
      section extents, rounded to 64 KB, with the old value as the pre-init
      default and a larger image free to push it up.
      XBOX_KERNEL_DATA_BASE, XBOX_STACK_BASE, XBOX_HEAP_BASE and the
      primary-TLS addresses are expressions over it. Its 58 call sites are all
      runtime expressions -- the case labels that look like a problem have the
      macro on the return side.

  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/heap_alloc_test.c
    Sixteen 16-byte pool blocks must fit in one page; a page-aligned request
    must be servable from a misaligned free block; the skipped lead must come
    back reusable. Its stub XBE has no sections, so it exercises the default
    low base.

Instrumentation (all opt-in, all read-only, none of it writes guest state)

  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/startup_probe.c + instrument_startup.py
    RECOMP_INTERP_TRACE=1 brackets sub_00024700 entry (0x24700) and exit
    (0x24962) and logs every call into the two setters 0x24480 and 0x24540.
    instrument_startup.py now installs eight sites, not four; --remove still
    takes them all out.

  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/main.c
    RECOMP_REPORT_MS=<ms>     periodic report interval, default 5000. This is
                              also the RECOMP_FB_DUMP sampling interval, and
                              5 s is coarser than the SEGA logo is on screen --
                              that is why it appeared in no dump of the first
                              two post-fix runs. Use 400-1500 to see the
                              startup sequence in order.
    RECOMP_HEAP_REPORT=1      xbox_HeapReport each period, for growth curves.
    RECOMP_STACK_REPORT=1     stack high-water, follows the layout macros.
    RECOMP_TOTAL_RAM_MB=<n>   diagnostic only, and it does NOT work for JSRF:
                              xbox_EnablePhysicalHeapAlias requires a <= 64 MB
                              layout and the renderer depends on that alias.
                              Left wired for titles where it does work; it
                              labels itself non-retail in its own log line.

  src/kernel/kernel_bridge.c
    Rate-limited reserve/commit log for NtAllocateVirtualMemory.

Also

  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/test_combiner_trace.py
    config 2 now expects two draws. Your vsh_render_test.c gained the
    alternate-winding strip after that expectation was written; the strip
    changes cull/front-face only, so sharing the combiner config is correct
    grouping. This was failing before I touched anything.


THE ARENA IS NOT THE PROBLEM
============================

This is the most useful thing in this handover. Four arenas, four failures:

  arena       live at failure   consumed   screens reached
  50,855,936      49,301,920      97.0%          3
  50,855,936      49,407,608      97.2%          3   (granularity + frontier)
  52,953,088      52,188,296      98.6%          4   (stack 6 MB)
  57,606,144      55,424,136      96.2%          4   (derived low block)

The title consumes 96-99% of whatever it is given and hits the same wall. The
largest arena reached no screen the previous one had not: the extra 4.5 MB
bought allocation, not progress. A bounded working set settles somewhere and
stops. This does not.

Do not spend more effort on arena size, stack sizing, reserve/commit
separation, or shaving slack. The remaining 1.9 MB of slack is faithful page
rounding by page-granular allocators and should stay.

What did change is the shape of the failure: the title stopped spinning on a
retry -- 207 failed requests instead of more than forty thousand -- and now
fails on 128 to 2,880 byte requests rather than megabytes. It gets much further
into its allocation sequence before dying.


THE ACTIVE LEAD FOR G9
======================

Per-export tallies (claude-heap-27):

  export  15  ExAllocatePoolWithTag        922 allocs /     430,384 bytes
  export  17  ExFreePool                     1 free   /         180 bytes
  export 166  MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx  673 allocs /  31,409,696 bytes
  export 171  MmFreeContiguousMemory        183 frees  /   1,765,376 bytes
  export 184  NtAllocateVirtualMemory       578 allocs / 146,271,184 bytes
  export 199  NtFreeVirtualMemory           258 frees  / 131,260,464 bytes

NtAllocateVirtualMemory is healthy: it churns 146 MB and returns 131 MB.
Contiguous memory is not: roughly 29.6 MB is taken and never given back.

The free path works and is not a missing bridge. With RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE=100000
every free carries its guest return address, and they aggregate to:

    257  ordinal 199 ra=0x00145A84      NtFreeVirtualMemory
    183  ordinal 171 ra=0x001928C1      MmFreeContiguousMemory
      2  ordinal 199 ra=0x0014A0F9
      1  ordinal  17 ra=0x001BCC48

So all contiguous frees come from ONE guest site, and it is reached.

Allocation side: 0x0018E6E9 and every other ordinal-166 return address in the
owner breakdown is a call site of an indirect call through MEM32(0x1C40F8),
the title's own D3D8 allocator vector. sub_0018E670 wraps one of them: it
builds an Xbox D3D resource header (MEM32(esi) = 0x1040001, size masked into
+4) and returns 0x8007000E, E_OUTOFMEMORY, when the allocation fails.
ra=0x0018E6E9 alone holds 20.3 MB across 231 live blocks.

Free side: sub_00192830 is the resource destructor. It frees through
MEM32(0x1C404C) from two sites -- 0x00192896 for the plain address and
0x001928C1 for the 0x80000000-mirrored one -- and picks between them, or skips
both, on:

    cmp esi, 0x20000 ; jne ...          esi is the resource type/flags
    cmp MEM32(edi), 0 ; js  -> skip     the Common field's sign bit
    cmp esi, 0x10000 ; je   -> skip
    cmp esi, 0x60000 ; je   -> skip

Only the 0x001928C1 path ever fires in our runs; 0x00192896 never does.

So the question is why sub_00192830 is reached about a quarter as often as the
allocator, or why it takes a skip branch when it does. Bracket it and the
refcount test in its caller exactly the way instrument_startup.py brackets
sub_00024700 -- that machinery is already there and takes about ten minutes to
extend. The FCMOVcc bug was precisely this shape: a comparison on a
resource-management path that silently went one way. Rule a second one out
before concluding the title is at fault.

Two smaller leads, both real, both minor against 29.6 MB: pool memory is never
freed either (922 allocations, one ExFreePool), and two pure 1 MB MEM_RESERVE
calls are charged real RAM, which bridge_NtAllocateVirtualMemory already
documents as a known gap. Everything else JSRF asks for is RESERVE|COMMIT.

A hypothesis I put in an earlier draft and then disproved, recorded so you do
not re-derive it: the harness's [D3D8-HLE] layer is NOT swallowing the
releases. main.c brings that layer up as a probe and says so in its own
comment -- nothing in JSRF routes through it, the title runs its own
statically-linked D3D8.


G10, NEW AND UNTOUCHED
======================

Upstream (sp00nznet/xboxrecomp, this tree's `upstream` remote) has a fix we do
not, in a file we have modified. Commit 0655e8e:
NV097_SET_SURFACE_COLOR_OFFSET is an offset inside the colour DMA object, not a
guest VA, and our nv2a_pb_exec.c treats it as one. On the Dashboard that
cleared 4.9 MB straight over the loaded XBE and the title spun in a pushbuffer
retry loop with no fault and no message.

JSRF is unaffected today -- its surface is a real heap allocation at
0x01160000 and the logos render correctly -- so this is latent, not urgent.
The same commit reports DMA_GET beside DMA_PUT; GET stuck behind PUT is the
shape of a pushbuffer-full hang and we log only PUT.

Also worth knowing: upstream's lifter still drops FCMOVcc
(git grep fcmov upstream/main -- tools/recomp/lifter.py is empty). The fix and
its test are ours alone and affect every title with an x87 fminf/fmaxf. It is
worth a PR, but I have not committed or pushed anything.

We are 41 commits ahead of upstream and 11 behind. Nothing upstream touches
contiguous-memory lifetime; kernel_memory.c has not changed there since the
initial import, so G9 gets no help from it.

DO NOT DO THESE
===============

  - Do not enlarge the arena, shrink the stack further, or shave allocator
    slack. Four data points say it does not help.
  - Do not reclaim the bump path's alignment padding. I tried; that padding is
    the tail of a page-granular allocation the title owns and writes into, and
    handing it out stopped the title dead at IoCreateDevice with no draws and
    no ADX tick. The comment in xbox_HeapAlloc says so.
  - Do not use RECOMP_TOTAL_RAM_MB for JSRF. It breaks the physical heap alias
    and the run dies before the HDD is created.
  - Do not treat a run without RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 as graphics evidence.
  - Do not count the cyan or blue full-screen frames as title screens.
  - Do not disable the untextured-draw rejection to make the Smilebit screen's
    background black. It is cyan because the fade overlay is an untextured
    draw the renderer rejects by design, and that rejection is reported:
    [TEXTURE] prepared=15705 rejected=126737.
  - Do not claim gameplay, menu reachability, input or sound.
  - Do not commit or push unless the user asks.
```

```txt
READ THIS FIRST

  /Users/andrewcollard/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Jet Set Radio Future/upstream_xboxrecomp_clean

EXECUTIVE STATUS
================

JSRF now boots to its animated "Now Loading" screen and streams stage assets.
The sequence that renders is:

  CRI ADX logo -> Presented by SEGA -> Created by Smilebit
    -> anti-graffiti notice -> "Now Loading" with a live progress bar

It then loads Stage 12 geometry, stage objects, a car object and the BGM
streams, finishes cleanly, and waits for a button press it can never receive.

That is the whole story: G13 ends at G5, host input. Not memory, not the
renderer, not the scheduler. Each of those was measured and excluded.


WHAT WAS WRONG, IN ORDER
========================

Five faults, each hiding the next. Every one was found by reading the
generated guest code against measured runtime state, not by reasoning from a
specification.

1. FCMOVcc was never emitted (7ed3441)

   The lifter had no case for it; it fell through to the generic x87 handler
   and became a bare comment. That is the whole of fminf (sub_0014C870) and
   fmaxf (sub_0014C850) -- with the move gone the trailing fxch/fstp discard
   the wrong operand and both return their SECOND argument. The colour packer
   sub_000A4CF0 clamps every channel with fminf(c, 1.0f) then fmaxf(c, 0.0f)
   and writes the result back, so it stored 0.0f into all four channels. The
   startup fade never moved.

   Your interpolator lead was close but inverted: sub_00024700 did step. The
   packer zeroed it on the way out.

2. Cross-block flag merge (yours, 7ed3441)

   Kept and covered. 110 branches in this tree still reach the `_flags`
   fallback where the condition is a constant zero; the lifter now marks them
   UNRESOLVED FLAGS and jsrf_unresolved_flags_ratchet pins the count.

3. Viewport scale/offset never reached the vertex constants (1a93eeb)

   NV2A keeps them at fixed slots in the constant file -- VPSCL = 58, VPOFF =
   59 -- written through SET_VIEWPORT_SCALE/_OFFSET, not SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT.
   The executor recorded both for the rasteriser and never mirrored them.
   JSRF's program ends with

       mul oPos.xyz, R12, c58
       mad oPos.xyz, R12, R1, c59

   so every vertex transformed to x=y=z=0 while w -- written one instruction
   earlier, outside the xyz write mask -- stayed correct. That asymmetry is
   what named it: the observed W of 31.3942 is exactly c[106].z * (z +
   c[109].w). 714,240 draws a run collapsed to a point; now zero do.

4. The untextured combiner was rejected (1a93eeb)

   93% of draws. The combiner input word packs each of A..D as [7:5] mapping,
   [4] alpha, [3:0] register. Textured stage 0 is 0x08040000, register 8
   (texture 0) times register 4 (diffuse). With no texture bound the title
   issues 0x04200000: diffuse times register 0 under mapping 1 (unsigned
   invert) = 1. Same four-stage program, texture-less stage 0. Sampling is
   skipped, the stage reads as opaque white, and the existing modulate path
   multiplies the diffuse in.

   Rejections 432,960 -> 0, triangles 40,950 -> 1,557,266.

5. Thread stacks were eight times too big (3e84ce7)

   PsCreateSystemThreadEx takes KernelStackSize as argument 2 and the bridge
   ignored it, handing every thread 512 KB. JSRF asks for 65,536. Four
   workers, 458,752 wasted each. Thread stacks 2,097,600 -> 262,592 bytes and
   out-of-memory failures 205 a run -> ZERO.

   The same commit carries four smaller allocator corrections: split
   granularity at the caller's alignment rather than a page, frontier
   coalescing, a low block derived from the loaded image instead of a fixed
   0x00700000, and stack-region sizing measured rather than guessed.


G5 -- ACTIVE, AND THE ONLY BLOCKER
==================================

The title loads Z:\Media\Mark\PRESS\JSRF_TEXS_0.JTX -- the PRESS START
textures -- stops all file I/O with a clean 51,200-byte read, and animates
while four healthy threads wait for a button.

There is already a host-side backend, src/input/xinput_device.c: SDL game
controllers plus RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1, which pulses A and START. It is
byte-identical to upstream apart from that addition, and NOTHING CALLS IT.
xbox_InputGetState has no caller. JSRF does not go through XAPI on the host;
it drives OHCI itself.

Upstream has no USB device model at all (`git grep -i "ohci\|HCCA"
upstream/main -- src` is empty), so this tree is the furthest along.

What now works (b5cacea, c5fc586):

  - HcInterruptEnable (0xFED00010) and HcInterruptDisable (0xFED00014) are a
    set/clear pair, handled by the MCPX write trap. As plain memory the
    controller-start write of MasterInterruptEnable was replaced microseconds
    later by sub_001BD295's write of RootHubStatusChange, and the ISR at
    0x001C288F tests bit 31 separately and declined every interrupt.
    Now: HcInterruptEnable reads 0x80000073, "device ISR vector 1 -> TRUE",
    and ord 119 gains call site 0x001C290F -- the ISR queuing its own DPC,
    which bridge_run_isr already runs after the handler returns.

  - HcRhPortStatus is not a value register either. Low half is commands (1 to
    bit 1 enables, bit 4 resets, bit 8 powers), high half is five
    write-1-to-clear change bits. As plain memory the driver's acknowledge of
    0x00010000 wiped CurrentConnectStatus with it, so the device vanished the
    moment it was noticed. ohci_port_write models both halves; a reset
    completes in place. HcRhPortStatus[0] now reads 0x00000001 and stays.

  - mcpx_hw_store is the other half of that. The runtime asserting a condition
    means "this is now the value", the opposite of a guest write, so the
    attach probe drops the guard rather than acknowledging the change it is
    announcing.

WHERE IT STOPS, AND THE NEXT QUESTION

Across a whole run the driver writes HcRhPortStatus 72 times,
HcInterruptEnable 63 and HcInterruptStatus 61 -- acking and re-masking every
pass -- and writes a non-zero endpoint-list head EXACTLY NEVER.
ControlListFilled is never set. It loops in the root hub and never issues the
port reset, so there is nothing for a transfer service to service yet. Do not
start writing one.

The path is read and recorded:

  sub_001BD295  root-hub poll. Walks four ports from ebx+0x54, tests
                CurrentConnectStatus, builds a change bitmap, acks each port,
                writes HcInterruptEnable = 0x40, calls sub_001C2220.
  sub_001C2220  walks the bitmap against a per-port "already seen" mask at
                this+0x461. An unseen connect sets the bit and calls
                sub_001BF8F6.
  sub_001BF8F6  tail-calls sub_001BF72C.
  sub_001BF72C  allocates a device object from the pool at 0x264858, stamps it
                (MEM8(esi)=0xFE, port at +4), links it, calls sub_001C06B3.
                *** If the allocation returns zero it branches straight to its
                exit at loc_001BF7ED. ***

So the next question is narrow, not open-ended: DOES sub_001BF72C RUN, AND
DOES ITS ALLOCATION SUCCEED? An empty device pool looks exactly like what is
observed. Probe it the way sub_00024700 and sub_00192830 were probed --
instrument_startup.py plus a read-only probe in startup_probe.c.

Only after that is answered is the HCCA transfer service worth starting. Then:
answer the port reset and the control transfers on the default endpoint
through the HCCA at 0x009E2000, and answer interrupt-IN with pad reports fed
from xbox_InputGetState, which already exists.


HYPOTHESES TESTED AND DISPROVED
===============================

Recorded so they are not re-derived. Each cost time; each was settled by
measurement rather than argument.

  - "The heap is leaking." It is not. Codex's resource probes show all 235
    resource allocations succeeding, Release working (126,000 calls, all
    decrements), and the texture cache holding 235 DISTINCT resources in 233
    DISTINCT slots with zero replacements. It is the real startup working set.

  - "Give the arena more memory." Actively counterproductive. ordinal 184
    ra=0x0014903F is a doubling allocator that retains every previous segment:
    1+2+4 MB at a 52.9 MB arena, 1+2+4+8 MB at 61.8 MB. Four MB more makes it
    take eight MB more.

  - "Separate MEM_RESERVE from MEM_COMMIT." Measured first, and the answer was
    no: the title commits 8,331,376 of its first 8,388,608 reserved bytes --
    99%. The pages are owed either way.

  - "The D3D8-HLE layer is swallowing resource releases." It is not. main.c
    brings that layer up as a probe and says so in its own comment; nothing in
    JSRF routes through it.

  - "The cooperative scheduler is deadlocked." It is not. Suspend counts stay
    at 0 and 1, and the object the loader waits on is woken 8,006 times against
    8,000 entries with zero timeouts.

  - "The USB driver is sub_001A1E74 / sub_001A52F7." Wrong -- those are APU
    code on the 0xFE801xxx aperture. The USB stack is the XBE's XPP section,
    0x001BC7C0, 30,616 bytes.

  - "MIE is lost, so shadow the enable register in xbox_McpxHoldRegisters."
    Right diagnosis, wrong placement: a poll cannot see a write that is
    replaced between polls. It needed the write trap. The polled version was
    removed.

xemu (github.com/xemu-project/xemu) was worth consulting twice, and both times
it KILLED a hypothesis rather than supplying an answer:

  - Constant delivery matches pgraph.c exactly -- slot = (method -
    NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT)/4, write [const_load][slot % 4], increment
    CONST_LD_PTR when slot % 4 == 3.
  - The +-96 D3DSCM correction is a red herring. convert_c_register is
    (((c>>5)&7)-3)*32 + (c&31) + 96, which is the identity for every 8-bit
    input; xemu's own source says so with a FIXME.

Use it that way: to rule things out fast, not to look up answers.


INSTRUMENTS ADDED THIS SESSION
==============================

All opt-in, all read-only, all off by default.

  RECOMP_REPORT_MS=<ms>     periodic report interval, default 5000. This is
                            also the RECOMP_FB_DUMP sampling interval, and
                            5 s is coarser than the SEGA logo is on screen.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-04_USB_GFX.txt`:

```txt
CLAUDE -> CODEX HANDOVER
Jet Set Radio Future / upstream_xboxrecomp_clean
4 September 2026

Continues CODEX_TO_CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-04.txt (the USB transfer-service
brief). Supersedes the input conclusion in CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-04.txt.


READ THIS FIRST
===============

Repository:
  /Users/andrewcollard/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Jet Set Radio Future/upstream_xboxrecomp_clean

State: main at 770cf92, pushed to origin/main, working tree clean.
Six commits on top of f37268a.

Tests: ctest 14/14. Build clean apart from the seven pre-existing DWORD/%lu
format warnings in xbox_memory_layout.c and the linker alignment warnings.

Two prior conclusions are WRONG and are corrected below. If you read only two
things, read CORRECTION 1 and CORRECTION 2.


EXECUTIVE STATUS
================

You can now watch JSRF boot, in a window, on this machine:

  env RECOMP_HDD_ROOT=/tmp/jsrf-hdd RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 \
      python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_bounded.py mytest --seconds 120

CRI/ADX logo, then the animated "Now Loading" screen, stable and flicker-free.
Behind it the CPU rasteriser reports, over 150 s, 267,400 draws and 3,052,519
triangles with ZERO batches rejected, ZERO skipped as not screen-space and
ZERO triangles off-surface, running the title's own vertex programs.

It does not get past the loading screen. That is the whole of what is left in
this line of work, and it is NOT input and NOT the renderer.


CORRECTION 1: THE RENDERER WAS NEVER THE BLOCKER
================================================

draws=0 in the [PUSHER] line is the D3D11 sink's counter. The CPU executor in
src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c is counted separately and draws. It is gated behind
RECOMP_PB_EXEC, and no run in the previous sessions' logs set it -- so every
run drew nothing, and "the renderer is missing geometry" followed from that
rather than from the renderer.

It is not missing geometry. ARRAY_ELEMENT16, SET_TRANSFORM_PROGRAM,
SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT_LOAD, the vertex-shader interpreter and texturing all
work on the paths this title uses. Do not start building a geometry path in
the pushbuffer sink; nothing in its unhandled list is on the critical path.


CORRECTION 2: THE TITLE IS NOT WAITING FOR A BUTTON
===================================================

CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-04.txt says the title "finishes cleanly, and
waits for a button press it can never receive", and that "G13 ends at G5, host
input. Not memory, not the renderer, not the scheduler."

That is the premise the whole USB stack was built on, and it does not survive
being tested. The button now arrives and nothing changes.

The test, and you can re-run it: RECOMP_PAD_SENTINEL=1 stamps a value nothing
else would produce into the pad's left stick, and the periodic report scans
guest RAM for it (pad_sentinel_scan in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/main.c).
That the report reaches guest memory was never in question -- the runtime
writes it there. Whether the title's input layer copies it out was.

  RECOMP_HDD_ROOT=... RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 \
  RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1 RECOMP_PAD_SENTINEL=1 run_bounded.py <name> --seconds 75

Result, every report, run claude-pad-sentinel-3:

  [PAD-SENTINEL] copy at guest 0x009E10B6
  [PAD-SENTINEL] copy at guest 0x009E10D6
  [PAD-SENTINEL] 2 copies of the pad report in guest RAM

Two copies in sixty megabytes, thirty-two bytes apart, both inside the USB
stack's own allocation region -- the HCCA is at 0x009E2000 and the device pool
at 0x009E4000 -- and shaped like XPP double-buffering the XID input report at
its 32-byte endpoint size. Nowhere else in RAM.

XPP takes delivery and stores it. The game never copies it out. The title is
not blocked on input it cannot get; it is not asking for input.

That agrees with the screen, which shows "Now Loading" and not a title screen,
and with the state machine (see THE ACTUAL BLOCKER).

The USB work was sound engineering against a wrong premise. It is real
infrastructure and the title will need it -- it enumerates and polls -- but it
did not unblock anything, and the premise should have been tested first.


WHAT WAS BUILT
==============

  src/kernel/xbox_usb_ohci.{c,h}          new
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/ohci_transfer_test.c   new

An OHCI transfer service and one Xbox gamepad. Pure functions over a
caller-supplied RAM window and register values, because the live caller is the
MCPX SIGSEGV handler -- it must not allocate or lock -- and the tests then
drive the identical code over a plain buffer with no guest at all.

The title now completes the whole USB conversation, reproducibly, in this
order, each request issued once the previous completed:

  80 06 00 01 00 00 08 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(DEVICE), 8 -- address-0 probe
  00 05 01 00 00 00 00 00   SET_ADDRESS(1)
  80 06 00 02 00 00 50 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(CONFIGURATION), 80
  00 09 01 00 00 00 00 00   SET_CONFIGURATION(1)
  C1 06 00 42 00 00 10 00   GET_DESCRIPTOR(XID), 16 -- VENDOR, not class
  C1 01 00 02/01 ...        GET_CAPABILITIES
  A1 01 00 01 00 00 14 00   GET_REPORT(input), 20 -- CLASS, and repeating

Two of those are worth knowing. The XID descriptor is a VENDOR request
(bmRequestType 0xC1, type bits = 2), not a class one; routing it as class
stalls it. And GET_REPORT on the control pipe, not the interrupt endpoint, is
where the pad actually goes -- the interrupt endpoint runs too, but XID polls.

Verified with a real DualShock 4 on USB (claude-usb-realpad-01): SDL2 opens it
and presses decode correctly -- Options as START, the D-pad as its four bits,
Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle as the analog bytes.

Window presentation:

  nv2a_pb_exec_surface() hands out the rasterised surface; dev_Present in
  src/d3d/d3d8_gl.c uploads it and draws it over the window with the existing
  fixed program. A hook, because the executor is xbox_kernel and that is
  xbox_d3d -- the arrangement the APU MMIO and USB pad hooks already use.
  Installed in main.c. Whole frames are snapshotted at NV097_FLIP_STALL.


FIVE OHCI BUGS, EACH FOUND BY A RUN
===================================

Logs are under build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/.

1. HcInterruptStatus was not write-1-to-clear, so the driver's acknowledge
   STORED the bit it meant to retire. An ISR storm, and fatal to everything
   after it: a WritebackDoneHead that can never be acknowledged is one
   transfer, then silence. (claude-usb-transfer-service-01)

2. Nothing advanced a frame, so the StartOfFrame count XPP uses to time the
   2 ms after SET_ADDRESS never finished. (claude-usb-transfer-service-02/03)

3. An unacknowledged done queue was being overwritten. XPP submits the next
   transfer from its completion DPC, BEFORE acknowledging the previous one.
   (claude-usb-transfer-service-04)

4. HeadP was left pointing at a failed TD. A retired TD is retired whether or
   not it succeeded; HeadP advances past it and only gains Halted.
   (claude-usb-transfer-service-08)

5. One mprotect guard window per register instead of one per event. A guest
   write landing in a window is stored as plain memory with none of the
   register semantics the trap exists to supply: XPP acknowledged
   ConnectStatusChange between the attach probe's two stores and wiped
   CurrentConnectStatus. mcpx_hw_store_n batches.
   (claude-usb-transfer-service-05)

   Remember this one beyond USB. Windows cannot be eliminated while the
   mechanism is mprotect; the rule is to open as few as possible. Any future
   runtime-side write to a guarded page should batch.


ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM OHCI
==================================

A short read does not raise DataUnderrun and does not halt the endpoint.

XPP asks for 0x50 bytes of configuration set and builds exactly ten eight-byte
IN TDs for it, bufferRounding on the last only. The modelled device has 32
bytes, so it underruns mid-chain; per OHCI that halts the endpoint, and XPP
reads that as a failed enumeration and resets the port, for ever
(claude-usb-transfer-service-10/-11). Completing the short read cleanly
carries it to SET_CONFIGURATION (claude-usb-exp-a2/-a3).

Read it as a symptom. That XPP asks for exactly 80 bytes and sizes its TD
chain to match is evidence the REAL controller's configuration set is 80 bytes
and the 32-byte one in xbox_usb_ohci.c is incomplete -- plausibly the
expansion-slot interfaces for memory units. Nothing was invented to fill it.
If you find a real descriptor dump, replace USB_CONFIG_DESC and the deviation
should go with it. Both sites carry the note.


THE ACTUAL BLOCKER
==================

The title reaches "Now Loading" and stays. Not slowly -- it stops.

  45 s run:  242 distinct files, 284 reads
  150 s run: 242 distinct files, 284 reads

Identical. File I/O finishes and never resumes, while the game loop runs hard
and the loading animation keeps ticking.

Ruled out by measurement, not argument:

  - No fatal error. No JSRF_FATAL.ERR on the emulated HDD.
  - No missing asset. All 253 failures are STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND on Z:\
    paths, the HDD-cache-miss-then-read-from-D:\ pattern; the D:\ read
    succeeds immediately after each.
  - No blocked thread. Two NtWaitForSingleObjectEx INFINITE calls in a whole
    run, both early, neither at the stall.
  - No heap exhaustion. Zero "out of memory", unlike the 2026-09-03 handover's
    Stg10_01.dat failure, which is fixed.
  - Audio healthy. ADX manager/server tick advancing, flag clear.
  - Not input. See CORRECTION 2.
  - Not rendering. Same 242/284 with and without RECOMP_PB_EXEC.

The guest is busy, not idle: 5.9M kernel calls, ~2.4M each of
RtlEnterCriticalSection and Leave. It is re-testing a predicate that never
becomes true.

Loading gets further than the previous session recorded. It loads the PRESS
START textures (Z:\Media\Mark\PRESS\JSRF_TEXS_1.JTX, JSRF_TEXSx1.JTX) and then
continues through player assets, sound effects, display sprites
(Z:\Media\Disp\SprNorm1.dat) and finally the BGM streams.


THE STATE MACHINE, AND THE EXACT NEXT STEP
==========================================

sub_00013A80 is the root object's per-tick update, reached by
sub_00025310 -> sub_00011070 -> sub_000123E0 -> sub_00013A80. Root object is
0x005E3A70 and stays there.

Its opening block tests a run of trigger fields and derives flags from them:

  if (MEM32(root+0x50) != 0) { call sub_00065C80; MEM32(root+0x40) = 1; }
  ... the same shape for +0x54, +0x58, +0x5C, +0x60 ...

RECOMP_STARTUP_TRACE=1 now logs all of them, widened this session for exactly
this question. Measured over 32,000 ticks with a pad held down throughout:

  +0x50, +0x54, +0x58, +0x5C, +0x60 -- all zero, always
  +0x40, +0x44 (derived from them)  -- all zero, always
  +0x94                             -- alternates 0 and 2 every tick

+0x94 is a per-frame phase flag, not a stall. It selects between two paths at
loc_00013B24 and is a red herring; earlier notes treating it as the state
machine's state are wrong.

So: NOTHING ever sets any of the five triggers. The next question is narrow.
Which of +0x50..+0x60 is supposed to be set, by what, and what is stopping it?
Work outwards from sub_000123E0 (the caller) and sub_00065C80 (what a set
trigger invokes), the way the FCMOV and shared-epilogue faults were found --
reading the generated guest code against measured runtime state.

Do NOT force a transition, fake a button or synthesise a trigger to get past
this. That rule has held for the whole project and it is why the measurements
above can be trusted.


TOOLING YOU HAVE
================

Probes: diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_startup.py adds read-only
observation sites at guest PCs; startup_probe.c implements them. This is how
the USB device path, the interpolator and the resource path were pinned down,
and it is the right tool for the state machine.

Useful environment variables (full list: grep -rhoE 'getenv\("RECOMP_[A-Z_0-9]+"\)'
over src/ and diagnostics/):

  RECOMP_PB_EXEC          run the CPU rasteriser; REQUIRED to see anything
  RECOMP_FB_DUMP=<prefix> write the surface to <prefix>NNN.bmp per report
  RECOMP_STARTUP_TRACE    root object trigger/flag fields per tick
  RECOMP_PAD_SENTINEL     stamp and hunt the pad report through guest RAM
  RECOMP_FAKE_PAD         pulse A and START once a second, no hardware needed
  RECOMP_OHCI_TRANSFER_TRACE  ED/TD dumps, [OHCI-SVC] and [USB-PAD]
  RECOMP_PEEK / _CHAIN    print named guest dwords as hex and float

Host notes, both macOS rather than code. open_controllers() runs once in
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-09_AUDIO_VOICE_ON.txt`:

```txt
JSRF AUDIO HANDOVER FOR CODEX
Date: 2026-09-09 (Europe/London)
From: Claude

PURPOSE
=======
The VOICE_ON question from CODEX_TO_CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-09_AUDIO.txt is
answered and fixed. JSRF now starts voices, retires them, raises the FECTL
idle trap and queues non-silent PCM. Sound quality has NOT been assessed and
the mixer is not paced.

Everything below was measured in this session. Nothing is inferred from a
counter whose trigger was not read first.


WHAT THE PROBE FOUND
====================
The handover's proposed experiment was run: a bounded, read-only probe on the
one path that reaches the VOICE_ON store, installed in a copy of the verified
archive rather than a regeneration.

  runtime  this worktree (identical to xboxrecomp_upstream_integration @ 30ff915)
  gen      copy of the verified archive, probe-instrumented
  script   diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_voice_submit.py
  probe    jsrf_voice_submit_probe in main.c, RECOMP_VOICE_TRACE=1

Result, at the title screen with no controller attached:

  [VOICE] entry        obj=80954344 flags=0301 count=1 ret=001A4202
  [VOICE] pre-voice-on voice_on=00000040 antecedent=0001FFFF i=0 model_on=0
  [VOICE] loop-done    model_on=0 fe=12 scv=0 shadow_av=0001FFFF shadow_on=00000040

None of the four candidate stopping points was the blocker:

  - the entry gate is open: flags=0301, bit 1 clear on every call;
  - the voice count is 1, never 0;
  - both NV1BA0_PIO_FREE spins exit on their first read.

The guest reaches 0x001A3F8D and writes the voice handle every time. It was
never a control-flow problem. That closes the first two branches of the
handover's decision list.


THE ACTUAL CAUSE: THE MMIO BOUNDARY LOST THE WRITES
===================================================
shadow_on=00000040 is the plain-memory contents of 0xFE820124 after the store.
The write completed as ordinary memory; the APU model never saw it.

Trap accounting (new, [MCPX-TRAP], printed with [APU-VOICE]) measured the
mechanism over 45 s:

  faults=41526 apu=230 vp=215 ack_windows=13553193 reprotect_failures=0

The APU aperture is guarded read-only so guest stores fault into
mcpx_trap_handler. The NV2A ack thread was advancing a free-running counter at
0xFE820010, which lives on the SAME 16 KB page as the voice-submission
registers at 0x020120-0x020304, by unprotecting the page, storing, and
reprotecting -- 13.5 million times in 45 s, roughly 300,000 windows a second.
Every guest store landing in one of those windows completed silently against
RAM.

215 VP writes reached the model in that run. Not one was VOICE_ON. That is not
a coin flip: 0x0202F8 is the FIRST store of the submission burst and so tends
to arrive with the page still guarded, while 0x020120 and 0x020124 follow the
handler's own reprotect and were reliably swallowed by the next ack window.


THE FIX
=======
src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c
  - MCPX_APU_MODEL_SIZE (0x30000) names the span the model answers reads for:
    the main registers plus the VP PIO window.
  - mcpx_trap_handler's model-backed branch now covers that whole span. It
    EMULATES the access -- it never unprotects the page -- so there is no
    window to lose a write in.
  - the ack thread's free-space counter is skipped when the model answers
    those reads (g_mcpx_apu_read_trapped). ack_windows drops to 0.
  - both discarded VirtualProtect results are now checked and counted.

src/apu/apu_vp.c
  - NV1BA0_PIO_FREE returns 0xFFFC instead of 0x80. There is no FIFO in this
    model, so it is always empty. The size matters: JSRF waits for
    (FREE >> 2) >= voices * 7 and the voice count is a byte, so 0x80 would
    have spun for ever at five voices or more. This replaces a monotonic ramp,
    which satisfied any comparison by accident; a constant must satisfy them
    on purpose.
  - g_apu_fe_method_count / g_apu_set_current_voice_count, reported in
    [APU-VOICE]. These are the positive control: they separate "the guest did
    not write" from "the write did not arrive".

The guest binary reads exactly ONE address in the whole VP window -- offset
0x10, PIO_FREE, at 33 sites -- and writes 45 other offsets. Routing VP reads
through the model therefore costs nothing: no JSRF code reads back a VP
shadow. That was checked across the whole generated tree, not assumed.


VERIFIED RESULT
===============
Built against the PRISTINE archive gen (no probe), 45 s, title screen:

  [APU-VOICE] on=8 off=3 idle_trap=3 processed=259789 fe_methods=1703
  [MCPX-TRAP] faults=43707 apu=1820 vp=1700 ack_windows=0 reprotect_failures=0
  [APU-SDL] queued audible batch: 256 frames, peak 5406

Before the fix the same three lines read on=0 off=0 idle_trap=0 processed=0,
and no audible batch was ever queued.

idle_trap=3 is the transition the previous handover identified as missing:
voice retirement raises SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE, which sets FETRAPREASON_REQUESTED,
which is what the guest's service routine at 0x001A25CA waits for. The whole
chain is now live.

No regression: no guest fault, frames still present, 27/27 ctest pass.


WHAT IS STILL OPEN
==================
1. PACING. "[APU-SDL] cleared overfull output queue" appears -- the mixer
   produces faster than 48 kHz playback and the queue is dropped when it
   overfills. This is the likely source of the glitchy audio reported before
   the New Game investigation. Nothing clocks the APU frame rate.
2. off=3 against on=8: most voices never retire. Watch for voice exhaustion
   over a long session.
3. apu_core.c:64 and :437 still test a multi-bit FEMETHMODE field with a mask
   (HALTED, 0x80, also matches 0xE0). Real, independent, untouched.
4. The two remaining windowed writes in mcpx_trap_handler -- PCRTC_INTR_0 and
   PGRAPH_INTR -- have the same shape as the bug fixed here. They have not
   been shown to lose anything; [MCPX-TRAP] is the instrument if they do.
5. Everything in the previous gameplay handover that is not audio: Gum and the
   player not rendering, the mission-resource backport's fate, 112 vs 76 dead
   _flags.


REPRODUCING
===========
  cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build> \
        -DRECOMP_GEN_DIR=<extracted archive gen>
  RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_METAL=1 RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 \
  RECOMP_REPORT_MS=10000 RECOMP_HDD_ROOT=<disposable emulated-hdd copy> \
    <build>/jsrf_first_fault

CMakeLists resolves JSRF_STOCK_DIR as a sibling of the repo root; a worktree
needs a jsrf_stock_test symlink beside it.

To re-run the probe, instrument a COPY of the gen:
  python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_voice_submit.py --gen <copy>
  ... --check   report what is installed
  ... --remove  take it back out
and add RECOMP_VOICE_TRACE=1 to the launch. The probe is opt-in and read-only;
it is not needed for the fix.

The preserved baseline and its archive were not modified.
```

```txt
THE BUILD MATRIX THAT WORKS
===========================
Not obvious, and three sessions were wasted on getting it wrong:

  runtime   xboxrecomp_upstream_integration/diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault
  gen       the DIRTY TREE's preserved gen (76 dead _flags), NOT a fresh
            integration regeneration

The integration tree's OWN freshly regenerated gen reaches the game loop but

  RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_METAL=1 RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1 \
```
