```txt
Without RECOMP_PB_EXEC the pushbuffer executor never runs and nothing draws.


INSTRUMENTS THAT LIE -- READ THIS FIRST
=======================================
Seven counters were misread this session, producing three retractions and one
retraction that was itself wrong. Verify a counter's trigger before reasoning
from it.

1. `draws=` in the [PUSHER] line is ALWAYS 0. The harness calls
   nv2a_pb_scan_set_external_executor(1). Read "[GPU] N triangles rasterised".

2. "[PUSHER] D3D11 sink unhandled methods" describes a sink that DOES NOT
   RENDER ON MACOS. Its list (0x1800 ARRAY_ELEMENT16, vertex shader uploads)
   is irrelevant here. The CPU executor prints its own list as
   "  [GPU]   0xNNNN xCOUNT"; raise the cut with RECOMP_PB_EXEC_TOP=<n>.

3. A high unhandled-method count is NOT evidence of a defect. JSRF drives this
   scene with programmable vertex shaders (mode=2), so the fixed-function
   matrices it "ignores" are genuinely not needed. [VSH] reports
   executed batches=98992 rejected=3 -- nothing is being dropped.

4. "[USB-PAD]" only prints on pad STATE CHANGE (memcmp over digital controls,
   4096 stick-jitter filter, 400 cap). Zero lines in an unattended run means
   nothing. It also logged zero while input demonstrably worked, because JSRF
   is served by the XInput/XPP bridge, not the emulated USB path.

5. "[PAD] port 0: PS4 Controller (opened)" appears even with the pad
   PHYSICALLY DISCONNECTED. It is not evidence of a live controller.

6. grep for "descriptor|SET_ADDRESS|endpoint" returns zero in a KNOWN-WORKING
   build. There is no enumeration logging; absence proves nothing.

7. Log-size comparisons across different scenes are meaningless. Gameplay
   submits orders of magnitude more pushbuffer traffic than the title screen.

Method that worked: get a POSITIVE CONTROL before trusting a negative. The
mode check below is the model -- Default-mode functions appeared, so the
absence of the other four modes was real.


WHAT WAS FIXED (verified)
=========================
1. tools/disasm/functions.py -- the startup fault (commit 95c1d82)
   Upstream 051a128's _pass_gap_prologues split table-reached switch
   dispatchers. Its gap test read only self.functions, while tail-jump and
   data-table bodies live in _alias_entries until _build_alias_entries runs
   last -- and it ran BEFORE _pass_data_ptr_targets, which claims ~3,100 JSRF
   bodies against the tail-jump pass's ~205.
   sub_00154D70 and sub_0015A020 are switch dispatchers whose cases end in
   "ret 12" with the next case following unpadded. Split at a case boundary,
   cases 0x00154DAA / 0x0015A0F9 were covered by nothing; their stubs popped 4
   and 12 bytes where the real blocks return 12, and the guest faulted far
   away in sub_00177FE0.
   Fix: gap test honours pending alias ranges (prefix-max), and the pass runs
   last among gap-testing passes. gap_prologue 363 finds -> 87; the 259 given
   up reappear under tail_jump_alias/seed_vtable_thunk. 18/18 disasm tests.
   THIS IS UPSTREAMABLE -- platform-neutral, fixes a real defect in their
   code, has tests. Best contribution candidate.

2. sub_001A308E override -- the New Game deadlock
   Clears object+0x12 bit 15 when bit 0 is set. Verified: the game passes New
   Game into gameplay and sub_001A308E appears nowhere in a live sample.
   THIS IS NOT AN AUDIO FIX. It clears one control-flow deadlock. Do not
   describe it as fixing DirectSound.

3. xbox_memory_layout.c -- logging on the hot path (commit 84ac2c8)
   RECOMP_PB_EXEC is required to render and armed the same flag guarding a
   per-DMA_PUT fprintf + fflush. 25,768 of 33,508 log lines in a 90 s run; a
   gameplay session wrote 24 GB. Printing now needs RECOMP_NV2A_TRACE.
   Measured A/B, same scene: log 1.2 MB -> 449 KB, frames 3000 -> 3300.
   (An earlier "5000x" claim compared different scenes and was wrong.)


THE AUDIO BLOCKER (root cause established, not fixed)
=====================================================
Chain, traced end to end:

  guest sub_001A25AA reads NV_PAPU_FECTL (0xFE801100), masks 0xF00
  (FETRAPREASON), and only reaches its sound path at 0x001A25CA when it
  equals 0xF00 (FETRAPREASON_REQUESTED).

  Live: FECTL = 0x100F -> trap-reason field is ZERO -> branch always taken ->
  sound path never runs. In a run where the intro tune DID play, FECTL was
  0x1FEF (FEMETHMODE=TRAPPED, FETRAPREASON=REQUESTED) and FEDECMETH was
  0x8000 = SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE with the voice handle in FEDECPARAM.

  FETRAPREASON_REQUESTED is set in ONE place: apu_vp.c:489, case
  SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE, gated on FETFORCE1 bit 15 -- and that gate is ALREADY
  OPEN (+1504 reads 0x00008000). The missing step is the call that raises it,
  fe_method(d, SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE, v) at apu_vp.c:1197, which fires only when a
  voice's ACTIVE_VOICE bit is found clear.

  Voice counters were added (apu_vp.c, reported periodically as [APU-VOICE]).
  AT THE TUTORIAL, WITH INPUT CONFIRMED WORKING:
      on=0 off=0 idle_trap=0 processed=0

  NV1BA0_PIO_VOICE_ON NEVER FIRES. The APU is never given a voice. The FECTL
  gating is a SYMPTOM. The fault is upstream, in the guest's DirectSound path.

Next step: determine why the guest never issues VOICE_ON. Note that
sub_001A1769 is a manual override whose own comment says "THIS MAKES AUDIO
SILENT AND IS NOT A FIX FOR AUDIO" -- a candidate, but not a complete
explanation, since the audible run showed real voice traps (handle 0x44) with
the same overrides compiled in.

A NOTE ON A PRIOR CLAIM: "APU voice retirement needs FE trap method 0x8000"
is CORRECT. I retracted it mid-session after searching NV1BA0_PIO_* names and
the word "retire" and finding neither. The method is named SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE
and apu_regs.h:216 defines it as 0x00008000. The retraction was wrong.

Also real but NOT the cause: apu_core.c:64 tests
`fectl & NV_PAPU_FECTL_FEMETHMODE_TRAPPED` -- a mask test against a multi-bit
FIELD VALUE. HALTED (0x80) also matches 0xE0, so a halted front end raises
FETINTSTS as if trapped. Should be
`(fectl & FEMETHMODE) == FEMETHMODE_TRAPPED`. Same pattern at :437.


THE GAMEPLAY BLOCKER (partially diagnosed)
==========================================
Symptoms: tutorial stops at the same place every time; SOME characters are
missing -- Corn and the dog render, GUM AND THE PLAYER DO NOT. That
selectivity is the sharpest clue available and is unexplained. Corn/Potts are
static NPCs; Gum and the player are rider characters with skeletal animation
and skinning. Whatever fails distinguishes those two classes.

RULED OUT, with evidence:
  - Rendering is not dropping anything. [GPU] draws 1211184 (1211184 with
    coordinates), 0 batches skipped as not screen-space, 0 triangles fully
    off-surface, [VSH] rejected=3 of 98992.
  - Wrong game mode. The decomp gives five modes (Default, Event,
    CoveredPause, FreezeCam, UncoveredPause) x three phases = 15 virtuals,
    each with its own CActBase::recursiveExecN<Mode> function. At the stall
    ONLY recursiveExec0Default (12 samples) and recursiveExec1Default (10)
    appear; the other four modes are absent. Positive control present.
  - The game is not hung. Main thread runs the normal loop, frames advance,
    triangles climb.
  - A sleeping controller. Confirmed the pad was disconnected during several
    "input doesn't work" reports -- but the stall reproduces with the pad
    live, so the stall itself is real.

DEAD BRANCHES EXECUTING DURING THE TUTORIAL (RECOMP_UNRESOLVED_FLAGS=1):
  site 39  0x000B4490  BENIGN -- verified. A redundant loop pre-check; the
           bottom `jl` back-edge bounds the loop correctly and the pre-check's
           correct value is always not-taken. Do not "fix" it.
  site 34  0x00056990  CMission::runListenerCmds. REAL. `test eax,eax` then a
           `je` that reads _flags. A predicate on a listener command is
           replaced by a constant, so the command body ALWAYS executes. Note
           the direction: commands fire unconditionally, they do not fail to
           fire. UNFIXED.
  site 32  0x00052402  inside CMission::InitResources. REAL, addressed below.


THE MID-FUNCTION SPLIT DEFECT (the systemic finding)
====================================================
This is the most reusable result of the session.

Promoting a mid-function entry to its own C function SEVERS FLAG DATAFLOW.
The generated flag temporaries _fa/_fb are function-local. If a split lands
between a flag producer and its consumer, the `cmp` is in one function and the
`jcc` in another, and the translator emits the constant-zero _flags fallback.

Concrete instance: CMission::InitResources matches a two-word key against a
table entry. Discovery promoted 0x00052402 -- FIVE BYTES, TWO INSTRUCTIONS --
to a function, landing exactly between the second `cmp` and its `je`. That
`je` is the ONLY edge to 0x0005240D, so the "found" path was unreachable and
the lookup could never succeed.

backport_mission_resource_match.py repairs it in the caller, where the flags
exist. IMPORTANT: the loop exists in THREE copies, because
recover_midfunction_entries.py replicates an owner's body at each recovered
entry. An earlier version patched only one -- the lookup then succeeded down
one path and failed down two, and the game stopped EARLIER than before. The
script now patches every copy; --check verifies all of them.

STATUS: UNVERIFIED. Applying it drops executed dead branches from three to
one, so it changes behaviour, but no run has shown a user-visible improvement.
The gen is gitignored, so the commit alone changes no build; revert by not
running the script.

GENERAL LESSON FOR THE RECOMPILER: mid-function entry promotion should either
avoid splitting between a flag producer and consumer, or the translator should
carry flag state across such a boundary. Other sites of this shape exist.


OPEN / UNEXPLAINED
==================
  - Why VOICE_ON is never issued.
  - Why Gum and the player do not render while Corn and the dog do.
  - Whether the mission resource backport helps, hurts, or does nothing.
  - Intermittent input failure with the pad connected and "(opened)" logged.
    Not reproduced reliably; some reports were a disconnected pad, at least
    one was not.
  - 112 vs 76 dead _flags in a fresh integration regeneration. The closing
    work is on dirty-main-preserved-2026-09-09.
  - macOS window behaviour: no .app bundle, no Info.plist, no
    setActivationPolicy / activateIgnoringOtherApps anywhere. Window is made
    at src/d3d/d3d8_gl.c:1211 with SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL|SDL_WINDOW_SHOWN only.
    Isolated from emulation; cheap to fix; untouched.


UPSTREAM AND REFERENCES
=======================

ANCESTOR OF HEAD. Upstream has not moved. There is nothing to port. The T&L,

  0x00056990 CMission::runListenerCmds

The mission system is an opcode-dispatched command interpreter (RunCmds,
RunImmediateCmds, runListenerCmds, setNextSwitchFuncFromCmdID).
```

```txt
Date: 2026-09-11 (Europe/London), midday

PURPOSE

Two independent faults were worked this morning: the Corn-tutorial animation

0. THE BRANCH
=============
    reference/xemu-oracle

in the worktree

    .../Jet Set Radio Future/xboxrecomp_upstream_integration

That is the only branch touched this morning. Three things about it matter:

  * It is **entirely local**. There is no origin/reference/xemu-oracle. Five

1. THE TREE AS HANDED OVER
==========================
One uncommitted file:

    MM src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c

It carries the **MCPX writable-alias** work: a shared file mapping gives two
views of the 8 MB MCPX aperture -- the guest view stays read-only permanently
while the device model writes through the second view -- so `mcpx_hw_store`,
`mcpx_hw_store_n` and `mcpx_trap_handler` no longer unprotect anything, and the
POSIX guard window disappears. The Windows path is unchanged behind `_WIN32`.

Provenance, stated plainly: **this is not Claude's work.** It is in substance
the same change as stash 31efe87, tagged `codex-ohci-alias-wip`, taken off
codex/upstream-integration at 12:19 BST; the copy in this tree differs from the
stash only by the mem-watch wiring that 9a114fe already committed here, plus one
comment-indent hunk that is the sole unstaged change. It is directly the fix for
[[mprotect-mmio-windows-lose-writes]] and for the rule in CLAUDE.md about
guarded MMIO pages.

As far as this session can determine it has **not been built or run** in this
worktree. It wants `cmake --build`, `ctest`, and one real run before it is
committed -- it rewrites the aperture's allocation path, so a silent failure
there degrades to "USB/audio register access will fault".


2. THREAD A -- THE ANIMATION FAULT (the objective)
==================================================
### Where it now stands, measured like-for-like

At the Corn tutorial, both sides, same tool, same 10 s interval:

    id 44:  xemu   2 dwords changed    recomp   8      <- near-static in BOTH
    id 45:  xemu 449 dwords changed    recomp 137
            shared 119 | xemu-only 330 | recomp-only 18

The 330 dwords xemu writes and we never do are structured, not scattered:

    +0x09E8           (1)
    +0x0CE0..+0x0DE4  (66)   <- the transform block; 4x wider than the 16 dwords
                                 previously measured, so the old window was too
                                 narrow
    +0x0E80           (1)
    +0x11D4..+0x120C  (4 groups of 3)      <- 3-dword groups read as vectors
    +0x12C0..+0x140C  (4 groups of 15)
    +0x1484..+0x14D4  (5+ groups of 3)

Shape reads as skeletal animation: bone matrices plus per-bone transforms. The
offsets **saturate** -- a 30 s xemu sample names the identical set with
identical counts as the 10 s one -- so this is a fixed per-frame working set,
and a longer recomp window can only ever show "absent", never "slower".

### Three framings died this morning, and that is the real progress

  * **+0x11C is not an identity.** 31 samples: id 44 takes 13 distinct values,
    id 45 takes 12, and **128 never appears in either series**. It is a mutable
    state/animation index. The whole "both characters were given the same
    identity" chain, the descriptor path and the four-way setter shortlist are
    dead.

  * **The animation machinery works.** In gameplay all four CPlayers show 16/16
    dwords changing at +0xCE0 -- the same rate xemu shows at the tutorial. The
    fault is scene-scoped to the Corn tutorial, not a general failure.

  * **The "suppressed low 2.5 KB" (section 17) was an artefact.** xemu does not
    write +0x0000..+0x09F4 at the tutorial either; that sweep is gameplay-only
    on both sides. It came from comparing our gameplay against our tutorial,
    which is not a differential at all.

  * **id 44 is static by design.** xemu changes 2 dwords on it in 10 s and the
    *same* two (+0xC94, +0x134C) in 30 s. Corn is id 45. Every reading taken on
    id 44 -- the 8-vs-2 dwords, the +0x11C / +0xE50 / +0xE58 comparisons -- was
    measuring correct behaviour.

### The mode theory, and the one measurement still outstanding

The JSRF-Decompilation author's video supplied the mechanism: every game object
has 15 virtual methods (exec, postexec, draw x five modes), precedence
CoveredPause > Event > FreezeCam > UncoveredPause > Default, and his own example
of the wrong mode is *"the player character's position and animation won't get
updated"* -- our symptom exactly. The decompilation's symbol table gives the
walkers:

    0x00011070  CActBase::recursiveExec0Default
    0x00011D00  CActBase::recursiveExec1Default
    0x000112A0  CActBase::recursiveExec0Event
    0x000114D0  CActBase::recursiveExec0CoveredPause
    0x00011700  CActBase::recursiveExec0FreezeCam
    0x00011930  CActBase::recursiveExec0UncoveredPause
    0x000123E0  CActMan::ActionExec

Measured so far:

    gameplay      Exec0Default 33916  Exec1Default 33917  ActionExec 3028
                  Event / CoveredPause / FreezeCam / UncoveredPause  ALL ZERO
    new-game menu Exec0Default 10020  Exec1Default 10000  others zero
    tutorial      NOT YET MEASURED     <-- the outstanding step

The mode booleans at CActMan +0x38..+0x48 are all-zero and **byte-identical to
xemu** at the Corn dialogue (only frame counters and the id-array base differ),
and all-zero demonstrably selects Default in two other scenes. So the inference
is that the tutorial runs Default too and mode selection is exonerated -- but it
is an inference, it is twelve counters and one human run to settle, and this
project has been burned four times this week by exactly that substitution.

### Also checked, and clean

  * 893 indirect-call targets resolved, **0 unresolved**.
  * 501 stubbed functions in the build, and **none** appears in CPlayer's vtable
    or four related class vtables. A virtual landing on a stub would dispatch
    correctly and silently do nothing -- the exact shape of our fault -- so this
    was worth eliminating.
  * Object layout was already verified twice: against the decompilation's real
    CActBase/CActMan headers, and by the 47-object field-by-field xemu match.


3. THREAD B -- THE "PAD-POLL STALL" IS TWO THINGS
=================================================
This is the correction with the widest blast radius. **Every prior stall
observation in the older handovers needs re-reading against this split.**

  (1) PAUSE. `polls` stops climbing, CActMan +0x3C and +0x40 both read 1, and
      `recursiveExec0CoveredPause` runs in place of Default. Caused by a START
      press. **Not a bug.** RECOMP_FAKE_PAD pulsed A *and START* once a second,
      so START opened the pause menu -- meaning every unattended "reliable
      reproduction of the stall" celebrated earlier in the session was the fake
      pad pausing the game.

  (2) polls flat or polls = 0 while **not** paused, with Default mode still
      executing normally. A genuine defect, and the one worth chasing.

Caught live, with zero instrumentation (so no perturbation):

    healthy (polls=1166)   Exec0Default + Exec1Default running
    stalled (polls=8790)   both absent, Exec0CoveredPause running   <- (1)

    genuine (polls flat at 1220, +3C=0 +40=0, live=145)
        Exec0Default 15 samples, Exec1Default 12, every other walker 0
        top frames: sub_0005E9B0 55  sub_00191440 48  sub_000B3E10 46
                    sub_001993A0 45  sub_000163D0 26  sub_00159650 24

`sub_000163D0` is the frame already recorded in
[[jsrf-corn-tutorial-input-poll-stall]], so (2) is the same long-standing bug,
now with the pause confound stripped out. The guest runs its whole frame loop
and simply stops requesting USB reports.

### Both interrupt theories are dead, killed by a positive control

    stalled run (polls flat at 1767):  OHCI-RAISE 0   OHCI-DROP 0
    healthy run (polls -> 14329):      OHCI-RAISE 0   OHCI-DROP 0

`ohci_raise()` is **never called at all**, healthy or stalled. No interrupt is
ever dropped because none is ever raised, and the worker's "operational after
N ms; device arriving on port 1" line never prints in any run. That kills both
the level-vs-edge-trigger theory and the worker-exit-guard theory. Without the
positive control, "0 drops" would have been filed as "no masking race", which is
the exact opposite of the truth.

A level-triggered delivery change to ohci.c was written, tested (one clean run,
one that never polled at all, one that stalled later at 3117) and **reverted**.
What remains in ohci.c is opt-in tracing only -- no behavioural change.

### Instrument weight precipitates (2)

    1118 probe sites -> froze at 30 polls
     578 probe sites -> froze at 253 polls
       0 probes      -> ran to 8790 polls

The instrument heavy enough to watch this stall is heavy enough to cause it
earlier, so the entry-differential approach is self-defeating here. Sampling
(/usr/bin/sample against the live pid) has zero per-call cost and is the only
unperturbed observer available. Consistent with
[[jsrf-instrumentation-weight-destabilises-jsrf]].


4. TOOLING CHANGED (all in 9a114fe)
===================================
  * `instrument_startup.py --skip-mismatched`. It asserted a per-site label
    count across all 84 sites and **5 had drifted** against this gen, so it
    refused to install anything -- which is why RECOMP_TRIGGER_TRACE,
    TREE_TRACE, RESOURCE_TRACE and STARTUP_STATE were all recorded as
    "unexplored". Each site is still validated individually; the 79 that match
    install, the 5 skipped are named. TRIGGER_TRACE and DIALOG_SCAN both work
    now and print usefully.

  * `instrument_func_hit.py --ecxpair VA:0` records `(this, vtable)` per call,
    so an object's class is identified directly with no dump correlation. Same
    skip escape valve: 545 of 550 counters installed, ran clean (scene
    live=164, 701,600 draws), 176 executed in gameplay.

  * `[JSRF-PAUSE] +3C=.. +40=..` printed every report in main.c, with an
    explicit "<== PAUSED (covered pause)" marker. One line, and it permanently
    prevents section 3's misdiagnosis recurring.

  * RECOMP_FAKE_PAD is now a START *window*, because a pad that never sends
    START cannot get past "Press Start" at all (the first fix attempt got this
    wrong):

        RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1        START for the first 90 s, then A only [default]
        RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=<n>      as above with an n-second window
        RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=a        never send START
        RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=always   old behaviour -- and it WILL pause the game

    The mode is announced at startup as `[PAD] fake pad: ...`.

  * ohci.c: OHCI-RAISE / OHCI-DROP counters, opt-in, read-only.


5. TRAPS PAID FOR THIS MORNING
==============================
  * `signature_scan.py` compares **one instant per side**. For any mutable field
    "distinct in xemu, identical here" can be sampling coincidence. Its output
    is a candidate list, and each candidate must be classified static-or-mutable
    over time before anything is built on it.

  * A pass/fail check of first-vs-last poll count labelled a run "OK" whose last
    three reports were identical -- it had stalled, just later. **The tail is the
    signal, not the endpoints.**

  * Freeze detection comparing `tail -1` against `tail -3 | head -1` matches
    spuriously when fewer than three reports exist, and produced a false stall.

  * RECOMP_FAKE_PAD does **not** bypass the USB path: `g_pad_polls++` sits
    *before* the fake-pad branch in `xbox_InputGetState`, so flat `polls` in a
    FAKE_PAD run is a real observation -- but see section 3 for why those runs
    were pausing themselves anyway.

  * `RECOMP_MEM_WATCH_MIRRORS` is not a switch. It is a compile-time
    `#define 28u` inside recomp_mem_watch.c with no env binding. An earlier
    handover line suggesting it be tried was wrong.


6. WHAT TO DO NEXT
==================
Ordered by evidence per hour. B is the only thread that iterates without a human
at the pad.

  A1. Measure the exec walkers at the Corn tutorial. Twelve counters, one run,
      `[JSRF-PAUSE]` now live so the run self-diagnoses. Default-only exonerates
      mode selection outright and puts the fault inside the Default exec method
      for id 45; anything else and the video's mechanism is our bug.

  A2. Find the writer of id 45's +0xCE0..+0xDE4 by gameplay-vs-tutorial entry
      differential -- same binary both halves, so whatever runs in one and not
      the other is the target. Use a **light** probe set (578 sites perturb the
      run). Static grep cannot find it: a 66-dword block plus 15-dword groups is
      a block copy or an indexed loop, not `mov [reg+disp]` stores.

  B1. Take a healthy and a stalled sample in the same run and diff the frame
      sets. The frames present when healthy and absent when stalled are the poll
      path that stops. Sampling only, for the reason in section 3.

  B2. Re-run the real-pad case. Four of ~14 real-pad runs flatlined and none was
      checked for pause state; `[JSRF-PAUSE]` now settles which of (1) or (2)
      each one is at a glance.

  C1. Build and test the MCPX alias sitting in the tree (section 1), then commit
      it on its own with a message that says why.

  C2. Harness, if A or B drags: xemu save states via `-monitor`/`savevm` makes
      the oracle measurement repeatable in seconds instead of a playthrough, and
      scripted pad input makes the tutorial half of A2 unattended. Roughly
      twenty-five playthroughs have gone into this investigation; that is the
      dominant cost, not compute.


7. ARTEFACTS
============
Correction to an earlier draft of this file: the run artefacts are **not**
lost. Every run this week is preserved under

    build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/<name>/{stdout,stderr}.log

(90 directories, gitignored but on disk), including the gameplay CPlayer-entry
baselines and every exec-mode count quoted above. Only the ad-hoc scratch
scripts live in an ephemeral /private/tmp session directory. That log corpus is
what made section 9 below provable without re-running anything.

The sampler itself was an inline loop around /usr/bin/sample taking a paired
healthy/stalled capture from one pid. Given that sampling is now the only
viable observer for thread B, it is worth writing properly into
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/ rather than rebuilt ad hoc each session.


9. THE MCPX ALIAS (ff5f578) IS IMPLICATED IN A NEW CRASH
========================================================
Added 11 Sep, after the alias described in section 1 was committed as ff5f578
"Keep MCPX guest writes guarded through a writable alias" and validated as
"SIGSEGV is pre-existing". **It is not pre-existing.**

### The measurement

Every preserved run under render-investigation/, classified by whether its
banner says "hardware writes use a permanent alias":

    alias builds      9 faults at 0x00000003FFFFFFBE / 18 runs
    non-alias builds  0 occurrences of that address, in 72 recorded runs
                      over two days

Faults in non-alias runs exist but are other addresses with other causes
(0x38508C487 is the mem-watch series, 0x38B04778D, 0x3FFFF7A89). The address
0x3FFFFFFBE appears **only** with the alias, and always identically:

    SIGNAL: SIGSEGV (11)   HOST FAULT ADDRESS: 0x00000003FFFFFFBE
    EAX=FFFFFFB4 ECX=000006C4 EDX=00002054 EBX=00000011
    LAST INSTRUMENTED GUEST FUNCTION: sub_00147EBB

0x3FFFFFFBE is guest VA 0xFFFFFFBE (base 0x300000000), i.e. a guest
dereference at -66 with EAX = -76 -- a negative/error value used as a pointer.

### The controlled A/B, run today

Same build directory, same gen, same environment
(`RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0`, 64 MB, fake pad), the only variable being
`git checkout ff5f578^ -- src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c` and a rebuild:

    alias, run_bounded 75 s          0 faults / 3   (~8,600 polls each)
    alias, sample_pad_poll harness   1 fault  / 3
    control, sample_pad_poll         0 faults / 5

So it is intermittent and load-sensitive -- the sampler harness provokes it --
but it never appears without the alias.

### Why the original validation missed it

Two confounds, both visible in the preserved logs:

  * The runs used to declare it pre-existing were themselves **alias runs**.
    The one named `alias-ref-long-1` -- the intended reference -- prints
    "hardware writes use a permanent alias" in its own banner. There was no
    control arm.
  * Those runs also differed from the morning's healthy baseline in two
    unrelated switches: `RECOMP_TOTAL_RAM_MB` was 128 rather than 64 (visible
    as "mapped 131072 KB", "Mirror 16: skipped", 27/28 views) and
    `RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE` was unset, so heap reserves landed at 0x04000000
    "outside physical RAM". Both differ from every healthy run on record, and
    neither was noticed.

Note that the project's own harness already knew about this shape:
`sample_pad_poll.py` hard-codes `RECOMP_SEPARATE_RESERVE=0` with the comment
that the separate-reserve path "has its own known 0xFFFFFFxx guest-address
fault".

### Recommendation

Revert or hold ff5f578 until the mechanism is understood. The change is
mechanically sound in intent -- it is the right answer to
[[mprotect-mmio-windows-lose-writes]], and its own instrumentation is clean
(12,469 trapped writes, zero guard windows) -- but it introduces a crash in
half the runs that provoke it, and nothing in the current investigation
depends on it. Do not carry it under the animation or input measurements: a
build that dies at ~10 s in half its runs will corrupt every differential
those threads rely on.

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_ORACLE.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER FOR CODEX -- THE WINDOWS DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE
Date: 2026-09-11 (Europe/London), evening
From: Claude.

Background and full reasoning: CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_ORACLE.txt,
written today, 389 lines. This file is the short version plus the one thing
that needs doing first. Read section 1 before you touch anything.


0. WHAT YOU ARE INHERITING
==========================
A Windows build of the JSRF harness now exists: mingw-w64 cross-compile, run
under CrossOver 25 on Apple Silicon. Purpose is a DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE -- one
tree, one gen tree, two hosts -- not a playable runtime. macOS is still the
only build that plays, and is verified unregressed by everything below.

The Windows build boots, loads the XBE, runs guest code, and delivers device
interrupts at 62 Hz. It stops in DirectSound init. Today found and fixed four
real bugs getting it that far, three of them in code shared with macOS.

Everything is UNCOMMITTED. 538 insertions across 9 files, both toolchains
clean.


1. DO THIS FIRST: A FIX IS APPLIED BUT WAS NEVER RUN
====================================================
The last thing I did was implement the suspected root cause. It compiles on
both toolchains. IT HAS NOT BEEN EXECUTED ONCE. Do not believe it until you
have run it, and do not build anything on top of it first.

What it is: the AC97 bus-master reset is WRITE-CLEAR, and on Windows nothing
implemented that. MCPX_WRITE_CLEAR (xbox_memory_layout.c ~line 836) lists the
eight AC97 NABM box control registers with the RR bit, but the function that
applies it -- mcpx_apply_write_clear, defined ~1129 and called ~1357 -- lives
INSIDE the `#if !defined(_WIN32) && defined(__aarch64__)` block that spans
934-1623. On Windows it is never compiled and never called.

Why that hangs the title: sub_001A6F52 is DirectSound's AC97 bus-master reset.
The tree already documents its exact shape, in the comment above the table --

    MEM8(cr) = 2;              // RR, "reset this box's registers"
    cl = MEM8(cr) & 2;         // read back ONCE, outside the loop
  L: if (cl) goto L;           // never re-reads memory

-- so the bit has to be suppressed AT THE STORE. Against plain RAM it sticks,
the stale read is 2, and the guest spins forever. That is where the Windows
main thread was last seen (see section 3).

The fix guards the AC97 page in the Windows VEH and applies the same table, and
extends the decoder to byte-width stores (0x88 / 0xC6), which it needed anyway
because the guest writes that register as a byte.

VERIFY IT LIKE THIS. Two lines should appear at startup:

    NV2A: PCRTC_INTR_0 page guarded for write-1-to-clear
    AC97: bus-master page guarded for write-clear (RR)

and then the single cheapest success check in the whole effort:

    macOS connects FOUR interrupts; Windows has only ever connected three.
        grep "KeConnectInterrupt" <log>
        macOS: vector 3, vector 1, vector 6, and vector 5 (routine 0x001A2681)
        Windows so far: 3, 1, 6 and nothing more.
    If Windows connects vector 5, the DirectSound stall is gone.

Also watch: "[APU] started by the title", ADX tick leaving 0, and NtOpenFile
count leaving 4 (macOS reaches ~1340).

IF IT DOES NOT WORK, the most likely reason is that the AC97 page guard fights
xbox_McpxApplyReady, which re-applies the codec-ready bit at 0xFEC00130 -- the
SAME page. On macOS that is handled by calling it from inside the trap handler
while the page is already unprotected. On Windows the ack thread writes it from
outside, so it will fault into the VEH; the handler completes any store on a
guarded page, so it SHOULD be fine, but it is untested and it is the first
thing I would suspect.


2. HOW TO BUILD AND RUN BOTH HOSTS
==================================
Windows (cross-compile from macOS; mingw-w64 has every import lib needed):

  cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build> \
    -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<toolchain>.cmake \
    -DRECOMP_GEN_DIR=<gen> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DXBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT=4"

  The toolchain file is four lines (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Windows, the three
  x86_64-w64-mingw32 tools, FIND_ROOT_PATH at the mingw sysroot).
  XBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT is NOT optional: RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD runs guest ISRs
  and bridge_run_isr pushes onto g_esp without establishing a stack, so the
  thread borrows a worker slice and the pool is 0 by default.

  Run under CrossOver, bottle "recomp-gate" (win10_64; the user's existing
  "JSRF-Control" bottle was not touched). Paths are Z:\ style.

  RECOMP_AC97_READY=1 RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD=1 RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1

  RECOMP_AC97_READY IS MANDATORY. Without it the APU aperture stays plain
  memory, the guest's writes never reach the model, and it initialises and
  waits forever. The file says so; it still cost a run to rediscover.

macOS: as documented in CLAUDE.md, plus RECOMP_METAL=1.

THE CROSSOVER WINDOW IS ALWAYS BLACK AND IS NOT A SYMPTOM. The guest
framebuffer is never connected to it -- xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource and
the event-pump hook are both POSIX-only in main.c -- so it can only ever be a
black unresponsive rectangle however far the title gets. The D3D8 probe is now
opt-in on Windows (RECOMP_D3D8_PROBE) so no window appears at all. Judge runs
by the stderr counters. This confused the session twice.


3. WHERE THE GUEST ACTUALLY STOPS
=================================
Main guest thread, last entries before it goes quiet:

    ... 001A6C67 001A6E59 001A1B7C 001A0EA1 001A4FA0 001A1B7C 001A4C3D
        0019E3B7 001A1BAF 001A706C 001A1B7C 001A0E3E 001A6F52 001A1B7C

sub_001A6F52 is the AC97 reset described in section 1. sub_001A1B7C is a scoped
IRQL raise (it calls kernel thunk slot 93 = ordinal 160 = KfRaiseIrql, read out
of the XBE at .rdata VA 0x001C3F60 / raw 0x001B4000) and is noise here; it is
called constantly by everything in DSOUND.

The interrupt side is healthy and is NOT the problem any more:
    [VBLANK] delivered=2797 over 44910 ms = 62.3 Hz  unacked_skips=0
    the audio ISR fires at the same rate on both hosts (5534 win / 5474 mac)


4. THE INSTRUMENT, AND HOW TO NOT BE FOOLED BY IT
=================================================
func_hit_probe.c now records, per thread, a CIRCULAR ring of the last 1024
function entries, printed by RECOMP_FUNC_HIT_TRACE as [FUNC-SEQ] thread N.
Arm sites with instrument_func_hit.py against a COPY of a gen tree -- it
installs counters into existing generated C and needs no regeneration.

Four ways this measurement produced a confident wrong answer today. All four
are cheap to repeat by accident:

  (a) THREAD INTERLEAVING. The ring used to be global. ISR and DPC entries
      interleave with the main thread, so 0x00193C50 (vblank ISR) and
      0x00194480 (D3D's vblank DPC, named as such in the NV2A_ACK comment)
      both read as guest-path divergences. Per-thread rings fixed this, and
      with them THREAD 0 IS IDENTICAL ACROSS 547 COLLAPSED STEPS on both hosts
      -- every "divergence" found before that was scheduling, not behaviour.
  (b) UNEQUAL POLL COUNTS. sub_00190F90 is a calibrated delay (load 400,
      decrement, return). macOS calls it 5 times, Windows 28, and Windows then
      CONTINUES NORMALLY. A positional diff reports a false divergence 80 steps
      early. Collapse consecutive repeats before diffing.
  (c) TRUNCATED TABLES. Extracting [FUNC-HIT] with `tail -N` cut macOS's
      245-entry table against Windows' 56 and invented 23 "Windows-only"
      functions. There are none; Windows runs a strict SUBSET. Take the last
      contiguous run of FUNC-HIT lines.
  (d) A HEAD-CAPPED RING. The first version recorded the first N entries. Both
      hosts are identical there; what differs is where a thread STOPS. It has
      to be circular.

And one instrument that lies outright: the Windows-only RECOMP_APU_TRACE in
apu_mmio_hook.c prints mcpx_apu_mmio_read(offset) -- the value read BACK from
the model -- not the value written, so correct writes to registers the model
does not store display as zeros. Use RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE instead (new; in
mcpx_apu_mmio_write, works on both hosts, prints the written value and the
issuing guest function).


5. THE FOUR BUGS FIXED TODAY
============================
  (a) GP/EP register blocks had NO storage in the APU model ("ignored for now")
      -- writes dropped, reads returning 0. The guest's EPRST |= 1 read-modify-
      write therefore wrote 0 and held the DSP in reset. Storage existed
      (d->gp.regs, d->ep.regs), unwired.
  (b) Device interrupt delivery required the guest to BLOCK: bridge_device_irq_
      poll had one caller, inside the guest's blocking wait. A spinning guest
      never reaches it. RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD (opt-in, default off) runs the pumps
      on their own thread.
  (c) PCRTC_INTR_0 had no write-1-to-clear on Windows, so the first vblank was
      pending forever and 1859 of 1865 deadlines were skipped.
  (d) [PAD-POLL] counters did not exist on Windows AT ALL. A Windows build
      would have silently reported polls=0 -- one of the two input failure
      signatures being investigated. They are wired to the real XInput path,
      not stubbed, because a counter that cannot move is worse than none.

Plus the portability work: 7 compile errors and 4 link symbols. The 1,310,876
lines of generated C needed ZERO changes; the blockers were latent Windows-path
bugs from macOS work, not portability gaps.


6. THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES ALL OF THIS
========================================
MACOS NEVER EXERCISES THE APU MODEL'S READ PATH. Its trap protects the aperture
PROT_READ, so only writes fault; every guest APU register read is an ordinary
load against aperture RAM that the write handler stores through. The guest
reads back only what it itself wrote, and mcpx_apu_read is never consulted.
Windows is the first host to reach it and failed on the second register it
touched. The model's read side is unvalidated on the platform this effort
debugs.

Two dead files worth knowing: src/usb/ohci.c is not the live controller (that
is src/kernel/xbox_usb_ohci.c) which is why it can call an xbox_AllocThreadTib
defined nowhere and still link; and src/nv2a/nv2a_mmio_hook.c contains a
complete Windows VEH handler called from nothing but the README.


7. FILES CHANGED (all uncommitted)
==================================
  src/apu/apu_core.c            GP/EP storage; RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE at the funnel
  src/apu/apu.h                 trace PC provider declaration
  src/apu/apu_sdl2.c            two globals missing from the Windows section
  src/input/xinput_device.c     pad-poll counters + [PAD-POLL] on Windows
  src/kernel/kernel_bridge.c    RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD; duplicate g_in_dpc removed
  src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c  PCRTC write-1-to-clear; AC97 write-clear
                                (SECTION 1 -- UNTESTED); Windows trap install
  src/kernel/win32_native.c     NEW: xbox_TraceSeconds, w32_thread_trace_report
  src/kernel/CMakeLists.txt     wires the above on WIN32 only
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/main.c            NV2A VEH route; guest-fn ring;
                                pad_inject on CreateThread; D3D8 probe opt-in
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/func_hit_probe.c  per-thread circular [FUNC-SEQ]

New opt-in switches, all default off: RECOMP_IRQ_THREAD, RECOMP_APU_REG_TRACE,
RECOMP_GUEST_TRACE_REPORT, RECOMP_D3D8_PROBE.

The archived gen at scratchpad/gen-baseline is the AS-FOUND tree, NOT pristine:
it already carried 13 jsrf_func_hit sites from an earlier session. It is still
the right baseline -- it is what the macOS build has been running -- but a
comparison that assumes it is clean will be wrong.


8. IF SECTION 1 WORKS
=====================
Expect the next stall, not the title. Nothing about this exercise has been one
fix deep. Re-run the two-host [FUNC-SEQ] comparison (thread 0 only, repeats
collapsed) and it will name the next one; that loop is now cheap, which is the
real deliverable here.

DO NOT fork this into a Windows-only tree. Every comparison above depends on
both binaries coming from one tree and one gen, and three of the four bugs in
section 5 are in code macOS shares -- in a fork they would have been
Windows-local patches with macOS keeping the latent versions.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_WINDOWS_RENDERS.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER FOR CODEX -- WINDOWS STOPS CRASHING AND STARTS DRAWING
Date: 2026-09-11 (Europe/London), late night
From: Claude.

Long form and reasoning: CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-11_DEPTH_CLEAR.txt and the
four progress notes of the same date. This is the short version plus the three
things worth doing next. Section 1 is the one that matters.


0. WHAT YOU ARE INHERITING
==========================
The Windows oracle no longer crashes. It boots, connects all four vectors, runs
the APU, raises AND acknowledges PGRAPH software-method notifies, loads game
media (1,157,120 bytes of Media\People\People01.dat), executes ~600 clears and
~600 draws, and puts pixels in the framebuffer. Every earlier run died inside
60 seconds in D3D init.

macOS is unregressed throughout and was never the point: 2.7M pusher methods,
~1880 flips, 61.8 Hz, ctest 21/27 -- the same five backport-presence failures
and the one ratchet this gen has always had. Nineteen commits, a8afcf5..a33f47a,
tree clean, nothing pushed.

The crash that ended every previous run is ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED, not guarded.


1. THE THREE THINGS TO DO NEXT
==============================
None of these has been measured. That is deliberate -- I stopped rather than
open a fourth thread -- so they are leads, not conclusions.

(a) WHY SUBMISSION STOPS AFTER ~600 DRAWS. The run ends with the GPU idle and
    one software-method notify outstanding. jsrf_software_method blocks the
    PUSHER thread until the guest acknowledges; the guest may in turn be
    waiting for the ring to drain. A deadlock between those two would look
    exactly like this. FIRST MEASUREMENT: is the guest's PGRAPH ISR still being
    dispatched during the stall? bridge_vblank_poll's software-method loop is
    gated on xbox_Nv2aSoftwareMethodPending() and on g_in_dpc/g_in_isr, and it
    runs from the guest's blocking waits -- if the only thread that would
    deliver it is itself blocked, nothing does.

(b) THE 0xBC60 VOICE LINK. The APU voice list walks four good entries and then
    a fifth link of 0xBC60, every frame, on Windows only:
        [APU] voice list 0 entry 4: handle 0xBC60 is out of range
    It is garbage, not an off-by-one, and it is at a fixed position. macOS
    never produces one. Find who writes that link.

(c) A RING THAT HAS NEVER WRAPPED TO ITS BASE. The pusher reports
    "healthy base wraps so far 0" after 600 draws. The PUT-backwards lines that
    accompany it are DIAGNOSTIC ONLY and their own comment records the desync
    as pre-existing and once-per-run, so they are not a Windows regression --
    but a ring that never wraps cleanly is worth understanding.


2. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND THE SHAPE IT KEEPS TAKING
=========================================================
0xFFFFFF00 was never a guest computation. It is a cleared Z24S8 depth pixel --
stencil 0x00 then depth 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF -- and clear_surface in our own
nv2a_pb_exec.c was painting 1.2 MB of it across the title's .data every clear.

Why: xbox_ContiguousAlloc is two different allocators. POSIX takes from the
guest heap, which already sits above the image. Windows bumped g_contig_next
from XBOX_CONTIG_BASE, so its first contiguous allocation had physical offset 0
and they climbed from there -- and the GPU addresses that window BY PHYSICAL
OFFSET, so everything below the image end aliased the title's own code and data.
The POSIX branch carries a comment describing this exact bug being fixed there,
for this same title.

That is the shape of nearly everything the oracle has found: a real bug in
SHARED code, fixed on one host and left standing on the other. Five of them so
far -- AC97 write-clear, PCRTC write-1-to-clear, the APU's GP/EP storage,
interrupt delivery, the PGRAPH notify -- plus this one and the voice-list bound.
Windows is not a port. It is a second observer of our own defects.

One cause, three symptoms, all now gone: depth surface 0x00248000 -> 0x004D8000,
framebuffer 0x001B2000 -> 0x00442000, and the push ring off physical 0x1000.


3. BUILD AND RUN
================
Windows, cross-compiled from macOS. Build ONLY the harness target: the
pb_scan_owner_test and d3d8_smoke targets do not cross-compile (setenv,
nv2a_vsh.h) and will fail the all-target build.

  cmake -S diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault -B <build> \
    -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<mingw-toolchain>.cmake \
    -DRECOMP_GEN_DIR=<gen> -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DXBOX_WORKER_STACK_COUNT=4"
  cmake --build <build> --target jsrf_first_fault -j8

Run it under CrossOver. The wrapper needs CX_BOTTLE, NOT WINEPREFIX, and it
mis-parses a long quoted argv, so drive it from a .bat inside the bottle:

  CX_BOTTLE=recomp-gate <CX>/bin/wine cmd /c 'C:\jsrf\run_ck.bat'

with the .bat invoking the exe and passing xbe path, game dir (over Z:) and hdd
root. RECOMP_AC97_READY=1 is still mandatory. The window is black by
construction -- xbox_D3D8SetGuestFramebufferSource and the event-pump hook are
POSIX-only in main.c -- so judge every run by the stderr counters.

Symbolising a Windows crash, which works well: the mingw .exe keeps its symbols
and is based at 0x140000000, so
    x86_64-w64-mingw32-addr2line -f -e jsrf_first_fault.exe <rip>
resolves any frame from a Wine backtrace or any host_pc a probe prints. Two
saved Wine reports are in docs/jsrf/artifacts/.


4. THE INSTRUMENTS, ALL OPT-IN
==============================
  RECOMP_STORE_WATCH=<va>:<len>  host page guard over ordinary guest RAM; prints
                                 the faulting HOST PC. This is what found the
                                 depth clear when three other watches could not.
  RECOMP_MEM_WATCH=<va>:<len>    guest stores routed through RECOMP_MEM_WRITE
  RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH=<va>       samples a dword either side of every bridge call
  RECOMP_TEXT_CHECKSUM=1         .text pages, ring window + control half
  RECOMP_DUMP_VA=<va>[,<va>...]  guest dwords once, at load
  RECOMP_SURFACE_TRACE=1         zeta DMA handle/base/limit/offset/pitch
  RECOMP_D3D_ALLOC_TRACE=1       twelve sites down both contiguous allocators
  RECOMP_PB_NOTIFY_TRACE=1       software methods the parser decodes
  instrument_block_writes.py     1571 lifted rep movs/stos, into a gen COPY
  instrument_d3d_alloc.py        the two D3D allocators, into a gen COPY

Coverage, so you know what a silence means: RECOMP_MEM_WATCH sees 79,114 macro
stores and NOT the ~2,735 plain lifted stores, NOT block copies (use the script)
and NOT the runtime's own device writes -- which is what this crash turned out
to be. Its header says so; I did not read it for several hours.


5. TRAPS THAT COST ME TIME TODAY
================================
  - PRINT CAPS ARE COUNTERS. [HEAP] stops at 64 lines (RECOMP_HEAP_TRACE) and
    jsrf_software_method prints its first 16. The first made "ordinal 166 is
    never called on Windows" survive every test while being false, and it was
    the plan's founding fact. The second made me report a healthy notify path
    as broken. Read the trigger before trusting the value -- CLAUDE.md already
    says this and it applies to log lines too.
  - g_xbox_code_lo..hi IS NOT .text. This XBE flags .rdata and .data executable,
    so that range is mostly data and sampling it reports the guest writing its
    own globals. Use g_xbox_text_lo/hi.
  - A GUARDED PAGE MUST NOT SHARE A LOCK WITH A DEVICE HANDLER. Sharing
    g_nv2a_pcrtc_lock stalled two runs, which reads as "the guard prevented the
    corruption" and means "the guard wedged the title".
  - BEFORE BELIEVING A WATCH SAW NOTHING, CHECK THE RUN REACHED THE WRITER.
    Two zeroes here were runs that stopped early.
  - CONSULT docs/pipeline/06-debugging.md FIRST. It prescribes the ICALL caller
    address and the target ring for exactly this class of crash; our build had
    dropped both, and restoring them named the caller in ten minutes after I had
    spent hours building four instruments.


6. DO NOT RE-RUN THESE
======================
Each died under measurement, with a positive control where an absence was the
evidence.

  .text corruption by the push ring    16/16 pages clean, both hosts
  the KeConnectInterrupt race          fixed; crash unchanged
  concurrent guest DPCs                interlock tried; crash unchanged; reverted
  the OHCI memset(out,0xFF,len)        run without OHCI; byte-identical
  unbridged ordinals leaking stack     1, 46, 144 all have correct arg sizes;
                                       the warning saying otherwise WAS the bug
  guest block copies                   positive control passing, then zero hits
  kernel bridge calls                  RECOMP_KERNEL_WATCH, zero hits
  the D3D contiguous allocators        identical call for call on both hosts
  the physical heap alias as the       superseded: the arena start was the
    pusher's problem                   cause, and it is fixed


7. WHAT I WOULD NOT DO
======================
Do not fork a Windows tree. Every finding above depends on one tree, one gen,
two hosts, and six of the seven bugs were in code macOS shares.

Do not chase the black CrossOver window. Connecting a framebuffer path on that
host is real work and answers nothing the counters do not.

Do not treat 8 nonzero pixels as rendering. It says the GPU model writes where
the display is pointed, which it never did here before, and nothing more.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/CLAUDE_TO_CODEX_HANDOVER_2026-09-12_WINDOWS_PLAYABLE.txt`:

```txt
JSRF HANDOVER -- WINDOWS RUNS THE GAME. WHAT IS LEFT IS SPEED AND INPUT.
Date: 2026-09-12 (Europe/London)
From: Claude.  To: Codex.

Supersedes every 2026-09-12 handover before it. Two of them
(ADX_STREAM_NEVER_STARTS, WINDOWS_NEVER_REACHES_GAMEPLAY) are marked RETIRED in
place because they are WRONG, and section 1 says why in one line.

24 commits, f3a12b3..dd2a094.


0. STATE, VERIFIED AT THE DESK
==============================
The CrossOver build boots, renders into a visible window, plays music, reaches
gameplay, and its intro animation runs. A human watched it. Audio was glitching
and is now fixed; the picture was tearing and is now clean.

    macOS     ~30 s to gameplay, GPU rasterised, pad works, audio 48004 Hz
    Windows   ~150 s to gameplay, CPU rasterised, pad NOT seen by the guest,
              audio 47983 Hz

Launch it:  wine --bottle recomp-gate --cx-app 'C:\jsrf\run_jsrf.bat'
The bottle has jsrf.exe, run_jsrf.bat, hdd\, and three probes with .bat files
(xiprobe, diprobe, padtest).


1. THE RULE THAT COST THREE WRONG HANDOVERS
===========================================
    NEVER COMPARE THE TWO HOSTS AT EQUAL WALL-CLOCK TIME.
    COMPARE AT EQUAL GUEST MAIN-LOOP COUNT.

Windows runs the guest main loop at roughly a fifth of macOS's rate. Every
"Windows never does X" finding on 11-12 Sep was a Windows run caught mid-boot
measured against a macOS run already in gameplay. on=4 vs on=5, fe_methods 177
vs 4369, "CRI's DirectSound driver is never entered", "the BGM directory is
never opened", "0 of 17 CPlayer markers" -- all of it dissolved when the runs
were anchored properly. Windows crosses the title at main loop 2408; macOS at
2400-2900. In guest time they agree almost exactly.

`[FUNC-HIT] 000123E0 calls=N` is the clock. Arm it with instrument_func_hit.py.


2. THE ORACLE, AND ITS ONE TRAP
===============================
diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/oracle_anchor.sh mac|win <clock> <outdir>

Runs one host to a guest-clock anchor, dumps the object inventory there, and
EXITS. macOS 13 s to clock 1000, Windows 37 s. Overshoot 0 on both.
RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP_AT=<n>[,<va>] is the anchor; RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP_EXIT ends
the run at it; the periodic report is switched off because at 2 s it cost 2.7x
of guest throughput.

Compare with compare_objects.py A.json B.json. It resolves pointers
symbolically, so two different heap layouts do not read as divergence.

Result, Windows against macOS at clocks 500/750/1000/1500/2000: ZERO divergent
field groups at every anchor. Evidence preserved in
docs/jsrf/oracle-evidence/2026-09-12_clock2000_zero_divergence/ with the clock,
the root address, the compared field lists and the method.

THE TRAP, and it nearly produced a fake finding. Anchoring by POLLING the clock
from the ack loop pins the FRAME but not the position inside it, because the
poller is not the thread running the guest. Anchored that way the hosts
"diverged" on id 7 +0x44 at clock 500 and id 4454/7665 at 750 -- and every one
of those reproduced between two runs of the SAME host. jsrf_func_hit_alarm now
fires the dump on the thread that takes the clock site's nth entry, which is
the same instruction boundary on both hosts, and the macOS noise floor at 750
went from two divergent groups to zero.

    A CROSS-HOST COMPARISON IS UNINTERPRETABLE WITHOUT A SAME-HOST CONTROL AT
    THE SAME ANCHOR. The noise floor is phase-dependent; measure it per anchor.


3. WHAT WAS FIXED, WITH NUMBERS
===============================
(a) NATIVE TLS ON WINDOWS -- 2.2x.  tools/windows/clang-mingw.cmake
    mingw-gcc implements __thread with EMULATED TLS: __emutls_get_address, a
    call per access, and the generated code is `#define eax g_eax` over a
    thread-local register set. 145 emutls symbols. clang, same sysroot, same
    source, emits _tls_index -- native, TEB-relative. Zero emutls.
        GCC/emutls    203 @30s   421 @60s   782 @90s
        clang/native  880 @29s  1574 @59s  1754 @84s
    Upstream does not have this problem because upstream builds with MSVC,
    where _MSC_VER selects __declspec(thread). We run a third configuration.
    Three things clang's driver does not do that gcc's does are handled in the
    toolchain file; read its comments before touching it.

(b) THE TRAP DECODER WAS COMPILER-DEPENDENT.  f37a9d0
    xbox_Nv2aHandleWin32Fault completed plain stores only, so every guarded
    MMIO page depended on how the compiler spelled `|=`. gcc emits load/or/
    store; clang emits `orl $imm, mem` and the clang build died inside its own
    memory-layout init. 0x81 and 0x83 with /1 and /4 now fold the current value
    in. ONE EXCEPTION, which cost a run: a read-modify-write states the final
    value, so it must NOT then have write-1-to-clear applied -- host code
    raises an interrupt with PGRAPH_INTR |= bit, and before & ~(before|bit) is
    zero, so the raise became a clear and the pusher waited for ever.

(c) THE WINDOWS PRESENTER SHOWS WHOLE FRAMES.  ad0474f
    It read the live surface on a 16 ms timer with no flip sync; a fullscreen
    image is two triangles and the CPU rasteriser manages a few frames a
    second, so it caught mid-draw almost every time and tore on a hard
    diagonal. nv2a_pb_exec_surface hands back the copy taken AT the flip, which
    is what the POSIX presenter has always used. Sampler went from oscillating
    0/19841/2690/12860 nonzero to a steady 153600/153600.

(d) WINDOWS AUDIO.  dd2a094
    XAudio2 queued three 1024-sample buffers, ~64 ms, and DROPPED the block
    when full. 3,496 drops in one run; output 43,750 Hz against the model's
    48,000. Now sixteen slots with at most eight queued (~170 ms), separate
    numbers so a slot cannot be recycled while still playing.
        gen_hz 43750 -> 47983     drops full 3496 -> 6

(e) THE WINDOWS BUILD HAS A PICTURE.  RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1, commit 0d45c25.
    src/video/fb_present.c is a Windows-only GDI presenter, wired into
    AvSetDisplayMode, linked into the exe, and never switched on by anything.
    Every older handover saying "the CrossOver window is always black" was
    describing the D3D8 route only.

(f) A DUALSHOCK 4 EXISTS ON WINDOWS AT ALL.  0d60248
    XInput only ever supported Xbox-family pads -- a DS4 is not an XInput
    device on real Windows either. Added a DirectInput8 fallback, consulted
    only when XInput reports nothing. Verified by a binary linking the real
    input file: CONNECTED with live stick values where it returned 1167.


4. THE TWO THINGS LEFT, IN ORDER
================================
(1) WINDOWS HAS NO GPU RASTERISER. This is the slowness.
    The accelerated path in nv2a_pb_exec.c is #ifdef __APPLE__ in its entirety.
    Measured with a counter added for the purpose (15d74e7):
        macOS    223,976 batches native, 0 software fallbacks,
                 0 batches + 0 triangles on the CPU
        Windows  0 native; every triangle through raster_triangle()
    and then that software rasteriser is itself binary-translated. The two
    effects multiply; neither alone makes the intro run.

    Upstream ships a D3D11 pgraph sink, it is initialised, and it implements
    nothing useful: unhandled = 15,078,354 of 15,078,354. The big misses are
    NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT16 (21.4M), NV097_SET_BEGIN_END, and the
    NV097_SET_TRANSFORM_CONSTANT block -- indexed vertices and vertex-shader
    constants. The CPU executor already implements all of it and xbox_vsh
    already runs the shaders, so this is a bounded port. nv2a_metal_draw is the
    structural model: one entry point taking the prepared batch state,
    returning a triangle count or -1 to fall back.

    DO NOT read [TEXTURE] prepared/rejected as a rate or compare it across
    hosts. The fields are different units and macOS's Metal path returns before
    the site that increments `rejected`, so macOS reads 28 where Windows reads
    439,082 for the same work.

(2) THE GUEST NEVER ASKS FOR INPUT ON WINDOWS.
    With a DS4 attached and working, past the title, in gameplay:
    polls=0. macOS at a comparable point polls hundreds of times. Our input
    layer is fine -- padtest.exe in the bottle returns CONNECTED with live
    sticks. The break is between our layer and the guest.

    The chain is: guest XPP schedules an interrupt transfer -> ohci_thread
    services it -> usb_gamepad_report -> xbox_InputGetState. ohci_thread is
    created only #if defined(_WIN32), and it CANNOT LINK, because ohci.c calls
    xbox_AllocThreadTib and this tree does not define it.

    xbox_GetConnectedInterrupt is now defined (8a0e349). xbox_AllocThreadTib is
    NOT, and the note where it would go in kernel_bridge.c explains why at
    length. Short version: I wrote the obvious one -- a stack from
    xbox_AllocThreadStack, the xbox_HeapAlloc trio PsCreateSystemThreadEx uses,
    xbox_SetupCurrentThreadTib, sized from g_image_tls_total which the loader
    now publishes -- it built on both hosts, macOS showed no object-state
    change, and IT WEDGED WINDOWS: "[ADX] tick STUCK at 1 (flag=0)", never
    advancing, where the binary without it runs the same configuration fine.
    Reverted.

    Prime suspect, unproven: ohci_thread starts during init and calls
    xbox_AllocThreadStack and xbox_HeapAlloc from a HOST thread while the guest
    is allocating on its own, and nothing says the guest heap is thread-safe.
    Pre-allocate on the main thread before the thread is created and hand the
    block over. Validate with a pad plugged in -- without one, a correct TIB
    and a broken one look identical.

    CHEAPER FIRST STEP: find out whether the pad does anything in GAMEPLAY ON
    MACOS. macOS polls properly and is a 30 second loop. If input works there
    and not on Windows, (2) is isolated to the OHCI path; if it works on
    neither, the problem is above both and this whole thread is a red herring.


5. DO NOT REPEAT THESE
======================
  * The register-context change. Consolidating the eight RECOMP_TLS scalars
    into one struct removes 13% of generated code (recomp_0000.c.o 8.32MB ->
    7.25MB) and buys NOTHING: title crossover 30.55 s -> 30.69 s, gameplay loop
    rate identical. _tlv_get_addr is 75% of the profile's samples and not 75%
    of the cost -- a profiler's top entry is a hypothesis. Written up in
    CLAUDE_PROGRESS_2026-09-12_REGISTER_STRUCT_NEGATIVE.md.
  * Keying RECOMP_TLS on _WIN32 so mingw-gcc takes __declspec(thread). emutls
    drops 145 -> 16 and the title exits through HalReturnToFirmware within
    sixteen file opens.
  * The DSOUND fatal latch 0x001BA04C, the byte [this+0x12] & 3 gate at
    0x001A43F0, and "two adjacent methods on one object". All measured on both
    hosts, all dead ends.
  * Calling xbox_OhciReport. It has no caller anywhere, and referencing it
    pulls in parts of ohci.c that need the undefined symbols above. It is a
    landmine, not a spare instrument.


6. INSTRUMENTS ADDED
====================
  RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP_AT=<n>[,<va>]  anchor the dump to the guest clock
  RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP_EXIT=1         end the run when it fires
  jsrf_func_hit_count(va)           the guest clock, readable
  jsrf_func_hit_alarm(va,n,fn)      fire fn on the thread that reaches n
  RECOMP_DSOUND_FATAL / RECOMP_CRI_DSOUND / RECOMP_CRI_SERVER
  [MCPX-TRAP] now counts VEH faults per page and undecoded opcodes (996f84c)
  [METAL] now counts batches and triangles that went to the CPU (15d74e7)
  [FILE] NtOpenFile now carries the guest caller
  diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/padcheck.sh -- can either build see a pad, in
    one second. Both hosts read the pad through macOS's HID layer, so a pad on
    the USB bus with no HID gamepad interface reads exactly like an unplugged
    one. That cost two runs.

A controller note, because it wasted time: a DualShock 4 works on both hosts
(macOS via SDL, Windows via the new DirectInput path). An Xbox Series X wired
pad works on both too, natively via XInput on Windows -- when it enumerates. It
intermittently sits on the USB bus presenting no HID interface at all, and in
that state it is indistinguishable from absent. Run padcheck.sh first.
```

```txt
CLAUDE -> CODEX, 13 Sep 2026
ONE QUESTION: WHAT WRITES CPlayer +0xCE0 ON HARDWARE AND NEVER IN OUR BUILD?

Everything else in here is context for that question. If you only read one
section, read 2.


0. STATE OF PLAY
================
The black screen on New Game is FIXED and pushed (a13aa04). The unattended path
now reaches the Corn tutorial in ~46 s with no human:

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/run_scripted.sh <name> \
        @diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/pad/new_game.pad 200

It holds live=61, seq=30 WaitEndStoryOrVsMission, m_bFatal=0, renders and
presents. JSRF_ABI_CHECK_ALL over every chunk reports four violations and all
four are the expected CRT signatures. The characters do not animate. That is
the only thing left between here and a playable tutorial.


1. WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED, WITH EVIDENCE
==========================================
Do not spend time re-deriving these.

  * NOT register clobber. ABI check armed across every chunk on the tutorial
    path: 4 rows, all CRT (__chkstk, __SEH_prolog/epilog, a thunk helper).
  * NOT exec scheduling. Corn's exec virtual (CPlayer vtable 0x001CCFF8 slot 1
    = sub_00080340) is dispatched 3,400+ times after the stall.
  * NOT mode selection. Slots 4,7,8,10,11,13,14 are all 0x00011C90, the nop, so
    every non-Default mode is a nop by design.
  * NOT the draw path. Both CPlayers are in the draw list (CActMan +0x7FA4,
    threaded on +0x34) every report, and Corn is visibly on screen.
  * NOT the +0xE50 state band. See section 2 -- xemu is IDENTICAL.
  * NOT the pose gate at 0x00080407. See section 2 -- xemu is IDENTICAL.
  * NOT the remaining 154 truncated switch dispatchers. None clobbers anything
    on this path.


2. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS
===============================
xemu (US ISO, GDB stub) and our build, at the SAME tutorial beat
("This is the GG's Garage. Hey, where's our pizza?"):

                  ours                        xemu
    scene         live=61 seq=30              live=61 seq=30
    id 44         e50=23 s11c=AA r38=0        e50=23 s11c=AA r38=0
    id 45         e50=25 s11c=AB r38=0        e50=25 s11c=AB r38=0

Identical, and static on BOTH sides across three samples over six seconds --
while Corn is visibly animating in xemu.

Then 64-byte block deltas on the same objects, 3 s apart:

    xemu id=45  30/96 changed: 09C0 0C80 0CC0 0D00 0D40 0D80 0DC0 0E80
                               11C0 1200 12C0 1300 1340 1380 13C0 1400
                               1440 1480 14C0 1540 1580 15C0 1600 1640
                               1680 16C0 1700 1740 ...
    ours id=45  10/96 changed: 0C80 11C0 1440 1600 1640 1680 16C0 1700
                               1780 17C0
    xemu id=44  26/96 (including 0CC0..0DC0)
    ours id=44   5/96: 0C80 1240 1280 12C0 1340

THE POINT: xemu writes +0x0CE0..+0x0DC0 -- the transform block -- WITH r38 == 0
and e50 in the skip band. So the copy loop at 0x000804A1 inside sub_00080340 is
CORRECTLY SKIPPED ON BOTH SIDES, and a SECOND, SEPARATE WRITER of that block
exists that runs on hardware and never runs here.

That second writer is the whole question.


3. WHY IT IS HARD TO FIND FROM HERE, AND WHAT I TRIED
=====================================================
  * No RECOMP_MEM_WRITE32 in the entire generated tree targets +0xCE0. The one
    known writer computes the address (edi = esi + 0xCE0) and writes through
    sub_0014C340, which is a three-float VECTOR ADD (dest.xyz += src.xyz), not
    a copy. So grepping for the offset does not find writers.
  * Candidate family by offset: sub_000836F0 writes +0x9E8, +0xE80, +0x9C0 and
    +0x9E4 -- four of the fields xemu changes and we do not -- and is called
    from sub_00084200, sub_00091AC0/C30/D70, sub_000A6B10 and sub_000A76E0.
    sub_0009D030/D0C0/D260/D7E0/D870 and sub_0009E910 also write +0x9E4/+0x9C0.
    Whether any of them runs at the tutorial IS NOT YET MEASURED -- see 4.
  * A GDB write watchpoint on xemu's Corn+0xCE0 would name the writer directly.
    I set one (Z2 accepted, OK), it never trapped in 20 s, and reading
    registers while the guest was still running desynchronised the stub. xemu
    then refused new connections and had to be killed. DO NOT REPEAT THAT
    without a stop reply in hand first; see xemu_rsp.py's docstring.


4. WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT, AND THE TRAP IN IT
===========================================
Put plain jsrf_func_hit counters (direct-mapped, O(1)) on sub_000836F0,
sub_0009D030/D0C0/D260/D7E0/D870 and sub_0009E910, run the unattended path, and
see which run at the tutorial. Instrument via

    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/instrument_func_hit.py --va ... --skip-mismatched

THE TRAP, and it cost me three runs today: a control run that stalls at the
title screen (live=157 instead of 61) is NOT necessarily instrumentation
weight. I attributed three such failures to probe cost. At least one was CPU
starvation -- a wedged xemu was spinning at 124% and the load average was 10.
CHECK `uptime` AND `ps -A -o %cpu,command -r | head` BEFORE blaming the probe.

Real weight limits that ARE established:
  * jsrf_func_arg does a LINEAR SCAN of up to 384 entries per call. Two of
    those at hot CPlayer sites stalled the title reliably. jsrf_func_hit is
    O(1); prefer it always.
  * RECOMP_OBJECT_DUMP writes a JSON file per report and stalls the title at
    any useful cadence. Use RECOMP_OBJECT_ACTIVITY / RECOMP_OBJECT_BLOCKS
    instead -- host-side digests, no files, never failed a control.
  * EVERY measurement needs a control run against the untouched binary first,
    and must be rejected if progression to the tutorial differs.


5. IF YOU WANT THE ORACLE BACK
==============================
xemu must be relaunched with the stub and the tutorial replayed (~4 min):

    /Applications/xemu.app/Contents/MacOS/xemu -s        # stub on 1234
    /usr/bin/python3 diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/xemu_cplayer_state.py

Snapshots did not save on this build, so there is no shortcut. The block-delta
method in section 2 needs no watchpoints and produced the whole answer; prefer
it.

===================
Given that hardware writes CPlayer +0x0CE0..+0x0DC0 every frame at the Corn
tutorial while +0xE50 is parked at 25 and [[this+0x2D0]+0x38] is 0, and our
build does not: which function is it, and why is it unreachable for us?
```

```txt
CLAUDE TO CODEX, 14 Sep 2026 (late)
THE INSTRUMENTS LIE. THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT A COMPLAINT ABOUT THEM.

Supersedes CLAUDE_HANDOVER_2026-09-14_THE_HARNESS_REACHES_GAMEPLAY.txt for
everything about input, interrupts and diagnostics. 19 commits, ctest 27/29
(the 2 are the usual deliberate pair), translator suite 186/186.

I want your read on sections 3, 6 and 7 especially. I have been wrong six
times today and the corrections are all recorded below rather than tidied away,
because the pattern in them is more useful than any single fix.


0. THE ONE PARAGRAPH VERSION
=============================
"Controller input not working" is the guest's USB driver dying, not the pad.
[PAD-TRACE] cannot see it, because [PAD-TRACE] is generated by OUR OWN injector
thread and looks healthy against a completely deaf guest. Ordinal 175 is the
honest metric and was in every log all along. Separately: bridging
KeSynchronizeExecution regressed the title and is now off by default; the
interrupt interlock was doing three unrelated jobs at once and has been split;
and the probe set is not armed in any freshly regenerated tree, so three
reports print zeros that read exactly like "the guest never called DSOUND".


1. WHAT IS COMMITTED
=====================
Accuracy (Tier 2 of ACCURACY_GAPS.md, essentially finished):
  * -fwrapv on the title, -fno-strict-aliasing tree-wide, -w replaced by -Wall
    minus four generator-inherent classes. Measured yield over the whole gen
    tree: 440 -Wuninitialized, 11 + 6 -Wmacro-redefined, nothing else.
  * fistp onto the RECOMP_F2I_* helpers, with new 16- and 64-bit siblings.
  * Signed conditions vs OF and operand width, across seven flag setters.
    `sar` at 8/16 bits was a wrong VALUE, not a wrong flag.
  * XBOX_FS_BASE's two conflicting definitions made explicit.
  * Controller released on SIGTERM/SIGINT (nothing did this before).
  * Interrupt delivery split into three concepts (section 6).
  * Two instruments stopped lying (section 5).

Harness: pad/gameplay.pad, play_scripted.sh with four verdict gates,
test_pad_schedule.py, irq_delivery_test.c, input_release_test.c,
apu_output_frames_test.c.


2. THE BIGGEST SINGLE LESSON: A STALE GEN TREE
===============================================
translator.py gained `ebp = 0` in b1f0531 at 18:44 on 13 Sep. The gen tree in
build-macos was written at 16:59 the same day. So for a full day, every binary
anyone measured carried 440 `PUSH32(esp, ebp)` reads of an indeterminate local
-- undefined behaviour the compiler may propagate at -O2 -- while the fix sat
in git looking done.

Nothing in the build says the gen tree is older than the tool that produced it.
If you touch tools/recomp, regenerate, or you are testing yesterday.


3. THE CONTROLLER WAS NEVER THE BUG  <-- WANT YOUR VIEW
========================================================
The guest's XPP USB driver stops submitting transfers, permanently, at a
different moment every run. Whether a run reaches New Game is simply whether it
was still alive when the presses arrived.

Measure with kernel ordinal 175 (MmLockUnlockBufferPages). Already in every
log's histogram. It separates every run cleanly:

    reached New Game   12963 23022 27676 30174 72421 72737 73945 74150 74603
    stuck at title       234  1100  5130  6684 10614

234 transfers in 300 s is enumeration and nothing else. That run was never
going to accept a button however many were pressed.

DO NOT TRUST [PAD-TRACE] OR nonneutral=. With RECOMP_PAD_INJECT=1 our own host
thread calls xbox_InputGetState at 50 Hz, so a deaf guest still produces a
healthy trace. Healthy ~172 polls/s, dead EXACTLY 50/s -- the injector alone.
There is a third producer too: RECOMP_PAD_SCRIPT's synthetic presses also raise
nonneutral. I asserted "your presses are reaching the guest" three times on the
strength of that counter. All three were wrong.

"START works but A does not" was the same illusion. One 20-byte report, one
writer, no threshold anywhere -- the STARTs landed before the driver died and
the A presses after it.

WHAT I WANT FROM YOU: the leading hypothesis for the driver death is the
WriteBackDoneHead latch. xbox_memory_layout.c:796 returns early while
HcInterruptStatus bit WDH is set; that register is write-1-to-clear and only
the trap implements that, but the same 16 KB page is unprotected and
reprotected ~120x/s by mcpx_hw_store_n, so a guest ISR write landing in a
window SETS the bit instead of clearing it and the pad is off for the run. That
is the hazard CLAUDE.md names, and the file's own comment at :1105 records the
same thing happening to the PORT STATUS register, measured. It is UNTESTED.
ack_windows= does NOT exonerate it -- that counter only covers the APU path and
there is no counter at all on mcpx_hw_store.


4. ORDINAL 153 REGRESSED THE TITLE, AND IS NOW OFF BY DEFAULT
==============================================================
Bridging KeSynchronizeExecution was correct on its own terms: the guest was
being handed a fabricated FALSE for a routine that never ran. It was also
shipped without being exercised at gameplay, and it made things worse.

    binary WITHOUT the bridge   3/3 New Game   ord175 74603 74150 73945
    with it                     1/3 New Game   ord175 27676 10614  5130
    with it, off by default     3/3 New Game   ord175 30174 72421 72737

Not the mechanism its own comment feared. Both guest call sites are inside DPC
bodies, so the bounded spin and g_in_isr code never execute -- which also makes
g_sync_exec_unsynchronised vacuous, and my reading of "unsynchronised=0" as
"the interlock was always acquired" was wrong.

What it really does is switch on ~41 previously-dead DSOUND functions. The only
instruction in the image that sets a bit in the DSOUND state word [this+0x6FC]
is inside the routine the bridge calls, so those arms were unreachable before.
They run inside bridge_run_isr -> bridge_run_dpc, holding the interrupt
interlock, and that interlock gates the only pump that runs the guest's USB ISR.

RECOMP_KE_SYNC_EXEC=1 turns it back on.


5. TWO INSTRUMENTS STOPPED LYING, AND AN AUDIT FOUND FIFTEEN MORE
==================================================================
Fixed:
  * [VBLANK] delivered= counted RAISES, not ISR entries, and incremented before
    a dispatch that can now refuse. Measured the moment it was split:
    delivered=1584 raised=1656 -- 4.3% counted and not delivered. Every
    "62.x Hz, the guest's clock is fine" claim rests on that number.
  * THE PROBE SET IS NOT ARMED IN ANY FRESHLY REGENERATED TREE.
    instrument_startup.py defaulted --gen to the tree regenerate.sh overwrites,
    so probes went into the live tree and the next regeneration deleted them --
    ~38 RECOMP_* switches that read as available and do nothing. Three reports
    printed zeros indistinguishable from "the site never ran". --gen is now
    required and the script stamps a marker; the harness prints
    [PROBES] NOT ARMED instead. The current tree has NO probes installed.

Still lying, ranked, not yet fixed:
  * fe_methods is a SUM of guest MMIO stores and our own model's internal idle
    traps (apu_vp.c:435 has two callers, :846 and :1993) -- while the code at
    :346 proposes it as the positive control for whether MMIO reached the
    model. Same shape as [PAD-TRACE].
  * idle_trap=0 has two causes: no voice idled, OR the guest never armed
    FETFORCE1, whose value is printed nowhere. THIS IS LOAD-BEARING: the
    "scripted runs are structurally blind" argument in STATUS.md:109 and
    ACCURACY_GAPS.md:340 rests on on=5 off=0 idle_trap=0.
  * [PUSHER] clears/flips/draws/unhandled describe the D3D11 sink, not the
    Metal path that draws the picture on macOS.
  * [APU-PACE] gen_hz/out_hz can print 0 because the clock never starts
    (g_apu_pace_start_us is set inside throttle(), which the frame thread can
    skip entirely). The comment tells the reader both-at-zero means the engine
    stopped. Not necessarily.
  * min_queued=0 is printed both for "drained to nothing" and "never measured".
  * unpaced= does not mean what its comment says, and the saturated case it
    would need to catch -- the lock-inversion freeze -- is not counted.

Twelve were checked and found HONEST; the list is in the audit if you want it.
[ADX-RATE] and [FRAME-WIN] are the two rate computations done correctly and are
worth copying.


6. THE INTERLOCK IS SPLIT, AND THE VALIDATION IS INCONCLUSIVE  <-- WANT YOUR VIEW
==================================================================================
g_vblank_delivery_active was one process-wide interlock doing three jobs, so a
guest ISR or DPC on ANY thread suppressed EVERY vector on every other thread.
Now: per-thread recursion depth; per-vector in-service; guest IRQL for
eligibility, with ineligible interrupts left pending.

The IRQL model already existed -- g_current_irql, maintained correctly since
the beginning, consulted by nothing -- and KeInitializeInterrupt has always
passed the vector's IRQL as arg 4, which this bridge discarded. That is WHY a
global interlock was standing in for a mask.

Six runs, 153 enabled in all, arms alternated:

    new     ord175 72765 29654 17451    ADX stalls 0  17  0
    legacy  ord175 30274 27857 27941    ADX stalls 17 18 18

NO RELIABLE THROUGHPUT WIN. I claimed 2.4x from the first matched pair; that
was one good-mode run against one bad-mode run and it is withdrawn. What
survives is ADX stalls in 1 of 3 new against 3 of 3 legacy, which is suggestive
at n=3 and no more. RECOMP_LEGACY_IRQ_INTERLOCK=1 restores the old behaviour on
the same binary.

I kept it because the semantics are right and tested, not because the numbers
justify it. Tell me if you think that is the wrong call.


7. THE BIMODAL DISTRIBUTION IS UNEXPLAINED  <-- THIS IS THE REAL OPEN QUESTION
==============================================================================
Across every configuration tried today -- 153 on, 153 off, new interlock, legacy
interlock, audio device alive, audio device dead -- runs land in one of two
modes and nothing we changed moves which one you get:

    good mode   ord175 ~72000    ADX stalls 0
    bad mode    ord175 ~28000    ADX stalls 17-18

That is not noise around a mean; it is two stable attractors. It is almost
certainly the thing we have been attributing to 153, to the audio device, and
to the interlock in turn. Each of those attributions was made on 2-3 runs and
each dissolved when n grew.

If you chase one thing from this handover, chase this. My instinct is that
whatever decides the mode is decided EARLY -- the bad runs are already slow at
the first histogram -- but I have not tested it and I have been wrong about
this class of thing repeatedly today.
```
