```txt
================================================================================
3. THE TWO FIXES, IN CASE YOU NEED TO REASON ABOUT THEM
================================================================================
3.1 rdtsc  (296a0a2)
sub_00145560 is JSRF's QueryPerformanceCounter and is literally `rdtsc`.
sub_00145571 is its QueryPerformanceFrequency and returns 0x2BB5C755 =
733333333, the Xbox CPU clock. At 0x00025370 the title compares an elapsed
value against 0xE4E1C0 = 15000000 ticks, about 20.5 ms. Over that it tail-jumps
at 0x0002537E to sub_0006F730, which pushes 0x400000 - the exact bit tested at
0x0006EE5C - and raises the disc-error dialog.

Implemented in src/kernel/recomp_tsc.c as a monotonic host clock scaled to
733333333, declared in templates/runtime/recomp_types.h, emitted by
tools/recomp/lifter.py.

*** build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/gen IS HAND-PATCHED at the three rdtsc sites
*** (recomp_0006/0007/0009: sub_00145560, sub_0015FA20, sub_00193C40) so this
*** could be tested WITHOUT resetting the seed accumulator. The committed
*** lifter change emits the same code on the next regeneration. Carry nothing
*** across by hand. gen/recomp_types.h was refreshed from templates/ likewise.

3.2 The disk cache  (8b450d3)
Upstream's Partition3/4/5 rules gave \Device\Harddisk0\Partition5 a mapping it
did not have, so JSRF's cache probe started succeeding and the title began
caching. Every cache write then failed: it writes through
Z:\Media\Font\jetfont.dat~ without creating the directories above it, and Font
is not among the directories it creates at startup. Fixed by creating parents
on any disposition that creates, keyed on O_CREAT so it cannot drift from
posix_open_flags.

3.3 INLINE_ARRAY  (1b44943)
JSRF pushes vertices with NV097_INLINE_ARRAY (0x1818), 1.2M times per 25s. The
executor knew only ARRAY_ELEMENT16. Inline data has no offset or stride: the
layout is implied by which attributes declare a non-zero size and what format
each gives, packed in attribute order, recomputed per batch. fetch_vertex() is
the single indirection; the rasteriser is unchanged.


================================================================================
4. WHERE IT ACTUALLY STOPS
================================================================================
4.1 GEOMETRY
draws went 0 -> 103,924, but ALL FORTY sampled batches are BYTE-IDENTICAL:
  prim 5, 12 dwords, stride 4 dw, attr0 position (2 floats), attr9 (2 floats)
  v0 (  -0.53,   -0.53) uv (   0,    0)
  v1 (2559.47,   -0.53) uv (2560,    0)
  v2 (  -0.53, 1919.47) uv (   0, 1920)
One full-screen triangle drawn 103,924 times. Not a scene.

The viewport is a textbook 640x480 one - scale (320,-240,16777215,0), offset
(320.531,240.531,0,0) - so the target really is 640x480 and the 4x is real.
The vertices are neither screen space nor NDC (through that viewport v1 lands
at x=819350). They are inputs to the title's VERTEX PROGRAM.

DO NOT DIVIDE BY FOUR. It lands this one triangle and is a coincidence fit. The
title uploads only c0 (1,1,16777215,1), c1 (0.53125,0.53125,0,0) and
c60..c62 - c0.xy is 1, there is NO scale constant anywhere - so the factor of
four is inside the instructions and cannot be recovered from outside them.

Note also: nv2a_pb_exec.c assumes attr0 is position and attr3 is colour. That
is a FIXED-FUNCTION assumption. In a programmable pipeline the semantics are
whatever the program assigns, and this program has not been read. The
"position" it plots may not be one.

4.2 ASSETS
sub_00025DD0 is the asset-open helper. Over 30s it is called EXACTLY THREE
TIMES and never again:
  #1 ret 0x00033AD7   a0 = a stack buffer
  #2 ret 0x0002C08E   a0 = "D:\Media\Font\jetfont.dat"
  #3 ret 0x0002C146   a0 = a runtime-built path (se_sys)
Not looping, not retrying, not failing. NOTHING ASKS IT FOR A FOURTH ASSET. The
stall is upstream of the loader, in whatever decides what to load.

There IS a cache state machine at sub_00026170 (jump table 0x000261E8, state 2
is a terminal "mov eax,1 / ret"), and it is NEVER CALLED. Do not start there.

12-second stack sample (build-macos/merge-audit/claude-sample-steady.txt) puts
the live work at sub_00151DD0 (heaviest, a domain-checked float routine),
sub_0014CCA0 (a maxss/minss clamp), the sub_00013A80 / sub_00013930 main-loop
chain, sub_000659C0, and a large cluster in the D3D section 0x0018D000-0x00198000.


================================================================================
5. THE TWO BLOCKERS, SCOPED
================================================================================
5.1 BLOCKER A - THE VERTEX PROGRAM
Everything visual is behind this. Texturing does NOT substitute: all four
texture units are programmed and src/d3d/d3d8_swizzle.h exists, but a texture
cannot help until a batch can be placed.

src/d3d/d3d8_vsh.c is a 1470-line NV2A microcode parser and it DOES NOT DECODE
MICROCODE. Checked against a program captured from JSRF:
  - insn[0] as bits 0..31 (what vsh_extract does): every slot is MAC=NOP ILU=NOP,
    because the first uploaded dword is zero in all of them
  - words reversed: ILU opcode 8 (the unit has 0..7) and constants c128/c143,
    which the title never uploads
The test vector is in that file and in docs/technical/nv2a-shaders.md. FIX THE
LAYOUT UNTIL IT DISASSEMBLES THAT, then run it in nv2a_pb_exec.c.

You need the real XVS encoding - xemu nv2a_vsh.c, envytools, or the SDK. Do NOT
reconstruct it from memory: a wrong field position yields a plausible shader
rather than an error, which is the worst outcome available. An empirical search
over five instructions is underdetermined; too many offsets survive while the
high word is zero.

5.2 BLOCKER B - INPUT
JSRF's XPP section is a USB stack. It drives the OHCI host controller at
0xFED00000 DIRECTLY. Nothing in src/input is reachable from the guest, in this
tree or upstream (see 6).

Two register-semantics bugs were fixed (1698432), measured not assumed:
  HcCommandStatus +0x08 bit 0 (HostControllerReset) is SELF-CLEARING; on plain
    RAM the reset never finished
  HcRhDescriptorA +0x48 low byte (NDP, port count) is READ-ONLY; XPP writes the
    register for NPS/NOCP and on RAM that zeroed NDP, so the root hub reported
    ZERO PORTS and nothing could ever attach
Both are now held from the NV2A ack tick. Two ports is a CHOICE, not a
measurement; RECOMP_OHCI_PORTS overrides it.

Attaching a controller still needs, in order:
  1. the connect announcement timed AFTER HcInterruptEnable has RHSC (0x40).
     The current probe gates on HcControl and fires too early - fix this first.
  2. an ISR path that accepts the interrupt. It currently declines.
  3. service for the control transfers XPP issues through the HCCA at
     0x01452000 - device/config/HID descriptors, ED/TD, completion writeback.
That is device emulation, sized as its own project.

WHETHER INPUT IS EVEN THE STALL IS UNPROVEN. See 7.1.


================================================================================
6. WHAT UPSTREAM DID ABOUT THESE (checked, not assumed)
================================================================================
sp00nznet/xboxrecomp does NOT solve either blocker, though its gap analysis
marks both done. Verified against upstream/work/v0.7.0-non-local:

  "USB/OHCI gamepad | N/A | Bypassed via XInput"
  "Controller polling (4 ports) | DONE | XInput backend"
    -> xbox_InputGetState / xbox_InputInit appear ONLY in src/input/* and its
       README across the WHOLE tree. Nothing in src/kernel, src/d3d, the thunk
       table, tools/, or generated code calls them. The XInputGetState in
       win32_compat.c is a POSIX stub for the HOST api, not a guest bridge.
       The bypass is an intention. The module is dead code there too - so this
       defect is INHERITED, not introduced by the JSRF merge.

  "Vertex shader microcode translation - DONE. d3d8_vsh.c/h: 1,868 lines"
    -> their d3d8_vsh.c is BYTE-IDENTICAL to ours (1470 lines, not 1868) and
       every VSH_FIELD_* offset matches. It fails the same vector.

Fair caveat: upstream targets Windows/D3D11 and that path was not exercised
here. But an uncalled function is uncalled on every platform, and the shader
file is the same file.

The test vector in docs/technical/nv2a-shaders.md is worth sending upstream.


================================================================================
7. RETRACTIONS - READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANYTHING
================================================================================
7.1 "Not waiting for a button" - WITHDRAWN
Commit 69f3b24 added RECOMP_FAKE_PAD, saw no change, and concluded the title is
not waiting on A/START. That is unsupported: xbox_InputGetState is unreachable
from the guest, so the title could not read the pad and the test was vacuous.
The hypothesis is OPEN. Do not re-run that test expecting it to mean anything
until src/input is wired to the guest.

7.2 "The 100k IRQL pairs are USB polling" - WRONG
sub_001BD5FF is a generic interlocked read-and-reset helper called from all
over the game code. The OHCI init sub_001BD14A runs EXACTLY ONCE (probed and
counted). The USB stack initialised and went quiet.

7.3 "readable geometry" (commit 1b44943) - OVERSTATED
Corrected in e089140. It is one triangle repeated, not a scene.

7.4 A DIAGNOSTIC IN THIS TREE HAS BEEN LYING
The device-ISR log line prints en(+0x140) and intr(+0x100) - NV2A PMC offsets -
against an OHCI regbase whose interrupt registers are +0x10 and +0x0C. EVERY
"ISR ... -> FALSE ... en=0 intr=0" line about 0xFED00000 in every log in this
tree reports the wrong registers and says nothing about USB. Worth fixing; it
is small.

7.5 STALE ELSEWHERE
CODEX_HANDOVER.txt and ROUTE_B_PLAN.txt predate all of the above. In
particular ROUTE_B_PLAN section 15 concludes the renderer "is never asked to
draw" and costs the remainder as title-specific state-machine RE. That framing
is wrong: the game was in an error dialog and the error was ours (3.1).

7.6 A TRIED-AND-REVERTED IDEA, DO NOT REPEAT
Padding a short read up to the requested length inside the file's last 512-byte
sector, on the theory that JSRF treats a short read as damaged media. Removed
every short read, changed nothing, and the premise was wrong twice: NT reports
the true count at EOF, and an Xbox disc sector is 2048 bytes.


================================================================================
8. INSTRUMENTS (all env-gated, all off by default)
================================================================================
RECOMP_PATH_TRACE=1        path translation incl. symlink resolution. XBOX_TRACE
                           is compiled out without _DEBUG, so the path layer is
                           otherwise silent in a release build.
RECOMP_FILE_BACKTRACE=SUB  guest stack scan at a file open whose path contains
                           SUB, plus a candidate this-pointer and its +0xA0
                           string. This is what identified the disc dialog.
RECOMP_DIALOG_SCAN=1       live message-box objects by vtable 0x001CC660. A
                           dialog that only sits on screen writes nothing and is
                           invisible otherwise. Reports NONE at 25s.
RECOMP_OHCI_DUMP=n         root-hub register block, n times.
RECOMP_OHCI_ATTACH=1       announce a device on port 1 (see 5.2; fires too early)
RECOMP_OHCI_PORTS=n        override the NDP the root hub reports (default 2)
RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1           the CPU executor (second sink; default path untouched)
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_VERBOSE=1   per-batch dump incl. inline layout and raw words
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_PROGRAM=1   every write to 0x0B00..0x0BFC and 0x1E9C..0x1EA4
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_TOP=n       raise the unhandled ranking past its top ten
RECOMP_PB_EXEC_NOCLIPTEST=1 rasterise batches rejected as not screen-space
RECOMP_FB_DUMP=prefix      framebuffer BMPs
RECOMP_FAKE_PAD=1          synthetic pad - USELESS, see 7.1
NV2A method names: src/nv2a/nv2a_regs.h, 469 authoritative NV097_ defines. USE
IT. It confirmed 0x1E9C/0x1EA4 and identified 0x0840 (SET_TEXGEN_PLANE_S),
0x0A50 (SET_EYE_POSITION), 0x0300 (SET_ALPHA_TEST_ENABLE).


================================================================================
9. THE TECHNIQUE THAT CRACKED MOST OF THIS
================================================================================
HAND-EDIT build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/gen AND REBUILD. It is git-ignored, it
does not touch the seed accumulator, and a regeneration discards it. Printing
MEM32(esp) at a function's entry names its caller, because each call site pushes
a distinct return address. That is how the disc-error call site, the OHCI init
count and the asset-loader count were all obtained.

THE GUEST TRACE HOOKS CANNOT DO THIS. diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/guest_trace.h
declares jsrf_trace_function, but RECOMP_GUEST_FUNCTION appears NOWHERE in the
generated code, so it is never called - verified against the main loop, which
runs constantly. A hook placed there cannot fire for any function.

Resolve addresses to functions with build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/disasm/
functions.json; the per-section disassembly is in disasm/asm/ (text.asm, D3D.asm,
XPP.asm, ...). XPP is the USB stack.


================================================================================
10. SUGGESTED ORDER
================================================================================
1. Fix d3d8_vsh.c against the vector (5.1). Everything visual waits on it, and
   it is the only item where the missing piece is a document rather than work.
2. Then run the program in nv2a_pb_exec.c and place the batches. Only then does
   texturing (nv2a_regs.h formats + d3d8_swizzle.h) mean anything.
3. Fix the lying ISR log line (7.4). Small, and it has been misleading readers
   of this tree for a long time.
4. What decides to request assets (4.2). Independent of 1-3.
5. USB device emulation (5.2), if input is the goal.

WHAT NOT TO DO: divide by four (4.1); trust d3d8_vsh.c (5.1); re-run the fake
pad (7.1); start from sub_00026170 (4.2); pad short reads (7.6); regenerate
just to repeat completed work - and if you DO regenerate, 3.1's hand-patch goes
away and the lifter change replaces it, which is correct and expected.
```

```txt
EXECUTIVE STATUS
================

1. Genuine graphics are working.

   JSRF renders its real 640x480 "Presented by SEGA" startup logo. This is a
   title-produced frame, not a synthetic triangle or forced colour. The best
   concise record is CODEX_PROGRESS_2026-09-03_FIRST_GRAPHICS.md.

   First visual evidence:
     build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/codex-dxt-depth-08/frame003.png

   Longer confirmation:
     build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/codex-graphics-09/

   The 300-second fresh-HDD run prepared 129,811 draws at its last report,
   with zero texture and vertex rejections. It completed the cache, did not
   fault, and remained on the SEGA logo. This is not gameplay evidence.

2. The graphics path is internally RGBA and alpha is rendered.

   DXT1/BC1 sampling produces RGBA. BC1 three-colour mode produces transparent
   black for index 3; bilinear filtering can make alpha fractional. The
   measured combiner multiplies texture RGBA by diffuse RGBA. Alpha GREATER is
   evaluated before writes, and source-alpha blending is implemented.

   The measured destination is RGB565, so that framebuffer stores RGB only.
   Alpha still determines discard and blending. The ARGB8888 destination path
   stores output alpha when selected. Do not describe the RGB565 surface as an
   RGBA storage format.

3. A real post-cache file ABI bug has just been fixed.

   JSRF's XAPI directory lookup reuses one string buffer. It shortens the
   ANSI_STRING Length to the parent directory, but does not insert a NUL before
   the basename. bridge_get_xbox_path() ignored Length and passed the entire
   NUL-terminated buffer to the host. The bridge therefore attempted to open:

     Z:\Media\Cache\JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE00.CMP

   with FILE_DIRECTORY_FILE. That failed as "path not found" even though the
   marker existed. The game repeatedly failed to recognize its completed cache.

   bridge_get_xbox_path() now copies exactly the counted Length to a thread-
   local snapshot and NUL-terminates the snapshot without changing guest RAM.

4. NtQueryDirectoryFile also had the wrong guest ABI.

   Xbox NtQueryDirectoryFile has TEN parameters. The bridge treated it as nine:
   it omitted FileInformationClass, read FileName and RestartScan from the wrong
   stack slots, and popped 36 rather than 40 bytes.

   The generated JSRF call at guest 0x00145F26 pushes ten arguments. The nxdk
   xboxkrnl declaration also confirms ten:
     https://github.com/XboxDev/nxdk/blob/master/lib/xboxkrnl/xboxkrnl.h

   The bridge and backend signatures now include FileInformationClass;
   ordinal 207 cleans up 40 bytes. Only XboxFileDirectoryInformation is
   accepted. Small buffers and truncated names are bounded and reported.

5. Directory enumeration contexts were leaking.

   The backend owns a fixed 64-entry enumeration-context table. Closing a
   directory before enumeration EOF did not release its context. NtClose now
   closes and clears a matching context on both POSIX and Windows paths.

   A new guest-ABI regression drives 96 open/query/close cycles, deliberately
   exceeding the former 64-context limit. It also verifies counted paths with
   no NUL, ten-argument stack cleanup, RestartScan, invalid info classes, short
   output buffers, guard bytes, and that guest string memory is not modified.

6. The file fix is verified, but the next visible state has not been reached.

   In fresh-HDD run codex-startup-state-13, file traces now show the directory
   path correctly as:

     path=Z:\Media\Cache\

   The run created 122,467,906 bytes and all completion names
   JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE.CMP plus JSRF_CACHE_COMPLETE00.CMP through 08.CMP. No
   JSRF_FATAL.ERR exists.

   Important: run 13 accidentally omitted RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1. It is valid file
   and startup-object evidence, but NOT a graphics regression run and it made
   no BMPs. Use run 09 or run 12 for the existing rendering evidence, and set
   RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 in the next end-to-end visual run.

sub_00024700 is a four-channel colour interpolator. At steady state in the

  current +0x98..+0xA4 = 0, 0, 0, 0
  target  +0xA8..+0xB4 = 1.0, 0, 0, 0
  step    +0xB8         = 0x3C088889 (approximately 1/120)
  colour  +0xBC         = 0
  active  +0xC0         = 0

The update-list loop reaches this object tens of thousands of times, yet the
sampled current alpha at +0x98 remains zero. On the face of sub_00024700 it
should increment by +0xB8 until it reaches +0xA8. Do not yet call this an x87
translation bug: a setter may be resetting the current value later in each
frame, or the entry may return before the sampled point. Measure entry and exit

Relevant generated code:

FILE ABI IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS / REVIEW NOTES
==============================================

src/kernel/kernel_bridge.c

  - bridge_get_xbox_path() uses a RECOMP_TLS char[UINT16_MAX + 1], copies the
    guest ANSI_STRING Length, and adds a host-only terminator.
  - bridge_build_oa() preserves OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES.Attributes and avoids
    overflowing MaximumLength when Length is UINT16_MAX.
  - bridge_NtQueryDirectoryFile reads arg 7 as FileInformationClass, arg 8 as
    FileName, and arg 9 as RestartScan.
  - stdcall_args_for_ordinal(207) returns 40.

  Review risk: bridge_get_xbox_path() does not yet validate that the complete
  counted guest range is mapped before memcpy. The previous implementation
  also dereferenced the guest buffer directly, but a robust follow-up should
  validate the span without regressing valid maximum-length strings.

src/kernel/kernel_file.c

  - Both POSIX and Windows backends accept only
    XboxFileDirectoryInformation.
  - Both reject buffers smaller than offsetof(..., FileName), bound filename
    writes, and return STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW when truncated.
  - POSIX retains the directory-context lock while copying readdir's name,
    preventing NtClose from invalidating it concurrently.
  - NtClose releases any matching directory context before closing the handle.

  Only the POSIX path was compiled and exercised here. The Windows changes were
  reviewed structurally but have not been built on Windows. In particular,
  the Win32 FileName-to-wide-pattern conversion still deserves a bounded-
  length review for Length >= MAX_PATH.

diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/counted_file_test.c

  - Calls the real guest thunk bridge rather than only testing host helpers.
  - Uses a private mkdtemp directory and removes only that fixture.
  - Runs 96 directory contexts to catch the previous leak.
```

```txt
CODEX -> CLAUDE HANDOVER
Jet Set Radio Future / xboxrecomp
Date: 2026-09-04 (Europe/London)

PURPOSE
=======

Continue from the exact USB-input frontier reached in the working tree. The
title already renders the CRI, SEGA, Smilebit, anti-graffiti, and animated
"Now Loading" screens, loads Stage 12, and waits for controller input. This
session proved that the root-hub device path is alive, fixed a real OHCI port
reset bug, and captured the title's first control request.

No commit was made. The changes listed below are intentional working-tree
changes on main (HEAD was f37268a at the start of the session).


BOTTOM LINE / HOW CLOSE
=======================

We are now one concrete subsystem away from the Press Start boundary: USB
enumeration plus controller reports. This is materially closer than the prior
handover. The game now detects the root-hub connection, allocates and links its
USB device object, completes port reset, and submits a valid GET_DESCRIPTOR
control transfer. It then waits because the runtime does not yet execute OHCI
ED/TD schedules or report transfer completion.

Do not promise "playable" yet. Passing Press Start may expose later menu or
gameplay faults. For the boot-to-input milestone, however, this is no longer an
unknown broad boot problem: the immediate blocker is a small, observable USB
transaction engine (or a carefully targeted high-level XPP bypass).


UPSTREAM XBOXRECOMP CLUE
========================

The requested upstream review found no OHCI device model to copy. Upstream's
own gap analysis explicitly says:

    USB/OHCI gamepad | N/A | Bypassed via XInput

Sources:

  https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp/blob/main/docs/technical/gap-analysis.md
  https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp/blob/main/src/input/xinput_device.c

The second file is a host XInput/SDL state backend, not a USB host-controller
or Xbox controller device implementation. That architecture works when a
recompiled title calls the host input shim. JSRF's statically linked XPP drives
the OHCI registers directly, and no caller currently reaches the existing host
backend. Therefore upstream confirms two viable strategies but supplies no
drop-in solution:

  1. Identify and override JSRF's high-level XPP input entry points so they call
     the existing xbox input backend; or
  2. Keep the now-working low-level path and implement the minimum OHCI
     control/interrupt-transfer service the title actually asks for.

Given the evidence below, strategy 2 is currently the shortest evidence-led
continuation: the first schedule is already available and fully decoded.


NEW PROOF: THE SUSPECTED DEVICE ALLOCATION WORKS
================================================

Read-only probes were added at:

  0x001BF72C  root-hub connect/device creation entry
  0x001BF73B  immediately after the device-pool allocation
  0x001C06B3  device-object link helper

Run evidence:

  build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/
    codex-usb-device-01/stderr.log

Relevant output:

  [USB-DEVICE] pc=001BF72C ... controller=009E4000 ...
  [USB-DEVICE] pc=001BF73B ... device=009E4020 ...
  [USB-DEVICE] pc=001C06B3 ... device=009E4020 ...

Conclusion: sub_001BF72C executes, the pool allocation succeeds at 0x009E4020,
and sub_001C06B3 links the object. The old narrow hypothesis that allocation or
linking failed is disproved.


REAL BUG FIXED: ROOT-PORT RESET COMPLETION ORDER
===============================================

The title's observed reset write is 0x009E0010. The runtime formerly:

  a. generated PortResetStatusChange (PRSC), then
  b. applied the guest write-one-to-clear high bits.

Because 0x009E0010 contains high W1C bits, step b erased the PRSC generated in
step a. Real hardware first acknowledges changes that were already pending,
then asynchronously reports reset completion. The instant model must preserve
that ordering even though both happen in one host call.

The fix in src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c now:

  a. clears old change bits requested by the write,
  b. applies port commands, and
  c. generates the new reset-completion change afterward.

The helper is exported as xbox_OhciPortWrite so a focused regression test can
cover the observed 0x009E0010 case.

After the fix, this run advanced to a real schedule:

  build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/
    codex-usb-reset-order-02/stderr.log

Milestone lines:

  HcRhPortStatus0 <= 0x009E0010
  HcRhPortStatus0 <= 0x00100000        (XPP acknowledges PRSC)
  HcControlHeadED <= 0x009E29A0
  HcCommandStatus <= 0x00000002        (ControlListFilled)


FIRST CONTROL TRANSFER: FULLY CAPTURED
======================================

An opt-in RECOMP_OHCI_TRANSFER_TRACE instrument now dumps the control ED/TD
chain both when XPP publishes HcControlHeadED and when it asserts
ControlListFilled. The second moment is essential: at publication the ED is
still skipped and empty; at the doorbell it is populated.

Canonical evidence:

  build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/render-investigation/
    codex-usb-transfer-dump-04/stderr.log

Relevant lines 1649-1655:

  HcControlHeadED <= 0x009E29A0
  [OHCI-ED] #1 va=009E29A0 flags=00084000 tail=00000000
             head=00000000 next=00000000
  HcCommandStatus <= 0x00000002
  [OHCI-ED] #2 va=009E29A0 flags=00080000 tail=009E3F50
             head=009E3FD0 next=00000000
  [OHCI-TD] i=0 va=009E3FD0 flags=E2E00000 cbp=009E3FB0
             next=009E3F90 be=009E3FB7
             data=80 06 00 01 00 00 08 00
  [OHCI-TD] i=1 va=009E3F90 flags=E3F00000 cbp=002648DC
             next=009E3F70 be=002648E3
  [OHCI-TD] i=2 va=009E3F70 flags=E3080000 cbp=00000000
             next=009E3F50 be=00000000

Decoded USB setup packet:

  bmRequestType = 0x80   device-to-host, standard, device
  bRequest      = 0x06   GET_DESCRIPTOR
  wValue        = 0x0100 DEVICE descriptor
  wIndex        = 0
  wLength       = 8      first eight bytes only (normal address-0 probe)

The ED is address 0, endpoint 0, max packet size 8. Its chain is the expected
SETUP / IN-data / OUT-status sequence, followed by the dummy tail TD.


EXACT NEXT IMPLEMENTATION STEP
==============================

Implement the smallest synchronous OHCI control-list service, driven when the
guest writes ControlListFilled (HcCommandStatus bit 1). Start with only the
captured address-0 GET_DESCRIPTOR(Device, length 8) request:

  1. Read HcControlHeadED and safely validate the ED and TD addresses against
     guest RAM.
  2. Parse the setup TD instead of keying solely on fixed addresses.
  3. For 80 06 00 01 00 00 08 00, copy the first eight bytes of an Xbox
     controller-compatible USB device descriptor into the IN TD's CBP buffer.
  4. Complete the TDs with OHCI condition code NoError and advance the ED head
     to its tail while preserving the ED carry/halt bits correctly.
  5. Link completed TDs through HcDoneHead / HCCA DoneHead as XPP expects.
  6. Raise WritebackDoneHead (WDH, interrupt-status bit 1) through the existing
     OHCI interrupt plumbing, respecting InterruptEnable and MIE.
  7. Observe the next control request and extend the model one request at a
     time (likely SET_ADDRESS, additional device/config/string descriptors,
     SET_CONFIGURATION, then the controller interrupt-IN endpoint).

Do not invent the entire Xbox USB stack up front. The trace facility exists so
each next request and completion contract can be learned from the title. Add
focused tests for descriptor walking, bounds checks, TD condition codes, done
queue order, and interrupt gating before connecting it to the fault handler.

Signal-handler caution: the MCPX guest-write trap currently runs as a SIGSEGV
handler on macOS. The read-only tracer already uses stdio because it is
diagnostic-only, but production schedule servicing should avoid allocation and
other non-async-signal-safe operations. Prefer a small allocation-free parser
and deferred interrupt delivery if the existing kernel plumbing permits it.

    PRSC acknowledgement, and reset on an empty port.

    Fixes reset/W1C ordering and adds RECOMP_OHCI_TRANSFER_TRACE ED/TD dumps.
```

```txt
NEW STATIC FINDING: THE VOICE_ON STORE EXISTS
=============================================
An initial text search for literal `FE820124` in generated C returned nothing.
That negative was misleading because the translator prints high addresses as
signed decimal constants in this block.

The original US XBE is present at:
  /Users/andrewcollard/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/
    Jet Set Radio Future/Jet Set Radio Future (US)/default.xbe

Its DSOUND section is:
  VA  0x0019E340, virtual size 0x1C55C
  raw 0x0018C000, raw size     0x1C32C

A byte search found little-endian 0xFE820124 at raw file offset 1645645.
That maps to guest VA 0x001A3F8D, inside sub_001A3E58.

The verified archived generated code contains the same store at:
  /private/tmp/jsrf-audio-trace-20260909.TeqU2p/
    jsrf-correct-dsound-gen/recomp_0009.c:1014537

The relevant generated statements are:

  MEM32(-25034464) = edx;   // 0xFE820120: SET_ANTECEDENT_VOICE
  MEM32(-25034460) = ecx;   // 0xFE820124: VOICE_ON

The signed-address conversions were verified explicitly:
  2^32 - 25034464 = 0xFE820120
  2^32 - 25034460 = 0xFE820124

This corrects the narrower earlier impression that the generated code lacked
the submission instruction. The instruction is present. Because the live APU
counter remains on=0, execution is not reaching this store (or, less likely,
the store is reached but not routed through the MMIO hook). The first case can
be distinguished directly with one opt-in guest probe.


EXACT BACKWARD PATH TO PROBE NEXT
=================================
sub_001A3E58 contains the VOICE_ON loop. Its direct callers in the archived
generation have generated call blocks beginning at these guest labels (the
actual five-byte call instructions start two bytes later, after `mov ecx`):

  label 0x001A41FB, call 0x001A41FD in sub_001A40F5
  label 0x001A42D0, call 0x001A42D2 in sub_001A4212
  label 0x001A492B, call 0x001A492D in sub_001A490D

The earlier New Game freeze sample already showed the live chain:
  sub_001A490D -> sub_001A40F5 -> sub_001A3E58 -> sub_001A308E

sub_001A3E58 has two concrete gates before VOICE_ON:

  1. Entry early-out:
       if (MEM8(voice_object + 0x12) & 2) return;

  2. After setup, the loop count comes from:
       voice_count = MEM8(voice_object + 0x64);
       if (voice_count == 0) skip the VOICE_ON loop;

If neither gate fires, each iteration reaches guest 0x001A3F8D and writes
VOICE_ON. Therefore the smallest proven next breakpoint is an opt-in probe in
the archived generated copy (or a source-backed instrumentation script) that
records, with a bounded count:

  - entry to sub_001A3E58 and caller/return address;
  - object address;
  - word at object+0x12;
  - byte at object+0x64;
  - arrival at 0x001A3F8D immediately before the VOICE_ON store;
  - optionally the MMIO offset/value observed by the APU write hook.

Use a positive control in the same probe: report a nearby VP write already
known to execute, such as SET_CURRENT_VOICE at 0xFE8202F8, so absence of
VOICE_ON cannot be confused with inactive instrumentation.

Do not patch around the gate until the run proves which value is wrong and
where it was produced. In particular, do not force voice_count nonzero or
blindly clear bit 1 in object+0x12.

  - voice_count zero: trace construction/population of object+0x64;
  - 0x001A3F8D reached but APU on stays zero: fix the VP MMIO routing boundary;
  - 0x001A3F8D and APU on both occur: advance to PCM/voice configuration and
    mixer-output evidence rather than changing the entry gates.

Preserve controller, rendering, and the manual sub_001A308E New Game behavior.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-15_SIX_DEFECTS_FIXED_AND_THE_PICTURE_IS_STILL_WRONG.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER, 15 Sep 2026 (late)
SIX DEFECTS FIXED, MEASURED, AND THE PICTURE IS STILL WRONG

Supersedes REVIEW_RESPONSE_2026-09-15_THE_GATE_NEVER_TESTED_DEPTH.txt, which
supersedes REVIEW_2026-09-15_WHAT_TO_TRUST_AND_WHAT_TO_CHECK.txt. Read section
1 before anything else; it is the reason not to trust the rest as progress.

State: 51 commits unpushed on main, tree clean, ctest 31/31, metal_hw_check
PASS, metal_batch_check IDENTICAL.


1. THE HEADLINE
================
RECOMP_METAL_HW=1 still renders the game wrong. Six real defects were found,
fixed and measured today, each with a test that fails without it, and a person
playing the game reports the picture is still visibly corrupted: scattered
black fragments and speckle on textured surfaces during gameplay.

Do not read the six fixes as progress toward the artefact. They are six
correctness bugs that happened to be in the same subsystem. The artefact is
unexplained.

The switch is still default OFF. Nothing here changes that.


2. WHAT WAS FIXED, AND HOW IT IS KNOWN
=======================================
  1. THE BATCHED HARDWARE PATH DREW INTO AN ENDED ENCODER. batch_flush() ran
     after `encoder` was bound, so every draw after it encoded into a committed
     command buffer. RECOMP_METAL_HW=1 with RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=1 segfaulted on
     its first draw. No gate crossed the two switches, so nothing saw it. This
     mattered beyond the crash: it made the configuration that fixes defect 5
     unreachable.

  2. THE DITHER WAS APPLIED ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THE BLEND. fs() does
     blend-then-dither, which is what the NV2A and nv2a_texture_copy.c do;
     fs_hw handed the biased colour to the fixed-function blend unit instead.
     8192 of 65536 pixels wrong on the dither matrix's own 4x4 lattice, where
     the software path scored 0. Fixed with a third pipeline, fs_hw_blend,
     selected only for draws that both blend and dither.

  3. THE DEPTH/STENCIL STATE CACHE KEYED ON NINE FIELDS AND ITS DESCRIPTOR READ
     ELEVEN. stencil_zfail and stencil_func_mask were absent from the key, so
     two draws differing only in one of those were served whichever state was
     built first. 8056 of 65536 pixels against the software path's 5.

  4. DEPTH WRITES WERE NOT GATED ON THE DEPTH TEST. depthWriteEnabled read
     depth_write alone while the fragment tail derives depth_test &&
     depth_write. An overlay with the mask still set stamped depth over
     everything it covered here and nothing on the other path.

  5. ONE RENDER PASS PER DRAW, RACING ON TILE MEMORY. Every draw was its own
     render pass and command buffer: load the surface into tile memory, draw,
     store it back. 80.7 command buffers per frame with 664,933 of 781,703
     starting before the previous one ended. Each 64x64 tile kept whichever
     buffer stored it last -- a mosaic of moments, which is what a person
     watching it called the background being cut and jumbled. Batching by
     default took grid-aligned seams from 17.0x chance to 0.0x.

  6. THE SURFACE WAS TORN DOWN ON EVERY SWAP. The backend retained one surface
     and the title uses three (measured: RECOMP_SURFACE_AUDIT reports 3
     distinct colour surfaces, with the named surface differing from the held
     one at 55% of flips). 12,448 readback-reallocate-re-upload round trips per
     run, about 18% of runtime. Now a swap back is a rebind.

Also fixed: nv2a_metal_discard dropped the retained surface without reading it
back and without being told which surface the guest was clearing (24,848 of
65536 pixels of finished rendering lost, default off); and the sink now asks
the shared blend accept test rather than its own enum map, so the two lists
cannot drift.


3. WHAT HAS BEEN ELIMINATED, AND WHY THAT IS SOLID
===================================================
  THE TEXTURE PATH, BY CONSTRUCTION. shade() -- texture fetch, mip LOD
  selection, register combiners -- is shared byte for byte between the two
  fragment tails, as are the Params it reads and the texture buffers it
  samples. A bug there would appear on the software path too, and the software
  path is clean at gameplay. This rules out every texture-shaped suspect
  without needing a run: wrong texels, mip selection, DXT decode, the texture
  cache.

  THE BLEND UNIT AND FRAGMENT ORDERING. RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=2 routes
  every blended draw through fs_hw_blend, which blends in-shader under
  raster_order_group(0) while keeping the real depth and stencil attachments.
  The speckle is unchanged.

  MISSING OR SILENTLY-IGNORED PIPELINE STAGES. Written out stage by stage:
  every stage is implemented or refused by name, and there is no third
  category. nv2a_texture_copy_prepare refuses about thirty states -- fog, logic
  op, colour write mask, texture address modes, texture filter and format,
  polygon offset, window clip, multisample. And the refusal path never fires
  for this title: prepared=750558 rejected=0, with 0 batches and 0 triangles on
  the CPU rasteriser.

  PER-DRAW TRANSLATION. metal_copy_test compares the backend against the
  rasteriser with an exact memcmp across combiners at one and two stages, alpha
  test, stencil with real ops, multi-texture, DXT1, DXT3, mip selection,
  untextured draws and dither. Both hardware arms match exactly.


4. WHAT IS LEFT
================
The real DEPTH attachment and the real STENCIL attachment, and whatever remains
of fs_hw's own behaviour (the z_cull branch, discard_fragment versus returning
the untouched destination).

The symptom agrees for the first time: the speckle is BLACK -- pixels where
nothing was written and the clear colour shows through. That is fragments being
rejected, which is the depth or stencil unit, not anything to do with colour.

RECOMP_METAL_HW_DEPTH_ALWAYS=1 and RECOMP_METAL_HW_NO_STENCIL=1 exist for
exactly this bisect. Both arms were started twice and killed twice by my own
runs competing for the binary. THEY HAVE NOT BEEN RUN TO A USABLE RESULT. That
is the next thing.

An earlier run of those two arms was reported as "still broken". That result is
VOID: it was scored with a black-pixel metric that was counting letterboxing
and intro art.


5. HOW TO MEASURE THIS, WHICH IS THE EXPENSIVE LESSON
======================================================
WHAT WORKS: comparing MATCHED SURFACES by eye. A flat wall on the hardware path
against a flat wall on the software path, magnified. It has separated the two
paths every time it has been used, in about a minute.

WHAT ALSO WORKS: a structural signature that scene content cannot have. The
tile metric in fb_score.py measures how many strong seams land on a grid
boundary against what chance would give, as a ratio inside one frame. That is
why it works where nothing else did: it needs no matched scene.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK, AND WAS TRIED SIX TIMES: any generic image statistic
compared across arms. speckle in three versions, temporal flicker, dark-blob
counting, black-pixel counting. All of them failed for ONE reason: the two
paths run at different speeds, a fixed pad schedule lands them in different
places, and a statistic over different pictures measures the pictures. Four of
them ranked the KNOWN-GOOD software path as the worst arm, which is the metric
telling you it is broken.

DETERMINISM DOES NOT SURVIVE FAR ENOUGH TO HELP. The two paths render the boot
logos bit-identically, but they diverge in TIMING within about ten seconds, and
from then on matched capture indices hold different moments. A promising idea
-- diff the deterministic intro -- produced 46 "identical" frames that turned
out to be a static logo on a flat background, and whole-frame differences as
soon as the sequence had any content in it. Do not spend time here again
without first solving the timing drift.

THE ARTEFACT IS LOAD-DEPENDENT. Device tests submit a few hundred draws and
read back immediately, so the GPU is never behind the producer.
metal_batch_test's own header says its first ring phase was "toothless" for
exactly that reason; the sentence is true of the whole file. A gate that cannot
get the GPU behind cannot see this class of defect. That is why every gate
passed for weeks on a renderer a person could see was wrong.


6. INSTRUMENTS BUILT TODAY
===========================
  fb_score.py          scores dumped frames. `tile` is validated and is the
                       metric that found the mosaic. `speckle`, `temporal` and
                       `specks` are NOT validated -- they detect their injected
                       artefacts in --selftest and do not measure the real one.
                       The file says so at the top; do not quote them.
  sample_window.sh     records the window at the display's frame rate and
                       extracts every frame. NOTE: macOS revoked Screen
                       Recording for the terminal mid-session and it then
                       captures black. RECOMP_FB_DUMP needs no permission.
  RECOMP_SURFACE_AUDIT counts, per clear and per flip, whether the surface the
                       guest names is the one the backend holds and whether
                       that one owes guest RAM unsaved rendering.
  RECOMP_METAL_HW_DEPTH_ALWAYS, RECOMP_METAL_HW_NO_STENCIL,
  RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=0/2, RECOMP_METAL_SURFACE_CACHE=0
                       bisect arms, each neutering one difference from the
                       software path. They render incorrectly by construction.
  recomp_switch.h      one predicate for opt-in switches, with a test. Ten
                       behavioural switches were presence-tested, so =0 turned
                       them ON -- RECOMP_PB_EXEC among them.


7. OPEN, RANKED
================
  1. RUN THE DEPTH AND STENCIL BISECT ARMS TO A RESULT. One run each, compared
     by magnified matched surface against the software path. This is the whole
     remaining search space.
  2. FRAME TIME IS UNVERIFIED. The 9.6% for the hardware path and the 14.5% for
     565 both predate batching, the dither fix's raster_order_group and the
     surface cache. An A/B of RECOMP_METAL_BATCH lost one arm to boot attrition
     and returned no comparison. Treat both figures as unverified, not wrong.
  3. THE DEFAULT FLIP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN WITH THE VARIABLE UNSET. Every clean
     capture passed RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=1 explicitly.
  4. metal_copy_test line 49 -- the software path's depth readback is now the
     only arm failing an exact comparison.
  5. A rejected draw is DROPPED, not CPU-rasterised (nv2a_pb_exec.c:2944), and
     is counted in neither gpu_fallbacks nor cpu_batches. JSRF never triggers
     it; a title using fog or a colour mask would lose geometry silently.
  6. The presenter reads s_snap while snapshot_surface() writes it, with no

8. A NOTE ON HOW THIS SESSION WENT
===================================
The useful findings came from a person watching the screen and saying what they
saw: that gameplay is worse than the intro, that characters and text are
unaffected while the world is not, that the black bars in the intro are graphic
elements, that the pattern looks granular, and that the window could be sampled
directly. Each of those redirected the search more than anything measured.

Against that, several claims in earlier notes were made before being checked
and had to be withdrawn: a 64-pixel alignment found by a search that only
looked at multiples of 64; a depth-precision mechanism that does not exist,
because both paths compare an interpolated value against the same CPU-computed
q/16777215; "the same class at finer granularity", from a magnified image whose
seam spacings are in fact irregular; "the granular noise is not a hardware-path
artefact", from a metric that ranked the known-good path worst; and a bit-exact

The rule that would have prevented all five: run the check before writing the
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_BUG_HUNT_2_THE_PAGE_TABLE_NOBODY_CHECKS.txt`:

```txt
BUG HUNT 2026-09-16 (night, second) -- THE APU'S PAGE TABLE HAS A BOUNDS
PARAMETER AND EVERY CALLER DEFEATS IT

Read-only hunt through the APU's memory path, prompted by 27,801 ADPCM decode
failures per 150 s that survived the refutation of the segment-stride theory
(see HANDOVER_..._NIGHT2..., section 1b). Three defects, one of them a strong
fit for those failures. Nothing fixed yet; each has its evidence.


=============================================================================
1. THE SCATTER-GATHER BOUNDS CHECK CANNOT FIRE
=============================================================================

    static hwaddr get_data_ptr(hwaddr sge_base, unsigned int max_sge,
                               uint32_t addr)
    {
        unsigned int entry = addr / TARGET_PAGE_SIZE;
        assert(entry <= max_sge);
        uint32_t prd_address =
            ldl_le_phys(address_space_memory, sge_base + entry * 4 * 2);
        return prd_address + addr % TARGET_PAGE_SIZE;
    }

The function takes a bound and asserts against it. ALL THREE call sites pass
0xFFFFFFFF:

    apu_vp.c:239   the descriptor dump
    apu_vp.c:3110  the ADPCM block fetch
    apu_vp.c:3188  the PCM sample fetch

so `entry <= 0xFFFFFFFF` is true for every possible entry and the assert is
dead code. A read past the end of the voice processor's page table therefore
loads whatever dword happens to sit at sge_base + entry*8, treats it as a
physical page address, and returns a pointer into it. There is no error, no
counter, and no way to tell the result from a valid translation.

The hardware does have the registers this parameter was meant to carry --
NV_PAPU_GPSMAXSGE, GPFMAXSGE, EPSMAXSGE, EPFMAXSGE (apu_regs.h:74-77) -- so
the bound is a real concept that this path declines to use.


=============================================================================
2. AND IT FITS THE ADPCM FAILURES, WHICH ARE STILL UNEXPLAINED
=============================================================================

What is measured about them:

    [APU-ADPCM-FAIL] first=0 last=1487 mid=26314
    last 8: v4 blk 161/170 hdr 08080808   (and 159/170, 160/170, 213/214)

    first=0   block 0 of a buffer NEVER fails
    hdr byte 3 is 0x08, and the decoder refuses any block whose fourth header
    byte is non-zero -- so this is ADPCM sample data being read as a header,
    i.e. we are looking at the wrong bytes, not at corrupt ones.

A 36-byte ADPCM block means 4096/36 = 113.8 blocks per 4 KB page. EVERY
observed failing block index is above 113 (159, 160, 161, 213) and block 0
always succeeds. That is what "the first page translates correctly and later
ones do not" looks like.

IT IS A FIT, NOT A PROOF, and two cheaper explanations have already died:
  - the segment descriptor's samples-per-block: MEASURED, no effect, and the
    scene has no streaming ADPCM voice at all.
  - samples_per_block > 1 making the block stride disagree with the fixed
    ADPCM_SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK=64 index: RULED OUT by g_apu_adpcm_oversize=0 in
    every archived run, which proves 36*spb <= 36*channels, so spb == 1 for
    the mono voices that are failing.

THE INSTRUMENT THAT DECIDES IT, and it is small: record, per failure, the
linear address, its page index (addr / TARGET_PAGE_SIZE), and the
prd_address the table returned for that page. Then read the FIRST failing
block index per voice. If failures begin at a page index and prd_address is
zero or implausible beyond it, this is the defect and the fix is to carry a
real bound and refuse rather than read. If failures are scattered across
pages with plausible prd_addresses, this dies too and the buffer itself is
being reused under us.

DO NOT "fix" the assert by passing a bound before taking that measurement:
an assert that starts firing in a player's build is a crash, and we do not
yet know whether the guest legitimately walks past the table.


=============================================================================
3. A STEREO SAMPLE THAT STRADDLES A PAGE READS ITS SECOND CHANNEL FROM THE
   WRONG ONE
=============================================================================

The PCM path (apu_vp.c:3184-3218) translates ONCE per sample and then walks
the channels on the translated PHYSICAL address:

    addr = get_data_ptr(..., ba + cbo * block_size);
    for (channel = 0; channel < channels; channel++) {
        ... read at addr ...
        addr += container_size;
    }

Physical contiguity is exactly what a scatter-gather table does not promise.
When a stereo sample's two channels fall either side of a 4 KB boundary, the
second channel is read from whatever physically follows the first page, which
is a different buffer.

The ADPCM path does NOT have this bug -- it re-translates per dword
(apu_vp.c:3110) -- which is the clearest evidence that per-read translation
is the intended discipline and this loop simply missed it.

LATENT AND UNMEASURED: it needs a stereo BUFFERED voice, and the voices
failing today are mono. Frequency is roughly one sample in 1024 for 16-bit
stereo, and only when the adjacent pages are not contiguous. Worth a counter
before a fix, for the same reason as section 1.


=============================================================================
4. A PERFORMANCE FINDING, NOT A CORRECTNESS ONE
=============================================================================

nv2a_metal.m's texture_buffer() confirms every cache HIT with a full memcmp
of the entire texture against the guest copy:

    if(entry->source==data && entry->size==size) {
        if(entry->buffer && !memcmp(entry->buffer.contents, data, size)) ...

Measured in a 130 s run: 537,605 requests, 534,232 hits -- i.e. half a
million whole-texture comparisons, O(texture bytes) each, on the thread the
guest is waiting on. The comparison is what makes the cache SAFE (it is why a
stale hit is impossible), so it cannot simply be deleted; but a cheap dirty
signal -- a hash kept per entry, or the executor's existing knowledge of
which guest ranges were written -- would remove most of them. Measure before
believing it matters: at 32 KB average this is ~1% of a core, at 256 KB it is
not.

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_BUG_HUNT_3_HALF_THE_FRAME_IS_SPENT_WAITING.txt`:

```txt
BUG HUNT 2026-09-16 (night, third) -- HALF THE FRAME IS SPENT WAITING FOR THE
GPU, AND THE PRESENTER REBUILT ITS TEXTURE SIXTY TIMES A SECOND

A hunt through the PRESENT path, which is goal G3's territory and had never
been reviewed. One fix landed, and one measurement that resizes G3 entirely.


=============================================================================
1. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS: 8.06 ms PER FRAME IN nv2a_metal_sync
=============================================================================

The instrument was already there. Nobody had divided it by the frame count.
From a 150 s gameplay run with everything on the GPU (render-investigation/
texq-1):

    [METAL] sync 24293 calls (8100 already clean):
            52751.3 ms draining the GPU, 12487.1 ms reading back and converting
    [FRAME] flips=8098 mean=16.05 ms (62.3 fps) p50=17.5 p99=40.5

    syncs per frame     3.00
    sync ms per frame   8.06   = 6.51 draining + 1.54 reading back
    frame mean          16.05 ms
    SHARE OF THE FRAME  50%

HALF THE FRAME IS A STALL. And the shape is not what the earlier handover
assumed: it described "the flip sync, 4.06-6.91 ms per frame, ONE CALL PER
FRAME". There are THREE syncs per frame, two thirds of them not the flip, and
the draining dominates the readback four to one. A mean drain of 3.26 ms per
real sync is the CPU waiting on waitUntilCompleted while the GPU finishes
work that was only just submitted.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT G3. The plan was "remove the flip's readback". That
addresses 1.54 ms of 8.06. The serialisation itself -- three full pipeline
drains per frame -- is the other 6.51, and the first question is no longer
"how do we present without a readback" but "WHY THREE, AND WHO CALLS THEM".
nv2a_metal_sync's callers need counting before anything is redesigned; the
instrument prints one total for all of them.

THE 8100 "already clean" CALLS ARE THE OTHER HALF OF THE STORY: a third of
syncs cost nothing because nothing was dirty. So two thirds of the calls do
real work, and whether the caller NEEDED the surface at that moment is a
question nothing in the log can currently answer.

Note the arithmetic against p50 rather than the mean: the median frame is
17.5 ms against a 16.68 ms budget, so the tail this has to fix is real, and
8 ms of stall is far more than the 0.8 ms the median is over by.


=============================================================================
2. FIXED: THE PRESENTER DESTROYED AND REBUILT ITS TEXTURE EVERY FRAME
=============================================================================

present_guest_framebuffer() called glTexImage2D once per Present,
unconditionally. That call does not upload into existing storage -- it
DESTROYS the texture's storage and creates it again, at a size that changes
essentially never. 640x480 RGBA is 1.2 MB of GPU storage torn down and rebuilt
sixty times a second, and a driver with the old storage still in flight must
orphan it or wait.

The discipline was already in the same function and applied to the CPU side:
the `rgba` staging buffer three lines above is reallocated only when the
dimensions change. The GPU side had no such guard because the size the texture
was allocated at was never recorded. It now is: glTexImage2D on a size change,
glTexSubImage2D otherwise, with counters on the [d3d8_gl] blit line so a run
says which path it took -- "I changed it" and "the change took" being
different claims.

Identical texels either way, so there is no arm to compare.


=============================================================================
3. NOT DONE: THE CPU CONVERTS 307,200 PIXELS A FRAME THAT THE GPU COULD EAT
   RAW
=============================================================================

fb_row_to_rgba expands the guest's RGB565 surface to RGBA8888 in scalar C,
per pixel, per frame -- 307,200 pixels at 640x480, and it also performs the
vertical flip while it is there.

GL can take the guest bytes DIRECTLY as GL_RGB / GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5.
That removes the conversion entirely and HALVES the upload (614 KB instead of
1.2 MB). The flip moves to the quad's texture coordinates, which is free.

WHY IT IS NOT DONE HERE: the colour expansion would move from this loop's
explicit bit-replication ((r << 3) | (r >> 2)) to the driver's, and those can
differ in the low bits. That is a PICTURE change, so it needs a switch and a
frame comparison, not a confident commit at the end of a long session. The
blit instrument is the natural verifier -- once its sample point is fixed,
which is item 1 of G3 and still outstanding.


=============================================================================
4. OPEN, RANKED, FOR G3
=============================================================================

 1. COUNT THE SYNC CALLERS. Three per frame, one instrument, no attribution.
    Everything below is guesswork until this exists.
 2. The per-frame sync HISTOGRAM the earlier handover asked for -- but now for
    all three syncs, not just the flip. Removing a stall moves the median only
    if the stall is on the median frame.
 3. Fix the blit check's sample point (expected bilinear blend, 1 LSB
    tolerance). It currently means "should be close", not "must be equal",
    and every later stage is verified with it.
 4. Then the direct 565 upload (section 3), then the surface-cache lookup of
    the flipped address, then the presenter itself.

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_BUG_HUNT_THE_VBLANK_THE_GUEST_NEVER_GOT.txt`:

```txt
BUG HUNT 2026-09-16 (night) -- I CLAIMED FOUR PER CENT OF THE SIMULATION WAS
DROPPED IN THE INTERRUPT PATH. IT IS NOT. READ SECTION 0 FIRST.

=============================================================================
0. THE RETRACTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE CLAIM SO NOBODY ACTS ON THE CLAIM
=============================================================================

Sections 1 and 3 below argue that 4.4% of vblank raises never reach the guest
and that recovering them is worth ~4% of game speed. I built the recovery
(RECOMP_IRQ_RETRY_PENDING) and measured it. THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED.

Scene-matched gameplay pair, 130 s each, held 82.5 s and 82.3 s:

                    off        on
    delivered Hz   55.4      101.0     <- hardware rate is 59.94
    raised         7694      7751
    delivered      7199     13131      <- EXCEEDS raised by 5,380
    frame mean    15.83     15.84 ms
    fps            63.2      63.1
    p99            39.0      39.5 ms

The guest's vblank ISR ran at 101 Hz against a 59.94 Hz hardware rate, and
the frame time did not move at all. So the deferred raises were never lost
work: xbox_Nv2aRaiseVblank() has ALREADY asserted the PCRTC source by the
time the delivery is refused, and the ISR that is still running sees and
acknowledges it. Re-delivering afterwards hands the guest a SECOND tick for
one assertion. The switch does not recover a missed step, it manufactures an
extra one -- which would run the game FAST, and burns CPU for nothing.

WHICH MEANS delivered= WAS NEVER A MEASURE OF SIMULATION STEPS. It counts ISR
ENTRIES, and one entry can service more than one assertion. "delivered <
raised" is therefore not evidence of lost work, and section 1's whole
arithmetic -- 446 raises lost, 95.8% game speed -- rests on reading it as if
it were. Do not repeat that reading.

AND THE 5% THAT LOOKED LIKE A WIN WAS NOISE. The first A/B of this switch
showed 59.4 fps off against 62.4 on, which I nearly reported as a result. The
second pair's OFF arm read 63.2 fps. One run per arm cannot see a 5% effect
on this host; two arms of one run each is what this project's own rules call
a lean, not a measurement.

RECOMP_IRQ_RETRY_PENDING stays in the tree at default OFF with this table
beside it, because the mechanism is sound and cheap and the next person will
otherwise re-derive it from the same false premise. Turning it on is a
correctness regression, not a speed fix.

WHAT SURVIVES from the hunt below: section 2 is still true and still worth
fixing (g_vector_pending has no production reader, so its "Pending, not
dropped" comment is false). Section 4 is a verified negative worth keeping.
Section 5's instrument gap is real, and I then added a seventh instrument of
my own that lied -- see section 6.

=============================================================================
6. AND I BUILT ONE THAT LIED, IN THE HOUR I WROTE UP TWO OTHERS
=============================================================================

The first measurement of this switch printed "retry_queued=5862
retry_delivered=5862" beside a delivered= that had not moved: 55.7 Hz against
56.0. I read the frame rate rising 5% in the same pair and reached for an
explanation -- the retries are reaching the guest, the counter cannot see
them -- which was TRUE about the counter (g_vblank_delivered is incremented
only at bridge_vblank_poll's own call site) and WRONG about the conclusion.
Fixing the counter is what produced the 101 Hz that refuted the whole thing.

The lesson is not "fix the counter". It is that I had a number that did not
fit, and my first move was to find a reason the number was wrong rather than
a reason the hypothesis was. The counter WAS wrong. The hypothesis was too.

A read-only hunt through the SPEED path (goal G3), which no review had
touched. Two verified defects, one instrument gap, and one assumption checked
and found SOUND. Nothing here is fixed yet; each has its evidence and its
shape.

THE PLAYER'S TARGET: "We want to hit 60fps and for the player to move at the
correct speed." On this title those are one number, and this hunt found a
second, INDEPENDENT four per cent that has nothing to do with frame time.


=============================================================================
1. A VBLANK THAT ARRIVES WHILE ITS OWN ISR IS RUNNING IS DROPPED FOREVER
=============================================================================

MEASURED, player session 16 Sep 2026:

    [VBLANK] delivered=9724 (raised=10170 retried=9) over 170097 ms
             = 57.2 Hz (target 59) deadlines=10190 unacked_skips=12
             max_gap=35 ms not_ready=0

    deadlines   59.75/s   -- the SCHEDULE is very nearly right
    delivered   57.20/s   -- what the guest's ISR actually ran
    lost        446 raises, 4.4%

The guest advances its simulation one step per vblank event (its vsync pump
waits on the event D3D's own ISR signals), so 4.4% of raises never reaching
guest code is 4.4% of simulation steps that never happen: ~95.8% game speed
BEFORE any frame-time effect is counted. That is on top of the frame-locked
loss the earlier handovers describe, not part of it.

WHERE THEY GO. bridge_irq_decide returns XBOX_IRQ_DEFER_VECTOR when the same
vector is already in service anywhere in the process, and
bridge_deliver_isr_ex then returns 0. defer_irql and defer_reentry are both
measured ZERO in that session and not_ready is 0, so essentially all 446 are
this one branch: a vblank raised while the previous vblank ISR had not yet
returned. [IRQ] reports deferred vector=7978 across all vectors, which is
where they are counted -- but not on the line a reader checks.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT HARDWARE BEHAVIOUR: on the real machine the PCRTC
interrupt stays ASSERTED until the driver acknowledges it at the source. It
does not evaporate because the CPU is busy in the previous handler; it is
taken when the handler returns. This model drops it.


=============================================================================
2. "PENDING, NOT DROPPED" IS FALSE -- NOTHING EVER RE-DELIVERS
=============================================================================

The IRQL branch of the same function reads:

    /* Pending, not dropped. The pumps revisit every connected vector on a
     * timer, so this is retried within one period once IRQL drops. */
    InterlockedExchange(&g_vector_pending[slot], 1);

g_vector_pending has EXACTLY these uses in the whole tree:
    3094  set here
    3096  counted, for a peak statistic
    3134  cleared after a successful delivery
    3169  read by xbox_IrqTestPending  -- a TEST accessor
    3191  counted in xbox_ReportIrqDelivery
    3183  cleared by xbox_IrqTestReset -- a TEST hook

There is no production reader. Nothing re-runs the deferred interrupt. What
the comment calls a retry is only the NEXT period raising its own, separate
vblank -- which is a different simulation step, not a recovery of the missed
one. The flag is decoration and the comment asserts a mechanism that does not
exist.

It happens not to cost anything today because defer_irql measures 0 in
gameplay. It is still a false comment guarding a real hole, and it is the
reason the DEFER_VECTOR branch above was written to just drop: the author
believed one of these branches queued.


=============================================================================
3. THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS BOUNDED
=============================================================================

Give the vector deferral what the IRQL branch pretends to have, and give the
pending flag a production consumer: on a deferral, set pending; when an ISR
completes and clears in_service, re-deliver any vector whose pending bit is
set. The flag is ONE BIT per vector, so a storm coalesces into a single
retry -- it cannot burst, which is the failure mode the vblank scheduler's
own comment (BRIDGE_VBLANK_PERIOD_US, "a title that misses a frame should see
one late vblank, not five at once") is written to avoid.

Behind RECOMP_IRQ_RETRY_PENDING, default off until measured, with the arms
scored on [VBLANK] delivered/elapsed against 59.94 and on [FRAME]. The
prediction is sharp and falsifiable: delivered should move from 57.2 Hz
toward 59.75 (the deadline rate), and the game should get ~4% faster with NO
change in frame time. If delivered rises and the frame rate does not, the
guest was never the bottleneck and this is not where the speed went.


=============================================================================
4. AN ASSUMPTION CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND
=============================================================================

bridge_irq_decide's recursion guard is documented "only for THIS thread".
g_dispatch_depth is declared RECOMP_TLS, so it genuinely is per-thread and a
long ISR on one thread cannot block delivery on another. Checked because a
plain static there would have produced dropped interrupts with exactly the
signature above. It is correct; do not re-examine it.


=============================================================================
5. THE INSTRUMENT GAP
=============================================================================

[VBLANK] prints delivered, raised, deadlines, unacked_skips and not_ready.
In the session above those name 12 of the 446 missing deliveries. The other
434 are only visible by opening [IRQ] and knowing that its cross-vector
"deferred vector=" total includes the NV2A. Print the per-vector deferral on
the [VBLANK] line, so "raised minus delivered" is always accounted for where
it is read. This is the same class as every instrument this project has had
to retire: a number that looks complete and is not.

```
