```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 (fifth of the day) -- THE FENCES, THE SOUND, THE EFFECTS
AND THE SPEED: WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT

Read CLAUDE.md first. This supersedes every earlier handover of 16 Sep where it
contradicts them, and it contradicts them in a lot of places -- including
conclusions I published today with confidence and had to retract by evening.

This is written to be the document that permanently closes four player-visible
complaints: DISAPPEARING FENCES, BROKEN MUSIC, NO SOUND EFFECTS, and SPEED.


=============================================================================
0. THE ONE PARAGRAPH VERSION
=============================================================================

Fences: FIXED, by the vertex-shader dot-product zero rule
(RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO). Confirmed twice, once by a player and once by a natural
experiment. Make it the default.

Music breaking up: the idle-voice trap was level-triggered where the hardware's
is an edge. RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_EDGE takes trapped subframes from 46.7% to
0.59%. Measured, scene-matched, both arms in gameplay. Make it the default.

Sound effects: FOUND, and it is not what four separate investigations thought.
Effects are the 3D positional voices; every one of them had its mixbin routing
overwritten with an HRTF submix, and the DSP reads two of thirty-two bins. 3D
heard=0, lost=375,382 in one run, against 2D heard=380,614 lost=0. One line
gates it.

Speed: fixed-function T&L now runs on the GPU. CPU vertex shading goes to ZERO,
the frame goes 23.53 ms -> 17.31 ms. The next and largest item is the flip sync
(4-9 ms/frame), which is designed and staged but not implemented.


=============================================================================
1. THE FENCES -- FIXED, AND HOW IT WAS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED
=============================================================================

CAUSE: mac_eval computed DP3/DP4/DPH with a plain multiply, while multiply() --
which implements the NV2A rule that a*0 is +0 even when the other operand is
inf -- was reached only by MUL and MAD. RSQ(0) is +inf by design, so through a
dot product it becomes NaN. Dot products build this title's texture
coordinates: 1,889 DP3/DP4 across the 126 vertex programs, 598 reaching a
texcoord. A NaN texcoord leaves the POSITION finite, so the triangle is
assembled, submitted and drawn, and then samples garbage. On an opaque surface
that is a wrong colour nobody reports. On an ALPHA-CUTOUT texture -- a wire
fence -- every fragment fails the alpha test and the object disappears.
Transparency is what turns "slightly wrong" into "gone", which is why fences
are what the player notices.

EVIDENCE: 13 mismatches -> 0 against the title's own 126 programs in the GPU
diff test, worst error 4.29e-4 -> 6.35e-6, no measurable frame cost (57.3 ->
58.6 fps). The player confirmed the fix on their own build. Then the decisive
one, which nobody designed: the player watched a SCRIPTED run's window and said
"the fence issue is back" -- and that run's log read `[VSH] (vsh_dp_zero OFF)`
while their own working session read `vsh_dp_zero on`. Same engine, same scene
type, one switch, symptom present and absent accordingly.

ACTION: make RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO default ON. It is a correctness fix with a
measured result and a human confirmation, and it is currently a switch only
because it was landed cautiously.

DO NOT re-open these, all measured out today: batch truncation (no-room=0
against a 9,681-index batch), INLINE_ARRAY truncation (12 words of 16,384),
DRAW_ARRAYS volume (0.01% of per-frame indices), alpha-test and blend
refusals (0 in gameplay runs two days apart), the texture cache (a hit
requires a full memcmp), mip base arithmetic / levels clamp / filter selection
(correct across all three implementations), the viewport scale (D3D bakes it
into the composite matrix -- "fixing" it would multiply the screen by 320
twice), the all-zero texture matrix (its enable is off), and float32
cancellation in area() (measured: rescues exactly 0 triangles).


=============================================================================
2. THE SOUND EFFECTS -- FOUND, AND FOUR INVESTIGATIONS WERE WRONG FIRST
=============================================================================

THE ANSWER: voices 0-63 are the 3D positional voices, i.e. the effects. Every
one of them had bin[0..3] overwritten with d->vp.hrtf_submix[] -- unconditional
-- while .hrtf is false and no HRTF runs. mcpx_apu_dsp_frame then reads
mixbins[0] and mixbins[1] and discards the other thirty, because the GP and EP
are stubs. So effects are generated correctly and mixed into bins nothing
reads.

    [APU-BIN] 2D heard=380614 lost=0 | 3D heard=0 lost=375382
              hrtf_submix=6,8,7,9 | lost by bin: 6:115742 7:115742
                                                 8:14054 9:14054 10:115790

2D heard=380,614 lost=0 is the positive control: music is audible, so that
number MUST move, and it does. 3D heard=0 lost=375,382 is the defect.

WHY IT TOOK ALL DAY. dbg->bin[i] is written in voice_process and read by
NOTHING -- grep returns one hit. No counter, log line or document in the tree
ever recorded which mixbin a voice landed in. Thirty of thirty-two bins were
discarded every frame in complete silence, so every instrument upstream read
healthy while the player heard nothing.

AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT SENT THREE INVESTIGATIONS THE WRONG WAY WAS ADDED
TODAY, BY ME. [APU-SE] prints `oneshot = on_count - on_loop_count` and asserts
"no one-shot voice started while the engine kept running: SE silence, not a
stopped APU". JSRF sets CFG_FMT.LOOP on every voice it starts -- 57 of 57
descriptor dumps read loop=1, and on == on_loop in all 251 report windows
across 15 logs -- so that quantity is IDENTICALLY ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION. It
never measured effects. Effects were starting the whole time: 348 and 366
voice starts in the long runs. RETIRE IT or give it a positive control; the
discriminator that actually tracks BGM vs effects in this title is the 2D/3D
split on v < 64.

ACTION: the gate is in the tree (RECOMP_APU_HRTF_BINS, default 0 = do not
apply the override, restoring the guest's own V0BIN..V3BIN). Verify with
[APU-BIN]: 3D heard must become non-zero with 2D heard still moving. If the
guest's own routing also points above bin 1, the remaining work is to widen
mcpx_apu_dsp_frame's mixdown to sum the routed bins -- about 20 lines, inside
the existing signature, because it already receives float mixbins[32][...].

A REAL GP/EP IS NOT NEEDED FOR THIS TITLE. JSRF issues gp=7 ep=8 writes
against vp=249,688 -- initialisation only, no command stream. Interpreting a
DSP56300 is ~3,000 lines and would buy nothing here.


=============================================================================
3. THE MUSIC -- THE TRAP WAS A LEVEL WHERE THE HARDWARE HAS AN EDGE
=============================================================================

SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE reports a voice TRANSITIONING to inactive. This model raised
it on the standing condition. The guest's DirectSound ISR has three early
returns that all leave a voice inactive and still linked -- including PERSIST,
a documented feature this model implements the same way -- so against a level
trap it loops at 1500 Hz with the driver behaving exactly as written. 89% of
raises in the player's own session named the same voice as the previous raise.

MEASURED, two 340 s scene-matched arms with a LIVE audio device, both in the
gameplay band:

    off  raises=23481  trapped=231245/495072 = 46.7%  on=348 off=343
    on   raises=305    trapped=2902/495184  =  0.59%  on=366 off=366
         edge_suppressed=1105858  rearm=289

rearm is the control that matters: suppressed climbing with rearm stuck at 0
would mean the latch shut instead of cycling. It cycled 289 times.

ACTION: make RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_EDGE default ON.

A CLAIM I MADE AND HAVE TO WITHDRAW: I reported a crossover where the front
end passes ~56% trapped and the output queue starves permanently. That does
not survive. `trapped=` is a CUMULATIVE ratio -- the same trap
ACCURACY_GAPS.md already flags -- and the one badly-starving run in the
archive (a1-exec-walkers-tutorial-1) has trapped=0 throughout. Neither 340 s
arm starved at all. The storm is real and worth removing; the starvation
correlation was an artefact of reading a cumulative counter as instantaneous.


=============================================================================
4. THE SPEED
=============================================================================

DONE: fixed-function T&L on the GPU (RECOMP_METAL_FF). 62.8% of index slots --
520 million of 829 million in one run -- were transformed on the CPU because
only programmable-shader draws were GPU-shaded.

    off  vsh draws 345065 GPU / 458142 CPU   vsh=5.17 submit=5.35 | 23.53 ms
    on   vsh draws 783829 GPU /      0 CPU   vsh=1.60 submit=3.39 | 17.31 ms
         438075 batches accepted, 0 left on the CPU
         mean 58.6 -> 61.8 fps, p99 42.5 -> 39.5 ms

CPU vertex shading is ELIMINATED. 6.2 ms off the frame, four times the
predicted win, because submit dropped too once the per-triangle CPU work
stopped. Gated by jsrf_ff_msl_diff_test: residual 0 over 15 states in both
modes, injected fault firing in every one, accept-parity clean, anchored to a
value measured from a real run. DO NOT ENABLE RECOMP_METAL_FF FOR A BUILD
WHOSE TEST HAS NOT PASSED.

CAVEATS: max frame went 72.4 -> 286.7 ms (almost certainly the one-time
shader compile) and over-33ms rose slightly. Take a second run before calling
p99 improved. And that A/B ran WITHOUT RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO, so it needs
re-scoring against a config that matches the player's build (see section 6).

NEXT AND LARGEST: the flip sync, 4.06-6.91 ms per frame, one call per frame,
~70% of all sync cost despite being a third of the calls. The frame is
serialised into submit -> stall the whole GPU -> read 614 KB back -> convert
-> present, and it exists only because the presenter is OpenGL and reads the
guest framebuffer out of guest RAM.

THE NAIVE FIX IS DEAD AND THE CENSUS THAT KILLED IT IS WORTH KNOWING: the live
Metal surface is NEVER the surface being flipped. Zero times, in two
independent gameplay runs ([SURFACE-AUDIT], three counts that sum exactly). So
"just present the Metal texture" would present the wrong surface on every
frame. The design must look the FLIPPED address up in the surface cache.

Staged design and patches for stages 0-2 exist. Stage 0 (the blit instrument)
must land first because every later stage is verified with it.

A CAVEAT ON THE PAYOFF: removing waitUntilCompleted removes the
SERIALISATION, not the GPU work. Nothing in the tree records the flip sync's
per-frame DISTRIBUTION, so it may move p50 and leave the p99 tail untouched. A
per-frame sync histogram should precede the presenter change.


=============================================================================
5. PLAYER SPEED / "JUMPING AND FLOATING" -- UNRESOLVED, AND A LEAD
=============================================================================

The player reports the character jumping or floating. NOT DIAGNOSED. The
leading candidate is the same dot-product defect as the fences: DP4 is what
transforms POSITION, and a corrupted dot product hits position and texcoords
alike. If RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO is defaulted on and the floating persists, that
hypothesis is dead and the next place to look is the fixed-function transform
chain -- but note the composite matrix already carries the viewport scale, so
do not "fix" that (section 1).

A SECOND OBSERVATION, AND A RETRACTION OF IT IN THE SAME BREATH. I reported
that 161,586-260,714 triangles a run are dropped on screen for having exactly
zero area, and ranked splitting that bucket as open item 1. THAT FIGURE IS AN
ARTEFACT OF A NON-DEFAULT ARM. Both runs it came from set
RECOMP_METAL_VSH=0, and on the GPU vertex path -- the default, and the
player's build -- triangle() returns before area() is ever reached
(nv2a_metal.m:3008-3009), so the counter only counts in the arm that has the
rejection. Scene- and switch-matched on the DEFAULT path:

    dp_off_1  collinear-distinct=162, of which 12 were on screen
    dp_on_1   collinear-distinct=846, of which  9 were on screen

Nine to twelve triangles a run, not a quarter of a million. This is CLAUDE.md's
`N triangles fully off-surface` failure recurring on a different counter: a
rejection counted only where the rejection happens. Do not spend a run on it.
The area_rescued=0 negative is still correct for the CPU path and the counter
is worth keeping; the framing was wrong.


=============================================================================
6. THE METHODOLOGICAL FAILURE THAT COST THE MOST, AND THE FIX
=============================================================================

THE HARNESS AND THE PLAYER'S BUILD WERE DIFFERENT SOFTWARE ALL DAY.

The player's app reads ~/Library/Application Support/JSRF/paths.conf, which
exports four switches. play_scripted.sh sets NONE of them unless the caller
remembers. So scripted runs contained bugs the player's build did not, and
lacked fixes it had. This is how the fence fix was nearly missed: most A/Bs ran
with RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO absent, i.e. with the fence bug present, while the
player's build had it fixed.

It was caught only because the player watched a scripted run's window and
said the symptom was back. That is not a repeatable way to find configuration
drift.

AN AUDIT OF EVERY CONCLUSION FROM TODAY HAS NOW BEEN DONE. The vblank A/B, the
voice-list ring A/B, the idle-trap A/B and the no-room figure are all SAFE --
arms verified to differ in exactly one token, both in a mission, held within a
second of each other. Two are not:

  - THE ALPHA-TEST ARM IS UNVERIFIABLE. RECOMP_METAL_NO_ALPHA_TEST prints no
    state, so which arm ran cannot be recovered from the log, and three of its
    four runs sat in the attract loop anyway. Give it a state print per
    recomp_switch.h's own rule before using it again.
  - THE DP_ZERO MATCHED PAIR EXISTS AND I SAID IT DID NOT. dp_off_1 and
    dp_on_1 differ in that token and nothing else across 20 tokens, both scene
    30, held 98.6 and 98.4 s. I wrote "the scripted A/B could not produce a
    matched scene" and left a clean pair unscored.

AND THE `on=` BAND IN CLAUDE.md IS DURATION-DEPENDENT. `on=` is cumulative, so
a perfectly healthy 149 s run reads 81-125 and falls in neither the 148-453
"gameplay" band nor the 4-12 "parked" one. Eight healthy arms today would have
been voided by that rule. The reliable scene gate is the sequence state plus
`held=`; `on=` is a voice-churn control and its band needs a run length
attached.

ACTION: make the harness's switch set EXPLICIT and REPORTED, and make any
difference from paths.conf visible in the run's own log. Do not silently adopt
the player's config -- an A/B must be able to differ deliberately -- the
requirement is that a difference is never silent. Every conclusion from today
should be re-checked for whether its arms had matching switch sets.


=============================================================================
7. INSTRUMENTS THAT LIE -- SIX FOUND TODAY, ONE OF THEM MINE
=============================================================================

  no-room=            no term for the INLINE_ARRAY path; quoted all day as
                      "nothing is dropped" while covering 2 of 3 paths
  texcoord-q=         fires for non-finite OR q<=0, and q<=0 is arithmetically
                      impossible for 123 of 126 programs
  fedec_hold          printed "on (default)" while defaulting to 0
  g_pcrtc_windows     read 0 while the trap handler opened a window 60x/s
  resident clears     counted one of two GPU paths, with the cost of the gap
                      attached to it
  [APU-SE] oneshot    a subtraction that is identically zero by construction.
                      ADDED TODAY, BY ME, AND QUOTED AS A FINDING.

Already in CLAUDE.md's known-bad list: `N triangles fully off-surface` is dead
on every Metal run.

AND ONE I BROKE: the [d3d8_gl] blit line no longer holds its exact-match
property. It compares a guest pixel against the drawable centre and matched
only while the drawable was an exact 1x the guest. It is now 4x on a 2x panel,
where texel centres land on pixel boundaries, so NO choice of sample point can
restore equality -- the fix is to compute the expected bilinear blend and
compare with a 1 LSB tolerance. Stage 0 of the presenter work does this. Until
then that line means "should be close", not "must be equal".


=============================================================================
8. THE V2 QUESTION -- ANSWERED: DO NOT REWRITE
=============================================================================

Our APU is 8,128 lines against upstream's 4,196. The voice processor is 3,963
against 1,247, so 68% of it is ours -- and I used that to argue the bugs were
ours. THAT WAS BACKWARDS. Checked defect by defect against merge-base 051a128,
every UNFIXED defect is inherited verbatim: the ADPCM stack smash, the ignored
return value, the VOICE_ON race, the dead segment fields, the HRTF submix
override, the GP/EP stub. The only defect that was ours is the voice-list ring,
and it is fixed.

And the +2,716 is not accretion: 55.5% is comment, most of the rest is
instrumentation, and actual behaviour change is about 272 lines across three
functions, each behind an A/B lever.

The missing capability is a wider MIXDOWN, not a different shape -- about 20
lines inside an existing signature. A rewrite would discard unusually good
instrumentation and reach no current bug.

THE ONE FINDING THAT WOULD JUSTIFY A REWRITE, stated so it can be tested: if
the VOICE_ON / frame-thread race survives widening the device lock over the
VOICE_ON body, then guest RAM is the wrong home for the voice register file
and the voice processor needs the shadow this tree deliberately avoided.


=============================================================================
9. OPEN, RANKED
=============================================================================

 1. Verify the HRTF bin gate restores effect audio ([APU-BIN] 3D heard > 0
    with 2D heard still moving), then widen the mixdown if the guest's own
    routing also lands above bin 1. Section 2.
 2. Default RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO and RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_EDGE. Both are
    evidence-complete. Sections 1 and 3.
 3. Make the harness report its switch set and diff it against paths.conf, and
    re-score today's A/Bs for matched arms. Section 6.
 4. The player's floating/jumping. Section 5. The leading candidate is the
    same dot-product defect as the fences, since DP4 transforms position.
 5. The flip sync: stage 0 (blit instrument), then the census, then the
    presenter. Section 4.
 6. Retire or fix [APU-SE]; add a positive control. Section 7.
 7. ADPCM: 19,465-108,074 decode failures a run emitting stack memory as audio
    at full scale. Counters are in, the repair is behind
    RECOMP_APU_ADPCM_GUARD. The stack smash is clamped unconditionally and is
    measured LATENT (oversize=0 everywhere).
 8. Widen the device lock over the VOICE_ON body -- and if the race survives,
    see section 8.
```

```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 (night, second) -- THE RE-RAISE WORKS, THE GLYPH IS RARE
AND TIMING-DEPENDENT, AND A REVIEW FOUND EIGHT MORE

Read CLAUDE.md, then docs/jsrf/goals/JSRF_GOALS_2026-09-16_EVERYTHING_ON_THE_GPU.md
(the active goal list), then the three earlier 16 Sep handovers. This one
supersedes HANDOVER_2026-09-16_NIGHT_THE_LATCH_THE_GLYPHS_AND_EVERYTHING_ON_THE_GPU
where they differ: that one proposed the bounded re-raise, this one measures it.

THE PLAYER'S TARGET, IN THEIR WORDS: "I want everything on the gpu", and
"We want to hit 60fps and for the player to move at the correct speed".
On this title those are one number -- a late vblank drops its period, so game
speed = 16.683 ms / mean frame.

1. THE MUSIC AND THE EFFECTS -- FIXED, AND THE FIX IS IN THE REARM CONDITION
=============================================================================

Neither trap arm was ever right. Level: the guest is told 1500x/s and the
music breaks up. Edge: it is told once, and if that once lands while its ISR
takes an early return the voice is never reclaimed, the free list empties, and

THE EVIDENCE FOR THE STEAL, from the player's 16:22 session (edge, no re-raise):
    [APU-BIN] 2D heard froze at 29597 twenty seconds in; 3D kept climbing
    [APU-IDLE-EDGE] edge_suppressed=1010411 rearm=51
    [APU-VOICE] on=98 off=94 off_commands=94   <- EVERY retirement was a guest

The edge latch stands, and a voice still inactive-and-linked one guest tick

    edge + re-raise    trapped 3.6%   raises 1467    2D heard 203741

1b. AND THEN THE PLAYER'S 18:33 SESSION FROZE 2D HEARD ANYWAY
=============================================================================

The player played the re-raise build (bundle 17:19, metal_ff on, idle_edge on,
detectors on) for ~170 s. The re-raise MECHANISM worked: reraise=6219,
rearm=136, [APU-POOL] on_active=0 -- no voice theft, the latch cycling. And
yet:

    window   2D heard    3D heard   cycles  selflink-term  trapped
      8        95324       36446       0           0          321
      9        95324       36446       0           0         1271   <- 2D stops
     22        95324      301950      44       65115        18502
     33        95324      614294      44      138045        26186

2D heard froze at window 9 and never moved again; 3D climbed to 614,294.

WHAT THIS RULES OUT, AND IT RULES OUT MY OWN TWO FAVOURITE ANSWERS:
  - NOT the voice-list cycle. walks_with_a_cycle stays 0 until window 22,
    THIRTEEN windows after the freeze.
  - NOT the self-link guard cutting the tail off. terminated= is 0 until
    window 13, four windows after.
  - NOT voice theft. on_active=0 for the whole run.
  - NOT starvation. starved=0, min_queued 6144 bytes throughout.
  - NOT the ADX music thread. [ADX] ticked to 11,485, flag=0, never stuck.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT, AND THIS IS THE OPEN QUESTION: whether the player
could HEAR music in that session. 2D heard counts subframes in which a 2D
voice produced a non-zero amplitude. It reads zero both when we have lost the
music and when the GUEST is not playing any -- a menu, a cutscene, a stretch
of the game with no BGM. Nothing in the log distinguishes those, and neither
do I. ASK THE PLAYER BEFORE INVESTIGATING FURTHER; if they heard music
throughout, this table is a scene, not a defect, and [APU-BIN] needs a
positive control that says "the guest asked for a 2D voice and we dropped it"
rather than "no 2D voice made a sound".

ONE REAL SIGNAL IN THE SAME LOG, INDEPENDENT OF THAT QUESTION: voice 1 raised
4,063 of the run's 6,369 idle traps, every one of the last sixteen flagged
[RC] (repeat + in-a-cycle). The re-raise is bounded per voice, so this is not
the old storm, but one 3D voice absorbing two thirds of all raises is a defect
in its own right and it is cheap to chase: the ring already names it.

ALSO IN THAT LOG, AND IT IS A REAL BUG -- BUT NOT THE ONE I FIRST NAMED.
[APU-ADPCM-FAIL] shows the SAME block
refused over and over -- "v11 blk 213/214 hdr 08080808", eight identical
entries in the ring. Header byte 3 is 0x08, and the decoder refuses any block
whose fourth header byte is non-zero, so we are reading ADPCM SAMPLE data as
a block header: a misalignment, not a corrupt stream. 44,775 of the failures
are middle blocks, 1,116 last blocks, ZERO first blocks -- a first block that
always decodes and later ones that do not is what a wrong block STRIDE looks
like. block_size for ADPCM is set to 36*samples_per_block, and the guest's segment
descriptor carries its own samples-per-block (seg_spb) which this model
decoded and then never read -- so I built RECOMP_APU_SEGMENT_SPB to use it.

THAT WAS WRONG AND THE A/B SAYS SO. Scene-matched gameplay pair:
    off  ok=697869 fail=27801  (3.83%)
    on   ok=584716 fail=25224  (4.13%)
No effect, and [APU-ADPCM-SPB] printed in NEITHER arm -- g_adpcm_spb_voice
was zero, so this scene contains no streaming ADPCM voice and the switch
could not have done anything. The failing voices are NON-STREAM ("v4 blk
161/170", no S flag in the ring), and a non-stream voice never consults a
segment descriptor. The switch is left in the tree at default OFF with that
table beside it, because for a scene that DOES stream ADPCM it is an
unmeasured behaviour change and default-on would ship an argument.

SO THE ADPCM DEFECT IS OPEN, and what is established about it is worth more
than the guess was: first=0 in every sample -- block 0 of a buffer ALWAYS
decodes -- while middle blocks fail 26,314 times and last blocks 1,487. A
first block that is always right and later ones that are not is a STRIDE or
BASE error, and the stride for a non-stream voice is
ba + block_index * (36 * samples_per_block) against an index computed as
cbo / ADPCM_SAMPLES_PER_BLOCK, where that constant is 64 and carries a FIXME
in apu_regs.h asking whether it should be 65. Read samples_per_block for the
failing voice first; nothing prints it yet. 27,801 failures in 150 s, each
emitting uninitialised stack as audio at full scale.


=============================================================================
2. THE GLYPHS -- REPRODUCED ONCE, THEN NOT IN ~4,800 FRAMES
=============================================================================

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:

  - It is REAL and it is the GPU fixed-function path. frame-bisect ffglyph2,
    tutorial scene, 24 captures per arm: ff-on/fb/flip013.bmp has two quote
    glyphs relocated onto the "C" of "Corn"; ff-off never does, in any frame.
    1 frame in 24 captures.
  - It is not the vertex DATA. [FF-WATCH] hashes every vertex of every batch
    drawn from the tutorial font page (tex 01737000) and reports the first
    vertex that differs between two draws of the same shape. Over a full run
    in both arms: ZERO changes. What the CPU fetched was identical every time.
  - It is not reproducible on demand. [FB-WATCH] compares the speech-bubble
    text region of the PRESENTED copy at every flip against the previous
    flip. In the parked tutorial, both arms: zero changes after the text
    settles, across ~2,400 flips each. The defect did not recur.

So it is TIMING-DEPENDENT, downstream of the fetch, and rare. The candidates
that survive, in order:

  a. THE RING -- AND A CLAIM I HAD TO WITHDRAW WITHIN THE HOUR. I wrote that
     the two arms stage different-sized vertex rows, so only one is exposed
     to a wrap bug. THAT IS FALSE AND THE ARITHMETIC IS TWO LINES: the FF key
     reads attributes 0x1E19, which is 7 attributes, 7*16 = 112 bytes, and
     the CPU path's `struct Vertex { float4 p,d0,d1,t0,t1,t2,t3; }` is also
     112 bytes. The rows are the SAME SIZE unless a normal is read (8 attrs,
     128 B), and the measured staging bears it out: 309,312 allocated vertex
     batches on ff-on against 306,985 on ff-off, 0.8% apart. So the ring
     wraps at the same rate in both arms and is a WEAK candidate, not the
     first thing to do. RECOMP_METAL_RING_AUDIT still prints
     reserves/wraps/waits/fallbacks and the pair is cheap to take, but do not
     expect it to separate the arms.
  b. THE SINK'S SKIPPED PER-VERTEX TEST, which is now the strongest candidate
     and is written up in section 3 as the review finding left unfixed. On
     every GPU vertex path triangle() returns before vertex_valid(), so a
     texcoord with q<=0 or a non-finite output is DRAWN where the CPU arm
     drops the triangle, and the fragment then computes uv = tc.xy/tc.w.
     That is a per-vertex divergence between the arms, it is timing-
     independent in principle but data-dependent in practice, and it fits
     "two quads sample from the wrong place" better than anything else here.
     Test it without changing the renderer: count, on the GPU FF path, the
     vertices whose q would fail, using the pass-through case (texmat off,
     which is 87% of batches) where oT is just the fetched attribute.
  c. The texture-buffer cache (128 entries, keyed on source POINTER and size,
     confirmed with a full memcmp on hit). A stale hit is impossible because
     of the memcmp; an eviction under a live command buffer is not, but the
     command buffers retain their references (no
     commandBufferWithUnretainedReferences anywhere in the file), so this is
     probably safe. Audit only if b fails.
  d. Something in the guest's own draw order that only the GPU path's timing
     exposes. Least likely, hardest to test, leave it last.

TWO DETECTORS ARE NOW IN THE PLAYER'S BUILD, because their session is the only
environment that has reproduced this twice:
    RECOMP_FB_WATCH=100,55,400,60      small per-flip changes in the text
    RECOMP_FF_BATCH_WATCH_TEX=01737000 vertex data changes for the font page
FB_WATCH prints only SMALL changes (< 1/4 of the region) and counts the rest,
so it is safe in a gameplay log. If the player sees the glitch, last-run.log
now says whether the data or the timing moved. COPY IT BEFORE RELAUNCHING.


=============================================================================
3. EIGHT DEFECTS FROM A REVIEW OF THE DAY'S DIFF, SEVEN FIXED
=============================================================================

A medium-effort review of the uncommitted diff (14 files, +1168) found eight.
Fixed tonight:

  1. THE GPU FF PATH SKIPPED THE CLIP-W REFUSAL. nv2a_ff_vertex refuses a
     whole batch when a vertex's composite w is 0 or non-finite ("fixed-
     function clip W", 1-193 batches in EVERY archived run); the GPU path drew
     them, dividing by zero and taking the vertex to NaN with no counter. The
     "strict subset" rule did not cover it because that rule is about batch
     SHAPES and this is a property of a vertex. nv2a_ff_clip_w_ok() now does
     the same test over the position the executor has already fetched, four
     multiply-adds, and refuses with the same string. Counted as
     "clip-w vertices" in the [VSH] fixed-function line.
  2. FUSED MULTIPLY-ADD. The MSL emitter compiles with contract(off) and the
     comment claimed "the CPU side is a plain C loop that does not fuse" --
     but nv2a_ff.c builds -O2 arm64 with clang's default -ffp-contract=on and
     had 71 fused ops, 28 of them on the accumulation that produces the clip w
     an EXACT ==0 test then decides a batch on. `#pragma clang fp contract(off)`
     added to nv2a_ff.c. The diff test's "residual 0" now means what it says.
  3. THE HRTF HEADROOM was still applied to bins 0-3 of every 3D voice even
     with the submix override gated OFF, so the guest's own routing got the
     wrong headroom -- and g_bin_hrtf_on was set regardless, so [APU-BIN]
     printed "hrtf=on" in BOTH arms of its own A/B. Both gated on the switch.
  4. __builtin_popcountll in the new [APU-POOL] code would not compile under
     MSVC, which this tree still targets. Replaced with a portable loop.
  5. "N batches accepted, 0 left on the CPU" counted acceptance BEFORE the
     backend was asked, so with RECOMP_METAL_VSH=0 (a documented arm) every
     batch would read as GPU-accepted while running on the CPU. Now
     decremented on refusal and counted as "backend refused".
  6. [FF-BATCH]'s batch= printed s_vsh.batches, which only counts PROGRAMMABLE
     batches -- consecutive fixed-function records carried the same number.
     Own counter now.
  7. g_idle_trap_edge_hold[] is uint16_t; REARM_MS above ~43,000 would make
     the re-raise never fire and read exactly like a shut latch. Clamped.
  8. `RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO=` (empty, the shell idiom for "leave the default")
     turned the FENCE FIX OFF, contradicting its own comment. Empty now keeps
     the default.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: the sink's per-vertex vertex_valid() test (q<=0 or
non-finite texcoord drops the triangle) is skipped on every GPU vertex path,
programmable and fixed-function alike, because triangle() returns before it
when vsh_gpu_culling is set. The CPU arm drops those triangles and the GPU arm
samples them. Fixing it means either transforming the texcoord on the CPU --
which is the work the GPU path exists to avoid -- or discarding in the
fragment shader on q<=0. The second is cheap and is the recommendation, but it
changes what every GPU draw does and wants its own A/B, not a change smuggled
in beside a glyph hunt. It is ALSO a live candidate for section 2.

play_scripted.sh now prints every RECOMP_* in its environment, writes them to
<out>/switches.txt, and diffs them line by line against the player's
paths.conf, naming each difference in both directions. frame_bisect.sh gained

=============================================================================
5. WHERE THE FRAME TIME IS (G3, NOT STARTED)
=============================================================================

Unchanged and un-begun: the flip sync, 4.06-6.91 ms/frame, one call per frame,
~70% of all sync cost. The frame is serialised into submit -> stall the GPU ->
read 614 KB back -> convert -> present, and it exists only because the
presenter is OpenGL (src/d3d/d3d8_gl.c) and reads the guest framebuffer out of
guest RAM. The live Metal surface is NEVER the surface being flipped (zero
times in two runs, [SURFACE-AUDIT]), so the design must look the FLIPPED
address up in the surface cache. There are NO staged patches in the tree --
the earlier handover's "stages 0-2 exist" means prose, not files. Stage 0 is
the blit instrument, and it needs its sample point fixed first: the
[d3d8_gl] blit line compares a guest pixel against the drawable centre and
that equality only held while the drawable was exactly 1x the guest. It is 4x
on a 2x panel now, so it means "should be close", not "must be equal" --
compute the expected bilinear blend and compare with a 1 LSB tolerance.

A per-frame sync HISTOGRAM should precede the presenter change: removing
waitUntilCompleted removes the serialisation, not the GPU work, so it may move
p50 and leave p99 alone. Player's last two sessions: mean 18.14 ms (FF off),
15.44 ms (FF on), p99 39-43 ms in both. The mean is nearly there; the tail is
not, and the tail is what "moves at the correct speed" means.
```

```txt
2. NO MUSIC + EFFECTS CUT OFF -- ONE DEFECT, AND IT IS THE IDLE-TRAP EDGE
=============================================================================

THE EVIDENCE (player session 16:22-16:28, idle_edge on, 37 report windows):

  [APU-BIN] 2D heard: 0, 2560, 19988, 29597, 29597, 29597 ... 29597 (x31)
            3D heard climbing the whole time (234045 at the end)
  [APU-IDLE-EDGE] edge_suppressed=1010411 rearm=51
  [APU-IDLE] first raises: 2D:v69 2D:v68 2D:v69 3D:v0 2D:v68 2D:v70 ...
             then 24 raises total over the whole session (level arm: 16220)
  [APU-VOICE] on=98 off=94 off_commands=94 idle_trap=65
  [APU-PACE] starved=0 empty=0 -- the output queue never ran dry

Music (2D, v68-v70) fell silent ~20 s in and never returned. Effects kept
playing but the player heard them cut off.

off == off_commands == 94: EVERY retirement was a guest VOICE_OFF command.
Zero model retirements (EOS, SSL exhaustion, envelope release). The music
voices did not run off the end of anything; the GUEST stopped them, and they
then sat "inactive and still linked" -- the state the level trap storms on
and the edge trap reports exactly once.

WHAT THE GUEST DOES WITH THE RAISE. Xbox DirectSound uses SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE to
run RemoveIdleVoice (the crash at 351439b is that function): it is how the
driver RECLAIMS a voice for its free list. Three early returns (PERSIST among
them) leave the voice linked and expect to be told AGAIN later. So:

  level trap  -> told 1500x/s -> reclaim works, storm costs the breakup
  edge trap   -> told once, at a moment the ISR returns early -> never
                 reclaimed -> free list empties -> new sounds STEAL playing
                 voices -> "effects cut off" -> a music voice is stolen ->
                 "no music" at ~20 s, permanently

That single mechanism produces both reports, in that order, and predicts the
2D-heard plateau. It is a hypothesis with a test, not a measurement:

  TEST: in the edge-ON log, count VOICE_ON on a handle whose last event was
  VOICE_OFF within the same report window, per handle, over time. Steals show
  as the pool (distinct handles started) shrinking to a handful being
  recycled at high rate from ~20 s on. The level-arm log should show a stable
  pool. [APU-IDLE-RING] and the voice_lifecycle_note() "retire" notes are the
  raw material; nothing prints the pool size yet -- add it ([APU-POOL]
  distinct handles on'd this window, handles reused within 1 window).

WHY IT CYCLED IN THE SCRIPTED ARM AND NOT FOR THE PLAYER: rearm=289 over
340 s came from a scene where the guest kept restarting the same handles
(rearm site B: any voice seen ACTIVE again re-arms). The tutorial the player
sits in does not; its music voices are stopped once and left. The edge arm
was validated on a scene that could not fail this way.

THE FIX IS NEITHER ARM. Both are wrong for the same reason: the model does not
know when the guest has FINISHED with the notification, so it either nags
forever or gives up after one. Two candidate fixes, in order:

  A. EDGE WITH A BOUNDED RE-RAISE (recommended first; ~30 lines, one switch).
     Keep the edge latch. When a latched voice is still inactive-and-linked
     N ms after its raise, raise again and restart the timer. N = one guest
     DirectSound tick (RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_REARM_MS, try 16 then 33). Worst
     case per stuck voice: 60 raises/s instead of 1500; music voices get
     told again until reclaimed. Verify: 2D heard keeps climbing for the
     whole player session, edge_suppressed and rearm both climbing, [APU-POOL]
     stable, trapped% under 5.
     Site: the suppress branch at apu_vp.c ~3925 (add a per-voice last-raise
     timestamp beside g_idle_trap_reported[]); the timestamp store is the same
     unlocked plain-store class as the bitmap, same justification.

  B. RAISE ONLY FOR MODEL RETIREMENTS, NOT GUEST VOICE_OFF (the hardware
     question). Whether the DSP raises idle for a voice the driver itself
     stopped is not known here. Do NOT take this on argument: with
     off == off_commands the guest's own stops are 100% of retirements in the
     tutorial, so B silences the notification entirely for that scene and
     the pool test above will say within a minute whether the guest survives
     it. Build only if A fails.

  ALSO CHECK, CHEAPLY, BEFORE A: does the latch set on a raise that was
  ATTEMPTED or one that was DELIVERED? [APU-VOICE2] raises_minus_idle_trap=0
  says the two counters agree, but if the FE can refuse a raise (the vblank
  path has raised != delivered) and g_idle_trap_reported is set on the
  attempt, the guest never saw the one raise the edge allowed. Read where the
  bit is SET (grep "g_idle_trap_reported\[.*\] |=") and what can fail after
  it.

DO NOT RE-ENABLE RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_EDGE for the player as it stands. It
has now silenced the music twice, once with the log to prove it.


=============================================================================
3. THE GLYPHS -- RECOMP_METAL_FF DRAWS TWO WRONG CHARACTERS
=============================================================================

Screenshot 16:23 (tutorial, "Let's see how much air you can grab. Press the
"A button" to jump."): the 'w' of "how" is a doubled/stretched shape, the 'y'
of "you" reads as another glyph ('$'-like). ~40 other characters, the
speech-bubble, the button glyph, the world: all correct. Positions correct;
TEXCOORDS of two glyphs wrong by a whole atlas cell, not a texel.

The same scene on the CPU fixed-function path draws clean text (every player
session before tonight). RECOMP_METAL_FF is the only rendering switch that
changed. Its stats line in the session: 765211 batches accepted, 0 on the
CPU, 0 texgen, 0 texmat anomalies.

RULED OUT BY READING (do not re-read these; go to the experiment):
  - The emitter's arithmetic: texgen pass-through `g.k = v9+u.k`, optional
    texmat ff_dot4 per row, same as nv2a_ff_vertex; the diff test's residual
    is 0 over 15 states and the texmat states are among them.
  - The input side: GPU FF fetches attrs in key->inputs (0x1E19: pos, D0,
    D1, T0-3, + normal if read) with the same fetch_vertex and the same
    s_vsh.current defaults for unsized attributes as the CPU branch.
  - The constants: nv2a_metal_vsh_constants stores a POINTER to
    nv2a_ff_constants, which nv2a_ff_params rewrites per batch. Harmless
    only because nv2a_metal_draw is called per batch (nv2a_pb_exec.c:3432)
    and setVertexBytes copies at encode. Cheap hardening: memcpy at the
    call. Not the glyph bug unless a draw is ever deferred.
  - Cache key collision: keysize 32 = 2 hash words, full memcmp after the
    hash, version byte in the key.

NOT RULED OUT -- THE DIFFERENCES THAT REMAIN BETWEEN THE TWO PATHS:
  a. WHAT THE DIFF TEST NEVER FED: a real text batch. make_inputs() is
     synthetic. Two glyphs wrong out of forty means those glyphs' BATCHES
     differ from the others' in some state (a second font page, a texmat
     enabled just for them, a different attribute layout such as texcoords
     supplied as shorts or as the SET_VERTEX_DATA "current" register rather
     than an array). The CPU path handles that state; the GPU path
     mishandles it. The per-batch key/state of the failing glyphs is the
     fact that decides this, and nothing captures it yet.
  b. The FF epilogue omits the programmable path's subpixel snap. Cannot
     produce a whole-cell texcoord error; listed so nobody spends a run on it.
  c. Fragment-side q handling for the FF-produced oT (float4 with q from the
     current register when the array is 2-wide). If q != 1 for exactly those
     glyphs' vertices, the divide moves the sample by a cell. Same fetch on
     both paths, so only possible if the CPU sink divides by q differently
     from the GPU-vertex sink (nv2a_metal.m:2846 area).

THE EXPERIMENT (one evening, no argument):
  1. Reproduce unattended: play_tutorial.sh reaches this text (state 61/65

  3. Diff the two arms' dumps for the glyph batches. Whichever field differs

  4. Only then re-enable RECOMP_METAL_FF in paths.conf, and after the

Frame time is why this matters beyond text: the game is frame-locked
(speed = 16.683 ms / mean frame), METAL_FF is worth 6 ms, and the player's
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_SIXTY_FPS_AND_THE_PICTURE_IS_RIGHT.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER, 16 Sep 2026 (late)
SIXTY FPS, AND THE PICTURE IS RIGHT

Supersedes HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_OPAQUE_DRAWS_NEVER_READ_THE_DESTINATION.txt
and, with it, everything in the 15 Sep handover about the renderer being
unexplained.

Two things happened today. The render artefact that had been unexplained for
days was found and fixed, and the frame rate went from 31.5 fps to about 60.


1. THE HEADLINE, WITH THE NUMBER STATED HONESTLY
=================================================
    31.75 ms / 31.5 fps   ->   16.4-17.0 ms / 58.9-61.1 fps

TWO RUNS MEASURED 61.1 AND 58.9 FPS, and calling them "the same configuration"
was WRONG -- their RESULTS.txt files carry different binaries (9fb5857f against
a5504fd7) and one additionally ran with the [METAL-CB] instrumentation on. Same
switches, not same build. The pinned hash is printed in every RESULTS.txt for
exactly this reason and was not read. So the truthful statement is "about 60
fps", and the spread is not yet characterised.

AND 60 FPS ON AVERAGE IS NOT THE TARGET. See section 5: the guest is paced by
an emulated 59.94 Hz vblank whose poll DROPS periods it misses, so every frame
over 16.683 ms permanently costs one simulation step. The metric is p99, not
the mean. Measured across gameplay windows: p50 16.5-19.0, p90 19.5-24.0, p99
21-27.5. Roughly half of frames still overrun. Section 7 is therefore not
polish; it is the rest of the job.

The artefact is gone at every step: 24 of 24 captured gameplay frames clean,
scored by the structural fingerprint described in section 5 at 31-32% against
the software control's 30% and chance's 25%.


2. WHAT THE RENDER BUG WAS
===========================
EVERY HARDWARE DRAW MUST READ THE COLOUR ATTACHMENT.

fs_hw wrote colour(0) and never read it; fs_hw_blend declares
`float4 dst [[color(0), raster_order_group(0)]]`, as the software tail does.
The renderer chose between them per draw -- fs_hw_blend only for a draw that
both blended and dithered -- so all the opaque world geometry wrote the
attachment with no destination read and no raster ordering. At gameplay that
rendered visibly corrupt on every frame: axis-aligned blocks, median 5x5 px,
holding black or fragments of other scene content.

Established by a ladder over four modes, one pinned binary, one pad, serial,
24 captured gameplay frames each:

    mode 0  no draw reads dst, and no mixing either   36%   corrupt
    mode 1  dithered AND blended draws (the old one)  43%   corrupt
    mode 2  every blended draw                        40%   corrupt
    mode 3  every draw                                30%   CLEAN
    --      the software path, as the control         30%   clean

Monotone in COVERAGE and nothing else. Mode 2 already took every blended draw
off the fixed-function blend unit and was still corrupt, so the blend unit was
not the cause; mode 0 removed fs_hw_blend entirely so the encoder never mixed
two blending modes, and was still corrupt, so the mixing was not the cause.

THE 15 SEP HANDOVER'S RANKED #1 -- "run the depth and stencil bisect arms to a
result. This is the whole remaining search space" -- was run and is NEGATIVE on
both arms. Depth compare forced ALWAYS: corrupt. Stencil ignored: corrupt. The
search space was not what it said, and the symptom description that led there
("the speckle is BLACK ... fragments being rejected") was wrong: the artefact
is blocks holding three or more distinct colours of other scenery, which
fragment rejection cannot produce.


3. HOW 60 FPS WAS REACHED
==========================
In the order the changes landed. Each row is its own A/B against the arm
immediately before it, so they do NOT chain arithmetically.

  a. THE RESIDENT CLEAR                        31.75 -> 27.06 ms, 31.5 -> 37.0
     nv2a_gpu_clear_color and _clear_depth_stencil were defined for the D3D11
     backend only, so on macOS every clear drained the GPU, read the whole
     4.9 MB colour surface back, converted it per pixel into guest RAM, let the
     CPU memset 1.8 MB, and made the next draw re-upload 6.4 MB. Twice a frame.
     None of it is necessary when the CPU is about to write one constant over
     every byte: the GPU writes the constant itself as a load action.
     `clear` fell 9.57 -> 0.25 ms. 7.4 ms of that reappeared in `sync` because
     the read-back moved to the guest's own FLIP_STALL, where it always had to
     happen; what actually disappeared is the drain and the re-upload.

  b. THE UNBOUND-SURFACE CLEAR                 27.06 -> 26.29 ms, 37.0 -> 38.0
     86% of colour clears named a surface the backend was not bound to -- the
     guest moves the colour offset register while surface_target only moves on
     the next DRAW -- and every one fell back to the CPU AND dropped cache
     slots. The surface cache sat at exactly 50% hit with 10,352 rebuilds a
     run, each reallocating four textures and re-uploading 6.4 MB. Clearing the
     cached texture instead took it to 100% hit and 5 rebuilds.
     `submit` fell 1.67 ms, which the rebuild arithmetic predicts. The 0.77 ms
     total is inside the noise envelope; the attributable win is `submit`.

  c. THE GUEST'S VERTEX PROGRAM ON THE GPU     29.79 -> 18.32 ms, 33.6 -> 54.6
     The single largest change. `vsh` fell 12.90 -> 3.29 ms.
     408,205,400 vertices transformed on the GPU across 639,089 draws, 21
     distinct programs compiled, NOTHING refused by the emitter, the compiler
     or either cache.

  d. THE 565 COLOUR ATTACHMENT                 18.32 -> 16.37 ms, 54.6 -> 61.1
     Two bytes a pixel instead of sixteen, in the guest's own format, so both
     per-pixel conversion loops become row memcpys and every colour transfer
     shrinks eightfold. It is also MORE correct: the frame stops requantising
     between draws, so the double rounding at the read-back boundary is gone.

RECOMP_METAL_HW, RECOMP_METAL_VSH and RECOMP_METAL_565 all now default ON, each
measured before being flipped, each with =0 still a real arm.


4. THE VERTEX WORK, AND WHY IT WAS SAFE TO DO
==============================================
nv2a_vsh_msl.c had emitted MSL for these programs for months and had NEVER BEEN
EXECUTED -- its own header said so. Before wiring it in, a differential test
dispatched it on a device against nv2a_vsh_execute over THE 126 PROGRAMS READ
OUT OF THE TITLE'S OWN default.xbe: 8064 vectors, 0 residual disagreements,
with an injected-fault control (the same program recompiled with oPos.x += 1)
still reporting 64 of 64.

IT FOUND THREE REAL DEFECTS, none subtle in effect:
  * Metal fuses a*b+c into an fma even under MTLMathModeSafe; the interpreter
    cannot, because multiply()'s zero rule is a select. 51 of 8064 vectors,
    worst 1.78 ABSOLUTE IN CLIP SPACE, concentrated in seven skinning programs.
  * The NV2A's a*0 rule was not reproduced, so a zero normal took rsqrt(0)=+inf
    into the normalise multiply: NaN on the GPU, 0 on the CPU, and THE NaN
    REACHED oPos -- the triangle vanished. In one program a later MIN laundered
    it into a finite wrong value, so it would not even announce itself.
  * LIT returned about 5e25 where the interpreter returns +inf.

THE CORPUS ANCHOR EARNED ITS KEEP IMMEDIATELY. The 12-slot program in
vsh_capture.h, taken from a running frame months ago, is asserted to be found
byte-identical at file offset 0x18A888. The first scanner stepped four words
after a failed run and began programs one slot early on a dead double-NOP,
producing a corpus of subtly wrong programs. Nothing else noticed.

WHAT THE VERTEX WORK STILL DOES NOT COVER:
  * DPH, DST, EXP, LOG and LIT appear in NO program this title ships. Fixture
    only. If one ever reaches the GPU path it is untested against the title.
  * Operand data in the differential test is synthetic uniform [-1.5,1.5]. Real
    constants are transform rows and bone matrices with very different
    magnitudes. RECOMP_METAL_VSH_VERIFY, specified in the plan, is not built.
  * 13 of 8064 vectors differ by up to 4.3e-04 and are classified
    ill-conditioned by perturbing operands one ulp and watching the
    INTERPRETER's own answer move as far as the gap. They are still real
    per-pixel differences in a rendered frame.
  * nv2a_vsh_hlsl.c STILL CARRIES ALL THREE DEFECTS. The two emitters were
    deliberate line-for-line siblings and are no longer. The Windows path has
    the NaN-reaches-oPos bug today.

TWO HAZARDS THE INTEGRATION HAD TO HANDLE, both of which corrupt silently:
  * The emitter's VS_OUT is not the Out the fragment tails consume -- different
    fields, different order -- and a vertex function in one MTLLibrary feeding
    a fragment function in another matches BY POSITION. So the program is
    compiled into the same library as the fragment tails and a wrapper repacks
    VS_OUT into Out field by field.
  * triangle() reads v[i][0] as a SCREEN position for winding, facing and the
    transformed texture coordinates. With the program on the GPU that slot
    holds attribute 0, an object-space position. The first attempt rendered
    characters as black silhouettes. Culling needs the transformed position,
    which is the thing that moved, so it moved too: setCullMode and
    setFrontFacingWinding at the encoder.
  * AND, caught by jsrf_vsh_render in 0.03 s: when nv2a_gpu_draw rejects,
    raster_batch falls through to the CPU rasteriser, which reads s_outputs as
    screen positions. On this path it holds INPUTS. Both are sixteen float4 per
    vertex and indistinguishable by inspection. The fallback now re-runs the
    interpreter first.


5. THE SOUND, WHICH WAS THE FRAME RATE
=======================================
Reported as "the sound goes out of sync over the course of a run". Measured
from three runs' own APU counters:

    frame        APU frames in 280 s   underruns (depth bucket 0)
    44.23 ms     405,208               0
    30.97 ms     405,112               0
    18.18 ms     405,080               0

THE APU EMITS THE SAME NUMBER OF FRAMES AT EVERY FRAME RATE AND NEVER
UNDERRUNS. It is locked to real time by throttle(), which is what it should be.
Nothing was wrong with the audio.

AND THE MECHANISM IS IN THE CODE, not inferred. The guest does not free-run:
bridge_vblank_poll delivers BRIDGE_VBLANK_PERIOD_US = 16683 us, 59.94 Hz, and
the title's own vsync pump blocks on it -- which is why d3d8_gl.c sets
SDL_GL_SetSwapInterval(0) and says so. The guest therefore CANNOT run faster
than 59.94 Hz and being faster than 60 is harmless.

The drift comes from the other side. kernel_bridge.c:2534, deliberately:

    "still reset from `now` rather than advanced from the previous deadline.
     A late poll DROPS the periods it missed instead of delivering them in a
     burst."

So a frame that overruns 16.683 ms costs one simulation step, permanently,
while audio keeps real time. Game speed is 16.683 / mean_frame_ms:

    best window     14.27 ms   p99 17.0    100% (capped by the vblank)
    typical         16.6-17.4  p99 21-23   96-99%
    worst           18.2-20.2  p99 23.5-27 83-92%

At 31.75 ms it was 52%, which is why the desync was gross. It is now subtle and
NOT GONE: about half of frames still overrun. Eliminating it needs p99 under
16.68 ms, which means a mean nearer 12-13 ms with tight variance -- not the
16.4 this session reached.


6. HOW TO MEASURE THIS, WHICH IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES
===========================================================
WHAT WORKS: capture 24 gameplay frames per arm and LOOK at them, as a contact
sheet, then magnified nearest-neighbour on a flat surface. It separated the
arms in about a minute on the first attempt, after six image metrics had failed
over two days.

WHAT WORKS AS A SCORE: only a structural property the artefact has and scene
content cannot. `x0 mod 4` -- the fraction of dark blocks whose left edge lands
on a 4-pixel grid, against 25% by chance -- is a within-frame ratio, so it
needs no matched scene. The clean software control reads 30%, the broken
renderer 43%. That is the bar, and it is the same shape of argument fb_score's
`tile` metric uses.

WHAT STILL DOES NOT WORK: a generic image statistic. An isolated-dark-blob
count written this morning scored the KNOWN-GOOD software arm at 835
exact-black pixels against the corrupt hardware arm's 761 -- ranking the good
arm worse, for the fifth time.

frame_bisect.sh runs arms one at a time against a pinned binary, captures 24
gameplay frames each, writes ARM.txt from THE BACKEND'S OWN REPORT rather than
from the environment it set, retries an arm that faults before gameplay, and
refuses to score one that never got there. That last guard fired three times
today and was right every time.

MISTAKES MADE TODAY, all of them process rather than analysis:
  * A source file was edited while a bisect was running, twice; the staleness
    guard refused the arms, correctly.
  * The bisect SCRIPT was edited while running, four times. sh re-reads by byte
    offset, so the trailing summary broke each time. Once this was asserted to
    be safe without checking.
  * An instrument was bundled with a change on the same run -- RECOMP_VSH_SPLIT,
    two clock reads per vertex over 206 million vertices -- so neither could be
    attributed. The switch's own comment warned it was exactly that weight.
  * A binary was measured stale after an edit-and-build in the same second,
    which make skips silently. Always confirm the "Building OBJC object" line,
    not just "Built target".
  * A frame-time figure was quoted from a run that was still going. A partial
    run's mean is not the run's mean.
  * `git add` on a file another agent was editing swept a test registration
    into the wrong commit, leaving a commit that referenced an untracked source
    -- a fresh clone there would have failed at configure. Split and rewritten;
    nothing was pushed at the time.
  * frame_bisect.sh's arm_env zeroed every switch as its baseline, so the arm
    whose whole purpose is measuring DEFAULTS forced the two new ones OFF while
    reporting itself as the default arm.


7. OPEN, RANKED
================
  1. HEADROOM. 58.9-61.1 fps over two runs of one configuration is at the line,
     not past it. `sync` is 5.2-6.1 ms and is the largest remaining stage; of
     it, roughly 3.6 ms is GPU DRAIN -- the CPU waiting on the GPU because
     nothing overlaps them -- which none of today's changes touch and which is
     a pipelining problem. `submit` is 4.0-4.2 ms and is still mostly the
     surface-swap sync inside nv2a_metal_draw, which a per-slot dirty flag
     would let a cache hit skip entirely.

  2. THE APU CRASH, DIAGNOSED, AND A FIX FOR IT REVERTED THE SAME DAY.
     Two windows are measured open -- 13,294 of 23,933 idle-voice raises happen
     while the guest holds that voice's lock, and 47,919 of 77,141 guest
     methods arrive while the front end is trapped, clobbering the decode pair
     the ISR is mid-read of. Guards for both were written, defaulted on, and
     REVERTED within the hour: with them on, 4 of 4 runs faulted at t=24.03,
     deterministically, against ~5 in ~25 at t=34-35 with them off. A fix that
     makes the crash worse is not a fix, however good the reasoning was, and
     the reasoning was static.
     The crash also reproduced WITH both guards on, from a ring entry
     3D:v0[]<-TVL carrying no flags at all -- not locked, not never-started.
     THERE IS A THIRD MECHANISM AND NOBODY KNOWS WHAT IT IS. The likeliest
     place to look is whether a released voice is correctly unlinked from the
     TVL/CVL/NVL cursor triple: a voice left at a list head is found by the
     walk for ever, and DirectSound cleared its owner long ago.
     Do not default either guard on again without five clean runs. The fault
     fires in about one run in five, so one clean run is not evidence.

  2b. THE OLD FORM OF THIS ITEM, kept because the diagnosis stands. sub_001A2E2E is DirectSound's
     RemoveIdleVoice called with a NULL this; our APU hands its ISR a voice
     handle DirectSound has no owner object for. All six dumped registers
     reproduce from ecx=0, the five-frame call chain is read off the stack
     dumps, and the fatal handle is voice 0 in 18 of 18 rings. 40 of 66
     recorded guest faults in this tree are this one.
     The mechanism -- VOICE_ON publishing the handle ~80 lines before setting
     ACTIVE_VOICE, unlocked, on a guest thread while the walk runs on the frame
     thread -- IS STATIC READING. The fix ships OFF behind
     RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_LOCK_GUARD and ONE RUN DECIDES IT: an `L` on the last
     ring entry proves it, an `N` without an `L` means the guard will not help,
     neither means the hypothesis is dead and [APU-FEDEC] is next.

  3. nv2a_vsh_hlsl.c HAS ALL THREE EMITTER DEFECTS (section 4).

  4. RECOMP_METAL_VSH_VERIFY is specified in
     docs/jsrf/plans/GPU_VERTEX_SHADING.md and not built. It is the only thing
     that closes the synthetic-operand gap, by running both paths on the
     title's real vertices and constants and diffing them.

  5. THE FENCE ARM WAS NEVER VALID. It waits beforeStages:MTLRenderStageVertex
     and a colour attachment's load is fragment-side, so "pass ordering is not
     the mechanism" is not supported by it. Re-run with
     beforeStages:MTLRenderStageFragment before treating that as closed.

  6. DOES [[position]].z REFLECT MTLDepthClipModeClamp? Applied to every
     encoder, and all three fragment tails then implement the guest's CULL
     policy from i.p.z. If Metal hands the shader the CLAMPED value then for
     JSRF's range the discard can never fire and the whole z-range policy is
     inert. One atomic counter and one run.

  7. UPSTREAM IS 80 COMMITS AHEAD and none of them touch src/nv2a. Worth
     merging for the translator and lifter fixes -- sar sign-extension, INC/DEC
     carry, jbe/ja after and/or/xor, MMX flag preservation, x87 rounding, the
     uninitialised generated ebp. Separate task: merging means regenerating,
     which is not bit-stable.

  8. SMALLER, ALL FOUND BY REVIEW AND NONE OF THEM THE ARTEFACT: clip_position
     models a vertex shader that does not exist and a recorded retraction rests
     on it; nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth returns 0 from inside the pixel
     loop after committing pixels, against its own header's promise; a retained
     depth buffer is re-read at the new surface's geometry, out of bounds; the
     "depth ownership is exclusive" invariant is not enforced when
     hw_depth_upload fails; shade() drops the CPU's clamp on the modulate path;
     three sinks implement three different z-range policies.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_FENCES_THE_RINGS_AND_A_BLACK_SCREEN_I_CAUSED.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 (third of the day) -- THE FENCES, THE RINGS, AND A BLACK
SCREEN I CAUSED

Read CLAUDE.md first, then the two companion handovers from today:

  HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_INSTRUMENTS_WERE_LYING.txt        the APU audit
  HANDOVER_2026-09-16_TWO_METHODS_THE_EXECUTOR_NEVER_DECODED.txt  the renderer audit

This one is the state at end of session. It supersedes the other two ONLY where
it says so -- specifically, the renderer-audit handover describes eight fixes
that are NOT in the tree any more. See section 3 before you trust it.

THIS IS A STATIC RECOMPILER, NOT AN EMULATOR. The title's x86 is translated to
C ahead of time and compiled native; nothing interprets guest instructions at
run time. What is emulated is the hardware around it -- NV2A, MCPX APU, the
kernel, the HDD, vblank. The distinction matters because it tells you where to
look: "guest CPU" time in the stage breakdown is COMPILED CODE, not an
interpreter, and no amount of runtime tuning touches it. (I got this wrong
repeatedly in conversation and was corrected.)


=============================================================================
1. WHAT IS COMMITTED AND PUSHED
=============================================================================

Two commits, both verified by a run before pushing:

  754c223  Map the NV2A aperture twice, and close the last two unprotect windows
  9408806  The APU's instruments were lying, and the lock guard was never the
           mechanism

754c223 closes CLAUDE.md's outstanding "PCRTC_INTR_0 and PGRAPH_INTR still have
this shape" note by giving the NV2A aperture the same double MapViewOfFileEx
alias MCPX has had since the 13.5M-window incident. Confirmed in a run:

    [NV2A] aperture aliased at 0x10cf6c000; the guarded view is never unprotected
    [MCPX] aperture aliased at 0x10df6c000; the guarded view is never unprotected

9408806 is the APU audit. The headline is that three counters were lying, and
one of them had been the standing justification for a guard. Do not re-derive
anything from pre-16-Sep APU numbers without reading that handover first.


=============================================================================
2. WHAT IS UNCOMMITTED AND WHY
=============================================================================

    src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c   NV_MAX_INDICES 4096 -> 16384
    src/nv2a/nv2a_metal.m       NV2A_METAL_MAX_VERTICES, count guard, static
                                assembly array, RING_SLAB_BYTES 2 -> 8 MB
    src/nv2a/nv2a_d3d11.c       the same cap on the Windows backend
    diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/packaging/   the .app bundle builder (new)
    docs/jsrf/handovers/...TWO_METHODS...txt  (new, and see section 3)

THE CAP RAISE IS THE FENCE FIX. Verified not-black in a run (guest centre
52 71 8C, 73 B6 A5 -- varied colour, window matching) and 35/35 ctest, but the
gameplay runs confirming it had not finished when the session ended. Commit it
once they have.


=============================================================================
3. A BLACK SCREEN I CAUSED, AND WHAT IS STILL OUT OF THE TREE
=============================================================================

READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE RENDERER-AUDIT HANDOVER.

That document describes eight fixes as landed. They were, and then the player
reported a black screen and they were REVERTED. They are saved, not lost:

    docs/jsrf/attic/2026-09-16_renderer_audit_fixes_REVERTED.patch

(815 lines, committed deliberately. It was first written to a session-scoped
scratchpad, which would have evaporated with the session and taken a day of
measured work with it. `git apply` it against the commit named in its header,
not against a later tree.)

WHAT THE BISECT ESTABLISHED, and it is worth having:

  arm 0  everything reverted          picture RENDERS (6B 69 63, 21 04 08, ...)
  arm A  audit fixes in, cap at 4096  STILL BLACK
  arm B  cap at 16384, audit fixes out  picture RENDERS

So the bug is in the EIGHT AUDIT FIXES, and the index-cap raise is INNOCENT.
That is why the cap is back in the tree alone.

The symptom, same scene and instrument either side:

    before  [d3d8_gl] blit N: guest centre 00 8A 8C -> window 00 8A 8C
    after   [d3d8_gl] blit N: guest centre 00 00 00 -> window 00 00 00

The window blit is FAITHFUL in both -- window centre equals guest centre -- so
the presentation path is not the cause. The guest framebuffer itself is black.

WHAT MAKES THIS HARD: every health counter reads clean in the broken build.
882,085 hardware draws, refusals=0, pipelines=0, zero software fallbacks, 6.9M
triangles, [VSH] rejected=0, [TEXTURE] rejected_draw=0, no shader or pipeline
error. The whole [METAL] report is identical to the working run apart from one
counter line that was added. Whatever is wrong produces no error anywhere.

The two suspects worth checking first, both static reading:
  - the MSL sample_lod change. The shader is a C string; a subtly wrong
    expression compiles fine and outputs black, and this one runs for every
    textured fragment on the live path.
  - the `extern` forward declarations added for g_tri_assembled, g_tri_culled
    and vsh_gpu_culling INSIDE a function, hundreds of lines above their real
    definitions in the same file. If a type disagrees, or if vsh_gpu_culling is
    read through a declaration that does not match its definition, culling
    changes with nothing to notice.

An agent was hunting this when the session ended; its answer did not arrive.

DO NOT REAPPLY THE PATCH WHOLESALE. Apply one fix, run gameplay, check the
blit line, repeat. That is exactly what I failed to do and it cost the player
two broken builds.


=============================================================================
4. THE FENCES -- CAUSE MEASURED, FIX APPLIED
=============================================================================

The player reported fences disappearing. It is not a shading bug and it was not
new: it is batch TRUNCATION, and it had been silent for the life of the file.

NV_MAX_INDICES was 4096. ARRAY_ELEMENT16 simply stopped storing once idx_count
reached the cap -- no counter, no log line -- and the batch was drawn anyway
with its tail missing. Measured once an instrument was put on the drop, in one
280 s gameplay run:

    no-room=43257098 (e16=86463170 e32=25513 da=0);
    biggest batch asked for 9681 of 4096 slots

9,681 indices in one batch, against an array of 4,096. Essentially all of the
loss is ARRAY_ELEMENT16 -- the oldest path -- not the two methods decoded
earlier in the day, which together account for 25,513 of 43 million.

RAISING THE CAP ALONE WOULD HAVE MADE IT WORSE. nv2a_metal_draw rejects
count>4096 and sizes its assembly array 3x4096 exactly, so every newly-admitted
batch would have been refused by the GPU and handed to the CPU rasteriser.
Both backends and the ring allocator were raised together.

NOTE ON THE COUNTER: e16 increments by 2 per dropped word while no-room
increments by 1, so those totals are not on the same scale. The ratio between
sources is right; the absolute numbers are not comparable. Fix that when the
counter comes back with the audit fixes -- it is not in the tree right now.


=============================================================================
5. SOUND -- ONE MECHANISM FIXED, ONE OPEN
=============================================================================

FIXED, and confirmed in the field. The output clock was 48,003 Hz: an EP frame
is 256 samples at 48 kHz = 5333 AND ONE THIRD microseconds and EP_FRAME_US
truncated the third, so the model generated 62.5 ppm more audio than the device
played, for ever. queued= climbed monotonically until apu_sdl2.c flushed the
whole queue in one jump -- the audible lurch at the end of a long session. Now:

    out_hz=48000  gen_hz=48000  starved=0  empty=0  min_queued=7168 (37.3 ms)

Pinned by jsrf_apu_pace with NO tolerance, because a tolerance is exactly what
hid a 62 ppm error.

STILL OPEN, and it is what the player still hears as glitching. Our copy of the
hardware voice list grows RINGS. VOICE_ON for a handle already reachable from
the head writes link(v) = regs[top] and sets regs[top] = v, splicing v in front
of a list that still reaches v. Measured in gameplay:

    [APU-CYCLE] relink=209 (of 388 top inserts) walks_with_a_cycle=184983
    [APU-IDLE-RING] 3D:v1[RC]<-TVL x15
    [APU-IDLE] busiest: v1=13957 of 17356 traps

FIFTY-FOUR PERCENT of top inserts. A voice inside a ring is visited twice by
one walk, so voice_get_samples runs twice and advances cbo/ssl_seg twice: a
streaming voice drains at 2x and starves, a looping voice plays at 2x pitch.
Everything behind the splice point is unreachable.

RECOMP_APU_CYCLE_BREAK=1 stops the WALK at the revisit. It is OFF by default
and should stay off until a run count says otherwise -- the previous APU guard
was defaulted on with an equally good argument and made the crash WORSE (4 of 4
faults at t=24.03 s against ~5 in 25 at t=34-35 s). It is also probably only a
mask: breaking the walk early still leaves voices behind the ring unrendered.
The real fix is likely at the INSERT, not the walk. An agent was designing that
when the session ended; its answer did not arrive.

Ring counters are currently OUT of the tree with the audit fixes. Note that
the ring EVIDENCE above predates the revert and stands on its own.


=============================================================================
6. 60 FPS -- THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOW MEASURED, THE NUMBER HAS NOT MOVED
=============================================================================

Gameplay, 280 s, reached gameplay:

    [FRAME] mean=14.82 ms (67.5 fps) p50=16.0 p90=19.5 p95=21.0 p99=40.5
            over-33ms=303

Mean clears 60 fps. p99 does not, and P99 IS THE TARGET, not mean: the guest is
capped at 59.94 Hz by emulated vblank and kernel_bridge.c DROPS missed periods,
so every frame over 16.683 ms permanently costs a simulation step. 303 frames
over 33 ms are visible hitches.

THE TWO STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS, measured this session rather than estimated:

  [STAGE] vsh=2.70 ms (81 calls) prepare=0.02 submit=3.56 sync=6.06 (1 call)
          clear=0.06 | rest=3.42 of 15.81
  [METAL] vsh draws: 508174 GPU, 707669 CPU
  [METAL] sync 38464 calls (12821 clean): 53579.9 ms draining the GPU,
          20735.0 ms reading back and converting

  (a) SYNC IS THE LARGEST SINGLE STAGE at 6.06 ms of a 15.8 ms frame, and 72%
      of it is the GPU STALL ([last_command waitUntilCompleted]), not the
      readback. 74 seconds of a 280 s run. The frame is serialised: submit ->
      stall for the whole GPU -> read 614 KB back -> convert -> present. That
      is a GPU->CPU->GPU round trip every frame, and it exists only because the
      presenter is OpenGL and reads guest RAM. Presenting straight from the
      Metal texture removes the stall, the readback, the conversion AND the GL
      re-upload in one change. Biggest single win available, and it is what
      "use the Metal GPU fully" actually names.
      NOTE: snapshot_surface() calls the sync BEFORE its `if (!s_snap_wanted)
      return;` gate, so the comment claiming "a run with no window pays
      nothing" is false -- the stall is paid unconditionally.

  (b) 58% OF DRAWS STILL SHADE VERTICES ON THE CPU -- 707,669 of 1,215,843 --
      because fixed-function T&L (nv2a_ff.c) has no GPU path. Only programmable
      -shader draws are GPU-shaded. Emitting an MSL vertex function for NV2A
      fixed-function T&L closes that and removes most of the vsh stage.

Neither is a tuning change. Both are structural, and neither was started.

Smaller, still recorded from earlier: depth read-back debt (~1.1-1.5 ms) and
narrow per-vertex copies (512 bytes copied to deliver ~64, ~0.7-1.0 ms). Note
the surface-swap sync was estimated at ~1.35 ms in an earlier handover and is
actually 6 ms -- 4x the estimate. Treat the other two estimates with suspicion.

7. THE MAC FRONT END
=============================================================================

New, uncommitted, in diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/packaging/make_app.sh.
Builds a double-clickable JSRF.app. Verified launching from Finder with NO
shell environment: both apertures aliased, HiDPI drawable 2560x1920, picture
correct, audio open at 48 kHz backend=SDL2.

Window work (currently OUT of the tree with the reverted patch, in d3d8_gl.c):

Cmd+F / F11 full screen, Escape leaves it, and a close button that actually
exits -- it used to print "window close requested" and carry on, leaving the
process running with no window. NOTE the window blit was PROVEN INNOCENT of the
black screen (window centre equals guest centre throughout), so this can go
back in with more confidence than the renderer half.

THREE TRAPS THE BUNDLE HIT, all worth remembering:
  - macOS is CASE-INSENSITIVE. CFBundleExecutable "JSRF" and a binary named
    "jsrf" in Contents/MacOS are THE SAME FILE; the launcher silently
    overwrote the Mach-O and otool then said "is not an object file" while
    every install_name_tool call quietly did nothing. The engine is named
    jsrf-engine for this reason.
  - sdl2-compat DLOPENS libSDL3.dylib. It appears in no LC_LOAD_DYLIB list;
    `strings` finds "@loader_path/libSDL3.dylib". Bundling only libSDL2 gives
    an app that dies at SDL_Init. The script checks for this and fails loudly.
  - CMake bakes the Cellar and /opt/homebrew/lib into LC_RPATH, and dyld
    searches rpaths in order -- so a bundle on the build machine loads
    Homebrew's copies and the bundled ones are never touched. It works, and it
    proves nothing. The script strips them.

ALSO: a GUI-launched app has its OWN TCC identity, not the Terminal's. A game
dump in iCloud Drive, Desktop, Documents or Downloads needs consent before the
first read, and the recomp BLOCKS FOREVER inside fopen() with nothing on screen
if it is not granted -- measured, 0.0% CPU for two minutes in __open_nocancel.
The launcher now reads a byte itself first and shows a dialog naming the
folder. Keeping the game files in Application Support avoids it entirely.

paths.conf is also where a switch can be tried without a rebuild; the generated
paths.conf.example documents RECOMP_APU_CYCLE_BREAK.
```
