`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_INSTRUMENTS_WERE_LYING.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 -- THE INSTRUMENTS WERE LYING

Supersedes nothing about the picture or the frame rate; those stand as
HANDOVER_2026-09-16_SIXTY_FPS_AND_THE_PICTURE_IS_RIGHT.txt left them. This is
about a different thing: a session spent auditing rather than changing, and
what the audit found was that several of the numbers this project has been
reasoning from do not mean what they say.

Read CLAUDE.md first. The rule "read a counter's trigger before trusting its
value" was already in it. This session is what happens when you actually do
that across a whole subsystem.


=============================================================================
1. THE NV2A APERTURE IS NOW ALIASED, AND CLAUDE.MD'S OPEN NOTE IS CLOSED
=============================================================================

CLAUDE.md carried a rule ending "PCRTC_INTR_0 and PGRAPH_INTR still have this
shape." They did:

  xbox_Nv2aRaiseVblank          unprotect, |= 1, reprotect -- 60 to 120 times
                                a second, on the page holding the register the
                                guest's vsync pump reads
  xbox_Nv2aRaiseSoftwareMethod  five stores with the whole 16 KB PGRAPH page
                                writable across all of them, and the reprotect's
                                return value discarded

A guest store landing in either window completes silently against RAM instead
of faulting into the model. That is the failure that cost 13.5M windows in 45 s
on the APU aperture and swallowed every VOICE_ON.

WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the detector cannot see the thing it was built to catch.
pcrtc_check compares the register against what the runtime last left there, but
the store at risk is the guest's write-1-to-clear of a bit that is ALREADY 1 --
so a lost store leaves the register bit-identical and the check compares 1
against 1 and returns. And its only call site is inside the vblank raise, which
stops being called once a lost acknowledge latches the pending bit. The
counter's ceiling is one. It printed zero and read as an all-clear.

THE FIX IS THE ONE MCPX ALREADY HAD: one CreateFileMappingA, two
MapViewOfFileEx views. The guest's view stays PAGE_READONLY for the life of the
process; the runtime writes through an alias. No window, so nothing to race and
nothing to detect.

  [NV2A] aperture aliased at 0x10cf6c000; the guarded view is never unprotected
  [MCPX] aperture aliased at 0x10df6c000; the guarded view is never unprotected

Verified by a 200 s scripted run: 199 s of presented frames, every one CHANGED,
no guest fault. The vblank path is the one this change puts at risk and the
guest advanced through all of it.

ANYTHING NEW THAT MUST WRITE A GUARDED DEVICE REGISTER GOES THROUGH THE ALIAS.
CLAUDE.md now says so.


=============================================================================
2. THE OUTPUT CLOCK WAS 48003 Hz, AND THAT IS THE AUDIO DRIFT
=============================================================================

This is the answer to "the sound goes out of sync over the course of a run",
and it had been printing itself in every run's report since the file was
written.

An EP frame is 256 samples at 48 kHz: 5333 AND ONE THIRD microseconds.
EP_FRAME_US is 5333. throttle() added it bare. So the model paced itself at
256/0.005333 = 48003.0 Hz against a device consuming at 48000 -- 62.5 ppm more
audio generated than played, for ever.

MEASURED, from an existing log, without needing a new run
(build-macos/jsrf-first-fault/frame-bisect/last/gpuvsh565/stderr.log):

  [APU-PACE] elapsed=270.0s subframes=405080 ... throttle=50636 ...

  subframes/throttle = 7.99984, so one throttle is one EP frame of 256 samples.
  50,636 throttles x 256 samples = 12,962,816 samples
  delivered over elapsed = 270.04 s
  => 48,003.4 Hz. Exactly the predicted truncation error.

And the consequence, also already printed and never read: `queued=` climbs
monotonically inside a single run -- 6144 bytes to 10240 over 200 s of
gpuvsh565. About 21 ms of audio latency added and never given back, roughly
6 ms per minute. apu_sdl2.c flushes the entire queue once it passes
APU_MAX_QUEUE_BYTES, which is the audible jump at the end of a long session.

Across build-macos, `out_hz=` reads 48003 or 48004 in thousands of report lines
and 48000 in 96.

FIXED by carrying the remainder: three EP frames are exactly 16000 us. Pinned
by diagnostics/jsrf_first_fault/apu_pace_test.c, which tests it as arithmetic
with NO tolerance -- a tolerance is exactly what hides a 62 ppm error -- over
one second and over a thousand.

NOTE ON THE REMAINDER: the drift observed in the field is a little larger than
62.5 ppm. The rest is host-device clock and is not ours. Fixing EP_FRAME_US
removes the half that is.

CONFIRMED IN THE FIELD, on completed runs: out_hz=48001 (apuclock1, 220.1 s)
and out_hz=48000 (apuclock2, 220.0 s). Across build-macos before the change it
reads 48003 or 48004 in thousands of lines. The residual +-1 Hz is the
resolution of a windowed rate at this length, not drift.

DO NOT QUOTE out_hz FROM A RUN IN PROGRESS. It is a windowed rate and it
wanders by several Hz early in a run. This session read it mid-run, got 48000,
said so, and had to withdraw it ten minutes later when the same grep returned
48002 on the same file. Same class of error as quoting a frame time from an
unfinished run, which this project has also done. Read the LAST line of a
COMPLETED run.


=============================================================================
3. COUNTERS THAT LIE -- THREE FOUND, ALL FIXED
=============================================================================

3a. `locked` was never a subset of `raises`, and the number that justified
    the lock guard was not the number it was reported as.

    g_idle_trap_locked_raises was incremented OUTSIDE the raise gate, so it
    counted every locked ENCOUNTER during a walk -- 1500 Hz, per voice, per
    list -- while g_idle_trap_raises counted actual raises. They were printed
    side by side as though one were a subset of the other.

    MEASURED: 42 of the 152 distinct [APU-IDLE-TRAP] lines in build-macos have
    locked > raises. e.g. `raises=10536 locked=16384`.

    CONSEQUENCE, and it is not small. apu_vp.c carried "13,294 of 23,933 raises
    happen while the guest holds that voice's lock" as the standing
    justification for RECOMP_APU_IDLE_TRAP_LOCK_GUARD. That is 13,294
    ENCOUNTERS over 23,933 RAISES. The "56%" is a ratio of two different
    populations and is not a percentage of anything. It is the best available
    explanation for why defaulting that guard on was predicted to help and
    instead took the fault from ~5 in 25 runs at t=34-35 s to 4 of 4 at
    t=24.03 s.

    NOW: locked_enc and locked_raises are separate and both printed, and the
    first gameplay run that printed both SETTLES IT (apuclock2, 220 s, reached
    gameplay, on=388):

      [APU-IDLE-TRAP] raises=17356 locked_raises=7 locked_enc=17657 ...

    SEVEN. Seven of 17,356 raises -- 0.04% -- happen while the guest holds that
    voice's lock. The old single counter would have printed `locked=17657`
    beside `raises=17356` on that same line, which reads as "essentially every
    raise happens while locked" and would have justified the guard harder still.

    THE LOCK GUARD WAS NEVER THE MECHANISM. That is the whole explanation for
    why turning it on helped nothing and hurt: it addresses four hundredths of
    one percent of raises. The window it was built for is real -- that came from
    reading VOICE_ON, not from the ratio -- and it is negligible. Stop here.
    See section 4 for what the mechanism actually is.

    g_idle_trap_lock_suppressed had the same flaw and now only counts raises
    that would actually have happened.

3b. `[APU-FRAME] trapped=` is structurally zero.

    g_apu_frames_trapped++ sat inside `if (!apu_active)`, but apu_active is
    TRUE while trapped once mcpx_apu_se_while_trapped() is on -- the default
    since 15 Sep. So it counted "frames SKIPPED because trapped", which is now
    always 0, and printed itself zero on the same line as episodes=17720 and
    longest_trapped_run=47 without anyone noticing the contradiction. mean_run
    divided by it.

    ANY EARLIER CONCLUSION OF THE FORM "trapped frames fell to zero" IS AN
    ARTEFACT OF THAT DEFAULT MOVING, not of whatever was under test. Worth
    re-reading the se_ab_* notes with this in mind.

    NOW: `trapped=` counts time spent trapped and `trapped_skipped=` counts
    frames actually lost to it. mean_run is meaningful again. The first
    gameplay run to print both:

      [APU-FRAME] total=330032 se=320177 trapped=155956 halted=9855
                  trapped_skipped=0 ... episodes=12428 mean_run=12.5
                  longest_trapped_run=63 (42.00 ms)

    FORTY-SEVEN PERCENT of frames are trapped, in episodes averaging 12.5
    frames. The line used to print trapped=0 for this. trapped_skipped=0 is
    RECOMP_APU_SE_WHILE_TRAPPED doing its job -- the engine renders through the
    trap, so no audio is lost to it -- but the storm underneath is entirely
    intact and is now visible for the first time. It is the same storm section
    4 explains.

3c. `idle_trap=` counts armed dispatches, not raises.

    g_apu_idle_trap_count only increments when FETFORCE1 has SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE
    armed -- but fe_method writes FEDECMETH/FEDECPARAM BEFORE that test. If the
    guest ever clears FETFORCE1 the two diverge silently AND every unarmed
    raise still clobbers the decode pair the guest's polling ISR reads.

    Equal in every run checked, so currently latent -- and nothing asserted it.
    [APU-VOICE2] now prints raises_minus_idle_trap so a divergence is visible
    the first time it happens rather than the first time someone looks.


=============================================================================
4. THE THIRD CRASH MECHANISM: VOICE LISTS THAT RING
=============================================================================

STATUS: MEASURED, and it is the mechanism. The instrument went in and the
first gameplay run that carried it answered the question outright.

The recorded story is that VOICE_ON for a voice that is ALREADY ITS LIST'S HEAD
writes link(v) = regs[top] = v, making a one-entry cycle. That is real and
RECOMP_APU_REON_HEAD_NOP exists for it.

The general case has no instrument at all. VOICE_ON for a handle that is
already somewhere in the list -- NOT at the head, so the head_nop guard does not
apply -- takes the same TOP-insert branch, writes link(v) = regs[top], and
splices v in front of a list that still reaches v. That is a ring of length >= 2
and everything behind the splice point becomes unreachable.

THE EXISTING TRANSCRIPTS ALREADY SHOW THEM. From
frame-bisect/vsh/hwdef/stderr.log:

  [APU-IDLE-RING] ... 2D:v69[]<-TVL  2D:v68[]<-v69  2D:v69[]<-v68 ...

link(v69)=v68 followed by link(v68)=v69, within the first three raises of the
run. From frame-bisect/cap3/cap64/stderr.log: `3D:v1[R]<-v3` fourteen times
then `3D:v3[]<-v1`. Rings look like the steady state of these lists, not an
edge case.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, and only the first is a waste of CPU:
  - the walk spins to its 256-iteration cap every subframe. Its break logs
    through DPRINTF, which compiles to nothing, so it has been silent for the
    life of the file.
  - voices inside the ring are RENDERED MORE THAN ONCE per subframe, each pass
    advancing cbo and ssl_seg again. A streaming voice drains at 2x and
    starves; a looping voice plays at 2x pitch. An audio-sync mechanism
    independent of the output clock in section 2.
  - our TVL keeps naming a ring member for ever. The guest's RemoveIdleVoice
    repairs ITS list and clears the owner but cannot repair ours, so every
    later walk finds the voice inactive and still reachable and raises
    SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE for a handle whose owner is NULL. That is sub_001A2E2E
    with ecx=0 -- the top crash site -- reached without either of the two
    windows the existing guards were built for.

It also fits the one piece of evidence that killed both previous hypotheses:
the fatal ring entry carried NO FLAGS. Not locked, not never-on. There was no
flag for "in a ring", because nothing looked.

THE INSTRUMENTS, all counters, no behaviour change:
  [APU-CYCLE] relink=N (of M top inserts) walks_with_a_cycle=N broken=N last=vX/listY
  and a new 'C' flag in the [APU-IDLE-RING] entries.

  relink   VOICE_ON for a handle already reachable from the head, counted
           BEFORE the insert. Positive control: the "of M top inserts"
           denominator, nonzero in every run. relink must never exceed it and
           must be >= self_link.
  walks_with_a_cycle  a list walk that reached the same voice twice.
  C        that voice has been seen twice in one walk at some point.

RECOMP_APU_CYCLE_BREAK=1 stops the walk at the revisit instead of spinning to
the cap. IT IS OFF BY DEFAULT AND MUST STAY OFF UNTIL A RUN COUNT SAYS
OTHERWISE. This repository has already shipped one APU guard on a good argument
and made the crash worse; the rule that came out of that is five clean runs
minimum, not a better argument.

THE RESULT (apuclock2, 220 s, reached gameplay, audio device live):

  [APU-CYCLE] relink=209 (of 388 top inserts) walks_with_a_cycle=184983
              broken=0 last=v1/list1 (cycle_break OFF)
  [APU-IDLE-RING] last 16 of 17356, oldest first:
              3D:v1[RC]<-TVL  x15 and one 3D:v1[RC]<-v1
  [APU-IDLE] 17356 idle-voice traps over 18 distinct voices;
              busiest: v1=13957 v5=3203 v3=81 ...

Read that in order:

  relink=209 of 388     FIFTY-FOUR PERCENT of VOICE_ON top inserts are for a
                        handle ALREADY REACHABLE from the list head. Rings are
                        not an edge case; they are what this title does. The
                        denominator is the positive control and the ratio is a
                        real one this time -- both counters are incremented on
                        the same event, one line apart.
  walks_with_a_cycle    184,983 list walks reached the same voice twice.
    =184983
  every entry carries C every one of the last sixteen raises is for a voice
                        that has been seen twice in a single walk.
  v1=13957 of 17356     one voice, in a ring, taking 80% of all traps -- the
                        same shape as the one-entry cycle written up on 15 Sep,
                        but at length >= 2 where REON_HEAD_NOP cannot see it.

broken=0 is the control working as intended: the counters moved with the
behaviour change OFF, so nothing about this number is an artefact of a fix.

WHAT TO DO NEXT, and it is an A/B not an edit: run with
RECOMP_APU_CYCLE_BREAK=1 and compare against the arm above. The switch stops
the walk at the revisit instead of spinning to the 256-iteration cap. Expect
walks_with_a_cycle unchanged, broken to rise to meet it, and the interesting
question to be what happens to v1's 13,957 traps and to the fault rate.

IT MUST NOT BE DEFAULTED ON UNTIL THAT SAYS SO ACROSS AT LEAST FIVE RUNS. The
fault fires in roughly one run in five with everything off, so a single clean
run proves nothing -- this is the exact rule that came out of shipping the lock
guard on an argument.

CAVEAT ON GETTING THESE RUNS: with a live audio device the scripted boot
reaches gameplay in roughly one attempt in three (see the long note at the top
of play_scripted.sh -- the tension is real and there is no trick for it). Run 1
of this batch stayed on the title screen with on=4; run 2 reached gameplay.
Budget several attempts per arm.


=============================================================================
5. SMALLER, FIXED
=============================================================================

- voice_off posted MCPX_HW_NOTIFIER_SSLA_DONE unconditionally, with no check of
  the prior ACTIVE_VOICE. Retiring an already-retired voice re-posts into guest
  memory and re-raises FEVINTSTS|FENINTSTS -- a route to DirectSound touching a
  torn-down object, independent of the idle trap and not in anyone's model of
  the crash. The arithmetic says it happens: off=415 against on=409 in
  gpuvsh565, so at least six voices were retired twice. COUNTED, not
  suppressed: suppressing it is a guess about hardware and this model has been
  burned by shipping one of those. [APU-VOICE2] off_already=.

- SET_VOICE_TAR_HRTF indexed d->vp.filters[] with FECV as a SIGNED int, guarded
  only from above, while every other reader casts it to uint16_t. A negative
  value passed the test and wrote out of bounds. This title never writes a
  handle >= 0x100 so it is a code property rather than a live bug; the
  disagreement between the two idioms is what was fixed.

- voice_resample re-read rs->ncarry between testing it and computing the
  memmove length. voice_reset_filters runs from VOICE_ON on a GUEST thread
  while this runs on the FRAME thread, so a reset landing in that gap made
  (size_t)(0 - 1) == SIZE_MAX the memmove length: a host SEGV, in a subsystem
  that already has an unexplained crash. Closed with one local.


=============================================================================
6. STILL OPEN
=============================================================================

From the audit, not acted on, in rough order of value:

- THE WALK DOES NOT UNLINK. Nothing in src/apu ever removes a voice from a
  list; removal is entirely the guest's job (see the comment at apu_core.c:130).
  That is believed to match hardware, but combined with section 4 it means our
  view of the lists can only ever diverge from the guest's, never re-converge.

- RECOMP_APU_SELFLINK_END does not honour the driver's contract. link(v)==v is
  CMcpxVoiceClient's documented "not in any list" marker, written by
  SetupVoiceProcessor for all 256 voices at boot. With the switch off we treat
  it as a successor and raise for a voice the guest has told us it removed;
  with it on we terminate, which is also wrong because our insert has by then
  overwritten a real successor. The correct reading at the HEAD is "this list
  is empty", which is neither behaviour on offer.

- THERE IS NO APU INTERRUPT. pci_irq_assert/deassert are empty stubs and
  nothing in src/kernel or the harness injects one. SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE reaches
  the guest ONLY by polling FECTL/FEDECMETH/FEDECPARAM. Every comment in
  apu_vp.c that reasons about "raising an interrupt" or "126,181 guest
  interrupts" is reasoning about a delivery mechanism that does not exist here.
  Practical consequence: the window in which the decode pair must hold still is
  not "until the ISR runs", it is "until the guest's next poll" -- unbounded and
  not under our control. Nobody has measured that interval, and it is the real
  width of the FEDEC corruption window. mcpx_apu_read already sees the polls;
  histogramming raise-to-next-poll is one counter and one run.

- Voice-list heads are zero-initialised, so all three lists are headed by
  voice 0 between SECTL being enabled and the guest writing TVL.
  mcpx_apu_reset_locked, which would fix this, HAS NO CALLERS -- it is dead
  code. Measured currently benign (never_on=0 across every run, with raises in
  the tens of thousands as the positive control), but the never_on instrument
  only covers the inactive branch: if voice 0's ACTIVE_VOICE happened to be set
  in that uninitialised RAM the walk would PROCESS it with no counter anywhere.

- mcpx_apu_shutdown can hang: mcpx_apu_wait_for_idle waits on d->is_idle, which
  the frame thread only sets when no software-mixer voice is active.
  Shutdown-only, low priority.

- get_data_ptr is called with max_sge = 0xFFFFFFFF at both call sites, so its
  bounds assert can never fire. The mask in apu_shim.h prevents a host OOB, but
  arbitrary guest memory can be played as audio.

- voice_resample extrapolates past its carry window when rate < 1 (a positive
  PITCH, source above 48 kHz). Measured unreachable so far: every [VOICE-RATE]
  line in the tree reports rate min >= 1.0, with the same line's max moving as
  the positive control.

- E1/E2 races, static only, medium confidence: d->regs[top_reg] is
  read-modify-written unlocked in VOICE_ON while the guest's own TVL write goes
  through mcpx_apu_write also unlocked. If a guest `TVL = next` lands between
  our read and our write it is LOST, and the voice the guest just removed is
  relinked into our list with its owner already cleared -- a second, independent
  route to the same fatal state as section 4. Depends on DirectSound genuinely
  submitting from two threads, which was not established. d->vp.ssl[v] is
  likewise written from both threads with no lock.

Not from the audit, carried forward:

- Performance. 16.37 ms mean at gameplay, p50 16.3, which straddles 60 fps
  rather than clearing it. The target is p99 < 16.68 ms, not the mean, because
  the guest is capped at 59.94 Hz by emulated vblank and kernel_bridge.c drops
  missed periods -- so every frame over 16.683 ms permanently costs a
  simulation step. Known headroom: depth read-back debt (~1.1-1.5 ms), narrow
  per-vertex copies (512 bytes copied to deliver ~64, ~0.7-1.0 ms), skipping
  the surface-swap sync on a cache hit (~1.35 ms, needs a texture-overlap
  counter first). The architectural prize is fixed-function vertices: 134 ns of
  frame each against 35 ns on the GPU path, 6.7 ms of a 16.4 ms frame. Note
  that in the title-screen scene measured today, vsh draws were 396984 GPU and
  0 CPU -- the fixed-function cost is a gameplay-scene cost.

- Upstream is 80 commits ahead with translator/lifter fixes worth merging.

- Renderer defects recorded and not fixed: clip_position models a vertex shader
  that does not exist; nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth returns 0 mid-pixel-loop
  after committing pixels; a retained depth buffer is re-read at new surface
  geometry; "depth ownership is exclusive" is not enforced when hw_depth_upload
  fails; shade() drops the CPU's modulate clamp; three sinks implement three
  z-range policies; the HLSL emitter has a 4th divergence around output w.

```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_OPAQUE_DRAWS_NEVER_READ_THE_DESTINATION.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER, 16 Sep 2026
THE OPAQUE DRAWS NEVER READ THE DESTINATION

Supersedes HANDOVER_2026-09-15_SIX_DEFECTS_FIXED_AND_THE_PICTURE_IS_STILL_WRONG.txt.

That file's open item 1 -- "run the depth and stencil bisect arms to a result.
This is the whole remaining search space" -- is run, and the answer is negative
on both arms. The search space was not what it said. The cause was found
elsewhere, on the same day, and one existing switch removes it.


1. THE HEADLINE
================
RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=3 RENDERS THE HARDWARE PATH CLEAN AT GAMEPLAY.

Sixteen arms were run today, each 280 s, one at a time, reaching gameplay, with
24 captured frames apiece. The decisive three were taken against ONE pinned
binary, same pad, run serially:

  arm    mode  what it does                          blobs  x0 mod 4  frames
  hw       1   dithered AND blended draws only        9676     43%    CORRUPT
  rog2     2   every BLENDED draw reads dst under     11464    40%    CORRUPT
               raster_order_group(0)
  rog      3   EVERY draw reads dst under              8133     30%    CLEAN
               raster_order_group(0)
  sw       -   software path, the reference               -     30%    CLEAN

`x0 mod 4` is the artefact's structural fingerprint: the fraction of corruption
blocks whose left edge lands on a 4-pixel grid, against 25% by chance. The
clean software control reads 30%. Mode 3 returns the hardware path to that
number, and the frames are clean by eye across all 24.

WHAT THIS LOCALISES. Mode 2 ALREADY takes every blended draw off the
fixed-function blend unit and gives it a destination read. It is still corrupt.
Mode 3 adds only the UNBLENDED draws. So the fixed-function blend unit is not
the cause -- it was already bypassed for blended draws in the arm that failed.
THE FIX COMES FROM GIVING OPAQUE, UNBLENDED GEOMETRY A DESTINATION READ UNDER
raster_order_group(0).

A trivial confound is ruled out by the same three arms: rog2 did FEWER draws
than rog (457,192 against 797,902; 56.9M triangles against 106.6M) and is the
corrupt one, so "fewer draws renders cleaner" is contradicted outright.

IT IS NOT SLOWER. rog rasterised 106.6M triangles in its 280 s against hw's
99.6M, with 797,902 hardware draws against 735,206 -- more work in the same
wall clock. That is one host and one scene, and it is not a frame-time A/B.
Treat it as "no cost was visible", not as "measured faster".


2. THE MECHANISM, SETTLED
==========================
Mode 3 changes TWO things at once, and the three arms in section 1 cannot
separate them:

  (a) opaque draws gain a destination read under raster_order_group(0)
  (b) the encoder stops MIXING two blending modes against the same pixels --
      under modes 1 and 2 a batched encoder alternates between fs_hw (writes
      colour(0), never reads it, fixed-function blend) and fs_hw_blend (reads
      colour(0) under raster_order_group(0), blend unit disabled), and nothing
      flushes the batch between them: batch_flush() fires on
      `hw != batch_encoder_hw`, not on a pipeline change.

RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=0 separates them, and it was run. Mode 0 removes
fs_hw_blend entirely: NO mixing anywhere, and NO raster ordering anywhere. It
is CORRUPT. The full ladder, all on the one pinned binary:

  mode  coverage                              blobs   x0 mod 4   frames
    0   no draw reads dst; no mixing          12518      36%     CORRUPT
    1   dithered AND blended draws (default)   9676      43%     CORRUPT
    2   every blended draw                    11464      40%     CORRUPT
    3   every draw                             8133      30%     CLEAN
    -   software control                       8635      30%     CLEAN

Monotone and unambiguous: partial coverage leaves the artefact regardless of
whether the encoder mixes blending modes, and only FULL coverage goes clean,
landing on the software control's own number.

SO (b) IS DEAD AND (a) IS THE MECHANISM: opaque, unblended geometry writes the
colour attachment with no destination read and no raster ordering.

Mode 0 also carries its own separate defect -- it deliberately puts the dither
on the wrong side of the blend, measured in this file at 8192 of 65536 pixels
on the dither's own 4x4 lattice -- which is why its blob count is the highest
of the five. That contaminates the statistic but not the eye, and what mode 0's
frames show is the BLOCK artefact: black rectangles holding fragments of other
buildings, not a flickering checkerboard on blended surfaces. The two are not
confusable and the judgement was made on the pictures.

DO NOT SHIP MODE 3 BY FLIPPING THE SWITCH. It is still spelled as a diagnostic.
The principled change is for the hardware path to use ONE uniform access mode
rather than choosing per draw, with a frame-time A/B behind it and a gate that
fails without it. That is the next commit, not this one.


3. THE SYMPTOM WAS MIS-DESCRIBED, AND THAT IS WHY DEPTH WAS RANKED FIRST
=========================================================================
The previous handover, section 4: "the speckle is BLACK -- pixels where nothing
was written and the clear colour shows through. That is fragments being
rejected, which is the depth or stencil unit." Measured from frame dumps:

  * Not pixels. BLOCKS -- median 5x5 px, largest 133x51, 528 in one frame.
  * Not one colour. They hold RECOGNISABLE FRAGMENTS OF OTHER SCENE CONTENT --
    pieces of buildings, HUD glyphs, rails. A rejected fragment leaves the
    destination untouched and therefore shows exactly one thing.
  * Not rare. Every frame, heavily.

The capture is what corrected it. Every earlier attempt scored this with an
image statistic across arms that never reach the same scene; this one captures
24 gameplay frames per arm and looks at them.


4. THE ELIMINATION TABLE
=========================
Every row is a 280 s gameplay run with 24 captured frames unless marked
otherwise, and each backend NAMED ITS OWN SWITCH STATE in its report -- which
is new, and is why these are not void (section 6).

  STILL CORRUPT:
    RECOMP_METAL_HW_DEPTH_ALWAYS=1   depth compare forced ALWAYS (states=6)
    RECOMP_METAL_HW_NO_STENCIL=1     stencil unit ignored        (states=6)
    RECOMP_METAL_SURFACE_CACHE=0     no retained surfaces
    RECOMP_METAL_BATCH_MAX=64        batches bounded
    RECOMP_METAL_DRAIN=1             every sync drains the whole queue, 22,072
    RECOMP_METAL_FENCE=1             an MTLFence updated after fragment and
                                     waited before VERTEX on every pass, 50,149
                                     updates -- SEE THE CAVEAT IN SECTION 7.2
    RECOMP_METAL_565=1               colour attachment 16 B/px -> 2 B/px
    RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=2      every blended draw in the shader

  MUCH WORSE:
    RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=0             one pass per draw. Solid black rectangles
                                     64 px wide, left AND right edges on a
                                     64-px grid 17 of 18 times (chance 1.6%),
                                     bottoms on a 32-row grid 16 of 18.
                                     64 x 32 x 16 B = 32 KB = one Apple tile.
                                     THAT coarse artefact is tile-shaped.

  MEASURED ZERO, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL:
    RECOMP_METAL_READBACK_AUDIT=1    19,777 gameplay syncs checked, 0 raced,
                                     0 pixels changed after a full queue drain.
                                     THE READ-BACK IS FAITHFUL; the corruption
                                     is already in the texture when it is read.
    surface.hazardTrackingMode       reads `tracked`, asked of the object. Not
                                     heap-suballocated, not silently untracked.

  BY CONSTRUCTION, no run needed:
    the vertex ring      ring_reserve() calls batch_flush() BEFORE checking the
                         next slab's in-flight count, so a batch can never span
                         a wrap.
    the texture cache    a fresh MTLBuffer per upload; the hit path re-verifies
                         with memcmp. Never mutated under an in-flight buffer.
    the presenter race   open item 6 of the previous handover. The dumps are
                         written from the PUSHER THREAD at FLIP_STALL, the same
                         thread that writes s_snap, so they cannot see it -- and
                         they show the artefact anyway.
    the texture path     shade() is shared byte for byte, and the software arm
                         is clean at the same scene.

THE 4x4 GRANULARITY IS NOT THE TILE, and the arithmetic settles it:

    RGBA32Float   16 + 4 + 1 = 21 B/px  ->  32 KB tile is 32x32
    B5G6R5Unorm    2 + 4 + 1 =  7 B/px  ->  32 KB tile is 64x64

A tile-derived granularity would have moved 4x between those arms. The measured
granularity is the SAME 4x4 in both. So the fine artefact is in pixels, not in
bytes, and only the coarse 64x32 rectangles under RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=0 are the
tile. The one 4x4 screen-space lattice anywhere in this codebase is the ordered
dither matrix, b[(xy.y&3)*4+(xy.x&3)].


5. A SECOND, SEPARATE BUG: A REPRODUCIBLE GUEST SIGSEGV
========================================================
    SIGNAL: SIGSEGV (11)
    HOST FAULT ADDRESS: 0x00000070FFFFFFBE      (guest 0xFFFFFFBE)
    HOST PC: sub_001A2E2E +0x670                (DSOUND, VA 0x0019E340..)
    GUEST REGISTERS: EAX=FFFFFFB4

Identical function, offset and fault address in four runs today. It fires when
the run's timing is perturbed:

    SDL_AUDIODRIVER=no_such_driver                    died at t=41 s
    RECOMP_METAL_CB_STATS=1 CB_GPU=1, hardware arm    died at t=35 s
    RECOMP_METAL_CB_STATS=1 CB_GPU=1, software arm    died at t=35 s
    RECOMP_METAL_SHADER_BLEND=3, first attempt        died at t=35 s

It is PROBABILISTIC, not deterministic: the same SHADER_BLEND=3 arm re-run
immediately afterwards reached gameplay and ran the full 280 s. And it is not
simply "slower crashes" -- RECOMP_METAL_BATCH=0 is far heavier and survived.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TODAY: the hardware/software COMMAND-BUFFER OVERLAP COMPARISON
IS NOT MEASURED. Both arms died at t=35 s in the logos. The numbers they did
produce (overlapped 726 against 765) are BOOT-PHASE ONLY and must not be quoted
as a gameplay result.


6. INSTRUMENTS BUILT TODAY
===========================
  frame_bisect.sh      Runs arms ONE AT A TIME against a pinned binary,
                       captures 24 gameplay frames each, writes ARM.txt from
                       the BACKEND'S OWN REPORT rather than from the
                       environment it set, and refuses to score an arm that
                       never reached gameplay -- it prints "*** this arm proves
                       nothing ***" and says why. That guard fired three times
                       today and was right every time.

  [METAL] bisect:      RECOMP_METAL_HW_DEPTH_ALWAYS and _NO_STENCIL now name
                       their state AND count the states they altered. They were
                       read inline in hw_depth_state_for and were INVISIBLE IN
                       THE LOG, which is why the earlier pass at this bisect had
                       to be voided. states>0 is the positive control: the
                       switch being on is what the environment says; states>0 is
                       the backend saying it reached the descriptor.

  [METAL] shader blend mode N
                       Was a boolean over four states. An arm that cannot name
                       itself cannot be verified, and mode 2 versus mode 3 is
                       the whole result in section 1.

  [METAL] surface hazard tracking
                       Asks the MTLTexture what it is rather than assuming what
                       the descriptor requested.

  RECOMP_METAL_READBACK_AUDIT
                       Reads the surface, commits and waits an EMPTY command
                       buffer to drain the queue properly, reads again, counts
                       pixels that changed. Separates "the corruption is in the
                       texture" from "the read-back caught it mid-store" -- two
                       different bugs nothing else here could tell apart.

  RECOMP_METAL_DRAIN   Waits for the QUEUE, not for one command buffer. Apple
                       documents only that a command buffer STARTS after those
                       ahead of it start; nothing about completion order. This
                       backend has always assumed more. Measured: changes no
                       pixel, so the assumption holds on this host today. It is
                       still undocumented, and that is now written down.

  RECOMP_METAL_FENCE   An explicit MTLFence between passes. See 7.2 -- the arm
                       as written may not test what it looks like.

  RECOMP_FB_DUMP_FLIP=<stride>[:<after-seconds>]
  RECOMP_FB_DUMP_DRAW=<stride>[:<after-seconds>]
                       The 24 capture slots used to start counting at process
                       start, so any stride large enough to still be capturing
                       at gameplay spent most of them on the logos. SECONDS,
                       NOT A PRESENT INDEX, because the arms do not run at the
                       same speed -- this project's oldest measurement trap.


7. OPEN, RANKED
================
  1. TURN MODE 3 INTO A FIX. Section 2 has settled WHAT it is fixing: every
     hardware draw needs a destination read under raster_order_group(0), not
     just the blended ones. So the change is to stop choosing the fragment tail
     per draw and give the hardware path one access mode, with

       * a frame-time A/B behind it. The "no cost was visible" in section 1 is
         one host, one scene, and triangle counts from runs that got different
         distances through the title. It is not a measurement of frame time.
       * a gate that FAILS without it. Every device gate passed for weeks on
         this renderer because none of them could get the GPU behind the
         producer; a gate that cannot reproduce the artefact cannot protect
         the fix. The cheapest honest one is the ladder in section 2 -- four
         modes, x0 mod 4 against the software control -- which is a scripted
         run, not a unit test, and should be named as such.
       * the switch kept, as the control arm. =0 is the "before" picture and
         the only way to re-measure the cost later in one binary.

  2. THE FENCE ARM MAY NOT HAVE TESTED PASS ORDERING. It waits
     `beforeStages:MTLRenderStageVertex`. A colour attachment's
     MTLLoadActionLoad is fragment-side tile setup, not a vertex-stage
     operation, so a vertex-scoped wait does not obviously order it. The 50,149
     updates prove the arm RAN, not that it covered the load. Re-run with
     beforeStages:MTLRenderStageFragment before treating pass ordering as
     closed.

  3. DOES [[position]].z REFLECT MTLDepthClipModeClamp? setDepthClipMode:Clamp
     is applied to every encoder, and all three fragment tails then implement
     the guest's CULL policy from i.p.z. If Metal hands the shader the CLAMPED
     window-space z, then for JSRF's measured range (z_lo=0, z_hi=16777215)
     the discard can NEVER fire and the entire z-range policy is inert. One
     atomic counter on the discard branch and one run answers it.

  4. THE DSOUND SIGSEGV (section 5). Reproducible on demand, blocks the overlap
     measurement, and is a guest-correctness bug independent of the renderer.

  5. UPSTREAM IS 80 COMMITS AHEAD and none of them touch src/nv2a -- upstream
     has no Metal backend. Their graphics work is in src/d3d, which this title
     never calls. WORTH MERGING ANYWAY for the translator and lifter fixes: sar
     sign-extension, INC/DEC carry, jbe/ja after and/or/xor, MMX flag
     preservation, x87 rounding, the uninitialised generated ebp. Those are
     guest-CPU correctness and we have an unexplained guest fault. Separate
     task: merging means regenerating, which is not bit-stable.


8. DEFECTS FOUND BY REVIEW TODAY, NONE OF WHICH IS THE ARTEFACT
================================================================
Ranked by the reviewer's own ordering. Each carries a file and a reason.

  1. clip_position() MODELS A VERTEX SHADER THAT DOES NOT EXIST. It clamps z;
     the real vs() explicitly does not and says so in capitals. The audit then
     applies Metal's clip volume to the clamped value, so the far plane cannot
     fire by construction -- and the retraction recorded in nv2a_metal.m
     ("discarded by the far plane 0 ... the vertex shader clamps z") rests on
     that model, not on the shader. The 37.7M-triangle measurement quoted there
     measured the model. audit_z_below/audit_z_above already collect the data
     to redo it.

  2. nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth RETURNS 0 FROM INSIDE THE PIXEL LOOP,
     after an arbitrary prefix of the triangle's pixels and their depth and
     stencil updates have already been committed to guest RAM. Its own header
     promises "no guest memory is accessed here", and the caller counts the
     return as a clean rejection. Should continue, or hoist the test.

  3. A RETAINED DEPTH BUFFER IS RE-READ AT THE NEW SURFACE'S GEOMETRY. The
     bounds check is gated on use_zeta, so a depth-less draw at a larger clip
     size reads the previous zeta at the new width and height -- hundreds of KB
     past the validated range.

  4. nv2a_metal_discard() AND reject() INVALIDATE THE LIVE BINDING BUT NOT THE
     SURFACE CACHE, where nv2a_metal_invalidate() does. After a discard the CPU
     writes the clear into guest RAM, the next draw takes the upload path, the
     slot matches, and the PRE-CLEAR textures are rebound -- the clear is lost
     entirely. Latent: RECOMP_CLEAR_DISCARD defaults off and the runs report
     `clear discards=0`. reject() is a hardware-path-only route into the same
     hole the moment a fallback occurs.

  5. stencil_surface IS UPLOADED FROM UNINITIALISED HEAP UNDER
     RECOMP_METAL_565=1 -- the buffer is filled only in the non-565 branch and
     the replaceRegion is unconditional.

  6. "DEPTH OWNERSHIP IS EXCLUSIVE" IS NOT ENFORCED when hw_depth_upload fails:
     `hw = hw_state_on() && hw_depth_tex && hw_stencil_tex` silently takes the
     software tail with the hardware path on, which is exactly what the comment
     beside it forbids. Should be hw_state_on() alone with a reject().

  7. shade() DROPS THE CPU'S fminf(1,..) CLAMP ON THE MODULATE PATH, so an
     over-bright vertex colour carries a value above 1 into an RGBA32Float
     attachment where the CPU rasteriser clamped at the multiply.

  8. THREE SINKS IMPLEMENT THREE DIFFERENT Z-RANGE POLICIES. fs does CULL and
     CLAMP; fs_hw and fs_hw_blend do CULL only; nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth
     reads none of z_clip_min, z_clip_max or z_cull and saturates
     unconditionally. The oracle can therefore never disagree with either tail
     here -- one concrete thing the gate structurally cannot test.

  9. A5: the comment at d.depthWriteEnabled asserts that nv2a_texture_copy.c
     gates depth writes on the test. It does not -- its zp is non-NULL when
     depth_test||stencil_test -- so with stencil-only and the depth mask set,
     the CPU writes depth and both GPU tails do not.

  WITHDRAWN, and worth recording because it was reported as live: the stencil
  writeMask divergence in hw_depth_state_for. prepare() assigns stencil_write
  only inside `if (M(0x32c))`, which also sets stencil_test, so
  stencil_write implies stencil_test for every state the executor can produce.
  The code divergence is real; it is unreachable.


9. HOW TO MEASURE THIS, PROVED AGAIN TODAY
===========================================
WHAT WORKS: looking at the frames. 24 per arm as a contact sheet, then
magnified NEAREST-neighbour on a flat surface. It separated the arms in about a
minute, on the first attempt, after six metrics had failed over two days.

WHAT WORKS AS A SCORE: only a structural property the artefact has and scene
content cannot. `x0 mod 4` qualifies -- it is a within-frame ratio against
chance, and the clean software control reads 30% against the corrupt path's
43%. That is the same shape of argument fb_score.py's `tile` metric uses, and
it is the bar.

WHAT STILL DOES NOT WORK: a generic image statistic. An isolated-dark-blob
count written this morning scored the KNOWN-GOOD software arm at 835
exact-black pixels against the corrupt hardware arm's 761 -- ranking the good
arm worse, for the fifth time.

THE MISTAKES MADE TODAY, all one mistake: a source file was edited while a
bisect was running (the staleness guard refused two arms, correctly), and the
bisect SCRIPT was edited while running, four times (sh re-reads by byte offset,
so the trailing summary broke each time). Once this was asserted to be safe
without checking. No conclusion was corrupted, because the guards held. Do not
touch a measurement's inputs while it is live, and check rather than assert it.

A NOTE ON WAITING FOR A RUN: `pgrep -f "frame_bisect.sh <name>"` matches the
WAITER'S OWN command line, so a shell that polls for it waits forever on
itself. Two of those were left spinning today. ab_switch.sh's header already
warns about watching the wrong thing; this is the same trap one level up.
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_VBLANK_WAS_THE_HANG_AND_THE_FENCE_IS_PER_TRIANGLE.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 (fourth of the day) -- THE VBLANK WAS THE HANG, AND THE
FENCE TURNS OUT TO BE PER-TRIANGLE

Read CLAUDE.md first. This supersedes the three earlier handovers of 16 Sep
wherever it contradicts them, and it contradicts them in several places.

=============================================================================
1. WHAT IS FIXED, MEASURED, COMMITTED AND PUSHED
=============================================================================

THE VBLANK SUMMARY WAS LOST AND NOTHING COULD RESTORE IT.  bridge_nv2a_mirror
_intr modelled only half of PMC_INTR_0: it cleared the summary bit when the
source was clear and never set it when the source was set. Any interleaving
that lost the bit lost it permanently, because the re-raise is gated on the
source being clear. Vblank delivery latched shut mid-run in EVERY run:

    off  delivered=1738 raised=1910 unacked_skips=8266   10.2 Hz
    on   delivered=9859 raised=10133 unacked_skips=2     58.0 Hz

The PGRAPH half of that same function has had the identical repair since the
anti-graffiti-screen hang, and its comment describes this failure verbatim.
The PCRTC half was never written. RECOMP_NV2A_PMC_UPMIRROR, default off.

THIS WAS THE PLAYER'S "STUCK ON NOW LOADING" AND THEIR SILENT MUSIC. The
"[ADX] tick STUCK" line that three sessions read as an audio bug is a CRI
worker that parks in NtSuspendThread and is resumed once per vblank. No
vblank, no resume. It is not the ADX server and the fault is nowhere near
suspend/resume.

THE VOICE LIST SPLICED VOICES IN FRONT OF THEMSELVES.  walks_with_a_cycle
93,611 -> 0 with relink staying non-zero (67 -> 51) and on_top in the churn
band both sides. The cross-check holds exactly: mtf_head + mtf_deep = 28 + 23
= 51 = relink, counted independently by two walks. The 256-iteration walk cap
fires 93,611 times a run and NOBODY HAD EVER SEEN IT: it reported through a
DPRINTF compiled out by a DEBUG_MCPX that is never defined.

Also pushed: the index cap raise (4096 -> 16384), ARRAY_ELEMENT32 decode
(407,055 indices a run that were silently dropped), five kernel defects
(below), the dot-product zero rule, fixed-function diagnostics, and the
restored window/fullscreen work.

=============================================================================
2. FIVE KERNEL DEFECTS, ONE OF WHICH HAD ALREADY RUINED A RUN
=============================================================================

g_kernel_call_count WAS A SIGNED INT. On overflow it goes negative, which
turns full per-call tracing permanently ON and the [KERNEL] summary and
ordinal histogram permanently OFF. Already happened in
render-investigation/a1-exec-walkers-tutorial-2: last summary at
2,141,517,829 calls, then 10,632,107 negative-numbered lines, and the call
rate collapsed 56x. Current builds hit INT_MAX at t=342 s -- inside a player
session, outside the 240-280 s the harness runs, which is why no A/B crossed
it. Check any log with: grep -c '\[KERNEL\] #-'

THE TIMER TABLE published the armed flag first and the deadline last with a
whole GetTickCount() call between, polled lock-free by every guest thread. A
poller in that window fires the DPC immediately instead of after the delay.
Now a seqlock. FIRST RUN REPORTED claim_lost=9 -- nine occasions where two
pollers raced for one firing, so the race was real and being hit.

THE TRAP HANDLER still opened a writable window on the guarded NV2A pages on
every acknowledge (~60/s) -- the thing CLAUDE.md forbids absolutely -- and
g_pcrtc_windows read 0 the whole time because its only increment is in a
branch that stopped executing when the alias landed.

=============================================================================
3. THE FENCE: EVERYTHING IT IS NOT, AND THE ONE THING IT IS
=============================================================================

RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT. Do not re-litigate these without new evidence:

  batch truncation      no-room=0 with biggest batch asked for 9681 of 16384
  INLINE_ARRAY          biggest batch 12 words of 16384
  DRAW_ARRAYS           0.9% of batches, 0.01% of indices, <1 batch/frame
  alpha test / blend    rejected=0 in two gameplay runs two days apart
  texture cache         a hit requires a full memcmp; stale bytes impossible
  mip base arithmetic   agrees across all three implementations, term by term
  levels clamp, filter  correct
  VIEWPORT_SCALE        VOID -- see below
  texture matrix zero   TMAT0 is all zeros but its ENABLE is off

THE VIEWPORT SCALE CLAIM WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE. An audit found that
nv2a_ff.c never applies NV097_SET_VIEWPORT_SCALE, which is true, and
concluded 58.8% of draws collapse to a dot. Measured instead:

    in=(4505.22 -743.87 0 1) -> clip/w=(768.14 150.33 16785482)  surface 640x480

Screen pixels. D3D bakes the scale into the composite matrix. Applying it
again multiplies the screen by 320 TWICE. The counter-evidence needed no run:
the picture is broadly correct and could not be if that were happening.

WHAT THE SYMPTOM ACTUALLY IS, from the player's 23 s capture analysed at the
game's own frame rate (974 unique frames out of 2,793 captured):

  AN OBJECT DOES NOT VANISH WHOLESALE. It renders as a THIN SKELETAL OUTLINE
  in one frame, a sliver in the next, and nothing in the next.

That is PER-TRIANGLE dropping, not per-batch, and it reframes the whole
search: every hypothesis above was about losing a batch. The relevant
instrument is already in the tree and already says something:

    degenerate split: nonfinite-area=0 strip-stitch(duplicate vertex)=30337822
    collinear-distinct=265785, of which 260714 were on screen with every w>0

260,714 triangles a run, on screen, every w positive, dropped because
area() returned exactly 0. area() is a float32 2D cross product
(nv2a_metal.m:2841) on screen coordinates, and the reject is `ar==0` exactly
(:2878). NOT YET A CONCLUSION: distinct indices pointing at coincident
vertices is also how strips legitimately stitch. The next step is to split
that bucket by whether the three positions are actually distinct, and to
compute the area in double for comparison.

STILL OPEN AND UNMEASURED: the dot-product zero rule (RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO) is
the last surviving batch-level candidate. It removes all 13 shader-diff
mismatches over the title's 126 programs and costs nothing measurable (57.3
-> 58.6 fps), but the scripted A/B could not produce a matched scene, so
whether it changes the picture is unproven.

=============================================================================
4. INSTRUMENTS THAT LIE, FOUND TODAY
=============================================================================

Four, and every one of them had been read as evidence:

  no-room=            has NO term for the INLINE_ARRAY path. Quoted all day as
                      "nothing is being dropped"; covered two paths of three.
  texcoord-q=         fires for non-finite OR q<=0, and q<=0 is arithmetically
                      impossible for 123 of the title's 126 programs, which
                      never write oT.w. The bucket is mostly NaN.
  fedec_hold          printed "on (default)" while the accessor defaults to 0.
                      "held=0 (fedec_hold on (default))" read as "armed, never
                      needed"; the truth was "off, never once exercised".
  g_pcrtc_windows     0 while the trap handler opened one 60 times a second.

Add to CLAUDE.md's known-bad list, now done: `N triangles fully off-surface`
is incremented only in the CPU rasteriser, so it is dead on every Metal run.

AND ONE I BROKE. The [d3d8_gl] blit line -- the instrument that tells
"picture correct" from "picture black" -- compares the guest centre pixel to
the drawable centre, and matched exactly only because the drawable was an
exact 4x the guest. Full screen makes it 4.52x, so the sample is a blend of
neighbours and the two sides no longer agree (29 51 63 -> 17 46 4D). NOT
FIXED. Move the sample to a texel centre before reading that line as strict.

=============================================================================
5. HOW THE EXPERIMENTS KEPT GOING WRONG
=============================================================================

SCENE-MATCHING IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT COST A RETRACTION. A confident
"DRAW_ARRAYS is the black screen", with exact arithmetic over four runs,
compared two gameplay runs against two attract-loop runs. Check
[APU-VOICE] on= before scoring any arm: 148-453 is gameplay, 4-12 is parked.

AN ARM THAT PARKS IS NOT A CONTROL. Three A/B arms were scored before the
positive control was read: relink=0 (of 5 top inserts) means the run never
reached voice churn and every other counter in it is meaningless.

LIVE AUDIO WAS THE WRONG ARM FOR A VOICE-LIST A/B. With a device live these
runs barely start voices (on=5-12 against 148-453 with it off), so all three
arms parked. The ring is a DATA-STRUCTURE bug -- the counters that score it
do not need an audio device. Only judging how it SOUNDS does.

ZSH DOES NOT WORD-SPLIT UNQUOTED VARIABLES. `env $SW ...` passed both
switches as ONE argument, so the second was never set and the log said
`move_to_front OFF` in an arm named "both". Read your own switch-state lines.

THE EARLY ABORT PAYS FOR ITSELF. ~20% of runs never leave the title and used
to cost 280 s each; ABORT_AT=60 catches them with 2x margin, because
successful runs reach a mission at t=29.5 s.

=============================================================================
6. OPEN, RANKED
=============================================================================

 1. The fence, as a PER-TRIANGLE problem. Split collinear-distinct by whether
    the positions are genuinely distinct; compute area in double and compare.
    Section 3.
 2. Does RECOMP_VSH_DP_ZERO change the picture? It is enabled in the player's
    paths.conf; their eyes are the experiment the harness cannot run.
 3. The player reports the character jumping/floating. DP4 transforms
    position, so it may share a cause with 2. Unmeasured.
 4. A large black region along the bottom of several captured frames, in both
    arms of the last A/B. Unexplained, on no list.
 5. Fix the blit instrument's sample point. Section 4.
 6. Sound effects never START (on= freezes) -- a self-linked voice pins the

    on.
 7. The boot question: 3 of 12 runs with the ring patch compiled reached
```

`docs/jsrf/handovers/HANDOVER_2026-09-16_TWO_METHODS_THE_EXECUTOR_NEVER_DECODED.txt`:

```txt
HANDOVER 2026-09-16 -- TWO METHODS THE EXECUTOR NEVER DECODED

Companion to HANDOVER_2026-09-16_THE_INSTRUMENTS_WERE_LYING.txt, which covers
the APU. This one is the renderer, from two read-only audits run the same day:
the CPU reference rasteriser and texture path, and the pushbuffer executor plus
the two vertex-program emitters.

Read CLAUDE.md first. The headline finding here was found the same way the APU
one was -- by checking an instrument against what actually triggers it -- and
it had been sitting in plain sight in every run's report for months.


=============================================================================
1. ARRAY_ELEMENT32 AND DRAW_ARRAYS WERE NEVER DECODED
=============================================================================

There are four ways a title hands the NV2A its vertex indices. This executor
decoded two of them.

  0x1800  NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT16   handled
  0x1818  NV097_INLINE_ARRAY      handled
  0x1808  NV097_ARRAY_ELEMENT32   NOT HANDLED
  0x1810  NV097_DRAW_ARRAYS       NOT HANDLED

The two unhandled ones fell through to `default:`, which recognises only the
two vertex-array register ranges, and so landed in the unhandled-method
histogram -- which prints them, every run, at the top of the report:

    [GPU]   0x1808 x164101
    [GPU]   0x1810 x10462

with 0x1818 and 0x1800 ABSENT from the same table. That absence is the positive
control: the histogram does distinguish handled from unhandled, and these two
were unhandled 174,563 times in a single run of measure/methodaudit.

WHAT IT COST. A batch whose indices arrive that way reaches SET_BEGIN_END(0)
with idx_count == 0, and draw_primitive returns before it increments
s_gpu.draws. So the batch is not drawn, not counted as a draw, not counted as a
vsh reject, not counted as a texture reject -- invisible to every instrument in
the file. A renderer whose picture has been called "right" was silently
dropping geometry. And a batch that mixed ELEMENT16 with ELEMENT32 kept only
the 16-bit half, so its TOPOLOGY was wrong and it was drawn anyway.

WHY IT SURVIVED SO LONG, and this is the part worth remembering.
src/kernel/nv2a_pb_scan.c's method-name table labelled 0x1808 "INLINE_ARRAY".
INLINE_ARRAY is 0x1818. So the one survey that answers "which methods does this
title use" named an unhandled method after a handled one. Anyone who looked at
that table saw a method they knew was implemented.

Checking the rest of that table against nv2a_regs.h found SEVEN more wrong
labels: 0x0B00 and 0x0B80 swapped (TRANSFORM_PROGRAM vs TRANSFORM_CONSTANT),
0x0130 "SET_FLIP_READ" for FLIP_STALL, 0x033C "SET_CULL_FACE_ENABLE" for
SET_ALPHA_FUNC, 0x0340 "SET_DEPTH_MASK" for SET_ALPHA_REF, 0x0350
"SET_CLEAR_DEPTH_VALUE" for SET_BLEND_EQUATION, 0x1D6C "SET_ZSTENCIL_CLEAR" for
SET_SEMAPHORE_OFFSET. All corrected, and INLINE_ARRAY added.

A NAME TABLE IS DOCUMENTATION THAT GETS READ AS EVIDENCE. Cross-check it
against the register header, not against memory.

BOTH METHODS ARE NOW DECODED, with the index source reported so the change is
measurable rather than asserted:

    [GPU] indices by source: elem32=N draw_arrays=N (N calls);
          dropped: too-wide=N no-room=N

elem32/draw_arrays nonzero proves those batches now reach a draw. too-wide and
no-room nonzero would mean geometry is STILL being dropped -- which is exactly
what the old code did silently, so they are printed rather than assumed zero.
idx[] is uint16_t, and an index that does not fit is counted rather than
truncated: a truncated index is geometry that draws in the wrong place and says
nothing. (nv2a_regs.h:1493 records that the hardware itself raises an exception
for a DRAW_ARRAYS start above 0xFFFF, so the guard is the right shape.)


=============================================================================
2. THE LOD GRADIENT WAS SCALED FOR A FORMAT ALREADY IN TEXELS
=============================================================================

Live on the Metal path, and present identically on the CPU one.

sample_level normalises uv by (w,h) for rgba8/dxt1/dxt3 and NOT for the fourth
accepted format, LU_IMAGE_R5G6B5 -- an image rectangle, whose coordinates are
already in texels. sample() in nv2a_texture_copy.c says so in as many words:
"Nonlinear textures use normalized coordinates, unlike image rectangles."

sample_lod multiplied the gradient by (tw,th) for all four. So an image rect
got rho multiplied by the texture width a second time: log2(640) = 9.3 where
the true lod is 0.

The levels<2 guard does not save it. That zeroes the mip INDEX; the
magnify-vs-minify decision two lines further down reads the RAW lod:

    if(lod+s.lod_bias[u]>0&&s.min_filter[u])linear=(s.min_filter[u]&1)==0;

so an image rect was permanently "minifying" and the MAG filter from
SET_TEXTURE_FILTER was discarded in favour of the MIN filter's parity. shade()
calls sample_lod unconditionally, before the combiner split, so there is no
branch that avoids it on the hardware path.

A 1:1 blit hides it -- bilinear sampled at exact texel centres is nearest --
and any blit that is offset or scaled does not: a full-screen fade or
post-process card comes out blocky when it should be smooth, or blurred when it
should be crisp. Such draws exist in this title today; measured, 30 occurrences
of

    [METAL] software fallback (initialization): combiner=0 mask=0x1 untextured=0
            format=0/0 levels=1 size=640x480 bpp=2 ...

format=0/0 is rgba8=0, dxt1=0 with levels=1 at 640x480 -- a
LU_IMAGE_R5G6B5 draw.

FIXED in both sinks: scale only what is normalised.


=============================================================================
3. THE TWO SINKS DISAGREED ABOUT DEPTH WRITES, AND THE COMMENT SAID THEY DID NOT
=============================================================================

nv2a_metal.m carried, verbatim:

    * The NV2A does not update depth when the test is disabled, and
    * neither does nv2a_texture_copy.c.

The second clause was false about the file it named. There, depth_write is
assigned OUTSIDE the depth-test guard, and the write is gated on
(depth_test || stencil_test):

    uint8_t *zp = (s->depth_test||s->stencil_test) ? depth + ... : NULL;
    if (zp && s->depth_write) { ...stamp z24... }

So a stencil-only draw with depth_write set stamped depth on the SOFTWARE arm
and not on the hardware one. They cannot both be right, and the hardware rule
is that ZWRITEENABLE does nothing with ZENABLE off -- so Metal was right.

THE REASON THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE WRONG PIXEL: the software arm is the
visual control every render A/B in this project is scored against. A control
that disagrees with hardware is worse than a wrong result; it is a wrong
oracle. Exactly the cross-file assertion CLAUDE.md warns about -- written to
justify the gate in one file, never checked against the sibling it named.

FIXED: the CPU sink now requires depth_test, and the comment records what it
used to claim.


=============================================================================
4. THE REUSE CACHE LEAKED ON EVERY REJECT PATH
=============================================================================

prepare_vertices clears its reuse bitmap by re-walking the batch's indices at
the bottom of the function. The comment above that clear already says what
happens otherwise: "entries leak across batches and a later batch reuses a
transform computed from a different vertex array, different constants or a
different program -- silently wrong geometry rather than a crash."

VSH_REJECT was a bare `return 0` from inside the per-vertex loop. Seven of the
eight exits skipped the clear. The comment was right about the consequence and
wrong that the code prevented it. Rejects are not hypothetical -- "[VSH] 21
oPos is not finite" in boot/on-3/stderr.log.

Latent only because RECOMP_VSH_REUSE is off. That is exactly the switch the
next person reaches for when chasing the frame-time p99, which is the worst
possible moment to be handed intermittently wrong geometry.

FIXED: VSH_REJECT now goes to a shared exit that does the same clear.
reuse_active had to be hoisted above the first reject, because a goto that
jumps past an initialiser leaves the object indeterminate and the earliest
reject is a hundred lines above where it was declared.


=============================================================================
5. COUNTERS THAT LIE -- RENDERER EDITION
=============================================================================

5a. "[GPU] N triangles rasterised" has three meanings and the newest arrived
    silently. One variable, s_gpu.tris_drawn, three producers: the CPU
    rasteriser (counts degenerate and culled triangles as drawn), Metal with
    CPU-side culling (post-cull), and Metal with GPU-side culling, where
    triangle()'s first statement is

        if(vsh_gpu_culling){out[(*n)++]=a;...;return;}

    skipping vertex_valid, the degenerate test and the cull test entirely.
    That third definition BECAME THE DEFAULT ON 16 SEP when RECOMP_METAL_VSH
    flipped on, and nothing said so. Any triangle-count comparison straddling
    that flip compares two different quantities.

    NOW: [METAL] triangles assembled=N culled here=N (culling on the GPU/CPU),
    and the line says outright which quantity "rasterised" is reporting.

5b. "[TEXTURE] prepared=N rejected=N" was one counter with two denominators.
    s_copy.rejected is incremented both when prepare refuses a whole DRAW and
    when triangle_depth returns 0 for one TRIANGLE. Measured in win-explode:
    rejected=3382034 beside prepared=279618, with the reasons table underneath
    summing to 766 -- so 3,381,268 of them were triangles, printed against a
    batch count, where the line reads as one draw in twelve refused.

    3.38M against 52.31M drawn is 6% of assembled triangles leaving
    nv2a_texture_copy_triangle_depth by a `return 0`. AND THERE ARE FOUR SUCH
    EXITS AFTER PIXELS HAVE ALREADY BEEN COMMITTED, not the one that is
    recorded: :699, :724, :726 and :737. Two of them test the finite-difference
    probe points at (x+1.5,y+0.5) and (x+0.5,y+1.5), which on a strongly
    projective triangle sit outside it where q legitimately crosses zero -- so
    a probe falling off the projective pole abandons the rest of the triangle
    mid-scanline.

    NOW: rejected_draw and rejected_tri are separate, with the reasons table as
    rejected_draw's positive control (the two must agree). THE FOUR MID-LOOP
    EXITS ARE NOT FIXED. Splitting rejected_tri by exit site is the next step,
    and it is one counter.

5c. "[VSH] executed batches=N rejected=N" -- batches counts only mode==2
    batches while rejected counts all of them. Measured 56% understatement in
    boot/pilot-off: executed batches=72798 against [TEXTURE] prepared=166167.
    NOT FIXED. It reads correct today only because every batch in the recent
    gameplay runs is programmable, which is why it went unnoticed.


=============================================================================
6. FOUND, VERIFIED, NOT FIXED
=============================================================================

Ranked. Every one is static unless it says measured.

- inline_layout() accepts only type 2 (F) and type 4 (UB_OGL) and returns on
  anything else, leaving s_inline_stride 0 -- and the batch then draws nothing
  with no reject anywhere. Type 0 is UB_D3D, and fetch_attr's own comment
  records that JSRF declares its diffuse colour as exactly that. s_gpu.attr[]
  is sticky across batches, so a declaration written for an array batch reaches
  an inline one. Measured latent: the sampled inline batches declare only
  a0/a9 with the type-0 attribute at size 0.

- Vertex array stride is truncated from 24 bits to 8:
  `a->stride = (param >> 8) & 0xFF;` against a 0xFFFFFF00 field. Any stride
  >= 256 aliases and every vertex of that batch reads from the wrong place,
  with no reject and no counter. Measured not reached -- every
  "[VSH] late batch attrs:" line in the tree shows st0 or st32.

- The colour half of CLEAR_SURFACE ignores both the clear rect and the
  per-channel mask, while the depth half honours the rect. The Metal resident
  clear REFUSES exactly the partial-mask case and falls straight into the CPU
  loop that gets it wrong. Measured not reached: [METAL] clear refused: mask=0.

- s_outputs[s_gpu.idx[v]] in the blend trace is indexed by the index VALUE
  where every other reader uses the index POSITION -- s_outputs is [4096][16][4]
  and idx is uint16_t, so this reads up to 16 MB past the array. Needs
  RECOMP_BLEND_TRACE, which is off.

- nv2a_vsh.c scalarises the shared C operand for paired scalar-ILU
  instructions: `sw->y = sw->z = sw->w = sw->x` destroys the MAC's third
  operand for any ADD/MAD paired with a scalar ILU. This feeds the interpreter
  AND both emitters, so it is a shared wrong answer no divergence check could
  catch. Measured not reached: decoding the 556 captured instructions found
  mul+rcc, mov+rcp, dp4+rsq, dp3+mov, arl+mov -- and zero add/mad pairings.

- a0-relative constant reads have THREE behaviours: MSL clamps to c[191], HLSL
  reads off the end of a 192-entry cbuffer, and the interpreter REFUSES the
  draw. Worse than recorded -- the HLSL header says "nothing here has been
  measured against a title program that indexes that high", and it has been
  measured now: 189 of 556 captured instructions use rel-addressing with base
  indices 107-110, so the margin is a0 <= 81.

- RECOMP_CLEAR_DISCARD does not require the depth clear rect to cover the
  surface, and if the guest never wrote SET_CLEAR_RECT the default is a 1x1
  rect. Guarded today by g_clear_refuse_rect reading 0; off by default.

- nv2a_vsh_msl.c's own header understates its file by one fix: it still says
  "LIT is still knowingly wrong" and names two fixes where the code contains
  three. The LIT fix is present at :466-482 and is correct.

- The CPU sink implements NO z-range policy at all: z_clip_min/max and z_cull
  are decoded into the struct and never read again, and nv2a_d3d11.c has no
  reference either. So it is four policies across four sinks, two of them
  "none" -- worse than the recorded "three sinks, three policies". And
  metal_batch_test.c:113 asserts the opposite of the code ("the software path
  clamps every fragment to [z_clip_min, z_clip_max] when z_cull is off"), which
  is load-bearing for that fixture's base_state() fix.

- g_hw_state_refusals counts real refusals (return nil, safe) and SILENT
  SUBSTITUTIONS (cmp forced to ALWAYS, stencil ops forced to KEEP -- the draw
  renders wrong) in one variable, against a header that promises "refuse the
  STATE, never silently guess it". Measured never fired: refusals=0 in every
  metal_hw line in the tree.

- The software fallback pipeline is built once at init as RGBA32Float and the
  surface is B5G6R5Unorm when hw_565 is on, so any draw taking the software
  tail while hardware is up binds mismatched formats. Measured never reached:
  2,396 "MIXED draws" lines, all =0.

Smaller, all measured latent: MSL cmpu has no zero-func default where the CPU's
compare_value does; MSL shade() drops the diffuse for untextured non-combiner
state; combiner_input can index past a 14-entry register file and only the
D3D11 emitter defends; the zeta format is validated only when the depth test is
on; sample_lod's mip stride omits the rgba8 case; the [BLEND] dedupe key has
overlapping fields; s_texture_reasons and s_vsh_reject drop reasons past their
caps with no overflow counter; sa_clear counts clears with nothing retained;
capture_draw writes object-space inputs under a field named "vertices" whenever
RECOMP_METAL_VSH is on, which is now the default; the "over-33ms" bin actually
starts at 33.5 ms.


=============================================================================
7. AUDITED AND FOUND CORRECT -- DO NOT SPEND TIME HERE
=============================================================================

Verified line by line against the NV2A encodings and, where applicable, across
all three sinks:

  fill rule and edge functions; barycentrics and perspective correction;
  register combiners including input mapping, the alpha-half channel select,
  the register file indices and the final combiner; DXT1/DXT3 decode; the Xbox
  rectangular Morton swizzle; texture register decode including the signed
  13-bit lod_bias; the mip walk; stencil in full (ZERO vs KEEP, the two masks,
  operation order); Z24S8 packing; blending and dither; the `direct` fast path
  and its guards; every texel and framebuffer bound; primitive assembly across
  all three sinks; the Metal texture cache (keyed AND memcmp-verified, measured
  2,738,761 hits of 2,755,903); the enum tables and their static asserts;
  nv2a_dma_resolve's RAMHT arithmetic; nv2a_pusher.c's header decode; the ring
  loop in main.c; frame_pct/frame_stats_flip; and the three 15-Sep vertex-shader
  fixes (fp contraction, the a*0 rule, pow()-based LIT) in BOTH emitters --
  all three verified correct as landed.

Also confirmed: vertex arrays are not DMA-relative in this title (measured,
base=0x00000000), so fetch_attr's absolute-VA assumption holds; and
s_vsh_gpu_batch / s_vsh_force_cpu have no lifetime leak on any path.
```
